ekegusii: Komenta nayio, the Mean Score nigo ere 8.7. Nigo yatiira korwa ase 8.3 ase omwaka o 2011. Ntwe nigo togoteba buna mbuya mono and congratulations ase Nyabururu Girls High School, ase egasi engiya ase KCSE 2012. May God continue to bless Kenya.

english: The History of Mwanyagetinge: Abande Namokwanwa, Leader of the Maeba Clan, The Famous Warrior!
ekegusii: Emebayeno Ya Mwanyagetinge: Abande Namokwanwa, Timonga Chinkore Chia Maeba, Chigocha Chiaichora Enyongo!

english: People with good intentions who understand this history are asked to come forward and share it with Mwanyagetinge, which has been passed down through generations and elders: Petronilla Ogoti, Gusii.com
ekegusii: Abaminto omorabaro oyo okobwatia nigo ore oyomo ase emebayeno eri yainto ntwe Mwanyagetinge, eri yateretwe ase enchera y' omoino amo na abagaka baito abakoro: Petronilla Ogoti, Gusii.com

english: Good people should work together to make things easier, so that Abande Namokwanwa, Leader of the Maeba Clan, The Famous Warrior can be remembered. Is this the reason for this story on Mwamogusii?
ekegusii: Omogaso oyomo tokare koria ritoke omogoye, omogaka sokoro ominto nigo antebetie buna Abande Namokwanwa Timonga Chinkore Chia Maeba, Chigocha Chiaichora enyongo. Bono ninki eng'encho y' omorabaro oyo o Mwamogusii?

english: Gusii Proverbs: Are people discussing this with advice? Returning respect to the family of Maeba, who lived in Kebura Nchogu, South Mugirango, Kisii County. Pictures with Petronillah Ogoti, Gusii.com files.
ekegusii: Amaridadi a Gusii: Baminto motakomenta echae n' amandasi naende? Kobweria endagera ase enka y' omogaka Maeba, aaria Kebura Nchogu, South Mugirango, Kisii County. Picture na Petronillah Ogoti, Gusii.com files.

english: Truly, gather around, everyone, so that the story of this history can be heard. It is also important to remember that the elder got tired of being disturbed by Maeba. This elder is known to be wise and knowledgeable, and they always have wisdom to share with those who seek it. Furthermore, this elder is still alive today and remembers everything clearly, and their respect for their ancestors remains strong.
ekegusii: Aaiga, ritangani, sokoro nigo antebetie buna omogano bw' omorabaro yo nore aroro. Nigo sokoro antebetie buna abwo kare kare, omogaka gete narengeo orenge korokwa Maeba. Bono omogaka oyo nigo amanyekanete koba omuya ase ekenyoro kiaye, naende nigo arenge omogaka bw' amasikani ase eng'encho arenge korwa obokonyi bonde bwensi gocha ase ekenyoro eke kiaye. Ase boigo, omogaka oyo nigo ekiage kiaye giachire kera engaki, naende endagera tiyarenge kobora ase enka yaye.

english: Elder Maeba has spoken.
ekegusii: Omogaka Maeba nigo achiete nguma

english: So Maeba spoke and his children listened carefully. His children were grateful, and they continued to live according to his teachings, and the wisdom he shared helped them overcome challenges and succeed because of Maeba. That person is always helping others, and whenever they see someone struggling, they help them and encourage them to persevere.
ekegusii: Bono Maeba nigo anchete korageria na koa abaamate baye ebinyugwa. Abaamate baye ekero baigotire, nigo barenge komotera n' omoino bakomotogia, ase eng'encho onde taiyo orenge kobakonya na kobarageria buna Maeba. Omoyega oyo oye nigo orenge korenta abanto oroche, gocha bwoye ekiagera nigo bare koragera na konywa ebinto ao ao.

english: Those who listen to him, their lives will be blessed, just like the clan that benefited from the knowledge. So let the children learn and continue to live according to the traditions of Abande Namokwanwa, Leader of the Maeba Clan, The Famous Warrior!!
ekegusii: Abanto kibaikire bwoye, nigo enyongo yarenge goterekwa n' amarwa, kere ne chinkore erinde abanto banya gosiberia n' omogoko. Bono ekero abaamate barageire na konywa buya, nigo barenge gotera omoino bagoteba buna Abande Namokwanwa Timonga Chinkore Chia Maeba, Chigocha Chiaichora Enyongo !!

english: Consider this, this story is worth sharing! Respect the elders and people, who tell stories about this week. Goodbye now and thank you for listening.
ekegusii: Gochakera abwo, omobayeno oyo okaba ogotebwa! Koru ase omogaka sokoro ominto, oyo noro omobayeno oito for this week. Mbuya mono and thank you for listening.

english: The language of the Gusii people is rich and has a large vocabulary used by both elders and children, including various names. The home is also rich in traditions passed down from parents and grandparents to their children and grandchildren, which are carefully preserved over time.
ekegusii: Enyangi y’Omogusii nigo yarenge n’engencho enene ase abamura na abaiseke amo ne’chiamate chiabo. Enywomo nero yarenge egetambokero ase omomura n’omoiseke korua ase amaboko abaibori babo na gochaka koagacha omochie obo.

english: In ancient times, the home was not like what it is today. In the past of the Gusii people, skilled craftsmen and builders built houses with their own hands and decorated them beautifully.
ekegusii: Engaki eyuo, enywomo tiyare koba onye enyangi teraba. Engaki ya kare ase Gusii, omosubati obegete ebitinge nigo are koegwa amasikani amanene kegima, ekiagera oyuo ’ng’ina ’monto (‘banto) okoagacha egesaku. Yare gotoka buna oirerwe kare nchera, nigo are gokobwa goika mwaye, koenekia buna oikire buya.

english: These stories tell us about the history of the Gusii people; these stories of old are told during important ceremonies, which bring joy and unity ('people') together and create a sense of community. It happened that when someone died, they were mourned greatly, and songs were sung to comfort them, hoping they would return.
ekegusii: Egetabu eke nigo kebwate obosemia obuya kegima ase engaki ya rero; obo obosemia obonene bw’okoagacha emechie, mono kobwatekana buna ense yaonchokire ekero abange batari korora buna enywomo n’egento ki’engencho enene buna egwenerete.

english: Uhuru has been communicating with the government throughout the entire period; Col (rtd) Cyrus Oguna
ekegusii: Uhuru tabwateraniri na gokong’a kwobogima ime yense; Col (rtd) Cyrus Oguna

english: Written by Zachary Mayieka on July 6, 2022
ekegusii: Written by Zachary Mayieka on July 6, 2022

english: The spokesperson, Cyrus Oguna, stated that President Uhuru Kenyatta should not be allowed to continue interfering with the affairs of the entire country of Kenya
ekegusii: Omonogeri bwe eserekali Cyrus Oguna otebire omorai bwense Uhuru Kenyatta tabwenereti gotamerwa ase ogokina kwa amagori yebinto ime yense ya Kenya

english: According to reports from various media outlets, Oguna explained that interference with the affairs and continuous communication secretly causes more harm than good to Kenya under Uhuru.
ekegusii: Gokwana ne egetaseni ekemo kioboraria , Oguna nigo aenekia buna ogokina kwa amagori nomochando obwateraneti chinse chinyinge aseigo mochando oywo tori o’ Kenya gose Uhuru.

english: He further stated that Uhuru Kenyatta does not want to take responsibility for his actions regarding the ongoing war between Russia and Ukraine which has caused great suffering to the people of Kenya.
ekegusii: Nigo Oguna amentire goteba buna Uhuru Kenyatta tabwati kobua konde gwensi ase chisegi chigendererete gati yense ya Russia na Ukraine eyu egerete anene mono ase ogokina kwobogima bwa abakenya.

english: They are now discussing the differences between Deputy President William Ruto and the allegations that the relationship between President Uhuru and Raila Odinga which was established through a handshake in 2018, led to interference in the affairs of the entire country of Kenya.
ekegusii: Boigo nairaneria amang’ana yoomokonyi bwomorai bwense omosike William Ruto ase atebete buna ogokwanania gati yomorai bwense omosike Uhuru na Raila odinga okwo komanyekanete buna handshake omwaka bwe chiribu ibere na ikomi na isano na isato (2018), nenchera eyemo esegetete ogokina kwamagori yebinto ime yense ya Kenya.

english: He urged politicians to stop making statements that they cannot fulfill and to focus on uniting the country. He also explained that it is important for leaders to work together, peacefully and with clear goals.
ekegusii: Obaboririe abanasiasa batige gotumeka amang’ana buna aywo atabwati bokeene bonde bwensi ase okogania kwemanyekani . Boigo naenekia buna koru abarai abwo babere bakwanani, omorembe na amagenderero arorekanire.

english: Bono went to visit his mother in Bitutu village, Manga Esikimu, who is very sick and needs help from Bwanchi Bwamang'eire, Ntengora Bokorigia. Is this the reason he went to see Mwanyagetinge?
ekegusii: Bono tokare nchera kogenda ase enyangi ya Bitutu aaria Manga Esikimu, omong'ina magokoro baba ominto okare goteba buna Bwanchi Bwamang'eire, Ntengora Bokorigia. Bono ninki eng'encho y' omorabaro oyo gocha ase tore ntwe Mwanyagetinge?

english: Website address: Gusii.com at home in Metamaywa, Borabu, Nyamira County. They say people should compete to help their neighbors who are suffering, so they can get assistance when they need it. When people help each other and work together, it brings joy to everyone!! Mwanyagetinge.com/2014
ekegusii: Amaridadi ya amaiso: Gusii.com at home aaria Metamaywa, Borabu, Nyamira County. Nabo omoiseke arenge koanga gosiganwa gochia ase omomura oria atancheti. Kobaorokia abamura aba bachire ase ekerorano buna ere tatageti momura oyio, nigo arenge koabusa ekeoreri, riria baikaransire. Bono riria abamura aba baikaransire bakagete buna nkogenigwa bare, enyaroka yachaka koabusa omochi obo !! Mwanyagetinge.com/2014

english: This matter should be investigated further. Yes.
ekegusii: Chinyangi tichiarenge gokorerwa nchera. Yaya.

english: Friends, these things happen, and life is full of surprises, including challenges. Come on, people, let this issue be resolved quickly!! People should compete, striving to help others.
ekegusii: Aaiga, aya akwaneire, n' enyangi gati y' moiseke, amo n' omomura. Ritang'ani, baminto manya ng'a chinyangi chia kare nchiagakoreirwe nchera !! Omoiseke nigo arenge gosiganwa, goetera ase okorigia obochege.

english: Bono wants people to compete, and leaders and elders should come together to solve this problem completely, looking at both sides of the story. The truth will prevail, and it will bring peace to the community.
ekegusii: Bono nonya omoiseke osiganirwe, nigo abagaka amo na abang'ina abanene barenge kounenkia emechie eye ebere, koenekia gose emecheie eyio n' emiya. Emechie emebe, bigo yarenge gotwara obokongu konyora omomura, gose omoiseke omuya.

english: In Ekegusii culture, Okomang'ana always helps those in need, offering support and encouragement. It is important to respect traditions and customs, and to maintain unity and harmony.
ekegusii: Ase Ekegusii ki' omobayeno oyo, Okomang'ana nakw' ogochoka obwanchani ase enchera endonge, gose okoria oboko. Ekero okonyora ase okonywoma korwa, nigo okonyora kwamang'ire omochi okonywoma koru boikeranu, naende gwatwara obomaene buna oboiri obo n'obuya.

english: The old Gusii people were known for their kindness. It is good to remember the past and learn from our ancestors, so we can continue to live in peace.
ekegusii: Abagusii abakoro mbamanyete kare. Nigo ere buya kounenkia omochie oria otagete konywoma, gose konywomwa gochi

english: As we look ahead, we should strive to create a better future for our children, ensuring they have access to education and opportunities. This tradition has been passed down through generations, and we must uphold it.
ekegusii: Ase okoenekia, nigo okoboria abanto erinde otware omogano omuya naende omoikeranu. Enchera ende omobayeno oyo n' ogosegeta buna ekero otagete konywoma, nere buya oenekie kegima buna enyomba okonywoma gose okonywomwa gochi, teri mbe.

english: In the past, the Gusii people did not tolerate injustice, and they stood up against oppression. Today, we must honor their legacy by supporting Bwanchi Bwamang'eire, Ntengora Bokorigia. Let us unite and help those in need, remembering the importance of compassion and empathy.
ekegusii: Ase engencho Omogusii omokoro atagete chinywomo chitari gosiboka, naende chire n' obwanchani, ekagera agatoa omobayeno oyo ogoteba buna Bwanchi Bwamang'eire, Ntengora Bokorigia. Korwa ase omongina magokoro baba ominto, oyo noro omobayeno oito ase ewiki eye.

english: Thank you very much for listening.
ekegusii: Mbuya mono and thank you for listening.

english: Little children's stories
ekegusii: Chianga chiane chiesukuru

english: This story is about a child who learns something, big and small. This story is adapted from the "SEED story" developed by the University of KwaZulu-Natal.
ekegusii: Ase omogano oyo omwana nigo akoerengia chianaga chinge, chinene na echi chimoisane. Omogano oyo nigo orwete ase “SEED story” korwa eyunibasiti ya Kwazulu-Natal.

english: The mother and the pot
ekegusii: Omotugi n’enasari yaye

english: The story tells of a woman who finds a beautiful pot while walking in the forest. The pot is made of clay and decorated by skilled craftsmen.
ekegusii: Omogano igora ya ogokonya ebirerwa bieching’iti chikoretwa ase enasari ye chitangana. Ebirerwa ebio nigo bikorerwa nomonto obene na abakonyi bande.

english: How can we make peace?
ekegusii: Ning’o orobare goika ikomi?

english: How can a person solve a difficult problem through wisdom and intelligence?
ekegusii: Ning’o orabe omoruoti bweching’iti chiorosana maega yeechui korwa oboruoti?

english: Anansi asks the sky god for stories
ekegusii: Anansi orenteire abanto emegano

english: Opening a difficult lock
ekegusii: Kobara chinyang’au chiorosana

english: The lock is very strong and hard to open, but it can be opened with skill and effort.
ekegusii: Chinyang’au nigo chire nerang’o aseigo chibare buna chigochia konywa amache.

english: A generous person
ekegusii: Omonto omotambe mono

english: That person who shares this story is a generous person and someone who always helps others and does good deeds. That person is known for their ability to understand and appreciate everything around them.
ekegusii: Omonto oyo ore ase omogano oyo nigoare omontambe mono na ase igo keregento nigokere ekieng’e na egeke asare. Omonto oyo nigo agotatora obokong’u goetera ase okoreng’ania ebinto bionsi bimoreng’ane.

english: The greedy giant
ekegusii: Omoguko ogokwana

english: Gusii Culture And Customs CXIX: Is Petronillah Indeed a Daughter, a Woman of Character and Good Reputation?
ekegusii: Abagusii Culture And Customs CXIX: Bono Petronillah Inee, Omokungu Ngosereta Arenge Na Kobuna Enyomba?

english: Mwanyagetinge.com has been thoroughly investigated. It is through this investigation that we have understood the character of the Gusii woman, her reputation and her household. This investigation reveals things that were hidden, and I now understand how to approach and investigate further. Perhaps, it is because the elder approaches people with kindness that the Gusii community respects them greatly, their reputation and their possessions.
ekegusii: Mwanyagetinge.com ntwaborigwa riborio. Bono nigo twaborigwa gose omokungu Omogusii ngosereta arenge enyomba. Bono riborio eri kiriaba riikongu, nche nigo naimogete nkagenda o sokoro, koboria. Kinaboria, nigo omogaka sokoro ominto antebetie buna Gusii yaito amang'ana y' egekoro narengeo, ayio arenge ay' eng'encho mono.

english: Sources of information: Gusii.com at home is located at Menyinkwa Market, Nyaribari Chache, Kisii County. Pictures from Petronillah Ogoti, Mwanyagetinge.com files.
ekegusii: Amaridadi y' amaiso: Gusii.com at home aaria Menyinkwa Market, Nyaribari Chache, Kisii County. Picture na Petronillah Ogoti, Mwanyagetinge.com files.

english: A woman who appreciates good manners is respected!
ekegusii: Omokungu komumekeria egechuuri nigo yarenge chimuuma!

english: If someone does not want these things to be done, then let things happen as they may, let them be. However, a person should not despise another’s household, but rather appreciate their efforts, so that they can appreciate their own household in return. Yes. Appreciating others is like appreciating the elder’s household.
ekegusii: Bono onye amang'ana aya tare koba takorwa, nigo ebinto gete ebibe, biare koba. Ase omobwekano, ekero omokungu akoagacha enyomba ebe, naende aseerete obonyansi, tarenge komumekeri enyomba igoro. Yaya. Okomumekeria nigo kwarenge kw' omogaka bw' enyomba.

english: Moreover, remember that when an elder matures, good manners become apparent! This honest person in the household, always appreciates good manners, and the household is well regarded. But if someone doesn’t care, the reputation will not be appreciated. Work hard at it, and you will be praised, people will respect you.
ekegusii: Naboigo, inyora buna omogaka gakuure, nigo egechuri kiarenge kobunwa! Bono omosacha nyene enyomba, nere orenge komumekeri egechuuri, enyomba keyakorirwe goseretwa. Bono ko onye taiyo, nigo omosereti akoyemumekeri. Korwa abwo, etwani yanyenywa, abanto baragera.

english: It is the elder who is honored, who receives gifts and blessings, even in old age!
ekegusii: Nigo omogaka akaganyirwe, goikera ekero akoirana bwoye, neba n' emiaka ikomi!

english: However, also know that if an elder is not present, their wisdom still prevails, and they are remembered, receiving gifts and blessings even in old age!
ekegusii: Ase boigo, nabo yarenge koba buna omogaka nyene tari aange, gose nigo akameneyete aare. Aaiga, onye omogaka oyo tari aang'e, nigo akoganywa, goikera kaa ekero akworoka bwoye, neba n' emiaka ikomi!

english: Comment also on the reputation of the household, so that the reputation of the household is maintained (respect for the household’s foundation). If you work hard at it, it shows that this woman is a good person, possessing qualities, and she won’t lack anything. An honest person in the household always appreciates and works hard to maintain its reputation!
ekegusii: Komenta nayio omosereti enyomba tarenge gosereta enyomba akore, tatigari orogoma (ensemo gotira y' enyomba ekona ). Aise gokora igo, nigo yarenge boba buna nigo omokungu oyio akoima omosacha oye, eng'encho ende, atagete akwe. Omosacha nyene enyomba nere orenge gosereta na gokora orogoma rwe enyomba!

english: Mr. Amos Wako has been given respect. America has refused that the Constitution of Kenya will not be American. What is it? It seems there is no intention of amending the constitution of Kenya and amending citizens. Truly Mr. Amos Wako fell ill, and he went until he reached Charles Njonjo. He went to wear the suit of the attorney general Njonjo which was very old and almost torn, so it wasn't good to be seen by Americans because they were suspicious. Many leaders of Kenyan politics wore that suit. It was a terrible thing. And now the British have come. Then Mr. Wako calmed down and went to the area near the American Embassy and also the American representative office in Kenya, and the following things happened: 1. Kenyans were angered. They contributed Ksh. 1.7 million for the campaign. But they haven't yet received legal assistance. We don't want the leadership of this politics. He disagreed with Eric Holder with a stamp.
ekegusii: Mhe. Amos Wako osiekeirwe isiko. Amerika yakanire inga Omonene Bwa Amachiko a Kenya tatacha Amerika. Ase ki? Kiabeire inga tari gokora gasi ya okorenda amachiko a Kenya na korenda Abananchi. Ekero Mhe. Amos Wako aigwa igo, nigo aimoka ogenda impaka o Charles Njonjo. Nigo agenda kwoyia esuti yo omogaka Njonjo ekiagera eyaye konyora terainagwa korwa Amerika ase yachiete gosibigwa. Momanyete abanene ba amachiko Kenya nigo bakobeka esuti eyemo. Ebwate chinchwara. Erio ne richiko Abangeresa baetetie. Nigo Mhe. Wako aminyoka na amagoro impaka aaria ase Embasi Ya Amerika na koa Omotenenri bwa Amerika ime ya Kenya, riuko rikobwatia:1.Abakenya nigo banganchete. Nigo bakongakana Ksh. 1.7 millioni kera omotienyi. Igo bado tibaramenta chialawensi. Inwe timwancheti omonene bwa amachiko aino. Nigo mogoakana Eric Holder chifudi sitampu chioka.

english: 2.We had 50 states. We remember commenting about joining Hawaii in 1959! This matter is confusing. Mention the states. Currently Kenya has 210 constituencies. And we continue with this government.
ekegusii: 2.Inwe nigo mobwate chistate 50 chioka. Timwanya komenta kende gesa mobeka Hawaii omwaka 1959! Chingaki chiachenchirie. Menta chistate. Intwe Kenya nigo tobwate chikonstituensi 210. Naende intomente echinde.

english: 3.We have many workers from different homes who are Kenyans. The workers of Eric Holder are from Mexico.
ekegusii: 3.Nimbwate abakori emeremo ba nyomba bonsi bare AbaKenya. Abakori emeremo ba Eric Holder nigo barwete Mexico.

english: 4.There is a suit that goes around the area. And there is trouble with the suit and the cloth coming from Zimbabwe and Sudan. That cloth troubled the citizens. America goes around the area.

english: 5.Kenya has problems. There is no peace anywhere since the politics are disturbed. That is what causes trouble and hardship for the citizens. However, America, it is stable and prosperous. english: Long ago, years and years ago, Mansamu and Ogasusu had a very big problem. Because of this, they searched for solutions to their problems, and finally they found some peace. With this peace, they found it with their mothers, and then they lived happily.
ekegusii: Abwo kare kare, emiaka n' emiaka, Mansamu n' Ogasusu mbarenge aroro. Bono aba babere nigo banchaine ekianda gia ikomi, naende nigo bamenyete aamo orosana ime. Aaiga orosana ime, aba babere nigo bamenyete na abamama babo, abwo konye bagotire kegima.

english: When they asked their mothers, Mansamu and Ogasusu were told a strange story, a very strange story. It was surprising, Mansamu said, “What kind of story is this, and what does this story mean?” Below, Mansamu listened carefully to the story they were told.
ekegusii: Ko baonia abamama babo, Mansamu n' Ogasusu bakagora endagera egotonontera baire nka, koinagera. Ogoitera chindende, Mansamu nigo eboretie buna, "Ndi ngocha goika nka, na kobweria endagera eye?" Below, Mansamu oyio okoayerera gochi nka n' endagera bagorire.

english: That day the weather was very good, and everything looked beautiful. After that, the pot began to boil. Ogasusu and Mansamu wanted something, like the contents of the pot. But Mansamu took a closer look at what was happening, so people wouldn't blame the pot.
ekegusii: Engaki eyemo omorakera okaba omotindi, n' ebimeri bikaoma mogondo. Korwa abwo, enchara egacha etindi. Ogasusu na Mansamu bakarea mono, ase eng'encho ye enchara. Bono Mansamu agatwara ekerengererio gio okoonia ng'ina, erinde banyore eng'eria tibakwa enchara.

english: They gathered their friends and relatives together, to help them with their work. Ogasusu told Mansamu that she would finish the work. However, despite this, Ogasusu went ahead and did things her own way, and put the leftovers aside.
ekegusii: Bagatebania babeke abaibori babo chigunia ime na babaire echiro, kobakorera oboonchoreria. Ogasusu akang'aina Mansamu buna mbakunora chigunia echi. Nonya nabo igo, Ogasusu akagenda akabisa ng'ina, na kobeka ebichanchabe eguni eyio ime.

english: When it was time to leave, they asked their mothers, and Ogasusu refused to tell them the secrets of the things they knew, saying they should stop bothering her with those matters! But they insisted on asking their friends and kept searching. When they met, they told each other different stories.
ekegusii: Ko baika echiro, bakaoni abamama babo, korende Oogasusu agakana buna mbaigora ebinyorini ebi egekogera nigo barabaise kominchoka batame korwa ebinyorini ime! Bono aba bakaonia abaibori babo na koegwa chibesa. Ko bakoirana, bakagora chindagera ao ao.

english: But again Ogasusu just continued to be stubborn!!
ekegusii: Bono ng'ina Ogasusu oyio okare kwerindori gocha !!

english: They went back to their homes, and remembered the strange story. Quickly, when the story ended, Mansamu grabbed his belongings and ran towards Ogasusu who was still being stubborn, rushing home so they could remember the story!! But Mansamu realized something, which Ogasusu noticed and refused to share.
ekegusii: Bagoika riabo nyomba, bakarosia endagera egotonontera. Keri keri, riria endagera yayire iga, Mansamu agaakwa n' ekeondoko ekero aroche ng'ina Ogasusu okare kwerindori, gosoa nyomba erinde basange endagera !! Bono Mansamu agasinyua eki agokora, ekiagera nigo Ogasusu among'ainete akaonia ng'ina.

english: After that, Ogasusu and Mansamu became very close.
ekegusii: Korwa erio, Ogasusu amo n' Mansamu mbachieti koigwana.

english: This is a true story, a story from the heart, a story about kindness. Thank you very much and thank you for listening.
ekegusii: Oyo noro omogano oito, korwa ase magokoro, ase omokubio oyo. Mbuya mono and thank you for listening.

english: Kisii Municipal Council Deputy Mayor Patrick Aming'a Siro lost his seat due to an election petition. Kisii Resident Magistrate Njeri Thuku ruled that the petition was valid because Siro was accused of bribery and influencing voters in Nyaura Ward.
ekegusii: Kisii Municipal Council Deputy Mayor Patrick Aming'a Siro lost his seat rituko ria igoro. Kisii Resident Magistrate Njeri Thuku nigo arwete obogambi inga Siro taakeretwe kura buya na kobua korwa Nyaura Ward.

english: Kisii Resident Magistrate Thuku ruled that the case was strong enough because there were witnesses, including Charles Ombuna. Witness Ombuna testified that there were irregularities during the 2007 elections, which led to Patrick Siro being elected.
ekegusii: Kisii Resident Magistrate Thuku nigo arwete obogambi obwo ase ekina kiabegetwe ase ekoti no omokansora omokoro, omosike Charles Ombuna. Kansora Ombuna nigo agoteba inga amagoso narenge aroro ase chikura chio omwaka o 2007, echio chiagerete omosike Patrick Siro akaba omobui.

english: Resident Judge Njeri Thuku stated that “the Nyaura Ward election was free and fair. She added that the election results for Nyaura Ward were accurate.” In addition, Magistrate Njeri stated that she would hold The Interim Independent Electoral Commission (IIEC) responsible for conducting future elections.
ekegusii: Resident Judge Njeri Thuku nigo atebete inga "chikura chia Nyaura Ward tichiarenge free and fair. Igo natebire inga chikura chiaakwe naende korwa Nyaura Ward". Komenta nayio, nigo Magistrate Njeri atebete inga goika The Interim Independent Electoral Commission (IIEC) ebe responsible ase ogoakia chikura chinyia.

english: However, Siro and IIEC lawyer Charles Otiso stated that they would appeal. "We will appeal so that this decision can be reviewed by a higher court." Siro also said he would consult with his lawyers.
ekegusii: Nonya nabo igo, Siro amo na IIEC lawyer omosike Onchari Otiso nigo batebete inga imbache babeke e appeal. "Goika to appeal ase obogambi obo bwarurwe ekiagera tibori obwe ekeene". Nabo Siro atebetie abariki abwo isiko ye Ekoti.

english: Siro stated that he was not given a chance to tell his side of the story, Magistrate Thuku stated that Siro did not submit anything. No court documents, did not call witnesses, and that the truth could only be determined through another election.
ekegusii: Nonya Siro otebete inga taetwe ribaga goteba his side of the story, Magistrate Thuku nigo atebete inga Siro did not file anything. No court briefs, did not call witnesses, naende inga ekeene nigo keratoke through probability eyio egocha koba possible through another election.

english: Ombuna and his supporters claimed that they had won the election in Boronyi Ward. Ombuna stated that he wanted to show them how they voted in Nyaura Ward, but that option was not available on the ballot paper.
ekegusii: Ombuna amo na abasaidi baye nigo bagoteba inga nigo baagete chikura ase Boronyi Ward. Nigo Ombuna atebete inga tiyare konyarekana baakere ekura ase Nyaura Ward ekiagera option eyio tiyarenge on the ballot paper.

english: In his application to the High Court, Ombuna stated that residents of Nyaura Ward were denied a chance to vote due to confusion at the polling stations. Ombuna testified that the irregularities occurred under the now-defunct Electoral Commission of Kenya.
ekegusii: Ase application yaye gochia se Ekoti, Ombuna nigo atebete inga abaaki chiukura ba Nyaura Ward were denied a chance to vote ase engencho ye mix-up ya polling stations. Ombuna nigo agoteba inga amagoso nigo akoretwe na now defunct Electoral Commission of Kenya.

ekegusii: Okorusigwa ekerogo gwa Siro as e deputy mayor nigo kore e big blow ase Kisii Mayor Sam Nyangeso ekiagera abwo babere nigo bare abasani abanene sana.

english: The jackfruit family includes trees from the fig family (Moraceae, specifically the mulberry tree). It originates from Asia and especially the Pacific islands. Jackfruit trees grow well in tropical climates. The breadfruit tree is closely related to Artocarpus altilis. Artocarpus integer (Cempedak), Artocarpus heterophyllus (Jackfruit, Nangka), and also Artocarpus odoratissimus (Marang) all belong to the jackfruit family.

english: This information comes from the Marang (Artocarpus odoratissimus) fruit. It grows mainly in the mountains of Borneo, Indonesia. english: Welwitschia (Welwitschia mirabilis) is a unique plant found in the deserts of Namibia and Angola in Africa. Welwitschia itself is very strange because it only has two leaves throughout its life. The plant grows slowly and lives for a very long time, with some specimens living for over a thousand years, appearing like large, old piles. Welwitschia is a plant that survives through fog.
ekegusii: Welwitscha (Welwitscha mirabilis) nigo kere ekemeri kiamete amatuko amatang’ani amwanyabanto, egekwama ase asinine ase ekengeka ki’enyancha ime ya Namibia na Angola ya maate. Welwitschia maene nigo ore omote korende tori kororekana boigo ekero okororekana ritang’ani. Ekemeri ekegima nigo kebwate ritina erimo rinene ribwate amato abere amanene akwama-aya akororekana buna ebisicha ebinene bieringete bikaba ebigare. Welwitschia ndire ekororekana buna egetunwa ki’eubi.

english: The plant also has a strong stem (like a trunk, woody) - which does not branch like other plants. Welwitschia is a plant that grows from the ground, with its roots (deep and shallow) spreading widely to absorb moisture. The leaves are always green (even when they are old) and have many small ridges on them.
ekegusii: Ekemeri eke nigo botambe kere ase engaki y’okomera (nonyen’enkaki y, obotobu) – eyio etari gokoreka mono ase ebimeri. Welwitschia n’ekemeri getari koibora gioka, igo ebimeri bibere (egesacha n’egekungu) mbiganeiri korosia entetere. Ebisicha nigo bire buna chichuba (buna biri bie chipaini gose chisikadi)bire gati gati y’amato.

english: This unusual plant can survive extreme heat and drought, and it stores water in its stem and roots.
ekegusii: Chikoni chinsubati echikwerusekani ekero chiakinire korusia chinteretere chiabo chire chingusu, echio chigosiaru bwango n’embeo.

english: It belongs to the group of plants called Gnetophyta which are related to conifers (Pinophyta). Gnetophyta has three families with similar characteristics: Gnetum vines with shiny leaves, Ephedra - with branches resembling Welwitschia's stems.
ekegusii: Nigo chigotoka ase ekemeri egekoro gia Gnetophyta ebi bire oboiribwang’e ne chikonifa chikorokwa (Pinophyta). Gnetophyta ebwate ebisaku bitato ebing’ao ekero okorigereri okororekana kwabo: Gnetum lianas ebwate amato amororo, Ephedra – ebwate amagwa amona Welwitschia enyene.

english: Welwitschia is named after the Austrian botanist Friedrich Welwitsch who discovered it in 1860. Welwitschia is also a symbol of Namibia.
ekegusii: Welwitscha nigo yanyorete erieta riaye korwa ase omonyamete korwa Slovenia okorokwa Friedeich Welwitscha oomwaka o 1860. Welwitschia nkwama ere ase ebendera ya Namibia.

english: Welwitschia also tolerates harsh conditions and is able to live. It needs little rain but also endures strong winds from the ocean. These adaptations allow it to survive in the harsh environment of Welwitschia. A major reason this plant doesn't die is because it has deep roots that reach underground. Its roots spread wide (sometimes up to 2–5 meters wide) absorbing moisture from the soil. It takes Welwitschia a long time to grow and develop, but once established it becomes very strong. The root system is strong and helps support the plant. Also, it continues to grow slowly and remains stable for many years. To survive, Welwitschia relies heavily on fog, which provides moisture to the plant, even though it lives in a dry area. This plant is truly remarkable and shows how plants can adapt to survive in difficult environments.
ekegusii: Welwitscha nabo ekoigwana bwango n’ase are aomo mono.Tari buna nigo etegemeete embura mono naende nabo ekonyoraamache aisaine korwa ase amare agocha korwa nyancha. Aya n’amang’ana atakeire oinyore ekero okoyosimeka omote o Welwitschia. Esababu enene omote oyo o Welwitschia otari kwama buya n’ekero aobekeire amache amange egereogunda. Igo netakeire chintetere chiasimekea ase omochanga (wchinyeke chibe chimirimita 2–5 ase obogare) ekiagwera amarabaakogacha amache egeka gtari maya ase ogokinna kwaye. Netakeire Welwitschia eumoreru amache n’okorenda okonene gose ebekerwe omoika. Chintetere echikomera ase echuma eyemo. Nabo naende chirasimekwe chibekwe ase etirisa igoro chirigererie maate. Ekero ogosimeka Welwitscha, goika obe omoremereria mono ekiagera ekemeri eke nigo gekwama ng’ora mono nigo ere e dainosa ase ogokwana ekeene. Eise koegwa oborabu obonge moono amo n’amache amange, kemer eke ngekwama gekaokwe ogetige.

english: It is time to move forward. This practice which continues to perpetuate FGM and child marriage, shames Kenya. Nyamira County Women's Representative, Hon Alice Chae said that we should forget about the past and encourage the Abagusii people to move on, so that this harmful tradition does not continue.

english: We need to thank the government for taking action against those who commit these crimes, both current and former officials, including leaders and former leaders, and all those involved in this bad behavior," Hon Angwenyi added. “The future of the Abagusii people depends on ensuring our children are safe” Hon Angwenyi concluded.

english: This matter also concerns Mwingi North MP Hon John Munuve, who supported Hon. Angwenyi and urged everyone to be careful, and emphasized that our children deserve protection. english: And further, Hon Chae added that the law is already in place, and she respects the traditions of her people. ekegusii: Ase boigo, nigo Mhe Chae atebete buna ekemira eke nigo kere ekebe, naende giateire amatuko aye. They will rejoice because the rains have come, so they can farm! Let the year pass quickly, so that we can start working on the next year.

Nigo barenge gototebia buna toganya embura etwe, omaye kogenda gotenya! Toganya omwaka oike gati, omanye gochaka kobanga eki otagete gokora omwaka oyo omonyia.

english: The year 2013 started very well! Good health to all the children of Mwayagetinge who are interested in the website of Gusii.com. Happy new year, and many blessings to you throughout the year 2013. By Petronillah Ogoti. Gusii.com Proverbs, Culture And Customs Editor. Greetings Kende - Greetings from Masaba [December] 31, 2012.
ekegusii: Omoyega o 2013 obwatire nse pi! Mbuya mono ase abana ba Mwayagetinge ase ogokinia ekebute eke kia Gusii.com. Ogochenga okuya, n' ebisio ebinge ase kera oyomo ase omwaka oyo omoyia o 2013. Na Petronillah Ogoti. Gusii.com Proverbs, Culture And Customs Editor. Egesunte Kende - Egesunte Kia Masaba [ December] 31, 2012.

english: This year was a good year for Kenya because it received sufficient rainfall and the food situation improved greatly. The harvest was abundant, like Borai harvesting maize, and they were full! However, there are some people who don’t understand that a good year doesn’t last forever.
ekegusii: Inyora omwaka oyo nari ense yaito ya Kenya egocha gotwara obochori obotang'ani ase richiko eri riyia riaetigwa bwango iga. Ekurate enene neri buna Borai mboora nguru, boe kiige bori bwomo! Eng'encho ende, rigia abarai bari bare n' obomanyi erinde ense yaito techa gotakaa.

english: Mwayagetinge, I remind you that this year started very well, it was peaceful,
ekegusii: Mwanyagetinge, narorire buna omoyega oyo nigo obwatete inse pi, ebusa yayire,

english: the economy improved, and businesses flourished. People rejoiced and worked hard. Also,
ekegusii: amandasi arosigwe, n' chimbori chianyenyirwe. Baminto ntonywa na koria bobe. Are mono,

english: Gusii.com wants to thank everyone for their support, for visiting the website and sharing information about the Gusii people. Thank you very much, and we will continue improving the website. Anyone who wishes, the website is always available. We wish our child Mwanyagetinge success and blessings throughout the year 2013.

english: The days of the past year passed with Omonguru leading the children of Mwanyagetinge towards progress. Happy New Year 2013!

english: The woman identified herself as having been involved in a road accident and reported stealing items from a house in the Chela area of Siaya County following a dispute with her husband which led to separation, she claimed the disagreement stemmed from her refusal to share property worth Ksh 1,500 which was given to her as dowry.
ekegusii: Omong’ina oyomo bwe emiaka ya igatwa nigo agendererete gokendia ebitingiro biaye aaria echela ya Siaya nyuma y’ogotebekana goita oyomwabo goika ekerengo kio’gokwa, ase engencho egotebekana buna nigo nyagosiran oyio arenge bobwatania ebinto bia omoiti oyo nerideni erio ria chibesa chia kenya 1,500 erio asinyirwe goakana.

english: The incident reportedly happened in the home of Asembo Boi Kasabong in Siaya County and involved several relatives. The suspect, Philister Arega, who claims to be a member of the Tin-to-Ler Women Group, denied the allegations leveled against her by Benter Akinyi's family, claiming they were falsely accusing Akinyi of theft and attempting to seize her property.
ekegusii: oboiti obo bwatigire ekenyoro kia Asembo Boi Kasabong ime ye ekaonti ya Siaya ase amaisugusu amange nyuma ya ababwatani be ekeombe eke ki’abang’ina. Nyagosira, Philister Arega, oyokabeire omorai ase Tin-to-Ler Women Group nigo aumerana na amakweri ase enka ya Benter Akinyiase bachiete na abarai bande gotema koonia enibo ya Akinyi’ erio koirania chibesa echio.

english: Speaking to our correspondent, Esther Odero, Akinyi Akinyi stated that she lent Akinyi Sh2, 000 in April and is now demanding repayment along with interest on the loan.
ekegusii: Koreng’ana na omonyakerogo bwe’keombe ekio omosubati Ester Odero, Akinyi Akinyi nigo asabete chibesa Sh2, 000 korwa ase ekeombe omotienyi bwe Rigwata (April) ase ariete eira yogoakana magega y’omotienyi oyomo.

english: |John Omedo reports on Philister Arega, the suspect accused of theft in the home of Asembo Boi Kasabong in Rarieda Constituency, alleging she went to steal their belongings. . [reported by TITUS MUNALA/STANDARD]|
ekegusii: |John Omedo okoreera ng’ina Philister Arega nyagosira oyio oitwa na oyomo bw’ekeombe aaria Asembo Boi Kasabong’ ime ya Rarieda Constituency amagega y’okogenda kwoyia ridenii riabo. . [omobwekano na TITUS MUNALA/STANDARD]|

english: The local administrator said he had received numerous complaints from people who claimed they had been defrauded by those who borrowed money from them and failed to repay it, leading to disputes. It is alleged that the suspect Arega confessed to being 55 years old and suffering from a mental illness. Residents lamented that thieves were becoming bolder and robbing them during the day. It is also alleged that Omosa, who is over 80 years old, refused to cooperate with police and declined to provide information about the incident, making it difficult for investigators to make arrests.
ekegusii: echuma yaera nigo yarenge nemeremo emekong’u mono ekiagera abarai aba nigo babeire bagoetanana ase baria basabete ebitoki bakaanga goakana koirera koonia chinibo chia abasabi aba.Korende nigo egotebekana buna nyagosira Arega nigo abogoretie ekaraya akamobutoria omong’ina bw’ emiaka 55 akamora nse buna enchogu. abanyakeombe nigo batama magoro nyanche ebitingiro bikabaira gotoria amagima abo. Nigo egotebekana buna Omosacha oyorenge karaire nere ochete gokonya na gotoria ekero anyorete omong’ina oyio oraire bakabuga nigo embeo yamoerera korende bakanyora otwekire mo.

english: This incident occurred in the Nandi Hills area and has caused anxiety among residents who fear that criminals may target them and steal their property. Akinyi, however, filed a report at the Aram Police Station regarding the attack. Rarieda OCPD Johana Chebii confirmed that suspects and Omosa will be arrested and charged with robbery.
ekegusii: Onyango oyo ogokora emeremo aaria Nandi Hills nigo acha inka ase omotimoko omoke na tamanyete buna omorugi oye konye osabire chibesa korwa ekeombe ekio. Akinyi bono nigo abwatire aaria Aram Police Station chingaki obotuki bwachakire. Rarieda OCPD omosike Johana Chebii oyoigete agwo nigo atebete buna abarai na omosacha omosoerwa nere bachikirwe korika oroboti

english: He added that residents should avoid confrontations and resolve issues peacefully instead of taking the law into their own hands, warning that such actions could lead to more problems.

english: Truly, things are very bad; Banana Pedla has completely ruined everything, causing great sorrow and trouble. On behalf of the Omogusii community I want to take this opportunity to express my anger for you over what you did yesterday.
ekegusii: Erieta riane nigo nkorokwa Banana Pedla gose omoonia amatoke korwa taracha. On behalf of the Omogusii community I want to take this opportunity to express my anger for you over what you did yesterday.

english: My brother, you are the most idiotic human ever born by a Kisii woman. Boss, how could you buy a brand new Range Rover worth Ksh15million for a woman/agasagane? It's truly shocking. The sons of Kisii are ashamed of this act.
ekegusii: My brother, you are the most idiotic human ever birthed by a Kisii woman. Boss, how could you buy a brand new Range Rover worth Ksh15million for a woman/agasagane? Yaa gwatoiyeirie pi. Basacha bagusii ntwakabeire igo.

english: Boss, Are you really a typical Kisii man who spent nine months in his mother’s womb? Meaning he worked tirelessly, struggled, and saved up millions only to buy a stranger a car? Did those people like Ongwae Mekenye and Filbert Misire approve of this?
ekegusii: Boss, Are you really a typical Kisii man that spent nine months in his mother’s womb? Yaani okabara esiringi eyemo..ibere..isato mpaka bibitini mirioni just to buy a stranger a car? Abagaka baria babo Ongwae Mekenye na Filbert Misire mbaroche aya?

english: On that note nevertheless, I still wish to take this opportunity to thank our ancestors wherever they are in their graves for preventing it from happening. May their souls reign forever.
ekegusii: On that note nevertheless, I still wish to take this opportunity to thank our ancestors wherever they are in their graves for preventing it from happening. May their souls reign forever.

english: But then again, why would you spend so much money on a woman you have never even met? Is this foolishness reaching its peak? Is this person bewitching you? This is a terrible thing you’ve done, boss.
ekegusii: But then again agaisia aka yaa, why would you buy erori enkon’gu igo for a woman you have never even seen? Omosubati obiarete mpaka orosire? Yaa omotu oo nomoronge ore rakini? Agaisi kari yaa aye nemeseke bosa.

english: Ringitoni, don't you realize that you are bringing shame upon the Gusii people by spending lavishly on women and flaunting it around in Nairobi? What kind of example are you setting? You have disgraced us all, boss. You deserve to be severely punished for this behavior. You have lost your senses, boss. And you did it knowingly.
ekegusii: Ringitoni yaa nomanyete rakini buna inchandegete Gusii aiga nkooni amatoke naye kogotiringa chibesa Nairobi abwo? Maa bono omoerio oye ogosokirie yaa. Aye nerisaera mogongo bosa. Obwenerete gokenyerwa chisese chirie. Aye nomonto negwasiondo bosa. Yaa naye kwabikorire.

english: Now, where are you going to take that vehicle? That car will cause endless problems and bring misfortune, leading to constant arguments and disputes. That car will bring more tears than joy, causing pain and suffering. But honestly, what were you thinking when you made this decision? This matter will lead to serious consequences. Don't think you can escape responsibility. Why are you acting so recklessly? It’s shameful, boss.
ekegusii: Now, where are you going to take that vehicle? Onia egari eyio togore amachagachaga atano chichaburuti tonya kobogoreria emechanga na omeno korwa bogere. Engotu eyio kware kogorera egari nigo ebwate ebichuchu bitano ebiaririe nechitwani chitabauti. Bono aye yaa, inki kerabu ogochi komena? Chianga chioka kwabegete nebiraka. Erongi okobuga ng’a nembeba yariete. Yaa gochi otare koragora erongi engiya obeke? Enyonga bosa.

english: Consider the advice of elders and listen to wise counsel to avoid making further regrettable decisions.
ekegusii: Kora origerie abagaka kende otosabe amabera totarakoragereria.

english: The old man walked a long distance and found little money. Then he went to visit Boreba Mobisa Mbokorura Ocharoke Ko Na Igesa Iganya. “What is this thing about the old man?” He then started complaining bitterly.
ekegusii: Omogaka sokoro ominto nabwate eng'ana. Nigo sokoro agoteba buna Boreba Mobisa Mbokorura Ocharoke Ko Na Igesa Iganya. "Bono ekio ninki omogaka?" Nche nigo natang'ang'a nkoboria.

ekegusii: Omoremi nkogenda are gosamora chibando aaria Nyanguru Hill, Kisii County. Kang'wanigwa n' rise n' chinyanduri, omoremi oyo agaansa gokura, ogotumatuma na gochachana! Nyanguru Hill eyio. Ng'ai miino ere? : Picture na special correspondent, Gusii.com files.

english: Then people noticed that this was how the Abagusii people were being treated. After thoroughly examining this treatment, the old man refused to accept it.
ekegusii: Nigo sokoro ominto antebia ng'a oyio n' omobayeno oito ntwe Abagusii korwa bokoro. Ase ogotosomia igoro y' omobayeno oyo oito, omogaka sokoro nigo antebia omogano.

english: And the old man realized this time and again, this reporter was persistent. Why does this reporter continue to chase news so that he can fulfill his duties? Quickly quickly, I almost forgot, he reconciled with the person he had previously disagreed with.
ekegusii: Nigo omogaka ateba ng'a abwo kare na kare, omoremi oyomo narengeo. Bono omoremi oyo akamanora gochia kogesa chibando chiaye korwa ase endemero yaye. Keri keri, kare nchera kwagachia, akaumerana n' omobisa oye nchera abwo mbarabare.

english: Oh! This person is troubled by heat and dust!
ekegusii: Obe! Omobisa oyio n' rise n' chinyanduri!

english: So when they reconcile with this reporter to discuss important matters, this person complains about the heat and dust!
ekegusii: Bono ko baumerana n' omoremi oyo gochia korigereria ensemo iga, omobisa oyo akamong'wania ne rise n' chinyanduri!

english: “Aah… what is going on?...”
ekegusii: Aaachie che che...bono ngaki ngokora?.........

english: This reporter refuses to rest, gets excited and jumps around refusing to be calmed down. Because of this, this life seems like it won’t end, he continues chasing after it. Despite all this, those people, the old man who was persistent has been honored with all these years.
ekegusii: Omoremi oyo agaansa gokura, ogochachana na gotumatuma gaansa korurwa. Korwa abwo, omoyo okaamba gokwa nga tagenda mogondo, airane gochia bwoye. Nonya nabo igo, mbarabare abwo, omogaka oyomo narengeo oyatengerete amakore aya onsi.

english: Let us respect this person. Let everyone know their worth.
ekegusii: Tobwatekania omobisa. Aye manya ekerenga kiao.

english: Why did the old man notice this reporter wasn’t living well, so he encouraged him to continue pursuing news so he could fulfill his duties. The old man was very grateful. Why did the old man then realize that the person wanted to show them how they were being mistreated so they could address it?
ekegusii: Bono omogaka oyo agatebia omoremi oyo takwa omoyo, korende agenderere ne esabari yaye y' okogenda mogondo kogesa chibando. Omogaka oyo akamosegeta buya. Bono omogaka sokoro nigo agoteba buna omobisa nigo agotaka gokobogeria korwa ase emeremo yao eri bwanchente gokora.

english: Continue investigating and find out what this person’s value is so that people don’t take advantage of them. Little money is enough to make someone forget everything and abandon their responsibilities, so that they can fulfill their desires.
ekegusii: Korende nebeterereti ng'a goika omanye ekerenga kio omobisa erinde bweatanane korwa ase are. Eng'ana eye nigo egosegeta omonto otware omokia erinde omobisa tanyora ribaga ri' okomokorekania, egere atige emeremo yaye.

english: Indeed, let us remember the Abagusii elders who visited Boreba Mobisa Mbokorura Ocharoke Ko Na Igesa Iganya. Because of the old man and the people, this person will be our topic for this week and thank you for listening.
ekegusii: Eke nakio kiagerete Abagusii abakoro bagateba buna Boreba Mobisa Mbokorura Ocharoke Ko Na Igesa Iganya. Korwa ase omogaka sokoro ominto, oyo noro omobayeno oito for this week and thank you for listening.

english: One who doesn't hurry won't get far." The elders say they can't wait to get old.
ekegusii: Nintagete kogenda bware" Ebimura binde can't wait kogenda iburu.

english: Old age, wisdom comes with gray hair and experience in the Ekegusii language of our ancestors. People often live for many years, up to eighty or ninety years, before they prepare to become old. But nowadays, old age is celebrated during the month of December at the end of the year.
ekegusii: Iburu, maguta motwe no okwaroka na amarieta ye Ekegusii yo ogosara. Abaisia ki baikire emiaka ikomi mbaka ikomi ne ebere nigo bare goisanera kogenda iburu. Mara enyinge, iburu nigo yare gochiegwa ase engaki yo omotienyi bwe Egesunte kende (December) ase kera omwaka.

english: People strive for good health so that it may benefit them. They build houses and acquire possessions and livestock so that their homes are beautiful. A home without wealth is not admirable.
ekegusii: Abaisia nigo bare kwearigania ase omoyega oyo buna ekobwatia. Nigo bare korigia chingoko bagochia konyenya ne ebitugi bio ogouta omorero ekero bare nyomba. Inyora inga morero bwo omware tonya korima.

english: The community gathers to help those who are sick and the youth assist the elderly in preparing for old age. The tradition of honoring the months of old age, those months are when people and relatives visit the aged and share stories.
ekegusii: Omosari nigo arenge koba oyomo ase ekenyoro ekegima na abasae bataranywoma nabwo bare kobira abaisia ekero bare gochia iburu. Obotuko bwo ogokiera rituko rie enyangi ya iburu, aba be enyangi nigo bare korara na abamura barie bachiete iburu banyenya chingoko.

english: Truly speaking, it is the elderly who remember past events and are reminded through songs and dances about the months of old age. The young ones respect traditions and appreciate gifts.
ekegusii: Mambia maaambia, nigo abaisia aba bare koirwa roche gwesibia amache amakendu na korurwa ne chinyanduri ne risa egere beariganie ase enyangi eye. Abasegi nigo bare kobogoria amatimo na kweboyia amayo.

english: Poverty is said to prevent someone from understanding things fully. Sometimes, they are given assistance so that they may recover and become strong. Before something valuable is lost, it is better to prepare to become old and strengthen oneself to gather knowledge so that it remains.
ekegusii: Egetono nigo kiare korosigwa kiamanya koruma buna endo. Aaiga, nigo bare gotebigwa buna endo igo yare kobamera nande yabaroka. Ekero kio ogosarwa gwaikire nigo oyo ore kogenda iburu are gotarera omote gochia magega egere tarora amanyinga buna agoiteka.

english: Work done by women and men is carried out to improve the home. Wealth should be used wisely to ensure that everything is well within the home. If it is not managed properly, it will diminish and disappear quickly.
ekegusii: Korwa aiga amatera yo obware aterwa kwagachia ase omware are koirwa. Omorero nigo ore gosegeswa bwoka amatuko onsi pi omware are nyomba. Ki yare komochani orime, nigo yare koba chimuma naende yare kobetereria okorerane chisokoro.

english: A person should work hard and diligently, always striving to achieve success. Work alone, however, is not enough; one must also have blessings. A person who has blessings receives gifts and remembers the past.
ekegusii: Omware nigo are gosoa saiga na korwa gesieri korende tare koirorera goeta gesieri eke. Korwa bono, nigo are gotumia etirisa. Omware nao agasokeire etirisa ochia gwota ensakia korende kera rituko nigo are kweyaka ribu.

english: A home should be protected against thieves until it becomes established. People often save money. That savings, when used to rebuild the home, ensures that the home is secure and work continues.
ekegusii: Mware tare korora gose gwesibia mache mpaka arwe nyomba. Abare nigo bare kobeka egesena. Abwo nyomba, nigo bare gokora emekubio ene. Engaki eyio ye emekubio ene kiyaerire, nigo yare gokagerwa buna omware obwenire na korwa nyomba.

english: Before starting new work, a person should first assess their resources. They should then begin slowly and carefully. Work done by a person who plans ahead is successful because they know how to manage their time.
ekegusii: Ekero akorwa nyomba, mware tare gweeta gesierie keri asoerete. Nigo are kogenda roche bwesibia na kweboyia buya. Korwa aiga mware tare korara saiga aria ase arenge nyomba. Nigo are korara ase eamate amatuko abere omanya koirana sobo.

english: Preparing for tomorrow requires a person to be diligent and work consistently, always striving to succeed. Work today, therefore, is important.
ekegusii: Goansera aiga omware bono nigo are no obosiborwe bwo ogotumia gesieri kende gionsi gia saiga. Bono gochakera engaki eye, momura bwarogete tare gosoa ase abaibori bare korara. Echio ne chimuma. Inee rero enyangi eye nereo?

english: The heart feels like a person who has been troubled and does not understand how to continue studying the matter of the elders and their customs. Let them cry, the heart remembers the elders and their time. So, people say that the elders have power and can cause harm:
ekegusii: Omongina magokoro baba ominto nigo antebia buna nigo atagete kogenderera gotosomia igoro y' emegiro ende meke aase rituko ria rero. Ase okoinyora, magokoro natotebetie emegiro meke igoro. Ase rero, baba nigo agoteba buna emegiro ende nigo ekobwatia iga:

english: 19. Did he delay coming from Heaven, and when he came down, did he appear like a foolish child? What reason makes him sit quietly and listen to advice: A wise person who understands things well knows how to listen to advice from someone who speaks truthfully and wisely. Why? A wise person needs to learn things. And again, therefore he listens to advice carefully, a leader who knows what is good, knows how to choose good things over bad ones! It is very important.
ekegusii: 19. Nigo gwatindera aaria bw' Ombati, na gotumbaga kwagachia, gwaiika nka bwoo morogoba botuko? Aye rirorio goika oturere mokao korwa etirisa: Omosacha otamereti chinderu nigo agotura mokaye korwa etirisa onye oikire nka bwoye ekero chinyomba chiasiekirwe. Ninki? Ekiagera omosacha nigo agwenerete komera chinderu. Ase eng’encho ende, ere nigo agotura korwa sukunyuma, omokungu omanya koigora, omanya goeta korwa omorangu boronge! Emeremo emekong'u.

english: That is why: Tradition preserves the history of ancestors. And also this: The truth is that some people do not want others to live a righteous life. But what is the problem? They will be ashamed. The problem is a life that is not aligned with the ways of the ancestors, which has been corrupted by modern times. [ righteousness ]. In ancient Kisii, a person truly respected those who were disciplined. Consider how a parent treats a child, teaching them respect. This is the strength of Kisii culture, which has endured through hardship. Picture and Petronillah Ogoti, Gusii.com files.
ekegusii: Abwo nse: Egesanda kebekire erongori y' obori echiete aroro. Naende nse yaye: Ekemunwa keri omogaka sokoro ominto agocha kobekerwa obokima obotongore. Bono egesero ninki? Nabo oraborie. Egesero n’ obokima boria obotang’ani bw’o bori ekero bwagesirwe korwa aase endemero. [ obotongore ]. Aase Ekegusii gia kare, omogaka nyene omochie nere ogatongoire ritangani. Kerabe buna omogaka taaiyo aase omochie oyio, omomura omotangi nere ogatongoire. Gokora magega y' Ekegusii eke nigo yarenge chimuuma. Picture na petronillah Ogoti, Gusii.com files.

english: 21. The problem of old times always remains: Anyone who disrespects the ancestors [ righteousness ], a person who does not value tradition. Similarly, anyone who disrespects parents also does not value tradition. But what is the problem? The problem is a life that is not aligned with the ways of the ancestors, which has been corrupted by modern times [ righteousness ].
ekegusii: 21. Egesero ngekare miinto rero mogoroba: Onye omosubati ore mwaye ogesire obori [ obotongoire], omogaka nere ogotanga koegwa egesero. Korende onye mogaka taaiyo ase enka eyio, omomura omotangi nere okoegwa egesero. Bono egesero ninki? Egesero n’ obokima obotang’ani bw’obori ekero bwagesiru korwa mogondo [ obotongore ].

english: 22. Remember this point: A wise person does not reveal secrets carelessly. Be careful, and let wisdom guide you. Also, a leader should not be careless, lest they regret it. Let everyone carry their own burden, Kisii people know how to bear it.
ekegusii: 22. Koramera tikoiyo: Omosacha otanywometi tanya koramera ebwate. Naramera, ere n' chingaki asaretie. Naboigo, omokungu otasogeti nere naramera tirikobwata. Goika aba bonsi baratwara chinka chiabo, Ekegusii kemanye kobwata.

english: 23. I finish speaking these important words: A person carries a heavy burden when they travel and find themselves in a difficult situation. Let them go slowly. Why? Because it is better to be cautious than reckless.
ekegusii: 23. Nainche nimbwate rikobu rineene: Omonto obwate rikobu rineene tanya kogenda ase ekegege gie chintuga. Agende igo mbobe. Ninki? Nigo chigosira ekero chiabokire.

english: This message brings comfort to the heart. He says that if they accept it, let them remember this thing. Drink these waters, and thank you for listening.
ekegusii: Chitoro chiabwatire magokoro naende. Nigo ateba buna bwatera abwo, goikera chingaki chiinde. Monywe mache maya, and thank you for listening.

english: Don't despise a small beginning lest you stumble on a large rock, a good heart among people is what helps someone so that the traditions of our ancestors don't disappear completely. Yes. Cherish your family, so that it remembers its roots.

english: And people remember good things from their families. It is said that one should be careful, and also respect work, so that visitors don't find fault. It is important to help each other always and share problems, so that they can be solved.
ekegusii: Nigo abairi barenge gotomwa korigia omorabera omuya. Emechi nigo yarenge kounenkigwa, amo n' obotuki bwakorwa, erinde ogweiiti tigocha koba. Nigo omosacha arenge goeta kera aase gose nanyore omokungu ori baranchane, erinde banywomane.

english: This person who helps and shares with others from their family, knows how to cherish their home, understands that cherishing one's children is a good thing for those who haven't matured yet!!
ekegusii: Bono omosacha oyo gaetire na goetanana kera aase komorigia omokungu oyo omuya, omoerio oye, omanya konyora omwanchwa oye korwa ase atakagerete !!

english: 1. A child who cries a lot causes trouble and also causes annoyance. In our Gusii culture, people cry a lot when they are happy and when they cry because of sadness. Anyone who doesn't know how to cry, let them learn how to cry so that when they cry because of sadness, they will be lucky.
ekegusii: 1. Tori korora risase ase rikorwa na ase rikogenda. Aye nigo ogocha gotaboboka onyore inga bwairire. Ekero ore Gusii, nabo okorora buna omogaso ogoansa mambia naende buna risase rikorimera morogoba. Onye kore ase chinse chinde, goika oakane chibesa otarigwe impaka ase atambe erinde ororore buna risase rikorimera, onye kore ne bahati.

english: Anyone who is a true Gusii person, cries a lot when they are sad.
ekegusii: Onye tori nka Gusii, tori korora buna risase rikorimera

english: 2. Rats don't have respect. This world is full of people who cause trouble.
ekegusii: 2. Mache tari gwansa. Ekio nakio egento egetangani okorora.

english: 3. Old men don't have respect. Sometimes old men say things that hurt others, and it is considered bad manners. Let old men speak only good things and avoid saying hurtful words.
ekegusii: 3. Mabere tari gwansa. Nobeka amabere angana inaki ase echae, aye ne chinsa ogosaria. Egento amabere ye chinse chinde are, nigo abekire ebinto bigokobotia.

english: 4. A foolish person boasts and says, “Today is my day.” In our tradition as Gusii people, boasting is discouraged and said like, “I have finished working at Manoti… Manoti is very far away…”.
ekegusii: 4. Onde bwensi mokoumerana nigo agokoboria inga, "Aye seino ingai" Korende ekero ore nka seino Gusii, nigo okoborigwa inga, "Aye tori mochokoro o Manoti......Manoti nomosani one.....

english: 5. A lazy person does not succeed. Our ancestors said that laziness leads to poverty, and one should work hard to earn sugar. Don't be idle. Lazy people always complain about their lives like a boat without an oarsman…don’t bother the oarsman…
ekegusii: 5. Nyoko koro tari gokobisera kende. Ekero okogenda gokwania nyokokoro, nigo agoikoinekera naende okobisera ebisukari. Onde takobikuna. Nyokorome nigo agokonyenyera engoko oteba inga ekebwato eke neki omoigwa....onde tasumbua omoigwa...

english: 6. Birds chirp while pecking at grains in the field. These are small birds. It is appropriate to listen to them and watch them.
ekegusii: 6. Nyoni tichiri kogoterera rimaambia echuni. Nyoni tichiyo. Nigo obwenerete gweterera aye bweka.

english: 7. People boast as if they own everything. They speak carelessly. In Gusii culture, people brag about owning large farms…they boast about being wealthy and having many wives…what is the benefit of bragging?
ekegusii: 7. Nigo okona korenda inga ne chinsa irenga chire. Aye negetongu giensa. Ekero ore Gusii okona goaka oboche aaria etuka maate..... gose okona gosiswa etuki na abasani bao... ningo ore na acha n' chinsa?

english: 8. A good custom is a good thing, and a bad custom is a bad thing. A bad custom and a good custom of the Gusii people can ruin someone. Be careful when dealing with people who behave strangely.
ekegusii: 8. Omogaso ekero ochire, oyio no omogaso. Obokendu ekero bwachire, obwo no obokendu. Obokendu na omogaso o Gusii tona goita onde. Ekero ore ase chinse chinde naende batebe inga ense neche ekende, wewe chunga sana.

english: 9. Greetings. Small birds. Old men who cry. This is a curse. Salt, soda, sugar, cooking fat, millet, sorghum…all those things are not free. Learn from wise people who understand life and appreciate valuable things.
ekegusii: 9. Chinsaga. Tichiyo. Amabere amaroranu. Echio ne chindoto. Rinagu, risosa, ebisukari, erongori yobori, egesare, rikuneni.. ebio bionsi tibiyo. Goika origi obongaini bonde konyora ebinto ebio.

english: 10. Christmas has come with its joy (remember what was said in point 7 above). In our Gusii culture, Christmas is a time for eating meat and drinking beer.
ekegusii: 10. Ekerisimasi nerituko erimo rioka (inyora buna aye negetongu giensa - namba 7 igoro). Ekero ore nka Gusii, ekerisimasi nomotienyi omogima na gochi igoro.

english: 11. I remember this Gusii land. Again and again, people boast as if they are Gusii people, associating themselves with the elders.
ekegusii: 11. Narotire kinde Gusii. Nankio nankio, nigo okona korota buna nao ore nka Gusii, kore amo na abasani bao.

english: Gusii is a land of abundance.
ekegusii: Gusii n' erwenyi y' omwando.

ekegusii: Amaoga a Thanksgiving korwa ase Aida Morgan

english: They wrote about it on November 6th, the pilgrims of England (United Kingdom), in the year 1620. They traveled from another country to a new land. They arrived in Massachusetts, a beautiful place of arrival and rest (America). After a few days, they built houses and prepared to plant. On November 11th, they landed on a rock (American shore), and they remembered their journey to this area called Plymouth Rock. After writing and building boats, the group of 102 passengers thanked God greatly. It was difficult. Sickness and Indians. Hunger. They came to America seeking freedom. In 1607, the colony of Jamestown (Virginia) almost failed, and only half of the 102 passengers survived. But God helped them, and they established a strong colony in Virginia. The colony thrived. And because of God's grace, those people and the Indians became friends and lived together peacefully, thanking God for his help. That tradition of giving thanks continued. In 1789, President George Washington declared that day as a national day of thanksgiving. Later, in 1941, Congress officially designated the fourth Thursday of November as a major American holiday.
ekegusii: Nigo barwete Bongeresa chitariki 6, omotienyi o Kianda (Tureti ya Kebaki), omwaka 1620. Bagatara ase enyancha ase emetienyi ebere. Bagaika Massachusetts omoerio bwo omotienyi o ikomi na rimo (Egesunte). Nonya nabo igo, ase tarenge aroro agiya ase obwato bwarenge kobekwa. Rakini ase chitariki 11 chio omotienyi o ikomi na kabere (Egesunte Kende), bakanyora ase agiya aaria Plymouth Rock. Nonya banyorete ase bakobeka obwato, emechando ya abanganyi aba 102 korwa Bongeresa konyora teraera. Amarwaire. Chisegi na Abaindi. Enchara. Nigo baigete Amerika engaki yo obokendu. Ekero omotienyi o Kane (Rigwata) omwaka 1607 ochiete goika, konyora enusu ya abanganyi aba 102 bakure. Buna Nyasae abangete, bagasimeka endagera engaki eyio ye Rigwata. Endagera ekama buya. Ase ogoakera Nyase inga imbuya mono, abanganyi aba amo na Abaindi bari barenge abasani bagateba inga tiga omoyega obe aroro bwo ogoakera Nyasae asante. Rituko rio ogoaka inga imbuya mono rikaiborwa. Omwaka o 1789, Omogambi George Washington agateba inga tiga rituko rio ogoaka imbuya mono ribekwe. Rakini nigo yairete impaka omwaka o 1941 ekero Bunge yaetetie inga kera Tichi Kane yo omoerio bwe Egesunte obe eholidei enene Amerika.

english: Today we celebrate that day of thanksgiving and remember God. We celebrate that day remembering the events of that year. Recently, Barack Obama, son of Nyaberi Orongo Manyange, was inaugurated president that year (America). The leaders of the church and the pastor Nyaberi were present. This event was widely publicized and celebrated as a blessing from God in 2009. Greetings, thanksgiving to the readers of Gusii.com. Anyone who has information should visit the website. Share this story with others. Let us thank God for the gift of speaking Ekegusii.
ekegusii: Inche nigo ingoaka inga imbuya mono ase obomoyo korwa ase Nyasae. Nigo ingoaka inga imbuya mono ase ebisio nanyorire ase omwaka oyo. Akamoisia gaito, Barack Obama Ochwoga Nyaberi Orongo Manyange nigo kaiborwa omotienyi omotangani (Engatiato) omwaka oyo. Abachokoro bo omongina Kerubo no omogaka Nyaberi inkona komentekana bare. Ekio nakio ekeegwa ekenene sana ase inche korwa ase Nyasae ase omwaka o 2009. Eria Kabere, imbuya mono ase abasomi ba Gusii.com. Onye tari inwe nanga ewebusaiti eye teiyo. Ninwe mogotoa omokia kera rituko. Nigo ingoakera Nyasae inga imbuya mono ase okobaa ribaga rio ogosoma Ekegusii.

english: What now? Are you there? Can you hear me clearly? What about resting? Is everything alright? What about building a boat? What about peace and prosperity? How is life going? Come back soon. Praise Jesus for his blessings. The preacher speaks. Let us pray diligently to God. Happy Thanksgiving Day. America celebrates. Kenya celebrates.
ekegusii: Inee? Aye rende? Inkwaboka bono mambia? Nobwate ase okorara? Kwarire kende rero? Nobwate agachanchabe okona kobeka? Nobwate mosani onde? Moiri onde rende? Buya sana. Tebia Yeso inga imbuya mono. Omonguru bweka. Intobwati kende otatiga korwa ase Nyasae. Rituko rigiya ria Thanksgiving. Amerika Egenderere. Kenya Egenderere.
