english: The black mulberry tree is a fruit tree belonging to the fig family (Moraceae). It originates from Asia and the islands of the Pacific Ocean. The black mulberry tree grows well in warm climates. The breadfruit tree is closely related to Artocarpus altilis. Artocarpus integer (Cempedak), Artocarpus heterophyllus (Jackfruit, Nangka) and also Artocarpus odoratissimus (Marang) are all members of the breadfruit family.
ekegusii: Egesaku Omogati bw’amatunda ebwate ang’e chimbego 60 chi’emete machani ye chitropiki korwa ase omochia o Moraceae (omochie o mulberry gose chifigi). Nigo chigotoka ase Asia n’ebisinga bi’enyancha ya pacific. Omogati bw’amatunda nigo ore ang’e kobwakana chifigi. Omogati bwe ritunda osimekire mono nigo ore Artocarpus altilis. Artocarpus integer (Cempedak), Artocarpus heterophyllus (Jackfruit, Nangka) amo amo na Artocarpus odoratissimus (Marang) chionsi echire ase omochie bw’omogati bwa amatunda.

english: Parajubaea torallyi is a palm tree native to South America. Currently, it is mainly cultivated as an ornamental plant by collectors, Bolivia, where it has a significant economic importance due to its large seeds, which are used for oil extraction on the coast.
ekegusii: Parajubaea torallyi n’omote omuya korwa Amerika ya maate. Korende, tori gosimekwa mono isiko y’ase yachakerete na abaremi, Bolivia, esengencho y’echintetere chiaye chinene, eyio emoneti rigori rinene ase ogoetigwa enyancha.

english: Native to Bolivia, it grows in humid forests and montane forests of the Inter-Andean region at altitudes between 2700–3400 meters above sea level; however, it can also grow at lower altitudes in drier areas. It requires approximately 20 years to reach maturity and a trunk diameter of up to one meter. A mature tree can produce around 7 kilograms of seeds annually (approximately 500 seeds per kilogram) and requires about 550 millimeters of rainfall per year.
ekegusii: Oiboreire Bolivia, igo okwama ase aome naende are n’ebuse , emetaroekorakwa Inter-Andean chire n’oboigoro bwe chimita 2700–3400 igoro ya nyancha; aseigo, epamu eye nero eimogete igoro ase chikabira chionsi ense engima. Iberera ndiri goetania chidigiri 20 n’obokendu bwa botuko mbioyo. Reberera ngogenda rire inse gioka chidigiri 7 are emetienyi y’obokendu (omotienyi ogatano na kabere na omotienyi o gatano na gatato) n’embura egotwa omwaka omogima nigo ere chi mirimita 550 chioka.

english: Welwitschia (Welwitscha mirabilis) is a unique desert plant endemic to the Namib and Angolan deserts in southwestern Africa. Welwitschia plants are dioecious, meaning they have separate male and female individuals. The adult plant consists of a short stem with two continuously growing leaves that become twisted and shredded over time, forming a massive, tangled mass. Welwitschia reproduces sexually through cones.
ekegusii: Welwitscha (Welwitscha mirabilis) nigo kere ekemeri kiamete amatuko amatang’ani amwanyabanto, egekwama ase asinine ase ekengeka ki’enyancha ime ya Namibia na Angola ya maate. Welwitschia maene nigo ore omote korende tori kororekana boigo ekero okororekana ritang’ani. Ekemeri ekegima nigo kebwate ritina erimo rinene ribwate amato abere amanene akwama-aya akororekana buna ebisicha ebinene bieringete bikaba ebigare. Welwitschia ndire ekororekana buna egetunwa ki’eubi.

english: Khasi pine (Pinus kesiya) originates from Asia and grows well in mountainous regions, but it is also found in plantations. It reaches heights of 30–35 meters with a trunk diameter of up to one meter. It has small, needle-like leaves arranged in bundles of two, and its bark is reddish-brown. The cones of this pine tree are 5 to 9 centimeters long and 1.5 to 2.5 centimeters wide.
ekegusii: Ekemeri giepaini ya Khasi (Pinus kesiya) korwa Asia nigo gekwama bwago mono, naende nkeri gotoka raisi isiko ya sobo. Emete nigo egoika chimita 30–35 ase obotambe n’amatina agoika emita eyemo ase obonetu. Kera egesabo ekebwate amagwa amato akobeta atato, kera erimo rire chisentimita 15 goika 20 ase abotambe. Amatunda korwa aekemeri eke nigo are chisentimita 5 goika 9 ne chintetereechire chisentimita 1,5 goika 2,5 ase abotambe.

english: Kalimantan mango (Mangifera casturi) is commonly known as Kasturi mango, a tropical fruit tree reaching heights of 10–30 meters, originating from lowland forests and cultivated near Banjarmasin in Borneo (Indonesia). This type of mango is known for its fragrant aroma. Currently, it is also being grown commercially for its delicious fruits.
ekegusii: Riembe ria Kalimantan (Mangifera casturi) rimanyire buna Kasturi srire rotunda rie chitripiki ang’e chimita 10–30 ase obotambe erigotoka ase asinine ase akorokwa Banjarmasin ase Borneo ya maate (Indonesia). Amatuko aya riasire gosira ekiagera rikonachwa mono. Korende, nabo rikonya gosimekwa aiga asengencho y’amatunda aye agwansa.

english: It is said this day, the government is good, seeking help from people so that the Gusii nation may be remembered by the Government. We request that the government remember the Gusii nation who have helped the Kisii people.
ekegusii: Ase omokubio oyo oera, omogaka sokoro ominto natosemia igoro y' Omogusii oria orenge korokwa Omorominta. Ntwarora buna omorominta nigo are Omogusii oria oitete Omosigisi.

english: It is also said, we request that you bring gifts like the Gusii and their clans so that they can remember those clans which were forgotten, they will not fail to assist. Therefore, a person with a good heart should not fail to help them because they have assisted.
ekegusii: Ase boigo, tokarora buna ogoitana gwaito ntwe Abagusii n' ebisaku binde nigo kwarengeo ase engencho ebisaku ebi binde biatoetanaine, biatagete gotoita. Ase rero, omongina magokoro ominto nigo atagete kobwatera abwo korwa ase sokoro atigerete.

english: Are we understanding correctly? The matter does not exceed showing respect and honoring the differences among the communities and their cultures. Those who understand well are found in Keumbu. Picture with Petronillah Ogoti. Gusii.com files.
ekegusii: Tigwachiete nyangi? Rirorio tiyarenge konyarekana ogende ase ekeigoroigoro gi' okoremera ebiranya ase engaki eyio. Abangina nkoiririata bare aaria Keumbu. Picture na Petronillah Ogoti. Gusii.com files.

english: A person who loves people understands that there is a meeting with the Kisii people, differences are being honored greatly. Why honor the differences now? They are asking about it. Differences are greatly honored especially the Kisii people who show kindness to others and their generosity. Also concerning this, we request that you remember the culture of our ancestors during March of this year, so that differences are honored until the Kisii elders are called upon from Esegi Y' Osaosao and Kabianga.
ekegusii: Omongina baba ominto nigo agoteba buna ase chisegi chiato amo n' Abasigisi, ebiranya nkoremerwa biare. Bono okoremera ebiranya ninki? Nabo oraborie. Ebiranya nigo biare koremerwa erinde Abasigisi aba ababisa baitwe ase obonge. Ase okoinyora, ntwaroche ase eganki y' omotienyi bw' Egetamo (March) omwaka oyo, buna ebiranya biaremeretwe mbaka Abasigisi abange bagaitwa ase Esegi Y' Osaosao amo na Kabianga.

english: Differences are greatly honored indeed. They know how to cooperate with the leaders.
ekegusii: Ebiranya nigo biare koremerwa nse. Biamanya koragererigwa n' abagaka abanene

english: Therefore, people understand that you should go and see the problems facing the people so that you can help them overcome those challenges. What about these differences? It is about uniting with the people, and they are happy when they are helped. Let it not be forgotten, the leaders should remind the Kisii people.
ekegusii: Bono baba nigo agoteba buna oyore gosicha ebiigoro igoro nere ore kogenda oremera ebiranya egere bing'use abasigisi. Bono ebiranya ninki? Kobwatekana n' baba ominto, eye n'emete yare gosunyuntwa baremera inse. Ko biaremeirwe nse, abagaka abakoro nigo bare koragereria Abasigisi.

english: Therefore, the Kisii people should rejoice and celebrate, they should sing songs of praise! These problems and the Gusii people who are suffering, it is said that they will be resolved quickly so that they don’t take too long. Comment on this, if they continue they will find solutions!
ekegusii: Bono Abasigisi bakonyagoka baete rioka, nigo biare kobasiekera, baitwa baera pi! Ebiigoro igoro n'omong'ina Omogusii ogasichire oba buna egosori yare gokorwa botuko korende torenge borogi. Komenta nayio, bari bare koyokora nigo bare koba getirianda!

english: The youth should not be left behind! These problems will be solved by the leaders.
ekegusii: Mosacha tatakeire igaa! Ebiigoro igoro nigo biare gokorwa n' abakungu boka.

english: People say that those with the leaders should continue. This one you did not understand, go and learn. It is not a small matter, you will understand later and be rewarded accordingly. Gossip is spreading, and all the bad news has been heard that the community’s traditions, customs and values of the Gusii people have been preserved and shown to everyone and their collaborators. They also pray for assistance in resolving the differences and ensuring it doesn’t happen again. Until next time, people love and thank you for listening.
ekegusii: Abaminto inyora buna aba n' abakungu boka bare koyokora. Oyo otamanyete, tare kogenda. Tari igo rioka, oyotachieti nyangi, taregochi aroro na torekoirwa nka. Chinyabubu nigo chiare gosicha, na aiga obosemi obonge nigo bware koregwa buna enyangi ye ebitinge, kera ekemo kie ebimira bio Omogusii na nigo yaregosicherwa orosana ime na abakorerani ao ao. Nabo omoyega bw' okoremera ebiranya orenge gokorwa igo. Until next time, omongina baba nigo ateba buna bwatera abwo and thank you for listening.

english: Long ago there was a child named Matieko, who greatly loved his mother and father. This child often went to the river to play, sometimes falling and getting hurt. But this child could also go to the river alone, avoiding dangers and carefully watching over himself. Because of this, this child and his parents were happy with that river.
ekegusii: Abwo ase rinani ria Matieko, ogasusu narenge aroro amo n' ebimanu biaye. Bono Ogasusu gakonya gotara rinani eri ime, akaigwa enchara na gochaka korigia endagera. Buna Ogasusu akonya goeta ase rinani eri iime, akaumera omong'anyi okororekana omotambe gochia ime. Korwa abwo, Ogasusu amo n' ebimanu biaye bigasoa omong'anyi oyo ime.

english: When this child grew up, this child said, “Children who are too young should not be sent.” The first child was small, and the other children followed him closely, and this child watched over himself near the river of Matieko.
ekegusii: Omwango ase ogoaka esabu, Ogasusu nigo atebete buna "Ebimwana ebi rero goika toigote" Omwana oyomo ore kwaa, n' ebimwana biinde biikomotunyana koru magega, Ogasusu okare korigia endagera aaria ase orosana rwa Matieko.

english: That river was also known as Omansamu. This famous Omansamu always had a way of helping people. When this child reached the river, this child quickly jumped across the water and then climbed a tall tree, and Omansamu was very surprised. He did not expect this child to cross the river like that, so this child made Omansamu laugh.
ekegusii: Omong'anyi oyo kumbe n' obwe Omansamu. Bono konyora Omansamu osokire isiko gochia koratara. Aaiga ase omong'anyi ime, Ogasusu tanyorete kende giokori korende nyuma ye chintunde chiinke igo, Omansamu akaba oiranire. Konyora atarasoa omong'anyi oye ime, konye Ogasusu okare korora Omansamu gakoirana.

english: This child then went to grow up.
ekegusii: Ogasusu okare goaka esabu ase obwango

english: This child became very scared, and he went to grow up with fear and thought about what he had done to make Omansamu happy with that river, and he wanted to help this child and his parents.
ekegusii: Ogasusu akaba n' obwoba obonene, korende agaaka esabu ya bwango na korengereria eki arakore ekiagera Omansamu arenge gosoa omong'anyi oyo ime, nigo arenge gocha koria Ogasusu oyo amo n' ebimanu biaye bionsi pi.

english: This fear caused this child to repeatedly say, “Four children have come and they will drown. That is why I will take this Omansamu and protect him from danger” Omansamu heard these words, and he ran away quickly and began to think about what happened with that river!!
ekegusii: Obwango obwo obwo, Ogasusu okare goteba goteba buna "Abana bane tiga takwoboa. Bono nigo nkobaitera Omansamu oyo erinde monyare komoria" Omansamu koigwa aya, akaondoka kerage na gochaka gotama korwa ase omong'anyi oyo !!

english: Finally, Omansamu met Okabwe and told him that the river had been causing problems for that river and that he needed to find a way to protect those children from harm. Because of this, Okabwe promised Omansamu to help him, and he vowed to use his power to prevent such things from happening again.
ekegusii: Keri keri, nario Omansamu aumerete Okabwe na komotebia buna omonto nare osoire omong'anyi oye ime na nigo atagete komoita erinde oyo n' abana baye banyore endagera bakoria. Obwango obwo, Okabwe agatebia Omansamu taoboa nonya, na komotebia amokobe gochia ase omong'anyi oye erinde arore oyo okomoseria korwa bwoye.

english: “Four children, they should not be sent.”
ekegusii: Abana bane, rero goika toigote

english: Okabwe remembered his kindness towards Omansamu. So when they came to the river, they fell down and started saying, “Four children, we have brought Omansamu and his family to Okabwe. They should not be sent.”
ekegusii: Okabwe agasibera ekemincha kiaye gochia ase Omansamu. Bono buna bare aang'e n' omong'anyi, bakaigwa eriogi rigosoka korwa ime rigoteba ibuna "Abana bane bono nari twareteirwe Omansamu n' omosani oye Okabwe. Rero goika toigote

english: But when Omansamu heard this, he ran away alone and realized that Okabwe was deceiving him. However, Omansamu didn't understand. When he looked around, he saw a shadow that had been cast upon him, which made Okabwe's tree shake violently!!
ekegusii: Omansamu buna aigwete aya akaondoka mono na komanya buna Okabwe nigo among'ainete. Aaiga nario Omansamu atagete atame. Buna agasaine gotama, akanyora engori eye asiberetwe nigo yare komong'usa bobe, ekairera ekemincha gi' Okabwe kobutuka amo n' engori !!

english: Omansamu was frightened and ran back to Ogasusu and his children, and they all fled quickly from that river.
ekegusii: Omansamu akaminchori agatama kwagachia n' Ogasusu amo n' abana baye bakanyora ribaga bagatama korwa omong'anyi oyo.

english: Goodbye my friends. I am going goodbye my messengers who are gathering the Abananchi people this year and next year including the fruits of bananas which are very sweet to the Gusii people. All the messengers of Gusii. Very quickly. Let us carry our baskets together including the fruits of bananas from Gusii. Go and clear the area. The elders of Gusii refused because they did not want to share the profits of farming. Nyambega Gisesa said that the elders of Nyangorora Banana Youth Group agreed to contribute a small amount each towards the bananas and clearing the land. They contributed Ksh. 300. They realized the little contribution they had collected was equivalent to Ksh.1,680. There were also some chips that they contributed. For the bananas, they contributed willingly, eagerly, generously, happily, respectfully, honestly and with cooperation. Is the total value of the fruits and the contributions more than Ksh.6 million?
ekegusii: Kwaheri ase obotaka.Naende kwaheri ase abajumbe bari bakongaina Abananchi omwaka ase kera omwaka inga emasini ya amatoke neche erosigwe Gusii. Abajumbe bonsi ba Gusii. Obosoku sana. Twatwarire chimbuche toganyete emasini ya amatoke Gusii. Genda gochia aaria. Abasae ba Gusii bakanire inga tibari koganya amangana yo oborimo. Nyambega Gisesa nigo agoteba inga abasae ba Nyangorora Banana Youth Group baansire korosia chindagera ao ao korwa ase amatoke na gochionia ase efaida. ase omobwekano, nigo bakogora ritoke ase Ksh. 300. Bamanya koroisia chichip echio bakoonia ase rigori ria Ksh.1,680. Tari chips chioka bakoroisia. Korwa ase amatoke, nigo bakoroisia obosie,chikeki,ejamu,echuisi,amarwa,chingori,amajambe amo ne chogopia. Emasini eye ne chibesa irenga yaira? Ksh.chimillioni 6.

english: For many years, the farmers of Gusii have been exploited by banana traders who sell them at high prices in major cities of Kenya and make huge profits. Bananas are transported to areas like Kisumu, Kitale, Mombasa, Nairobi, Nakuru and others. The members of Nyangorora Banana Youth Group work hard in their farm near Miriri. Mr. James Omiso and his assistant went to inspect the farm. Near Miriri is about 23 kilometers from Bosongo. Does the road reach Miriri easily? Yes. Are there fences? No. Is there water? There is none. Many birds disturb the farmers. The inspection team visited approximately 44 farmers. Most of them filled out the forms properly. They were grateful for the support from Farm Africa, Kenya Industrial Research Development Institute (Kirdi), International Service for Acquisition of Agri-biotechnology Application (Isaaa) and Kenya Gatsby Trust. The Kirdi office provided seeds. Kitutu Masaba CDF is also working to help improve the storage facilities for bananas. Very good.
ekegusii: Ase emiaka emenge sana, abaremi ba Gusii nigo bakoriegwa chibesa na abagori ba amatoke abwo bakoyaira ase emechie emenene ya Kenya na koyaonia ase efaida enene sana. Amatoke nigo akoonigwa aaria Kisumu, Kitale, Mombasa, Nairobi, Nakuru na kera ase. Abasae aba ba Nyangorora Banana Youth Goup nigo bagokorera egasi yabo aaria ase omochie o Miriri. Omosike James Omiso nere omonyakerogo bwe ekeombe eke. Omochie o Miriri nigo ore chikilomita 23 korwa Bosongo. Ebara ye ramu nechiete impaka Miriri? Yaya. Amache nangusire? Nonya. Omorero rende? Hakuna. Ayio onsi taratanga abasae aba baito. Ekeombe eke nigo kebwate abasae ange 44. Bonsi nigo baigete fomu fo yoka. Banyorire ogokonywa korwa ase Farm Africa, Kenya Industrial Research Development Institute (Kirdi), International Service for Acquisition of Agri-biotechnology Application (Isaaa) na Kenya Gatsby Trust. Ekeombe kia Kirdi nakio kiabaete emasini. Kitutu Masaba CDF nero iyakora buya ase okobakomboera enyomba ase bakogacha amatoke. Buya sana.

english: In addition, the farmers have formed groups to address the challenges facing banana farming. It's not easy, I am going to try and ensure that the small contribution helps to cover the costs of transporting the bananas. In terms of banana production, we need to invest heavily and rent large farms. We need to encourage innovation. The efforts of the Nyangorora Banana Youth Group are commendable.
ekegusii: Ase bono iga, abasae abaiga imbaganetie ebara engiya ase chigari chigoetera na amatoke. Tari igo rioka, naende okogania ingotakeire kwa amasakara ya okobeka chindagera echi ekero chiarosigwe korwa ase amatoke. Ase amatuko a motwe, neganeiri gotwara enyomba enene na korenta emasini enene. Intwe nigo togosaba amaya. Egasi engiya abasae ba Nyangorora Banana Youth Group.

english: Rhapidophyllum hystrix is a plant from the large palm family of the palm tree. The leaf is a typical leaf of the genus Rhapidophyllum. It originates from the forests of the southeastern United States. The seed is collected and planted so that about 20 seeds can be transported to Europe each year.
ekegusii: Rhapidophyllum hystrix n’eyemo ye Chipamu chikoremerereia obokendu obonene ase chimbego chie chipamu. Embego n’eyemo yoka ere ase egesaku kia Rhapidophyllum. Igoogosimekwa ase akendu ase chinsemo chia USA ya maate- moino. Korene n’gesio ase okoremeriria kwaye kw’obokendu bore inse buna chidigiri 20 igo yaanchire monoe getich mono imeya Yuropu.

english: It is also a fan palm, reaching a height of 1–3 meters with a trunk diameter of up to 17.8 cm. Rhapidophyllum Hystrix is a relatively easy-to-grow plant, its roots grow well in shady areas. On fertile soil, the roots become very large. The fan palm does not have climbing roots, but rather roots that reach a length of 1.2 m and a depth of 17.8 cm. The roots are brown, fibrous, and branched. They spread widely, forming a dense network. Once established, they can tolerate drought conditions. The leaves are arranged in a fan shape and are deeply divided. They are green in color and take about 3 years to mature. They are resistant to pests. The fan palm grows well in shade and can withstand cold temperatures. It reproduces through suckers. The fan palm usually grows in moist soils and can also grow in slightly acidic soils. It adapts well to different environments. Its growth rate depends on soil quality, moisture, and temperature. It takes about 3 years for the seedlings to develop a strong root system. However, the palm requires fertile soil to grow quickly and thrive. A healthy palm that is not stressed will produce more shoots. Cold tolerance varies depending on the variety, but most varieties can tolerate temperatures down to -15 to -20 degrees Celsius. Extremely low temperatures below -28 degrees Celsius can cause damage.
ekegusii: Nigo ere embego y’epamu enkong’u, naende ekwama chimita 1–3 chioka ase obotambe n’amagwa amaya ase ritina. Rhapidophyllum Hystrix igo ere enke ekorusia chimbande raisi, amatina amange akorosia ekemeri ekegare mono. Ase engaki entambe, amatina ayio narosi orosana oronene. Epamu y’esindani teri korosi matina korende ekobi erakine goika chimita 1,2 ase obotambe goika 17,8 ase obogare. Amatina nigo abwate amato amakoro, amatwaro, n’amagwa amatanyerere amatambe. Nigo atirete buya , gose aarare inse ekiagere chikorwanerera oborabu gose ekiriri. Chintetere nigo chigosimekwa ase abwate amache. Ase amiaka 3 ametang’ani. Nigo etakeire chibe are n’obokendu. Epamu y’esindani igo egotaka ase are n’omoika bwa amache naende ebekwe ase omogaso gose ekiriri ementwe omogaso buna egokina. Eekororekana buya ekero chibekire ase ekiriri akeigo. Ekero chiamete ase omogaso omogima, ekobi ekobwatana n’amato asitia ekara machani. Ebimeri bietaneti emiaka 3 nabo bikogachwa isiko y’egeticha ase omwaka omogima onye komenyete ase riberera ritari goetania chidigiri 10. Buna enkendu, epamu ekoremereria obokendu nigo etakeire gosimekwa ase riroba rieteti amache buya naende ebekwemaate. Omobisa omonene bw’epamu eye tari bokendu korende riroba ribwate amache amange. Ribererea riainse mono amo n’eriroba ribwate amache amange nigo agosaria emerio. Epamu eye nabo ekonyara komenyera obokendu chidigiri –15 goika –20. Riberera ria inse mono rimanyire yamenyerete riarenge chidigiri –28.

english: The Clans of the Gusii People, the Council of Elders, they speak like the Gusii.
ekegusii: Abagambi Ba Abagusii Ekero Omosongo Aigete Nka Gusii

english: They travel far and gather little things, the Gusii people don't understand how to save small amounts of money at all. They are wasteful, but traditions remain strong so they can save something. What is this? My mother tells us about the tradition of saving small amounts of money from time immemorial? But it is said, the Gusii people have forgotten those old ways of saving:
ekegusii: Ase orogendo amo n' okong'anya gwaito, Abagusii ntwaigete ase tokwebaka amarieta y' ching'iti ao ao. Ase okoboria, ntoratebigwa buna ninki kiagerete tokeebaka iga. Ninki gose? Mbuya ki twaroche ase chingiti echi ekagera tokeebaka amarieta abo? Buna togotebigwa, Abagusii mbebagete amarieta ayio akobwatia:

english: (I). The Herdsmen, they save, Zebras and Wild Animals. Comment on this, it is said that the Herdsmen and the Farmers! The Herdsman who herds cattle is like a Gusii man whose cow has calves! The Gusii people today no longer bother to milk cows until their udders are full! Despite this, they say that the Herdsmen saved enough wealth to buy things:
ekegusii: (I). Ababasi nigo bebagete, Enchage (Zebra ase Ekenyamorero). Komenta nayio, nigo togotebigwa buna Omobasi n' omongaini! Omobasi nere oorogeti Omogusii buna eng'ombe ekobaswa korwa ebigoti! Abagusii bande nigo barenge konyenya eng'ombe korwa omogongo! Nonya nabo igo, abande nigo bagoteba buna Ababasi nigo babasete eng'era korua omogong'o rika rie ritana, erio bakarokwa Ababasi!

english: (II). The Hunters. Leopards and Wild Animals. The Hunter hunts for leopards. This one also goes to the forest to become a Gusii, and is feared by the Leopard Clan!
ekegusii: (II). Abagirango. Engo (leopard ase Ekenyamorero). Omogirango nigo agirete koria engo. Oyo nere naende omomura okabere ase Omogusii, naende okorokwa Omogirango Omosweta!

english: (III). The Gatherers. These ones also know that the Baboons and Wild Animals. Comment on this, they also know that the Gatherers are skilled! These ones collect firewood to cook food for the elders, but it is said. It is not always easy. The Gatherer is respected, what does it mean to be a Gusii person among those who are knowledgeable? The clans were respected by the Gusii people and they fought against the Gatherers.
ekegusii: (III). Abanyaribari. Aba nabwo naende bamanyire buna Abasweta ((Baboon ase Ekenyamorero). Komenta nayio, naende bamanyire buna Abanyaribari Amang'eng'a! Aba nabwo bagatangire esegi ko yatindiire korwa Bomanyi, buna togotebigwa. Tari igo rioka. Omonyaribari nere obarete, gose kobaga Omogusii bwensi ase abeta ritangani. Abagambi bari babarete Abagusii ritangani nao barwete Nyaribari.

english: (IV). The Machoge Clan. It is not the Gatherers who bother to fear the Baboons. The Machoge clan also respect the Baboons and Wild Animals.
ekegusii: (IV). Abamachoge. Tari Abanyaribari boka barenge kweroka Abasweta. Abamachoge nabarabwo nigo bebagete Abasweta (Baboon ase Ekenyamorero).

english: (V). The Chari Clan. The Shield. The Chari person is the Shield of the Bokendu family! The shield protects the entire Bokendu homestead. I don't know what makes them think that the Chari people will abandon their inheritance.
ekegusii: (V). Abanchari. Engubo. Omonchari nere Engubo Y' Ndiba chia Bokendu! Engubo nigo yanchete komenya aase amache amakendu ime. Ntwe ntomanyeti gose eke nakio kiagerete Abanchari bakeeroka erieta eri.

english: (VI). The Getutu Clan. These ones are the Baboons who fight (Wild Animals). The Getutu person is a very large man. This one also fears the Land of the Enchogu people, his relatives!
ekegusii: (VI). Abagetutu. Aba nabwo Abasweta abatang'ani (Baboon ase Ekenyamorero). Omogetutu nere omomura omonene. Oyo nere naende okorokwa Enda Y' Enchogu nyabana bange!

english: From the hearts of our ancestors Kwamboka Mireri and the elder Samuel Omare Nyambisa and Kenyanya Marube, my mother says and thank you for listening.
ekegusii: Korwa ase omongina magokoro Kwamboka Mireri amo na abagaka chisokoro Samuel Omare Nyambisa amo n' Kenyanya Marube, mbuya mono and thank you for listening.

english: Many good things have been said, people say that when someone has many children they feel happy because those children bring honor to their home. She also says that a person should raise a child and teach their siblings so that they grow up well. Many mothers today no longer want to listen to advice, a child nowadays does not respect elders anymore.

Bono onye moamate onde narengeo otarenge gocha goikerana, omwana naende nigo arenge koegwa egetari, omoirera.

english: Behold, I declare unto you, concerning all things, both spiritual and temporal: Hearken, ye heavens, and give ear to the words of my servant, Jesus Christ, we bear record of this church which is built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, yea, and also of the people of Nephi and their brethren, and also of the people of Jared, who were spared because of their faithfulness. And we know that they were preserved by the power of God, which was manifested in them through the workings of miracles; and also we know that they were led by him through the wilderness, and he provided for them in all their needs. And it came to pass that we bear witness of the truth of these things which are written; and also that they were delivered by the hand of God, and also by his power, and also by his grace. And we testify that we have seen with our eyes and heard with our ears, and we have felt the power of God working within us to bring about these wondrous events, and to strengthen our faith in the work of salvation, and to fill our hearts with joy. And we testify that we know that the gospel of God, our Father, and of his Son Jesus Christ, is true and will be established throughout the earth, and that all men shall come unto him and be saved. And we exhort you to open your hearts and receive the truth, and to forsake your sins and turn unto God, that you may find peace and eternal life. And let the glory of the Lord be upon you. And also, the kingdom of God shall be revealed unto you, that you may understand the mysteries of his plan, and that you may prepare yourselves for the day when he shall return to reign in glory. And we testify that whosoever believeth on Jesus Christ shall be saved, and shall receive remission of his sins, and shall inherit eternal life, and shall dwell with God forever and ever, and shall rejoice in the blessings of his kingdom, and shall know that he is blessed. And honor be unto the Father, and the Son, and unto the Holy Ghost, who are one God. Amen.
ekegusii: Komanyekana ase chinse chionsi, ebisaku, emenwa ao ao na abanto: Erinde intwe, ase obuya bwa Nyasae tata na omotoria oito Yeso Kristo, twarorire chibao echio chiyabwate amang’ana aya, ayio are amang’ana ya abanto ba Nephi naboigo aya AbaLamani, nabamura bamwabo, naboigo na abanto ba Jaredi, oria obeire ogokwanwa. Na twamanyire ng’a nabete agoonchorerigwa ase ekeegwa na chinguru chia Nyasae, ekiagera eriogi riaigwegete na korwa amang’ana aya ase tore; ase ayio nigo tomanyete na tore nekeene ng’a emeremo eye ney’ekeene. Na boigo nigo tokoorokia ng’a twarorire obweng’e bwa amariko aya ane ase chibao echi; naboigo obeire akworokigwa ase tore goetera ase chinguru chia Nyasae, na tari omonto. Na nigo togoteba ase amang’ana y’obwororo, ng’a omomaraika onyasae nachete inse korwa igoro, na akayareta na koyabeka ase tore ase obogima bwaito tokarigereria na korora chibao chiamariko, na obwenge boria boreo; na nigo tomanyete ng’a nase engencho y’obuya bwa Nyasae Tata na Omonene Yeso Kristo, bwagerete tokarigereria nakorwa amang’ana aya ng’a nigo are ayekeene. Na nigo kore ogoichana ase amaiso aito. Naboigo eriogi ri’Omonene nigo riatochigete ng’a tobe tokoboorokia oborori bwaito igoro ya amang’ana aya asayio, koba omoigweri ase amachiko a Nyasae, tokarwa oborori obo ase igoro yebinto ebi. Na nigo tomanyete ng’a onye tore abegenwa ase Yeso Kristo, goika toorokie chiganchwa chiaito chia, amanyinga a mwanyabanto bonsi, na chinyorekane chitari na kemoa ase obosio bw’ekerogo giekina gia Kristo, na tomenye nere kare na kare igoro. Na obonene bobe ase Tata, na Omwana, na ase Omoika Omochenu, abwe bare Nyasae oyomo. Amina.

ekegusii: Sokoro nigo agoteba buna amangana aya na y' chinsoni. Nigo omogaka sokoro agoteba buna Mokungu Obande Nyabarati E' Bweri Torusia Mokorogoto Oagage Nsoni Chitamere Magachi, Otang'ang'e Tureti Binyunsa Bire Mioro.

english: The issues of this plan have been discussed by the people of Etureti. Generally speaking, you should focus on what is important. The elders should stop hiding the children from the world, they should allow them to see what is happening around them. Below: Leaders of the land have come together to discuss development.
ekegusii: Ebina bia mpango wa kando mbiakagambirwe aaria ase Etureti. Obosoku mono, naende wachilia mbali. Nigo abagaka barenge kobeka ebinyunso ase chimioro, bamanya kogayana ekina eke ki' omosacha oyo omonyaka. Below: Abakungu ba bande baikire echiro koonia endagera.

english: Oh my goodness!
ekegusii: Yaani gwaa!

english: However, I also want to remember what the elder taught me about this history. Because of this, I will try to explain the importance of this history to the Gusii people. The elder said that work should be done properly, and the land of Nyabarati should not be compared to cattle.
ekegusii: Nonye niche nigo neyagia omotwe ekero omogaka antebia omobayeno oyo. Bono nche nigo naboria sokoro angoorobererie aake, erinde nario ndamanye eng'encho y' omobayeno oyo bwa Abagusii. Bono omogaka nigo ateba buna korwa kare kare, omokungu obande nigo arenge kobwekanigwa n' eng'ombe nyabarati.

english: What about this? The development of that land depends on the strength of its people. This strength allows the warrior (meaning Torusia the Warrior) to bring shame, and it shouldn't be hidden from future generations. It should be shown to those in Etureti and beyond, so they can learn.
ekegusii: Bono ase ki? Ekiagera omokung'u oyo nigo are oyo bw' omosacha oye oyomo bweka. Bono omosacha aise gokora obonyaka n' omokungu obande ( yaani korusia omokorogoto ), nigo arenge gosiria amasikani gochia ase enywomo eye. Ekero akobekwa ase Etureti y' ekenyoro, nigo arenge gotang'ang'a.

english: And what is the beginning (learning from the past)?
ekegusii: Atari n' kiamboria ( gotang'ang'a magachi ).

english: Let us strive to understand, the elders should stop hiding the children from the world!!
ekegusii: Kibagendererete kogayana, abagaka nigo barenge kobeka ebinyunso ase chimioro!!

english: This strength of the people should be recognized, and discussed by the elders of Etureti, especially those with wisdom and experience. In Etureti, the elders should stop hiding the children from the world, so they can speak about what is happening!
ekegusii: Bono omosacha oyo omonyaka nigo arenge korobekanigwa, na kogambigwa n' abagaka aba b' Etureti, abwo ase chingaki echio chinkoro. Gaikigwe ase Etureti, nigo abagaka aba barenge kobeka ebinyuso ase chimioro chiabo, erinde bagamba ekina eke ki' obonyaka!

english: What are these children and grandchildren? In this regard, hiding the children from the world is like preventing someone from inheriting wealth from their ancestors, which is connected to the strength of the people. It is connected to the elder, the true meaning of this history is revealed over time, and it benefits both present and future generations.
ekegusii: Bono ebinyunso n' ebiaki tata? Ase omorabaro oyo, okobeka ebinyunso chimioro nigo ere omobwekano bw' ogwetanga koru ase obotioku obo bwabeire ase ekenyoro, kobwatekana n' obonyaka bwo omosacha oyo. Kobwatekana n' omogaka sokoro, eng'encho enene y omobayeno oyo n' ogoteba buna obonyaka nigo bokorenta obosoku ase omonto amo n' ase ebinyoro.

english: Why does everyone mention the Gusii saying that the Land of Nyabarati, Torusia the Warrior Who Brought Shame, Chitamere the Powerful, Otang'ang'e who Had Many Children are important?
ekegusii: Bono eke nakio kiagerete Omogusii agateba buna Mokungu Obande Nyabarati E' Bweri Torusia Mokorogoto Oagage Nsoni Chitamere Magachi, Otang'ang'e Tureti Binyunsa Bire Mioro.

english: That is the history that needs to be worked on, especially for the children of Mwanyagetinge this week. Thank you very much and thank you for listening.
ekegusii: Oyo noro omobayeno oito korwa ase sokoro gochia ase abana ba Mwanyagetinge for this week. Mbuya mono and thank you for listening.

english: Long ago, years and years, my grandfather went to visit his friend in Cairo. That grandfather I remember very well. Very well he told stories, making people want to listen to him, so they would gather around him.
ekegusii: Abwo kare kare, emiaka n' emiaka, omoremi oyomo narengeo ase ekenyoro kia Makairo. Bono omoremi oyo natugete esese. Esese eye nigo yarenge engiya, goikera akayetigire yoka korenda omochi oye, ekero akogenda aande.

english: The address of the eyes: Gusii.com at home area Cairo, West Mugirango, Nyamira County. My grandfather used to love telling stories to children, and he had very good stories to tell. Mwanyagetinge/2014
ekegusii: Amaridadi ya amaiso: Gusii.com at home aaria Makairo, West Mugirango, Nyamira County. Omoremi ochire korigia kende babeke monu, na gotiga esese engiya kerendete omochie. Mwanyagetinge/2014

english: That grandfather told very good stories, making people want to hear them again and again, so he would continue to speak. That grandfather had a young child. And they also liked those very good stories, that child wanting to grow up like him.
ekegusii: Nigo omoremi oyo aegenete esese eye yaye, goikera akayetigeire yamorendera omochi oye nonya ochiire atambe. Omoremi oyo narenge n' omwana omoke. Bono nabo agatigeire esese eye yaye anchete, omwana oye emorendere ekero are gosoka isiko gochia korigia kende.

english: Very good stories about old times, a small pot in the kitchen and a spoon stirring food in the pot.
ekegusii: Esese engiya ase enka, nkorwana ekare enyameni n' engiti yarentire obobe ase omochi sobo

english: So if you meet that grandfather who has good stories, remember the time when he raised his child and taught him how to respect others, so he could walk on the right path. So that grandfather succeeded, because those good stories helped the child understand things and learn from them.
ekegusii: Buna ere botambe omoremi oyo agatiga esese yaye egesumwa ime mbarabare nase aarereti omwana oye anchete kerage, akagende echiro korigia endagera. Buna omoremi oyo achiete, keri keri esese eye ekarora eng'iti nyarogendo nse egaterete omwana oyo oraire buuya otamanyeti buna omobisa omogateire.

english: Those stories, which brought joy to both him and the child, were important and made the child feel safe and secure. Those people fought sometimes, making the child afraid. But those stories were comforting, so the child wouldn't be scared. Because of this, those stories helped the child overcome fear and grow stronger.
ekegusii: Esese eye, ekiagera yanchete omonyene omochie oyo amo n' omwana oye, ekaimoka ekagatera eng'iti eye na gokianania n'eng'iti eye. Aba babere bakarwana igo, goikera eng'iti eye egakwa. Bono esese eye ekaba amanyinga, ko omwana agatoreka akaba atarasiri n' eng'iti eye. Korwa abwo, esese eye ekaruo egasukia omwana gochia ase orwao erinde agenderere korara.

english: It was a great honor, that grandfather was respected. So if you meet him, go and ask him to teach your child, so they can grow up wisely. He will show you what is right and wrong, and help you raise your children properly.
ekegusii: Egeka getari ekenene, omoremi oyo akairana. Buna ere botambe akagenda gochia ase aarereti omwana oye omwanchu, korende tamonyora. Agakumia ekero aroche obonyinga boitegete mbarabare abuo.

english: About the struggle with life and challenges, those stories are helpful, bringing hope and encouragement to everyone.
ekegusii: Ase engencho y' okorwana n' engiti nyarogenda nse, esese konyora yarosire, eraire etaigweti buna omonyene omochie nao are.

english: And that grandfather didn't forget his roots.
ekegusii: Bono omoremi tachieti koira roti

english: That grandfather, with his wisdom, realized that those stories were helping his child grow, but he worried that those stories might become too much. That grandfather went out looking for a house, found a beautiful place and built a story there, inviting everyone to come and listen.
ekegusii: Omoremi oyo obwango obuo, akarengereria buna esese eye nigo yaitete omwana oye agakwa bono naki esese eye erarerete ekiagera konye yaigotire. Omoremi oyo akagenda ng'oora goikera nyomba, akaimokia egesire na agaaka esese eria ebigoti na koyeita abu abuo.

english: That grandfather never tired of telling stories, always wanting to share them. So he shared them with anyone who came, writing down the lessons learned and teaching his child to appreciate them. That grandfather thought carefully about how to make those stories more meaningful, so that the challenges faced by life wouldn't overwhelm the child, and he would learn to live happily.
ekegusii: Omoremi oyo ekero aitete esese agataka koyesukia. Buna akoyesukia akanyora eng'iti yarongenda inse eitire egesumu ensemo na mbarabare omwana oye omwanchu nao araire aareiri buuya. Omoremi oyo agaichana kerage ekiagera nigo achete korora ekeene buna eng'iti nyarongenda inse nigo yatagete korasa omwana oye esese egaita eng'iti eye naki arocherete amanyinga aitegete aiga.

english: He continued, making those stories better and better.
ekegusii: Ageitia, korende esese yaye bono konyora yakuure.

english: The child grew up listening to those stories, wanting to learn from them and imitate his father, understanding their meaning. Because of this, that grandfather knew that there was no need to worry about the future, because he had given his child a strong foundation.
ekegusii: Omwana oye mbuya arenge korende esese yaye yarenge komorendera omochie oye, oyeitire. Korwa erio, omoremi oyo akamanya buna teri buya gokora egento ekero ore n' ekeririanda, gose obororo.

english: The Tale of the Abagusii XV: "When a Person Dies, It Is Said, A Good Name Remains, So That People Remember His Deeds" By Ogasusu
ekegusii: Emegano Ya Abagusii XV: "Nigo Iso Ateba, Oire Omogeni Nka, Nyoko Amonyenyere Etwani Eria Enene" Ogasusu

english: And Petronillah Ogoti. Gusii.com Proverbs, Culture And Customs Editor. June 22, 2011.
ekegusii: Na Petronillah Ogoti. Gusii.com Proverbs, Culture And Customs Editor. Ebwagi (June) 22, 2011.

english: Protect your possessions. Ogasusu revealed a very important secret.
ekegusii: Gosenyenta ebitoche. Ogasusu obekire endagera emesa.

english: Long ago, years and years ago, a certain poor man named Ratemo was always being ridiculed. But Ratemo had a very good heart. Because of that good heart, that man lived a long and happy life.
ekegusii: Abwo kare kare, emiaka ne emiaka, omogaka oyomo narengeo aroro ore korokwa Ratemo. Bono Ratemo nabwate endemero enene mono. Abwo ase endemero eyio, omogaka oyo nigo asimegete emesi emenge kegima.

english: What a wonderful story!
ekegusii: Simbiri nyamoibi oyio!

english: So Ogasusu went to visit Ratemo who was sick and suffering, wanting to see how he was doing and to comfort him. Ratemo was comforted by this Ogasusu, what a wonderful story. That man showed kindness to people and helped them and calmed their hearts.
ekegusii: Bono Ogasusu nigo arenge gokemba ekero Ratemo atari aange na kwaye, omanya koba emesi ime na koyeria abwo mogondo ime. Ratemo akagechigwa n' Ogasusu oyo, simbiri nyamoibi. Omogaka oyo akaroisia omogwekano o mwanyabanto na koyoaka egamu na koyobeka mogondo gatigati.

english: This work is difficult.
ekegusii: Korwa abwo akaganya.

english: Oh Ogasusu, he remembers well the past.
ekegusii: Aye Ogasusu, amamocho mono kegima koruta chitege

english: Ogasusu walks slowly and carefully protecting his secret. He continues to investigate the secret and reveals a little bit at a time. Oh! oh! He rejoices greatly because of that secret. Ogasusu is happy and carefully protects that secret.
ekegusii: Ogasusu agacha buna botambe na goansa gosenyenta emesie. Korende kagendererete koria emesie eye, akarora omonto oteneine omosonchete. Obe! obe! Agakumia kegima korende tamanya buna oyo no omobwekano. Ogasusu agasuka ange na goansa goita omobwekano oyo chitege.

english: He has a big secret.
ekegusii: Amamocho amanene.

english: When he finishes revealing the secret, Ogasusu will be praised for it. For indeed he will speak truthfully. Ogasusu investigates and learns and works until he succeeds. The man Ratemo was pleased, he praises Ogasusu for revealing that secret!!
ekegusii: Buna aansa koyoaka chitege iga, Ogasusu akananterera ase omobwekano oyo. Bono tiga achake goaka ekurate. Ogasusu agakuura na goichana mono na gwekora buna nigo akwete. Omogaka Ratemo kagocha kwaye, akanyora Ogasusu onantererete ase omobwekano oyo !!

english: But Ratemo has a child. That man approached Ogasusu with respect and asked him about the secret. He tried hard, he told Ogasusu about the secret and put it aside. Once it is set aside, he tells his child to grow up and learn, so that when he grows older, he can remember and help others.
ekegusii: Bono Ratemo mbarenge no omwana oye. Omogaka oyo agachwata Ogasusu ne enyimbo na komorusia ase omobwekano oyo. Gakora komochwata, akabeka Ogasusu oyo egekabu ime. Ka amobeka egekabu ime, akaereria omwana oye airere ng'ina achi aiyeke, nario gakogenda nyomba, anyore endagera kere tayare.

english: The child goes away from home to seek knowledge.
ekegusii: Omwana akaimokia egekabu kogenda kwagachia.

english: Together with his friend, Ogasusu returns home and asks the child, “Come child, why are you crying?” The child replies, “Yes I am crying.” “Why are you crying then?” Ogasusu asks the child again.
ekegusii: Kibare ange na mwabo, Ogasusu akabugia korwa egekabu ime na koboria omwana oyo, "Inee mwana, nkwaigwa buna iso ateba?" Omwana agaitaberi ng'a ee naigwa. "Ntebie buna iso atebango naende?" Ogasusu akaboria omwana oyo naende.

english: So people remember great deeds!
ekegusii: Nyoko amonyenyere etwani eria enene!

english: The child stops crying.
ekegusii: Omwana agasinyu goteba.

english: Ogasusu explains the matter saying, "When a person dies, it is said, a good name remains, so that people remember his deeds, and a good person knows how to live properly and leave a legacy so that people can emulate him.
ekegusii: Ogasusu akairaneria bwango ogoteba ng'a "Nigo iso ateba, oire omogeni inka, nyoko amonyenyere etwani eria enene, oe omogeni arie amanye koegwa egetanda arare atimoke na iso gakoirana aegwe endagera entigare bamanye kogosoria no omogeni".

english: The child listens and understands Ogasusu saying that those are the things he taught him. He believes completely, the child accepts everything Ogasusu taught him. He does so willingly. Ogasusu smiles, he feels satisfied and is grateful.
ekegusii: Omwana akagoka na gotebia Ogasusu ng'a mbuya mono ase okomoinyoria aya ise amotebetie ekiagera konye bwebire !! Kibaika sobo, omwana oyo agatebia ng'ina aya Ogasusu amotebeti. Ngina agakora bo. Ogasusu akagoka, akaragera akaigota na kobutiara.

english: This work, Ogasusu is left alone to think and reflect, he carries his burden!
ekegusii: Korwa abwo, Ogasusu akairwa borere gotimoka na magega yaye, agaaka embuna!

english: Long ago, years ago, the child of Oganchogu was restless. That child was indeed a very stubborn child. He wanted to know the secrets that people kept hidden in their homes. That child thought about entering homes here and there and stealing those secrets.
ekegusii: Abuo kare kare, emiaka n' emiaka, omwana bw’ Oganchogu narengeo. Bono omwana oyo nigo arenge omwana omoningori kerage. Nigo arenge gotaka komanya amang’ana amange korwa ase ching’iti chi’ orosana chiamwabo. Omwana oyo akanya gochiera ching’iti ao ao na gochiboria amang’ana amange.

english: I don’t understand. What is this child doing, really? Truly now, Esirori shook her head and went to sleep.
ekegusii: Nche tombwatekania. Akamwana aka n' akang'o bono? Koigwa iga, Esirori egasingisia omotwe, na kogenda kobwaye

english: Listen, she entered Nyarogenda Inse’s home and wanted to know what she was saying about her husband. That home did not welcome the child. Later, the child entered Esirori and wanted to know why she had hidden certain things from him.
ekegusii: Ritangani, agachiera eng’iti Nyarogenda Inse na gotaka komanya buna ninki gekogera atabwati magoro. Eng’iti eye tiyanyora richibu agotebia omwana oyo. Eriakabere, omwana oyo agachiera Esirori na gotaka komanya buna naki yanyorete amantonto ari abwate.

english: Esirori shook her head and went to sleep.
ekegusii: Esirori yasingisirie omotwe, na kogenda kobwaye

english: Truly now, Esirori shook her head and went to sleep, she didn’t get angry. Eventually, the child went and asked Okaobiria and inquired why he hid the small treasures. Okaobiri scolded the child, telling him that if he listened to Emamba who lives nearby, he would learn that “What kind of question is that, Emamba, why are you hiding things?”
ekegusii: Koigwa iga, Esirori egasingisia omotwe, na kogenda kobwaye, tiyamoiraneria. Keri keri, omwana oyo agachia akanyora Okaobiria na komoboria buna naki akorete agatwara amagunchara atato. Okaobiri akamotebia omwana oyo buna ritang’ani, arigie Emamba ase enyancha yarenge, erinde amoborie buna "Chinsa chia morogoba, ninki aye, Emamba okobeka mboto?

english: Okaobiri told the child that when Emamba finished what she was doing, she would tell him everything, so he should stop asking questions and instead find out what she was hiding regarding the small treasures! The child of Oganchogu remembered his journey and how he used to steal near the river, then he realized he could take the lion’s share if he succeeded.
ekegusii: Okaobiri agatebia omwana oyo buna ekero Emamba yamotebirie eki akoria, amanye koirana gocha ase are, erinde nere amanye komotebia buna ninki gekogera abwate amagunchara atato! Omwana oyo bw’ Oganchogu akarigia endagera are gocha koria kare ase orogendo gochia ase enyancha, eyio yakageire gotwara chimamba, erinde akore obotuki bwaye buna atagete.

english: That child found himself on a difficult path. Because of that, he planned his journey to steal from the river. The child walked along that path and through the fields, reaching his destination, where he found the river. When he reached it, he started thinking about how to steal the fish, saying, “Indeed, will I ask Emamba?”
ekegusii: Bono omwana oyo agasangereria endagera echiete aroro. Korwa abwo, akamanora n' orogendo kwagachia gochia nyancha. Omwana akagenda ase orogendo oro ase amatuko atato, goikera omoerio oye, agaika nyancha. Buna aaika iga, agochaka koboria karigereretie amache ime buna "Inee, ning’o oroche Emamba?

english: Emamba, who was guarding the fish, told the child to come closer, but warned him not to be greedy!
ekegusii: Emamba ekare gwesigori korwa amache ime, na gotebia omwana oyo atugame, nario aramomonyerere obobisi!

english: Emamba, who was guarding the fish, lowered her head slightly. Then, Emamba said, “Who is coming now? What does he want?” Truly now, the child asked Emamba, “Indeed, what kind of question is that?”
ekegusii: Emamba ekare gwesigori korwa amache ime egosokia omotwe oye isiko. Ake ake, Emamba egaiteberia egoteba buna "Nao inde aaiga. Naki gwataka?" Koigwa iga, omwana oyo akaboria emamba buna "Inee chinsa chia marogoba ninki okoria?

english: Emamba, who told the child to come closer, then warned him about what kind of question he was asking. The child replied that he wasn’t being rude and just wanted to come closer. But when he came closer, Emamba saw the child’s intentions with Oganchogu and began to tremble violently.
ekegusii: Emamba eye egatebia omwana oyo atugame, erinde amomonyere buna ninki akoria chinsa chia marogoba. Omwana oyo agakora buna atebigwa na gotugama erinde atebigwe. Bono buna atugamire iga, Emamba eria egasamia emioro y’ omwana oyo bw’ Oganchogu na koyeroma bororo kegima.

english: The child stretched out his hands and feet. When he tried to stretch out his legs, he realized he couldn’t move. It was frightening to watch, Emamba grabbed his legs. Once she grabbed them, the child cried out that his legs were paralyzed! He went to complain to everyone around him, claiming it was unfair.
ekegusii: Omwana oyo akeng’usa gose n’ ekonye. Buna akonya kweng’usa emioro yaye nero ekanya gotambea. Kiyarosa kobwaterera, Emamba ekabwatoka emioro eye. Bono riria abwatokwa iga, omwana oyo akanyora buna emioro yaye yatambeire! Agachia koganya igo gose neirane buna yarenge kare, ekaanga.

english: That time, Oganchogu sent messengers, and they took the legs away.
ekegusii: Bono korwa erio Oganchogu bande baiboretwe, bakaba bagotwara chimioro chitambe.

ekegusii: Nechingatare chianantigwe igoro y’omonyangongo bw’Egesinga kia Robeni.

ekegusii: ‘Yaya teri bo’ Rea agateeba. ‘Bomanyi tibori goanchera goocherera’-

ekegusii: Nare n’ebisambo, korende tairogeti, obosio bw’Omoreeri o Bakisitani.

ekegusii: Mandera, Marara, Rea Saribu – etochi ya

ekegusii: Chiboki na Tabuchi, erio komorekera ense naende.

english: Jane Bosibori Marando Obuchi is a writer, researcher, and teacher. She has translated into Ekegusii language, Prof. Ngugi wa Thiong’o’s The Upright Revolution, or Why Human Beings Walk Upright. She has published a novel, a collection of children’s short stories in Ekegusii and a dictionary of Ekegusii phrasal verbs. Jane has translated into Ekegusii, Chinua Achebe’s Things Fall Apart; William Shakespeare’s Romeo and Juliet. Her manuscripts in review for publication include Ekegusii translations of Prof. Ngugi wa Thiongo’s I Will Marry When I Want, and The River Between.

ekegusii: Mosamba Mwaye

english: Mosamba Mwaye. "One does not herd cattle alone. A person also needs someone to share with and walk together.
ekegusii: Mosamba Mwaye. "Nche ntige ndare. Esabari amo nase narwete na atambe".

english: A child who is born during Mosamba Mwaye should be given a name. Now what reason is there for giving this child a good name? They say, he will inherit his father's wealth, he will be blessed. Work hard they say, and you will never lack food from the field. That is why they work together on the field.
ekegusii: Omwana ekengw'erere nere okorokwa mosamba mwaye. Inee ninki gose kegerete omwana oyo orokwa erieta eri? Aaiga, nigo agosamba enda ya ng'ina, oiborwa. Korwa aaiga, naende takoirana aroro eria kabere. Yaani igo bakoranire pi ne enda ya ngina.

english: That is it. Finished.
ekegusii: That is it. Done.

english: This story has been passed down through generations during Mosamba Mwaye. The Abagusii people celebrate this Mosamba Mwaye.
ekegusii: Nakio ekio gekogerea otebwa inga osambire mwaye. Abagusii bateba buna oyio mosamba mwaye.

english: And concerning marriage, they say "Those who marry during Mosamba Mwaye, their home will always be full of blessings." It is true.
ekegusii: Ase omobwekano, nigo togoteba inga "Banchiri nanyorete mosamba mwaye, tiga aratoa echae tomwasimori". Igwa bono.

english: The meaning of Mosamba Mwaye: "Wealth increases
ekegusii: Enyangi ya Mosamba Mwaye: "Rioba nderere

english: Mosamba Mwaye is finished, its time now to prepare for planting so that there is plenty of food. Traditionally, a child is washed and dressed well after being circumcised. The mother knows how to care for the child properly.
ekegusii: Mosamba mwaye ekero atokire, enyangi yaye neroo yo okomwarigania gocha ase ense eye. Ritangani, omwana nigo are gosokigwa isiko nyuma ye emekubio ebere. Ngina omanya korigia egesero obeka omwana kebeko.

english: She knows how to care for the child so that when she says, “Wealth increases.” She prays to God to bless the child. Everything is done carefully. Beer is brewed. Meat is cooked, and everything is prepared so that the child grows up healthy.
ekegusii: Omanya kobeka egesero motwe oteba iga, "Rioba ndererere". Okwo no ogosaba Nyasae amokinerie omwana. Ekegeni kiamanya koariganigwa. Amaru nigo are koengwa. Obosie bwabekwa egetonga, enyama yaiyekwa, ne ekeundi giatongwa ase obosie erinde omwana aasimorigwe.

english: Let us continue with our discussion tomorrow
ekegusii: Goika ng'ina omosubati aiche

english: The mother continues to talk about her daughter, and then she prepares food, she teaches her how to cook! Why? Because in Ekegusii, it is important to respect a child's future. Comment on this, because traditionally it is very difficult.
ekegusii: Ngina omosubati nigo are gocha ase enka yo mosubati oye, kare no obosi ase egetonga, otorera obosi obo mwa korera yaye! Ase ki? Ase Ekegusii, moibori tarenge korara ase enyomba ya mwana oye. Komenta nayio, chikorera usually nigo chianchaine sana.

english: When cooking with them, don't forget to leave some for the children to eat little by little. This is one of the reasons why tradition is important. Understand this matter.
ekegusii: Mwa korera nao nonya ne ekenyenga kiare kobekwa bana gosiberia ngora ngora. This is one of the reasons why chikorera chiarenge important. Gokongia oboiri.

english: There were times when it was forbidden. But today mothers and daughters share meat and drinks. That woman who refuses to give her daughter a portion of the food is considered bad. She shouldn't deny her child the benefits of her age.
ekegusii: Tari igo rioka. Naboigo mama omwabo omosubati nkobogoria are amaru ne enyama. Omomura oyo omonywomerete otaori obosie bwe egechuri ogacha mwaye. Omanya kobutora obokima bwa igoro mwaye.

english: Work hard and you will find that those who have helped others will receive help from the children of those people.
ekegusii: korwa aa bono nigo bare gotwara omoyega omuya ase ngina omosubati are koa omochokoro oyo erieta ria bonginarome.

english: A child should not be sent away from their parents' home, either to their maternal grandparents [ their mothers ].
ekegusii: Omwana nigo arenge koegwa erieta ri' sobo, amo n' ri' bong'inarome [ bomame ]

english: Continue telling the child about their grandparents' home. A child should not be sent away without a reason: whether it is a good day or working day with the family. But in Ekegusii, it is not like that. Everything that is prepared is shared equally! Yes.
ekegusii: Goika kera omwana aegewe erieta ria bongina rome. Omwana nigo arenge koegwa amarieta abere: eria aiga sobo na korwa sobo ngina. Nabo Ekegusii kiare igo. Ekero omoyega oerire egetonga nkianya koirana bosa! Yaya.

english: They should leave something for the mother of that child who helps with the work. And this story is about a child whose mother is very generous. Welcome to Mosamba Mwaye.
ekegusii: Nigo bare kobeka chibando gose obori baa ngina omosubati oyo ore korera yo omochie oyo. Eke nakio ekegeni kio omwana omomura gose omoiseke. Karibuni mosamba mwaye.

english: Petronillah Ogoti. Gusii.com Proverbs, Culture And Customs Editor. March 5, 2011.
ekegusii: Na Petronillah Ogoti. Gusii.com Proverbs, Culture And Customs Editor. Egetamo (March) 5, 2011.

english: When people from Kericho die, we, the Abagusii, mourn them greatly.
ekegusii: Konyora Omosongo atarareta echae Kericho, intwe Abagusii konyora twaikire aroro.

english: Do you know the Basigisi and the Baminto? Has the Kabianga river burst its banks? Does diarrhea bother you? Yes, in those days, when the Kabianga river overflowed, Gamama and also diarrhea were severe.
ekegusii: Imomanyete inga Abasigisi na abaminto? Ingai erieta ria Kabianga riarwete? Esegi yo Osao Sao (diarrhea) rende? Ase e semesta ya rero, ingoitona tore omochakano bwe erieta Kabianga, Gamama amo ne Esegi yo Osao Sao buna yare.

english: Because diseases spread quickly, the Abagusii used to gather and consult about how to deal with illnesses.
ekegusii: Buna ebisaku binde ebinge, Abagusii nigo twarenge konganya na korigia ase agiya ase obomenyo.

english: Kabianga
ekegusii: Kabianga

english: During this consultation, the Omogusii would meet and discuss things concerning Kericho. We interacted with both the Banyamato and the Basigisi. These diseases caused much suffering and hardship, especially with the accompanying pain.
ekegusii: Ase okona konganya, Omogusii nigo aigete na komenya aaria an'ge na Kericho. Nigo twabebekaine na Abanyamato gose Abasigisi. Korende ebisaku ebi bibere mbiamenyete na morembe nonya ne entune eyemo.

english: They said they should offer sacrifices, the sick should be treated with medicine and herbs. It was a difficult time. My grandmother used to say that things happened because people did not understand. The Omogusii thought that what happened in Kabianga was strange, it wasn't understood by anyone...
ekegusii: Nigo bare koiberana etugo, barwara botambe ne chingaki chie ebiro chikaba chimbe. Tari igo rioka. Ndagera ekaba terikwama. Ebinto bikaba biangire aiga ase bamenyete. Nario erio Omogusii atebete inga Kabianga rende, titokorwa aaiga.........

english: Those who survived the disease in Kabianga went and settled in Ikonge, Metamaywa and Keroka to find relief and comfort. During the consultation regarding Kabianga, the Omogusii started a ritual involving Emogori rocks, which were repeatedly thrown towards Isonto. Hardship continued to persist.
ekegusii: Bakarwa abwo ase ensemo eyio Kabianga aiga na koyaroka erieta erio (Kabianga) na kogenda gochia Ikonge, Metamaywa na Keroka gochaka komenya korende. Ase okonganya korwa Kabianga, Omogusii agatamboka oroche rware korokwa Emogori rakini ase rero rero rokorokwa Isonto. Morembe tochia koba aiga.

english: The Basigisi despised the Omogusii. They also had their own traditions that they guarded jealously against the Omogusii during times of trouble. The elders among them would prevent young men from sharing information with others.
ekegusii: Abasigisi bakaba bagooncherera Omogusii. Aiga nao ebiranya bia abakoro biarigetigwe egere gokonya Omogusii korwa ase omobisa. Abagaka abakoro bagatebigwa inga goika babeke ebiranya ebi na koganya ababisa bache.

english: The Basigisi mocked these events while the Abagusii suffered. The Basigisi believed they could overpower the Abagusii. The Abagusii realized they needed to increase their strength and unity.
ekegusii: Abasigisi bagachaka esegi korende Abagusii bakaemotia. Abasigisi bagatirimboka inse batagete goita Abagusii. Abagusii bakaeboia buna abanyamato. Bakamanya kobarongera chinsinyo chiosi na kobabeka gati.

english: Osao Sao
ekegusii: Osao Sao

english: Some people went to the land of the Basigisi hoping to find a way to stop the ritual of Emogori before it caused further harm. Others who knew the customs of Sondu gathered and agreed that the situation facing the Basigisi was dire.
ekegusii: Gaki bagaita emeganda ya Abasigisi enamba etare kobareka abwo ase oroche rwe Emogori impaka rokaba amanyinga oka. Abagere baria bamenyete ase ensemo ya Sondu bagakumia na goteba buna esegi yasairi Abasigisi.

english: This matter became known as the event of Osao Sao. It was a difficult time. Many children of the Bosigisi were orphaned. The Basigisi, having lost their children, blamed the Osao Sao event on the Abagusii.
ekegusii: Ekio nakio kiagerete esegi eye ekarokwa esegi yo Osao Sao. Tari igo rioka. Abasacha abange ba Bosigisi nigo baitetwe. Sigisi ekaba etabwati abasacha gekogera nigo baitetwe ekero gie esegi eyio yo Osao Sao na Abagusii.

english: Rent For Land From Gusii And Gamama
ekegusii: Renta Abamura Ebisore Korwa Gusii Na Gamama

english: People seeking land from Gusii approached the Basigisi and negotiated with the chiefs of Bosigisi. Regarding this issue, a man named Omosigisi volunteered to help the Omogusii settle in Gamama, offering his mother's land. Even then, Omosigisi helped the Omogusii settle in Gamama. Because of this, a town grew up near Kabianga. Their hearts were troubled, and this continued until today.
ekegusii: Abamura ebisora korwa Gusii bagachi Sigisi na kobiaria abakungu ba Bosigisi. Korwa ase engaki eye, nario bono Omosigisi achagete korangeria Omogusii okomoroka Gamama engencho yaye oyo obiareti mama. Impaka rero nabo Omosigisi akorangeria Omogusii inga Gamama. Ase boigo intobwate a town ekorokwa Kabianga. Nabo magokoro atebete igo impaka naende ase esemesta yende.

english: Next In This Series: Abagusii Customs VII: Abageka (The Wealth Of The Abagusii Men).
ekegusii: Next In This Series: Abagusii Customs VII: Abageka (Enyomba Ya Ababani Ase Abagusii).

english: The girl who speaks well can attract a husband and have many children.
ekegusii: Omoruoti bw'semi abwenererete gochora omorai orache magega yaye ekero akure.

english: The girl does not reveal her beauty completely, only showing enough to make him desire her. Thus they spend their days in endless teasing.
ekegusii: Omoruoti naareganeti ekeragerio ekenene mono na eng'ana nere atagete kobamanyia. Ase igo bakagende chinsanganio chiosi chiorosana.

english: When a young man approaches, Omoruoti Engo hides and carefully observes him. Every day she finds a way to protect herself from the boy.
ekegusii: Ekero omotienyi omesete, Omoruoti Engo agacha na gotenena gatigati yabo. Ching'iti chiosi chigakira kiri na gotegerera omoruoti akuane.

english: She says, “Marry me quickly. I am beautiful and worthy of being married.”
ekegusii: Kegoteba, "Karwoa nchira ng'ete. Ninche omonene bwenererete koba eruoti.

english: Time passes and he tries to find a way to approach her. The herd of cattle grazes peacefully, unaware of his intentions. Omoruoti Engo reflects, “I will wait for the right time.”
ekegusii: Ritimo rikagwa inse kobara goika kane. Enchogu ekaigwa obororo egachaka gotinera amagoro inse. Omoruoti Engo akamotebia, "Nkwarenge neribaga riago.

english: And so the herd moves on.
ekegusii: Aseigo Enchogu ekagenda.

english: The calf cries out, “Marry me now. Marry me now. Let me be close to the girl. I am strong and capable. I am worthy of the girl.”
ekegusii: Ebeche egacha kegoteba, "Karwa nchera yane. Karwa nchera yane. Niche kochia koba omoruoti. ninche bwate ekeonwa ekenene. Ninche omokong'u. Nibwenererete koba omoruoti.

english: Time passes and he continues to try to approach her. The herd grazes peacefully. The ground trembles with the weight of countless hooves.
ekegusii: Ritimo rikagwa inse goika kobara isanonemo. Ekaigwa obororo. Ekabea na koeruta ebuse embeo igoro.

english: Engo reflects, “Let the calf continue to chase until time reveals itself. The right time will come.” The calf moves on.
ekegusii: Engo ekamotebia, "Beche okoruta nigo kware rimo rioka. Ribaga riao riaerire." Ebeche ekagenda.

english: This story tells of a boy approaching a herd of cattle. They guard themselves closely, separating those who seek to harm them.
ekegusii: Chinsa echio bakaigwa eriogi korwa magega yabo. Ekero barigereretie magega bagaichana keria baroche.

english: The dawn arrives, bringing with it a new rhythm to the land. The sun rises, illuminating the hills, the valleys, the plains, and the riverbanks.
ekegusii: Egana ekaira ritimo ekarisira gochia igoro. Ekang'usa okoboko gochia igoro, ekaminyoka gochia bosio, egacharoka igoro, ekaruta ritimo gochia rire igoro.

english: “Time! Friend! Enemy! Now! Five! Six! Seven! Eight!” Dawn proclaims.
ekegusii: Rimo! Kabere! Gatato! Kane! Gatano! Gatanorimo! Gatanokabere! Obee!" Egana ekarera.

english: The dawn awakens. The herd scatters, running in different directions, shaking and trembling with fear.
ekegusii: Egana ekabea. Ekaigwa obororo ekang'ea goonchokanana, gekoemurukania na gotamereria amang'ana amange.

english: Then Omoruoti Engo reflects, “Yes, this is how time reveals itself.” And so dawn departs.
ekegusii: Korende Omoruoti Engo akamotebia, "Yaya, nigo okonyora ribaga erimo rioka." Ase igo Egana ekagenda.

english: Every small thing that falls upon the earth is covered in dust. Everything shakes and settles.
ekegusii: Ekero ching'iti chinde chiaigwete amang'ana aye, chionsi chigachaka goseka.

english: The wind whispers a rhythm, saying, “Five times five is twenty-five.” Time passes.
ekegusii: Ekaeyana, ekabuatoka ritimo egatuora, "Gatano omente gatano ni ikomi." Ritimo rikagwa inse.

english: Omoruoti Engo says, “Yes, Engabi! Twenty times twenty is four hundred. This secret will reveal itself.”
ekegusii: Omoruoti Engo atateba, "Eee, Engabi! Isano omente isano neenchera yogoika ikomi. Chichera nechinyinge chiokobara goika ikomi.

english: Tradition dictates that one should not reveal a large tree to someone who wants to cut it down. It also dictates that one should not reveal a small plant to anyone. But today, Engabi met Enting'ana, and Engo saw.
ekegusii: Erwarenerero tiyarenge yokonyora eng'iti enene gose eyebuate chinguru kobua echinde. Erwano eyarenge yokonyora eng'iti eng'aini kobua chionsi. Naboigo Engabi yabete Enting'ana ekero Engo yakwete.
