english: Abagusii Customs XV: The Respect of Elders
ekegusii: Abagusii Customs XV: Amasabo Ye Ribina

english: A father does not despise his children, even if they are troublesome; a mother doesn't reject her children, even if they make mistakes, she loves them just the same. But observe this important thing well. For sometimes, because of poverty, old people may fail to teach their children good manners:
ekegusii: Omogaka sokoro ominto nantebetie buna Mwanyagetinge ominto omokoro naegenete ebinto gete, ebio ekero biakorekanire, egento gete nigo kegokorekana. Nabo kerabe ekiya gose ekebe. Ase rituko ria rero, tiga ingo toyakwanere amang'ana aria abakoro baito babegete okwegena ase are buna ekobwatia:

english: 1. Teaching: A lesson taught repeatedly to a child, will stick with him forever and he will never forget it. And remember, it is better to teach children while they are young, than to try to correct them when they are grown up!!
ekegusii: 1. Ekiegesa: Ekero ekiegesa kiarenge koria omonto, nigo yarenge gotebekana ng'a aande aake omonto nare okare kogokwana. Na kogesiria, nigo kwarenge gotebigwa obare abana bamino ase omoyo ime, otari gokwana oigwekane !!

english: 2. Avoiding bad company: It is good to choose good friends carefully so that a child doesn't associate with bad companions, because bad friends can lead to trouble and ruin a good reputation, making it difficult to restore it.
ekegusii: 2. Gotamboka ebite bie ching'eni: Oise gotora ching'eni ebite erinde obitige inse omonto ache abitamboke, nigo ebianda bigokoria na ochake kominyoka ekero kwabekire ching'eni echi riiko, goikera gwachiyekire erinde gwachirire.

english: 3. Being careful with advice: It is good to listen to wise counsel, and to be humble enough to accept correction and learn from others’ experiences, so that you don't think you know everything and become arrogant. Therefore, always listen and let them advise you properly, so that you won't regret it later when things go wrong.
ekegusii: 3. Naiguure bwatiokire: Oise kogenda mw' omwamate oo, omanye konyora buna okorire koragera naende n' ebinto bakoenia korwa emesa, nigo yarenge gotebekana buna aye nigo okare gokwana omoamate oyo oo bobe. Korende oise goika onyore nigo bagotereka endagera emesa baragere gose mbagasaine koragera, nigo egotebekana buna nigo ogokwana omwamate oyo buuya.

english: 4. A foolish elder should be respected: An elder who speaks carelessly and makes reckless decisions, should still be respected so that he doesn't mistreat a younger person.
ekegusii: 4. Oyo tata nakamura aranyore: Omosacha mokaye ebwateranetie n' egioto geise komocharoka okogoro, nigo yarenge gotebekana buna omorugie oye nigo agocha koibora omwana omomura.

english: May God help us!! This story happened to the family of Mr. Simba Ndemo who lives in Kisii Town, Kisii County. Go and ask about it at Barclays Bank, Kisii Town. Mwanyagetinge.com/2015
ekegusii: Kai tata !! Egioto giacharokire amagoro y' omogaka Simba Ndemo aaria Kisii Town, Kisii County. Tokare goika n' magokoro baba ominto aaria Barclays Bank, Kisii Town. Mwanyagetinge.com/2015

english: 5. Regarding dreams: If someone has a dream and interprets it correctly, then it is believed that the dream is true and will come to pass.
ekegusii: 5. Endoto embe: Oise korota omonto orwarete buna ogwenire na konora nigo egotebekana ng'a endoto eye n' embe na nigo oyo arakwe.

english: 6. A child who cries a lot: A child who cries constantly, it is believed that he will grow up to be a thief.
ekegusii: 6. Omwana ngoseka are: Omwana omoke ekero araire aise goseka, igo nigo yarenge kororekana buna nigo arota buna ise okuure.

english: 7. A quiet child: A child who is very quiet, it is believed that he will grow up to be a liar.
ekegusii: 7. Omwana nkorera are: Omwana omoke ekero araire aise korera karaire, nigo yarenge gotebekana buna nigo arota buna ng'ina okuure.

english: 8. That elder is stubborn: If someone takes a child to an elder, it is believed that the child will not improve unless he is disciplined.
ekegusii: 8. Oyo tata nigo arabe oundu: Oise gotamboka omwana nigo egotebekana buna omwana oyo tagokina atambee gochia igoro.

english: 9. And the maternal uncle: A child who goes to his maternal uncle seeking help, it is believed that he will find favor and receive assistance.
ekegusii: 9. Oyo n' omogworu: Ekero omonto akorota oyomwabo buna okure nigo egotebekana buna nigo aragerete obotuko obuo akaigota kerage.

english: 10. And the inheritance: Sometimes people fight over property and quarrel bitterly, leading to conflicts. It is believed that a person who steals another’s property will suffer consequences. Sometimes such a person will be cursed and lose his inheritance.
ekegusii: 10. Eye yabeire ekeriero: Etwani iese kobuga chinsa chiri etabwenereti kobuga buna botuko gati, igo mbobe. Nigo yarenge gotebekana buna omonto bw' eamate eye nache atwe ekamo. Etwani buna eye nigo yarenge konyenywa ase obwango na koba ekeriero.

english: Greetings to our fathers and mothers, goodbye everyone and thank you for listening.
ekegusii: Koru ase omogaka sokoro ominto, mbuya mono and thank you for listening.

english: (Ebicha: Africapoint.com)
ekegusii: (Ebicha: Africapoint.com)

english: Did Father truly investigate this matter well? Now he has also investigated this story. He intends to thoroughly examine the case concerning the inheritance of property. We will discuss the property well so that people from Molo understand. This year, 1992, the people who helped us (or those who opposed the Gusii) changed this story which was causing division and conflict. The story caused problems because it made people fight and quarrel over land. This story had eyes that could see far and understand everything, understanding the helpers' intentions, understanding the powerful and the wealthy.
ekegusii: Tata inaki agaanchete obotugi abwo kare? Nonya bono naanchete emeremo eyio. Egento narorire egekong’u gotuga nechiombe. Ntwagatugire chiombe kare riri twamenyete aria Molo. Bono omwaka o 1992 Abatwomera igoro (ko abande bakobaroka Abasigisi) bagachaka esegi eyio ekabetereria tong’anye korwa aroro. Engaki esegi yaogete ning’iyorete abasacha bakoeinda nechinsara gochia korwania ababisa. Engaki eyio amaiso ane konyora tarang’ainia igo tinamaete ninki kiarenge kogenderera, tinamaete Omotwomera igoro ninki, gose Omomaanyi gose Omoikoyo.

english: Because of this, I went to look at the property that was given to me, hoping to find peace; however, I found many disputes about boundaries and many conflicts about ownership. Now, I realized something; it is better to avoid unnecessary arguments regarding the land dispute, avoiding trouble. Continue, and perhaps we can resolve this land issue peacefully and without conflict. These boundaries are very clear and well-defined, they are known to everyone and anyone who wants to know them. The elders have spoken and explained everything clearly to the community.
ekegusii: Ning’inyorete gingotara getii nakogenda ase chiombe chiakabekire esike, namanya koumora amache ime y’echingoro chiria chiremire n’amatimbo ime y’echabu eria. Bono egento nachete komanya neke; oise kobeka omorengari oo ase engoro y’eritimbo indigosoka, rikoirana ime. Korende oise gosuka ensemo iga ritimbo rikorora oborabu na gosoka. Amatimbo ayio arenge aria amanene amasomba-esike, aria abwate egento mosio bwe rigunchara ri’ekeobiria s’omotwe. Abamura baminto nabarabwo imbagatugire amaruma amo n’ebisusu.

english: Regarding this story, we discussed the land in Molo for many years, and four witnesses testified about the property. Now, again, did Father investigate this matter carefully? Those who understood the situation said that this thing would bring problems and cause disagreements, leading to chaos and confusion. Father discovered a secret agreement (with the powerful) and was surprised by what he learned. Those thieves stole meat and spread rumors, causing unrest and anxiety.
ekegusii: Korwa engaki eyio twatamete esegi aria Molo emiaka ang’e ekomi ne’ene egaeta abaibori bane bataratuga chiombe naende. Bono ng’ora ng’ora tata agachaka gotuga ebichuchu. Nabo abianchete ekerage nonya chingaki chinde obireta nyomba na kobisiekera nonya ebabu ime, biatioki enyomba nagotorentera chinda. Tata agatema gotuga ching’ondi chikamanya koibu (erabe na Abamaanyi) nakonyenyerwa ang’e na seito. Abaibi abwo bakaimoki enyama na gototigera amayio, eura n’amanyinga oka.

english: Father knows how to deal with someone who deceives, someone who steals, and also how to handle matters involving the Abakamba clan.
ekegusii: Tata akamanya korangeri omogaka gete omonyamesira, omogaka okong’ire, naende korwa egesaku ki’Abakamba.

english: I remember that deceiver who caused trouble and misled people, deceiving them and making them suffer. We all know that this problem affected those thieves.
ekegusii: Nkarora omonyamesira oyio gagosiba amariogo gete ase risakara na konyabisa ase akabaga gake gesieri abwo boeri. Timanyeti gose eriogo erio ndiabwatete abaibi abwo.

english: Again, Father investigated this property. He examined the cattle closely. There is a cow whose horn is broken. That cow with a broken horn knows how to be stubborn and refuses to be controlled. It keeps mooing loudly, attracting attention, and causes commotion everywhere, disrupting peace. Mother says, "Why does it make such noise and attract attention? Perhaps others will also come." And yet she doesn't realize how much damage that cow is causing. The powerful people came to try and solve the problem. That cow led Father to discover a treasure. Mother thought her husband wouldn't return.
ekegusii: Ng’ora ng’ora tata agachaka gotuga chiombe naende. Akagora chiombe isato. Ibere nyang’era eyemo nyabarati iga. Eng’ombe eyemo nyang’era ekamanya kobwatwa noborwaire gete. Egeka geke gekaera egasinyu koimoka, egachaka gosoki amasombogoku korwa monwa, na koruta chintacho rituko rigima. Mama akamanya goteba, “Oroche buna ekoruta chintacho na gosoki riuro? Nonya abanto nabo bagokwa iga.” Naende teireti egeka egetambe rituko erioerio egakwa. Abaamanyi bagacha bakanyeira gochia gotindeka. Rituko rikobwatia tata akagora chimbori. Mama agakona ko tatebeti tata kende.

english: That cow with a black spot remained calm. Father remembered a proverb, saying, "A black spot indicates a journey, meaning someone will travel to another place to explain things.
ekegusii: Eng’ombe eyemo neroo yatigarete. Tata agantomire inyesibe getii, omanya kong’inyori kera engaki,

english: That cow also tried to run away, trying to escape. But because it had already started something bad, it continued to create more trouble and destruction. The leader of the home saw everything and understood the seriousness of the situation. We realized that those people were capable of causing harm and stealing from us. This story reminds me of my father, who always sought justice and helped his neighbors. I swear, I won't forget this lesson ever.
ekegusii: “osibe egekundo buya tegenda o bande tochake kogamba ebina igaa.”

english: The Boindi Lotus (Nelumbo nucifera) is a beautiful aquatic plant that grows in muddy waters. The flowers are usually pink or white and can be up to two meters tall.
ekegusii: Lotus ya Boindi (Nelumbo nucifera) nigo ere ekemeri ki’amache ekiya mono n’amato machani agocheng’enena ase amache. Amaoga amabariri agotoka ase amatina amanetu agotira chisentimita chinyinge igoro y’amache.

english: Boindi lotus flowers are often grown in ponds and lakes and are considered sacred in Buddhism due to their symbolism of purity. This plant originates from Asia and has been cultivated for centuries. The Boindi lotus is also known as a water lily. It's not clear whether this plant is native to our region; it seems to have been introduced recently.
ekegusii: Amaoga a Lotus ya boindi igo akoirwa buna amachenu mono ekiagere agotumeka na chibuddhist ekero ki’emeyega y’ogosasima. Ekemeri ekegima nigo kere ekiya ase okoria;korende chintetere n’emerio nigo chikoriegwa mono ase maate ya moino ya Asia. Lotus ya boindi nigo ere ekemeri gekwama ase amache buna lily y’amache. Tari bokong’e kwamia ekemeri eke ase amachiko aito; etakeire omanye naki.

english: The cultivation of the Boindi Lotus flower, including its economic value, is supported by various research studies. It provides food for animals and humans alike, and its roots are edible. Moreover, the plant purifies the water, making it a valuable addition to the ecosystem.
ekegusii: Kwamia Lotus ya Boindi, ensemo enkong’u ya isiko nigo egosigikigwa ne risakara rikwara. Eye egwanchera amache aeta raisi naende onye tagoeta bo, ntetere tekomera. Korende, ekero ebekire ime y’amache, neire emiake mekeigo entetere emanye gokina.

english: More about the Boindi Lotus
ekegusii: Chintetere chikwama mono chia Lotus ya Boindi

english: Do you know how to propagate this plant successfully?
ekegusii: Naki okomanya ekero gwasigikiri entetere yaisaneire?

english: Many people don't know how to properly care for plants that have been planted in water. This type of plant requires special attention, especially during the first 24 hours, to ensure successful growth. If you haven't done so already, monitor the plant closely within the first 24 hours, and observe how it adapts. Monitor it regularly to maintain its health.
ekegusii: Omonto nabo akomanya ekero entetere yamerire ekero yabekirwe amche ime. Entetere eise gokina ebe kabere buna yare ase chinsa 24, togenderera gosigiki. Onye teraba bo, ogenderere gosigiki, irania entetere ase amache ime ase chinsa 24 chikobwatia, origererie buna eng’ani. Ogenderere bo goika entetere ebe kabere.

english: This plant needs water…
ekegusii: Entetere eganetie amache oka…

english: To grow well, the plant needs consistent moisture, meaning the water level should always be maintained. Maintain a temperature between 27°C and 28°C (even though some can tolerate temperatures around 20°C). At lower temperatures, the plant may grow slowly or become dormant. Refer to https://www.victoria-adventure.org/...om_seed.html for more information.
ekegusii: Ekero gwakorire gosigiki, ineka entetere ase echuba ebwate amache. Riberera riganerreiri asr amache ribe 27°C goika 28°C(nonye naende nabo ekomenta ase amache are riberera 20°C). ase riberera eri, chintetere echikomera bwanko chiakina ase echuma. Rora echibicha ase http://www.victoria-adventure.org/…om_seed.html

english: Also, use fertile soil rich in organic matter, mixing it with sand to improve drainage. The soil should be at least 30 centimeters deep. Don't mix it with fertilizer intended for the Boindi lotus.
ekegusii: Bwanko buna rito ritangani rikooroka, simeka entetere ekinete ase esike gose omochanga inse y’echuba. Amache agwenererete goika chisentimita 30 igoro y’omochanga. Nabo orabeke chinswe amo na lotus ya Boindi.

english: Generally, when the plant matures, it develops large leaves. Also, provide adequate sunlight, nutrients, and space for it to thrive. Maintain a temperature range of 20°C to 35°C for optimal growth of the Boindi lotus.
ekegusii: Ng’ora ng’ora, buna ekemeri kegokina, netake ribaga rinene. Nabo ogosimeka ase egesima ase egeticha, enyomba machani, gose ande onsi ase bokendu bonene botaiyo. Riberera rironge ri’ogosimeka lotus ya Boibdi igo ere gati ya 20°C na 35°C.

english: In terms of irrigation, regular watering is essential, and the plant thrives best in consistently moist conditions. This plant is also valued for its ecological benefits, contributing to environmental conservation, and its aesthetic appeal, resembling a water lily.
ekegusii: Ase eanga yaito, riberera ria inse erire mono korende ekemeri eke nabo gekwama bokong’u botaiyo. Ekero ki’omogaso nabo okoenia Lotus ya Boindi gochia egesima gia isiko, ekero ki’obokendu goika egachu nyomba. Ekero amang’ana abeire bobe mono, nabo ekong’anyigwa gochia ase abwate omoika bw’amache buna lily y’mache.

english: To encourage healthy growth of the Boindi lotus, use fertilizers containing nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium, applying approximately 60 to 80 grams per square meter every ten days. Use fertilizer that dissolves easily in water and mix it thoroughly with the soil before adding it to the pond. Avoid over-fertilizing, which can harm the plant.
ekegusii: Enchera endonke yokwami lotus ya Boindi n’ogotumia amagena akobwata kende korwa chirita chia amache 60 gose 80 chikoonogwa chiyuro 10 kera eyemo. Tumia enchera eyebeka chintetere chimerete ime y’esike ase gose omochanga ime y’enyongo y’amaoga omanye kobeka enyongo ime y’amagena. Konyora okwama okuya, ichoria amagena ayio n’amache.

english: The frequency of fertilization depends on the plant's condition and nutrient requirements. However, ensure that the Boindi lotus receives sufficient nutrients throughout its growing season. This plant also requires proper maintenance, including removing dead leaves and controlling pests.
ekegusii: Obuya bw’ogotumia amache nigo bore buna nabo okobeka ase egeticha ekero ki’obokendu gose nyomba mwao. Onye gokobeka nyomba, mbuya ekero obegete ang’e n’etirisa koenekia buna Lotus ya Boindi nkonyora ere omogaso omonge. Ekero ko’omogaso nabo okobeka ase ensemo ya maate nyomba gose geticha. Buna oroche Lotus ya Boindi nabo egosimekwa raisi- nonye nyomba ime.

english: Walking 10 km with burdens is tough!
ekegusii: Kogenda 10 km na amagoro kera rituko!

english: Stellah Nyayiemi also walks five kilometers to school daily. And when it rains, she struggles until she gets home. That journey is ten kilometers. Despite this, Stellah, 18, has excelled in her studies for four years, scoring an A- (minus) while at St Peter’s Suneka Secondary School, Kisii County.
ekegusii: Stellah Nyayiemi nigo are koboka rimaaambia echuni na gotara 5km gochia esukuru. Na kera rimorogoba, oayerera mbaka mwabo. Igo kera rituko nigo are gotara 10km. Nonya nabo igo, Stellah, 18, nigo akorete omokia aase amasomo aye na magega ye emiaka ene, akanyora A- (minus) korwa aaria St Peter’s Suneka Secondary School, Kisii County.

english: Moi University, we are coming. Our future chemical engineer. St. Peters Secondary School, Suneka, Kisii County star student, Stellah Nyayiemi. Picture with Joshua Araka, Gusii.com files.
ekegusii: Moi University, we are coming. Our future chemical engineer. St. Peters Secondary School, Suneka, Kisii County star student, Stellah Nyayiemi. Picture na Joshua Araka, Gusii.com files.

english: And because of the difficulty of that long journey to and from school, that journey became known as Stella's. People visiting her often praise Stellah for her great efforts in getting good grades so they can continue their education and succeed.
ekegusii: Na ekero yaigete rituko rie chisemi amo na okoegwa ebiegwa aase esukuru eyio, rituko nigo riaonchogete rikaba eria Stella. Omokwani gochia ase oyonde nigo bamotogia Stellah egekogera anene baria bakonyora egrade ekio nigo bagosoma chisukuru chinene ase bakomenya ime.

english: Stellah also faces challenges, including hunger, thirst, and poverty, yet she manages to get good grades despite being from Gusii. Because of the cost of education, the school requires a fee of Sh 50,000. Her parents have struggled to pay those fees due to their limited resources.
ekegusii: Stellah ere nigo aremereretie embeo, etintira, embura na obokendu na konyora e grade ekio getari gotoka Gusii mono. Ase engencho ya omokia oye, esukuru nigo yamoete epigipigi ya Sh 50,000. Boigo nabo anyorete ebiegwa ebinge korwa aase abageni ao ao.

english: Her mother, who supports her family, sacrificed greatly for them.
ekegusii: Omongina mama omwabo agasira kare kerasi isano ne emo

english: Stellah says she hopes to pursue a degree in Chemical Engineering at Moi University so she can help her father and support her mother who has sacrificed so much for them. "I thank God for everything. I wish I had scored an A plain so I could please God more," she told Gusii.com.
ekegusii: Stellah nigo agoteba buna ere nigo atagete gokora e degree in Chemical Engineering korwa aaria Moi University erio ache gokonya tata omwabo oyio omorendire korwa ekero mama omwabo asirete kare kerasi isano nemo. “Omonto nabo agoeta amatemwa korwa ande onsi. Nigo natagete konyora A plain korende nigo ingoakera Nyasae nga mbuya mono ase eki angete,” Nabo atebetie Gusii.com.

english: Thank you Dad for all your support. Stellah and her father during the academic excellence awards day at St. Peters Secondary School, Suneka, Kisii County yesterday. Picture with Joshua Araka, Gusii.com files.
ekegusii: Tari gotiga ise. "Thanks dad for all your support". Stellah amo na tata omwabo during the academic excellency awards day at St. Peters Secondary School, Suneka, Kisii County yesterday. Picture na Joshua Araka, Gusii.com files.

english: She attributed her success to hard work, group discussions, advice from her mother who told her to work hard and the desire to make her father proud. Her mother, Stella Nyayiemi, 69, has struggled to provide for her children so they can achieve their goals. Stellah is her only daughter.
ekegusii: She attributed her success to hard work, group discussions, advice from her mother who told her to work hard and the desire to make his father proud. Ise Stella, omogaka Nyayiemi, 69, nigo amosaberete amaya erinde asome erio ache gokonya enke yabo. Stellah nere ore omoke mwabo.

english: The school’s former principal, Mr. Godfrey Omoni who was praised for nurturing Stellah, said that if students work hard in their studies, they will achieve excellent results. Omoni, now heading Nyamagwa High School, said that Gusii people should strive for excellence.
ekegusii: The school’s former principal, Mr. Godfrey Omoni who got credited for molding Stellah nigo agoteba buna baria bakorwa inka kera emaambia nigo bagokora buya aase engencho bakonyora emechando. Omoni, now heading Nyamagwa High School nigo agoteba buna Gusii nabo ebwenerete gokora buya.

english: This is a good omen," Dr. Margaret Obaga
ekegusii: Kae chisemi ribaga", Dr. Margaret Obaga

english: “This is a sign of good things to come,” Omoni added. A lecturer from Daystar University, Dr Margaret Obaga, a prominent guest, congratulated the students saying this good omen indicates positive developments in the region.
ekegusii: “This is a sign of good things to come,” Nabo omosike Omoni atebete. A don from Daystar University, Dr Margaret Obaga, oyio orenge omogeni omonene nigo atebetie abaorokigwa bae chisemi ribaga baratiga emegoko emenge ya ense eye.

english: Another lecturer, Dr Samuel Ongoncho said that Stellah is a role model for other students. “We will get more Stellahs from this school. God bless that child,” Dr Ongoncho added.
ekegusii: Another don, Dr Samuel Ongoncho nigo atebete buna Stellah obeire omogwekano omuya ase abaana bande. “We will get more Stellahs korwa ase esukuru eye. Nyasae tiga asesenie omwana oyo,” Nabo Dr Ongoncho atebete.

english: And they cared. And they came in large numbers. On Saturday the 6th of November, 2010, people gathered to honor them. Relatives, friends and colleagues from America attended.
ekegusii: And they cared. And they came in large numbers. Rero Esabato chitariki 6 Egesunte (November), 2010, nigo bachicha ase obonge. Abairi, abaamate amo na abasani korwa Amerika engima.

english: We thank our Father God. Speeches were given by Bilha, Kinley and Ivyn
ekegusii: Naende imbuya mono Tata Nyasae. Speeches igoro ya Bilha, Kinley na Ivyn

english: The day went well. Former schoolmates, workmates, relatives and friends who had come to comfort them all gathered at Bradshaw Funeral Home, White Bear, Minnesota to remember Bilha Omare and her children, Kinley Ogendi and Ivyn Ogendi during their farewell.
ekegusii: Tari igo rioka. Former school mates, work mates, abarai ba kera aina amo na ababwatani korwa ase chikanisa ao ao nigo baichora aaria Bradshaw Funeral Home, White Bear, Minnesota ase ogoakera Bilha Omare amo na abana baye abanchwa, Kinley Ogendi and Ivyn Ogendi okwaheri.

english: Thank you very much Omonene for giving us an opportunity to know Bilha, Kinley and Ivyn. We thank our Father God for everything.
ekegusii: Gotera na gotogia Omonene for giving us an opportunity komanya Bilha, Kinley amo na Ivyn. Imbuya mono Tata Nyasae for everything.

english: It was a wonderful service. They brought great gifts to celebrate the life of Bilha and her children until this moment of leaving which reminded everyone of the love of our Lord Jesus Christ.
ekegusii: Nigo okorera kwarenge okonge. Nigo yarenge amagombo amanene korigereria chinka chia Bilha amo na abana baye impaka chingaki chio okoboka kwe rimambia ekero Omonene Yeso akoirana.

english: Those who knew them well remembered how kind they were. The singers sang non-stop. It was beautiful.
ekegusii: Omokwani ase kera omokwani nigo aimoka gokwana igoro ya marehemu. Nigo abange benyora bakorera nonstop. Amariga oka.

english: The service continued honoring the deceased. The singing was excellent
ekegusii: Korwa chinkwana igoro ya marehemu. Amariga nigo arenge amange

english: For all the efforts made in comforting, may they be rewarded for the tears shed throughout. The service was very touching from beginning to end.
ekegusii: Ase engaki yane yonsi yo oborisia, naborigwe gokwana ase emeyega emenge ye ebirero rakini tinanya korora abanto abange crying all through. Korwa omochakano impaka omoerio bwe e service.

english: The pain of losing Bilha and her children is immense and difficult to explain. Questions like “Why?” will never be answered except by our Father God. That is the truth.
ekegusii: Omogano bwo ogoitwa gwa Bilha na abana baye nigo ore omokongu ekiagera onde taiyo obwate an explanation. Amaborio inga "Why?" nigo tokoyatigera ase Omonene Tata Nyasae. Ase omosaraba bweka.

english: 4th tribute: City Of Vadnais Heights Mayor Sue Banovetz. "We have no words to thank the Mayor of Vadnais City and her community. She made it possible for the three bodies to be flown by Delta Airlines to New Jersey, free of charge, raised funds ($25,911.00), which covered the mortuary and coffin costs. And she went further to secure the venue, free of charge. We cannot forget mentioning her ability to mobilize the local community to attend the funeral service in large numbers. And yet she is determined to help start a fund for the surviving child, Savannah.” Mr. James Kinara, Vice Chairman, Mwanyagetinge.
ekegusii: 4th korwa okobee: City Of Vadnais Heights Mayor Sue Banovetz. "We have no words to thank the Mayor of Vadnais City and her community. She made it possible for the three bodies to be flown by Delta Airlines to New Jersey, free of charges, solicited for funds( $ 25,911.00), which cleared the Mortuary and coffins costs. And she went further to secure the Venue, free of charges. We cannot forget mentioning her ability to mobilize the local community to attend the funeral service in large numbers. And yet she is determined to help initiate a fund for the surviving child, Savannah." Mr. James Kinara, Vice Chairman, Mwanyagetinge.

english: Indeed the service was very well attended and many were touched. Those who hadn’t experienced such a thing before were changed.
ekegusii: Egento inkeri inga the service was very well attended naende kera oyomo nigo aba touched. Abande buna inche tari okorera gwoka twarera rakini nigo twaba transformed.

english: We sympathize with the family. We will surely continue to support the family in prayer. We pray that their journey back to New Jersey will be safe.
ekegusii: Intogotiga the family. We'll sure continue to lift the family to the throne of grace. We pray that their trip back to New Jersey will be safe.

english: “They left too soon.” Many felt that their lives were cut short
ekegusii: They left too soon." Kera oyomo ase ebirero nabo arenge goteba

english: Their memories remain. May Ivyn and Kinley rest in peace. Their children are also gone.
ekegusii: Amabera. Koa abagisangio babo, Ivyn na Kinley okwaheri. Abana barenge ase ebirero.

english: Many felt that their lives were cut short and said: “They left too soon.” We were all shocked by their passing. Farewell. We offer our condolences.
ekegusii: Kera oyomo orenge ase ebirero ebi nigo arera na goteba inga : "They left too soon." Bono nabo twatongetwe igo. Kwaheri. Timoka no omorembe.

english: With gratitude, our Father God alone knows the depth of sorrow we feel today. For now, let us not dwell on it.
ekegusii: Ase obwango, Omonene Nyasae nere bweka oratotebie igoro ya amangana amakongu buna aya. Impaka engaki eyio, tiga mosesenigwe.

english: Our esteemed people, we have been informed of sad news. University Lecturer, and presenter on Omoraria TV, Professor Joseph Nyasani has passed away. Professor Nyasani died yesterday morning at the Aga Khan Hospital, Nairobi while undergoing treatment starting on a date corresponding to January of this year. We were informed that Prof Nyasani was admitted to that hospital some time ago due to illness.
ekegusii: Mwanyagetinge ominto, twatebiigwe amangana amakong'u. University Lecturer, naende Omoraria bw' TV, Professor Joseph Nyasani osirire. Professor Nyasani nigo asirete igoro emaambia aaria ase enyagitari ya Agha Khan, Nairobi abwo ase konyora agendererete kobwenigwa koru etariki eyemo Engatiato [ January ] omwaka oyo. Nigo twatebigwa buna Prof Nyasani nigo airetwe ase enyagitari eyio ekero achagete korwara ase enkoro amo n' riini.

english: Professor Nyasani was born in 1936 in the location of Central Kitutu Chache. Later, Prof Nyasani went to study theology, then changed to study Philosophy. After completing his studies, Professor Joseph Nyasani became a Kenyan who tirelessly commented on issues of life and education in schools.
ekegusii: Professor Nyasani nigo aiboretwe ase omwaka o 1936 aaria ime ya Central Kitutu Chache. Ritangani, Prof Nyasani niogo atagete gosomera obosasiroti, korende agachaka gomsomera Philosophy. Goetera ase ogosoma kwaye, Professor Joseph Nyasani nigo arenge Omokenya ori orenge komenta abande omoyo ase ogokongia ase amosomo amo n' esukuru.

Professor Nyasani obtained an Arts degree from Urbaniana University, Rome (1963), a Diploma in Social Ethics from Woodstock College, Oxford in 1964, a PhD from The University of Cologne, Germany in 1969, and a Law Degree, New York University, School of Law in 1972.

Professor Nyasani nigo abwate Arts degree koru ase Urbaniana University, Rome (1963), Diploma in Social Ethics koru ase Woodstock College, Oxford ase omwaka o 1964, PhD koru ase The University of Cologne, Germany, ase omwaka o 1969, amo na Law Degree, New York University, School of Law ase omwaka o 1972.

english: In his career, Professor Nyasani worked at the United Nations Secretariat in New York as the Political Affairs Officer in the Department of Political and Security Council Affairs in 1971. Afterwards, Professor Nyasani became the Associate Professor at the City University of New York in 1973.
ekegusii: Ase ogokora emeremo, Professor Nyasani nigo akorete emeremo ase the United Nations Secretariat aaria New York buna the Political Affairs Officer ase the Department of Political and Security Council Affairs ase omwaka o 1971. Koru abwo, Professor Nyasani akaba the Associate Professor aaria ase the City University of New York ase omwaka o 1973.

english: As a commentator and analyst, Professor Nyasani was a presenter at the Voice of Germany (Deutsche Welle) in Cologne, Germany and the Voice of Kenya which is now KBC. Additionally, Professor Nyasani was a lecturer at The University of Nairobi from 1970 onwards.
ekegusii: Komenta na koba Omwoorokia, Professor Nyasani nigo arenge omoraria ase the Voice of Germany (Deutche Welle) aaria Cologne, Germany amo na Voice of Kenya eyio bono eye KBC. Ase boigo, Professor Nyasani nigo arenge omwoorokia ase The University of Nairobi koru ase omwaka o 1970 goikera bono.

english: In terms of positions held, Professor Nyasani was also the first chairman of the Council of the Kisii University from 2008 to 2013. Among the awards received during his studies, Professor Nyasani received the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation Fellowship and DAAD Foundation Scholarship in 1987 and 1992.
ekegusii: Ase emeremo emenge akorete, Professor Nyasani boigo nere orenge the first chairman of the Council of the Kisii University koru ase omwaka o 2008 to 2013. Gati y' ebieegwa b' ogosoma kw igo Professor Ntyasani aetwe nigo bire the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation Fellowship amo na DAAD Foundation Scholarship gati y' omwaka o 1987 and 1992.

english: Gusii.com sends condolences to relatives, friends, colleagues and family members of the son of Kenyans, Professor Joseph Nyasani. May he rest in peace under the grace of God Tata Nyasae.
ekegusii: Gusii.com nigo tokoru engora gochia ase abamwabo, abasani, abairi amo n' abaamate ba omwana bw' Abakenya, Professor Joseph Nyasani. Kera egento ase Omonene Tata Nyasae.

english: The fruit of Kalimantan (Mangifera casturi) is commonly known as Kasturi, a round fruit that belongs to the cashew family and grows around 10–30 years old, found in areas like Banjaramasin and Borneo Island (Indonesia). Its wood is used for making various tools and furniture. Currently, this tree is cultivated because its fruits are delicious.
ekegusii: Riembe ria Kalimantan (Mangifera casturi) rimanyire buna Kasturi srire rotunda rie chitripiki ang’e chimita 10–30 ase obotambe erigotoka ase asinine ase akorokwa Banjarmasin ase Borneo ya maate (Indonesia). Amatuko aya riasire gosira ekiagera rikonachwa mono. Korende, nabo rikonya gosimekwa aiga asengencho y’amatunda aye agwansa.

english: Kalimantan mango (Mangifera casturi) trees are large and produce fruits similar to ordinary mangoes. The height can reach 50 to 84 meters. It flowers twice a year – flowering – which yields fruit approximately six months later, resulting in abundant harvests. The skin color is yellowish. To improve the quality of the fruit of M. Casturi, grafting techniques are employed. Several varieties of Mangifera casturi - Kasturi, Cuban Mango and Pelipisan - are recognized. Kasturi is widely cultivated for its sweet taste. Cuban Mango and Pelipisan are also known as superior varieties. Pelipisan is considered a good type of mango similar to Kasturi, which is often sold as Kasturi mango. This origin has been extensively researched.
ekegusii: Okoren’gana kwe riembe ria Kalimantan (Mangifera casturi) nkori konene mono ekero okoreng’ania n’amatunda ande ye chimbego chia amaembe. Oborito bwaye ebore ang’e chigiramu 50 goika 84. Ekero ritaratoba, nigo rire machani – ekero riatobire – erangi yaye ere maraba gose gochia bure-emwamu naende ribwate risabo rikomesa. Gocherera erangi ya buru. Ogoonchoreria chirangi oko nakwo gokomanyia igoro y’amatunda a M. Casturi. Chikabira isato chia Mangifera casturi- Kasturi,Mangga Cuban na Pelipisan. Erimanyire mono Kasturi eseng’encho ye rimisu riaye. Mangga Cuban na Pelipisan nigo akororwa buna chimbego ching’ao. Pelipisan nigo ribwate rimisu rigiya buna Kasturi eyio ekoorokia buna erirwete korwa Kasturi. Oborigia obonge mbogendererete korimanya mono.

english: The flesh of the fruit is yellow and slightly sour, with a unique aroma and flavor. Kasturi is related to mango (Mangifera indica), but it differs significantly in terms of shape and texture. The roundness of the Kasturi fruit resembles an emerald green color.
ekegusii: Ime ye ritunda eri nigo rikomachia koarira ase erangi naende rikwara akeigo ne rimisu riansu. Etokobwekani Kasturi me riembe(Mangifera indica),kasturi ndiri gwansa mono rakini ndibwate obwansu obokong’u ne rimisu rikeigo. Ime ye rotunda ria Kasturi eribwate emerande emenge emiya.

english: Kasturi is loved by the people of Borneo Island who give it a special name. Its fragrance is said to be reminiscent of the following phrase: "As fragrant as Kasturi, as beautiful as a rainbow, everything begins." They comment, "Oh, the good mango of Kasturi, truly a delightful mango. The sweetness is unparalleled.
ekegusii: Kasturi erianchire mono ase abanto ba Borneo ya maate am one chiamate chiabo. Rimisu riaye erikogokia goika ogotera ogokoro gokarosigwa igoro yaye “Seharum kasturi, seindah pelangi, semuanya bermula.” komineti “O, rimisu rigiya buna Kasturi, rigiya mono buna omokobi nyongo. Obwanchani obo bwachakire esabari.”

english: In conclusion, further research is needed to understand the potential benefits of this fruit. Research on Kalimantan mangoes shows promise for future studies regarding their nutritional value and economic impact. This research is being conducted by researchers and communities after previous efforts were unsuccessful.
ekegusii: Okonacha kw’emete gotaancheri kwagerire omote oyo ngosira okare korwa orosana. Emete emekoro y’amaembe a Kalimantan igo arasire korwa okonacha gotaancheri ekiagere emete yabo ekorwa emenge naende emiya. Emete eye egosimekwa ase ake ake ase emechi ya abanto nyuma y’ebiticha biabo gose emegondo yabo emeke.

english: Kalimantan mangoes are widely grown throughout Indonesia, especially in tropical regions where they thrive. The vast lands of Kalimantan are suitable for growing these mangoes due to the fertile soil and favorable climate (the fertile soil of Kalimantan is also known as the soil of Banjaramasin). People from Mataraman began cultivating them in the 1980s, and production increased significantly around 2005. However, this round fruit is still relatively unknown to many people.
ekegusii: Riembe ria Kalimantan ndiri gosimekwa ase emegondo emenene gose ase obonge ime ya Indonesia buna amatunda ande agosimekwa ase chitropiki ekiagera akwama ng’ora. Emegondo emenene ya Kalimantani nigo ekoratoka ase ensemo enke ya Banjar (ensemo enke ya Banjar teri eyemo buna ensemo enke ya Banjarmasin). Abanto ba Mataraman mbatemete gosimeka ase emegondo emeke ase omwaka o 1980 korende rigesa ritang’ani eriarenge omwaka o 2005. Nonye rotunda eri rigotoka ase oboraisi, teri goisaneki banto ekiagere rianchire mono.

english: The quality of the fruit depends on its origin. Moreover, the people of Banjar (who are often referred to as the inhabitants of Borneo Island) utilize the mangoes to create various products for sale. Therefore, the people of Banjar use these mangoes to make diverse items. Remember that mango trees provide shade which makes the area cool and comfortable - mangoes fall without causing harm.
ekegusii: Amatumisi y’amatunda n’omote nigo are amake. Nonye emete emekoro kegotwara ritina rietaneti emita eyemo, abanto ba Banjar (egesaku ki’abanto baime na ab’enyancha batorete Borneo ya maate) ebagotumia amatunda oka akiagera omote oye okwama egeka. Eseigo, abanto ba Banjar nigo bagotumia emete emeng’ao gokora ebinto binde. Konyora amatunda nkori raisi ekiagere omote o Kasturi nigo okwama oba omotambe mono naende goika omonto arine ase anene mono konyoikera – amatunda akogwa inse tari amaya mono.

english: These mangoes are also processed into various snacks and preserved foods. It's said that those who taste the deliciousness of these mangoes will always remember them fondly. Various products are made from mangoes such as chips, preserves, sweets, and pickles (pickles made by elders). These products and others are derived from these mangoes and are enjoyed by the people of Banjar. These mangoes have great significance for the people of Banjar, contributing to their economy and prosperity.
ekegusii: Amatunda aya nabo akoriegwa amatobu gose arosiri buna echamu. Tari koonigwa mono ase chichiro ekiagera abaremi abanyene nigo bakonyaria ataraika chichiro. Ebinto binde bikorosigwa korwa ase amaembe nigo are chipurii,chichamu, echuisi, gose obosuguti (ebisuguti bi’abakoro). Ebinto ebi korende ebire ebikong’u gotoka ekiagera amatunda aya akoriegwa mono naende anchire mono n’abanto ba Banjar. Amatunda aya naende are rigori rinene korende ase abanto ba Banjar, mbari gpkumia ekiagera y’obwansu obonene.

english: People who steal and are bad. This is very important. Stealing is what destroys a home. Last week, Nyamira Gov. John Nyagarama spoke about this with reporters from Daily Nation. Because of the increasing problems, Governor Nyagarama said that the Gusii people should unite and work together, because of the many people who suffer.
ekegusii: Abaminto amakweri n' amabe. Tari koyiera. Amakweri nigo agochera onde bwensi. Ewiki eye yaera, Nyamira Gov. John Nyagarama natwara egambo amo n' abariki ba Daily Nation. Gati y' amang'ana akwanete, Governor Nyagarama nigo atebete buna Abagusii tiga torengererie na korigia obong'aini, kobwatekana n' ogotindeka baria baminto basirire.

english: It is only fair: Don't educate a child of Gusii, let him learn five customs, so his children can know everything, Kenya animals. Armstrong Atlantic State University, Savannah, Georgia, United States. Photo by Jared Nyaberi, Mwanyagetinge.com files.
ekegusii: It is only fair: Tiga kera omwana Omogusii, asomigwe ase amatuko atano, buna abana be ebisaku binde bionsi, Kenya engima. Armstrong Atlantic State University, Savannah, Georgia, United States. Photo na Jared Nyaberi, Mwanyagetinge.com files.

english: He also said that the tradition of taking gifts to the homes of the six clans, improving them, and giving them various items, is good education for schools. In those clans, the Gusii did not want to leave their homes, saying that they would not be allowed to take gifts to the homes of those clans, in this era.
ekegusii: Nigo atebete buna chinchera chiato chi' ogotwara ebirero ase amatuko a Tichi Gatano, chiagerire, gati ye ebinto binde ebinge, koiyeria amasomo ase chisukuru. Ase amatuko amake aetire, Abagusii titwabwate gochika konde gwensi, kogoteba buna nigo tobwenerete gotwara emegeya yaito y' ebirero, ase amatuko gete y' ewiki.

english: In the past, since 1985, people used to say that gifts were given on Saturday. Many leaders of the area came forward, such as Bobasi, saying that they would come to church on that day, like students.
ekegusii: Ase omobwekano, ekero tata sirete back in 1985, omoyega bw' ebirero nigo obete ase rituko rie Esabato. Nigo abagaka abanene b' ekenyoro giaito, aaria nka Bobasi batebete buna nigo ere buya gotwara ekanisa rituko erio, nka seito.

english: Many leaders of the time, such as the late Mishael Mosoti, the late Zedekiah Ochenge, the late Nyamugutu Siocha, and others, showed great respect. The church and the gifts were on that Saturday, like students.
ekegusii: Abagaka abanene ba amasikani buna marehemu Mishael Mosoti, marehemu Zedekiah Ochenge, marehemu Nyamugutu Siocha, amo na abatata moke abange, nabwo barwete obosemia obo. Ekanisa amo n' ebirero bikaba rituko erio rie Esabato, nka seito.

english: People who are Gusii don't forget this matter
ekegusii: Baminto tiga Abagusii torigererie eng'ana eye

english: Why does Governor John Nyagarama continue to talk about this issue? The Governor said:
ekegusii: Bono ninki gekogera Governor John Nyagarama atagete togayane igoro ye eng'ana eye? Nigo Governor agoteba buna:

english: [I]. Children shouldn't be taken to learn the customs of the six clans during school days, and teachers should go to homes while the children are suffering.
ekegusii: [I}. Abana tibari gotwara amasomo ase amatuko a Tichi Gatano ase engencho rituko erio, nario abarimu bakogenda ebirero ekero abamwabo basirire.

english: {II]. Also, Governor Nyagarama said that every school should teach lessons, about the importance of gifts given to schools on that day.
ekegusii: {II]. Ase boigo, Governor Nyagarama nigo atebete buna chisukuru chinyinge tichiri gotwara amasomo, ase eng'encho emeyega ye ebirero ekobera ase chisukuru ase rituko erio.

english: Because of these words, Gov Nyagarama said he will also try to give gifts to the homes of the clans on weekends. Furthermore, people should go to church on Saturdays, and take the importance of gifts on Sunday. Also, if people go to church on Sunday, they should take the importance of gifts on Saturday.
ekegusii: Kobwatekana n' egambo eye, Gov Nyagarama nigo agoteba buna nigo ere buya tokore ebirero biaito ase amatuko y' chiwikendi. Ase enchera ende, baria baminto tokogenda ekanisa ase rituko rie Esabato, totware emeyega ye ebirero ase rituko ri Omokubio. Ase boigo, nabaria baminto tokogenda ekanisa ase rituko rio Omokubio, totware emeyega ye' ebirero ase rituko rie Esabato.

english: Children of Gusii, they don't want to study, and when they are educated, many children, Kenya animals.
ekegusii: Abana ba Gusii, nigo batagete gosoma, na gosomigwa buna abana bande bonsi, Kenya engima

english: Governor Nyagarama said this, stating that the Gusii should not stop working hard, and those children should also be encouraged to study the five customs of this world. Also, teachers should remember, and do their job in the five clans, so they can show the customs of the five clans of this world.
ekegusii: Governor Nyagarama nigo atebete aya, ase okwegena buna Abagusii toise gokora igo, abana baito nabo baragenderere gosomigwa ase amatuko atano ase ewiki. Ase boigo, abarimu nabarabwo nenyarekane, bakore emeremo yabo ase amatuko atano, ekiagera nigo bagoakanwa eng'eria y' amatuko atano ase ewiki.

english: Some parents complain that Gusii doesn't have enough resources, and they won't work hard again. Also, they should understand that if those children stay in school, which is the culture of Gusii, they will work hard and succeed.
ekegusii: Abarai abange bakwaneire igoro yo obokongu tobwate Gusii, naende buna totari gokora amatemwa buya. Ase boigo, nabo ekororekana buna ekero abana baito bachire ase chisukuru chire isiko ya Gusii, nigo bagokora buya mono ase chisemi.

english: We don't know why we don't appreciate this good thing. Yes. We don't know why we don't value this initiative of Governor Nyagarama, because it helps the Gusii, develop education like a true Gusii.
ekegusii: Ntwe titori goteba buna tiga toonchorerie chinchera chiato bono iga. Yaya. Nigo togoteba buna, tiga twensi torigererie enkwana eye ya Governor Nyagarama, gose nebe eyemo y' chinchera chio ogotokonya ntwe Abagusii, gokinia chisemi nka seito Gusii.

english: Let teachers, leaders, and all those children value this initiative, and cooperate. Thank you very much.
ekegusii: Tiga abarimu, abaibori, amo na abarai baito bonsi barigererie enkwana eye, na koyegayana. Mbuya mono.

english: Whoever investigates this matter and finds out that someone has been stealing things, let them report it quickly. Also, whoever investigates and discovers someone causing trouble, let them reveal those who are involved in wrongdoing. Anyone who confesses will be forgiven if they admit their mistakes and seek reconciliation with others.
ekegusii: Onye gokagete buna oyo no omogano igoro buna seito tware konywa erongongori etainekiri, kana koganya. Gose onye gokagete ngogotebia nde buna seito tware gokama chingoko, kana gokenderera agwo ekiiriri kio omotembe. Tindi gwatora bobisi buna seito tware gokama chingoko ekero oboremo bwabete chincherere totabwate ase nonya n’ embori okoriisia.

english: This matter concerns a thief who steals valuable items, so let us work together to find him and bring him to justice. That thief is known as Mogaka. Many evenings he spends time wandering around, visiting homes and interacting with people. (This story is true, witnessed by many reliable individuals.) Let us unite and cooperate so that children can grow up well and become responsible citizens. This person, who is difficult to understand, is often referred to as "Mosaiga.
ekegusii: Oyo no omogano bw' omogaka oyomo obwate chisemi, korende ekero twarenge abana nigo tware komosekerera. Omogaka oyio nigo are korokwa Mogaka. Magoroba iga ko omobaso okendire nigo agaterekire ebusaa yo obori na abasani baye. (Tari eye ye chibando rero nonya na abaisia abasiniini bakonywa). Kobasiibire ekegara ne chinkore bakonakoererania buna abana ba ng’ina omo, nigo bagaterire emeino emiya. Oyo nanchente ginkonakobategerera nigo orenge korokwa “Mosaiga.”

english: It happened a long time ago when Americans discovered secrets and mysteries. To write a mystery novel requires skill and creativity, especially when dealing with complex characters. However, sometimes the truth is hidden within simple details and can only be revealed through careful observation. And even though it may seem impossible, anyone can achieve success if they persevere and dedicate themselves to their goals.
ekegusii: Gaki tiga mbatebie buna Abamerika nigo banchete chisese ne ebimoni mono. Okonyora ekemoni keroseirie nyomba kemenyete buya, nonya mbeba nchiyo kebwenerete goita. Endagera nigo gekogorerwa enga ebisuguti kiabekerwa na amabere. Nonya nase gekobeka echabu go kiabutiarire nigo kebwate abanyene bana goitora.

english: And indeed, that is what happened. The story unfolded gradually. A television program featured interviews with various people. The American story was presented as being similar to the Kenyan situation, but it was ultimately different. The American meat industry is very competitive. Remember how Ondieki once struggled financially but eventually prospered, overcoming numerous obstacles. Regarding the American novel, the American story is considered a unique and exceptional piece of literature.
ekegusii: Ne esese nero nigo yanchire mono. Emenyete nyomba, egoikaransa esoba seti igoro yarigereria etelebiseni na abanyene. Esese ya Amerika oise konyereta seito Kenya nigo erakwe bwango mono. Nyama mbese sese ya Amerika terikoria. Tenga buna Ondieki yaito yakaminyokirie egesusu gose egechure yabwata twaria, twanyea amauga. Buna ekemoni kia Amerika, esese ya Amerika nigo ekoroserigwa endagera special ekogorwa korwa etuka.

english: We have heard enough, fellow Gusii people, let us focus on important matters. Americans and their allies continue to engage in conflicts and wars, seeking dominance over everything, including stories and novels. These conflicts often lead to discoveries of secrets and mysteries, which are then exploited for personal gain. The consequences of these conflicts are devastating, leaving behind destruction and suffering.
ekegusii: Tiga bono naende, Omogusii ominto, ngotebie egento kende kiamaseko. Abamerika naende nkoratwara bare amasindano korora buna ning’o obwate esese gose ekemoni egeseera. Amasindano ayio ataraika nigo bakoira chisese ne ebimoni baakana chibesa biasibigwa na konintwa chinchara. Omobui bwa amasindano nigo akoegwa egekombe buna keria abagosoria bakoeegwa.

english: However, despite these challenges, there is still hope. Remember our ancestors, Nyaituga and his father. They valued honesty and integrity above all else.
ekegusii: Maene pi ndie esese, tindigokong’aina, Nyaituga o baba. Boria onde bwensi omenyete mache ng’umbu.

english: Secrets and mysteries cause problems for Americans; they don't know where to begin. They search for clues in both mysteries and secrets. It is said that an American citizen spent $4,000 (Ksh. 300,000) to bury a secret deeply.
ekegusii: Chisese ne ebimoni kobiarwarire Abamerika tibari gotiga bikwe. Nigo bakobiira chinyagetari chi ebimoni ne chisese. Nimanyete Omoamerika oyomo oakanete $4,000 (Ksh. 300,000) kobaara esese endwaire.

english: The secret continued to spread, leading them to give it a name, "Putting it to sleep" - they buried the evidence. Later, another person was also buried, Pet Cemetery, a place filled with secrets, mysteries, and the remains of Americans who had passed away. Burying something allows people to forget and move on, but it doesn't erase the past.
ekegusii: Esese koyangire kobwena nigo bagokora egento gekorokwa, “Putting it to sleep” – bakonyebeta esindani yakwa ng’ooora. Koyakuure, banyeira ase akorokwa, Pet Cemetery, ase chimbeera chie chisese, ebimoni, ne ching’iti chinde Abamerika batugete nyomba chigotindekwa. Kobanyetindekire nigo bachachana na gwechwanachania buna omoibori okwereirwe no omwana.

english: The secret itself, the novel itself.
ekegusii: Esese isiko, ekemoni nyomba.

ekegusii: --omoerio--

english: People, let us not forget our roots, so that we may be honored among the children of Omogusii, lest you forget your heritage which is very important. This heritage belongs to both Abagetutu and Abanyaribari and their descendants! Who is this elder then? He is Elder Onyangore.
ekegusii: Baminto, totaragenda aare, nigo twatebetigwe buna ase abana b' Omogusii, tiga toinyore egento ekemo ekenene mono. Egento ekio nkeri nga ise Abagetutu amo na Abanyaribari n' oyomo! Bono omogaka oyio nere ng'o? Oyio nere omogaka Onyangore.

english: The people of Nyaribari are the owners of Omogusii land where they settled. From Boigo, the leaders of Nyaribari and those who came with them spread the Gusii nation throughout the surrounding areas. Below: A picture of a homestead in Kiogoro, Nyaribari Chache.
ekegusii: Omonyaribari nere obagete Omogusii bwensi ase abeta. Ase Boigo, abagambi korwa Nyaribari nabwo babarete Abagusii bonsi ase omobaro bw' ritangani. Below: Goaka chitiero aaria Kiogoro, Nyaribari Chache.

english: Onyangore belongs to both Omogetutu and Abanyaribari. According to stories passed down, Omogetutu was given authority over the land because he had a child who was born prematurely. That child could not breastfeed until he reached an age where he could drink from a horn. Once he drank from the horn, he began to grow strong and became a leader of the entire Getutu clan of Nyakundi.
ekegusii: Onyangore nere ise Omogetutu amo n' Omonyaribari. Aase okoinyora naende, Omogetutu nigo aiboretwe korwa ase omosubati otabwate mwana momura. Omosubati oyo otarenge konyora bana nigo arigeti enyaroka akayenywoma. Ke enyaroka eye yanywomwa, ekaibora omwana oyio obisetu nyomba akarokwa Mogetutu gose Nyakundi.

english: Therefore, both Abagetutu and Abanyaribari are descendants of Elder Onyangore. What characteristic of Nyaribari is known everywhere:
ekegusii: Igo Abagetutu amo na Abanyaribari nigo bare basinto b' omogaka Onyangore. Bono chinyomba chire Nyaribari nigo chire buna ekobwatia:

english: Hey! We Gusii people, we have this story about a doctor who treats many people and heals them quickly. Who are these people? They will be healed.

english: The doctor is called Mang'ana Ntuboka, Mogayani Obora. Let us praise Yaikaransa who heals with strength and power. Strength and power heal people, “Will you forgive the sins of our fathers and their mistakes?” Mistakes happen due to years of wrongdoing. The medicine man refuses to reveal the secret of Roche to those who don’t respect him.
ekegusii: Nigo sokoro antebia buna Mang'ana Ntuboka, Mogayani Obora. Tureti Yaikaransa Yatebia Keore Na Ombere Omwabo Konya Bwango Gose Masio Are Korigererania. Keore N' Ombere Omwabo Batebia Banyene, "Komwangire Bagambi Bw’Abanto Na Gucha Mwayesinya?" Gucha Ngaasama Nkagayana Kina Kia Miaka Amechinini. Mokonywa Oteba Kogwankonyire Bogima Bwa Roche A Gucha Nainche Mboremo Nyakebuna Ndakoe.

english: Below: It doesn’t matter. Let us say he touched his hands three times, and they were completely cured. The great doctors said, “Aaaa tooooooo!!!!..These are powerful medicines!!” and rejoiced greatly. It happened that Keore and Ombere, they went to a place, and they found people suffering greatly.
ekegusii: Below: Onde tatigareti. Etureti nigo yaimogetie emekono igoro, egateba ng'a yaaachire. Abagaka abanene b' etureti nigo batebete nga "Aaaa tooooooo!!!!..Aya n' amakong'u!!" na koirana chinsobo. Nigo kiabete buna tiga Keore N' Ombere omwabo, bagayane ekina eke, egekogera aba mbachiete nguma.

english: Many days passed. The doctor then realized that things were happening slowly, and people were getting tired. Many of those who got tired gave up. They were told to persevere, continue working hard. This time the case was serious, Okeore and Ombere asked them to confess. What now? It seems those who get tired give up easily and refuse to finish the work.
ekegusii: Baminto igwa bono. Nigo omogaka sokoro antebetie buna abwo kare kare, abanto babere mbarengeo. Bono aba babere nigo barenge kobuna oboremo. Bakagambigwa igo, korende mbaigwana. Bono etureti kiyasinywaaa, ekaereri Okeore n' Ombere omwabo bakegambe. Ase ki? Ekiagera aba babere nabwo bachiete nguma kogayana ebina biri biare gosinya etureti.

english: Continue listening.
ekegusii: Korende aye tegerera.

english: Continuing to rejoice, those who were wronged were healed!! These days the great doctors and those involved in the case said, “Why are these people being forgiven, why aren’t our fathers and Egucha forgiving them?”
ekegusii: Kogenderera kogayana, aba nabarabwo bagasinywa !! Bono erio nario abagaka abanene amo n' etureti batebete buna onye aba basinyirwe, gokonywa n’ abanto n’ Egucha nero nebasinye?

english: Mang'ana’s medicines are used by the doctors. Examine the tools of the doctors.
ekegusii: Amang'ana amakong'u korwa ase abagaka. Tochaya enkwana y' abagaka.

ekegusii: Bono naki omogaka oria aayerera iga?

ekegusii: Obwango obwo obwo, abagaka babere bakarwa ase obosio bwabo. Omogaka omotang’ani akaayerera. Naki aayerera iga? Noria otigarete, nere akabwatia korwa magega. Omogaka omotang’ani agachia kwamboka oroche rw’ Egucha, akagwa iime.

english: However, sometimes things happen unexpectedly, and the doctor takes a long time to heal. The doctor should hurry and find a solution, otherwise he will ruin everything! This time it happens again, and he falls down while trying to help them with Egucha.
ekegusii: Nonya nabo igo, egobia abegete egacheng’enena amache igoro. Omogaka oria otigarete magega nere gachia goika ase oroche oro, akarora egobia y’ omogaka oria otang’aine gecheng’eneine roche igoro! Bono ogakare korengereria buna kero kende, nigo agwa roche iime gakwamboka abwo ase Egucha.

english: Sometimes they start with a problem, and they cry because Egucha has failed. Quickly, Egucha wakes up and starts shouting loudly!!
ekegusii: Ogakare gotiira ase obwango, amaene akanyora buna nigo egucha yamoirete. Keri keri, agaaka Egucha eye ime na komorusia aroro !!

english: That place........I remember everything well, and I understand.....
ekegusii: Oboremo oobwo........Nagotigeire bono gose noisaneke, na gontiga.....

english: Shouting loudly there, they say I remember that place, especially!
ekegusii: Kamorusia aaiga nario atebete buna omotigeire oboremo, nyakebuna!

This thing however, Omansamu stayed thinking about how he would help Ogasusu and make sure he doesn't forget, always remembering that he forgot the place and the secret within it.

ekegusii: Tabia mbaya. Bono Ogasusu oyio ekiage ime, koinagera na gokung'unta endagera yonsi pi

ekegusii: Omansamu gakirete iga, akaigwa omonto ogosensera. Ogochia gosiomia, akarora buna agochoba gochia ase ekiage kiare na gosoa ekiage eke ime. keri keri, Omansamu akaigwa Ogasusu okare gochoba ngora ngora.

english: Omansamu escaped and started to worry about the animal and the place and he tried to convince Ogasusu to return and work together and never forget to cooperate and not steal the place and the secret within it which is beautiful and valuable.
ekegusii: Omansamu akaminyoka na gotenena ase engoro eye igoro erinde akaganya Ogasusu asoke erinde amokorere aya atianete komokorera erinde nario atache airore koiba endagera ye ching'iti chinde konye chiachire chiarigiri na kogacha ekiage ime erinde chiche koria ekero ki'omorakera n' enchara.

english: Ogasusu was surprised when he woke up to see the animal and the place that had captured his attention. This Ogasusu remembered how he wanted to build a strong foundation and always run away.
ekegusii: Ogasusu agasinywa buna agosoka korwa ase engoro eye ime ekiagera engoro eye yabwate ase omong'anyi omong'ao. Bono ogasusu akarora buna goika arigie obokora boramokonye erinde asoke korwa aaiga.

english: Ogasusu is smart!
ekegusii: Ogasusu ngoita are obongo!

english: And so, Omansamu decided to bring his people. This Ogasusu used his intelligence, he remembered something important. Forget that Omansamu asked Ogasusu to return to work on the animal and the place, and forget that those things were lost. Work on the place, Ogasusu will start to feel comfortable, because he is now able to create something new.
ekegusii: Ase boigo, Omansamu tanyara komobwata. Bono Ogasusu agaita obongo igo, goikera akanyora richibu. Inyora buna konye Omansamu okembire ogasusu asoke korwa engoro eye ase egeka getari geke, na konye bono enchara yamorire. Korwa engoro ime, Ogasusu agachaka goaka omonu, buna ori okare koria egento egetonontu.

english: When he returned, Omansamu asked him why he ran away, “Why Ogasusu did you run away and leave me here? I have nothing left and my things are gone!” Ogasusu when he returned, he laughed and began to explain to Omansamu that “Your eyes are deceiving you, you don’t understand what I mean, look closely at me.”
ekegusii: Koigwa iga, Omansamu nere ogakare goaka omonu okobora, "Yaa Ogasusu naki okare koragera aye bweka iga? Gaki ndomi geke nainche enchara yanyarire?" Ogasusu koigwa iga, akagoka na gosasoka na ogakare gotebia Omansamu buna "Egento eke kegotonontera buuya, onye gotagete nkoromi naye orie geke, togoria amaiso nkoe bono

english: This Omansamu who looked closely!
ekegusii: Bono Omansamu oyio ogotogoria amaiso!

english: So then Omansamu refused and didn’t want to listen, he turned away and looked at another place. Then Ogasusu remembered that Omansamu was looking at another place, he showed him the truth and revealed to Omansamu the truth about that place!
ekegusii: Bono buna Omansamu arenge n' enchara, akaigwera na gotogoria amaiso gochia igoro. Bono Ogasusu korora buna Omansamu otogoiri amaiso, akaiomokia amaraba na gosiarera Omansamu amaraba aya gochia ase amaiso ime!

english: So this is amazing!
ekegusii: Bono kai tata!

english: Omansamu started to open his eyes and understand. Slowly slowly, Ogasusu realized his mistake, he regretted working on the animal and the place and stopped, he was tired. Omansamu remained alone in confusion. He saw Ogasusu leaving quickly and going away.
ekegusii: Omansamu agachaka komiga amaiso gakorera. Erio erio, nario Ogasusu anyorete ribaga, akaminchoria korwa ase engoro eye ime na kominchoka, agaaka embuna, tabwatwa. Omansamu agatigara kare n' obororo obonge. Nere Ogasusu agatama na korwa erio, akang'anya korwa aaiga na kogenda orwao.

english: The Bird and the Snake
ekegusii: Engoko Ne’Kebaki

english: Wiehan de Jager
ekegusii: Wiehan de Jager

english: My father, the bird and the snake they often meet together with all kinds of birds. They always look for their own things.
ekegusii: Abwo kare, engoko ne'kebaki nigo bamenyete amo nomorembe nechinyoni chionsi pi. Nigo barenge gokora ebinto biabo amo.

english: When it rains, the ground becomes slippery. The snake crawls very slowly on the ground. It moves carefully. “Come quickly so that we can both escape from this place,” said the snake.
ekegusii: Rituko erimo, enchara egacha ase ense. Ekebaki kegatara are sana korigia endagera. Gekairana kerosete sana. "Goika kobe neng'encho ende engusu gotara." ekebaki kegateba.

english: They were planning to steal eggs from another village, the bird was thinking about flying away. It feared being caught by the owner of the birds when they approached the coop. “Don’t let us be seen while approaching those eggs, otherwise we will be caught,” it said.
ekegusii: Ekero babogete korwa chitoro chingiya, engoko ekaba nokogania okuya. Egachaka koarigania amarionya yechinyoni chiria chionsi konyora chiakure. "Tiga toyasone amo igoro yamarionya aya aito are mobere. Nabo eyio eragere ogotara gwaito kobe okogusu.

english: It was then that the snake suddenly remembered an old story about a certain person who had been punished. It started to explain how people used to punish others in the past, and it reminded the bird of its own bad deeds.
ekegusii: Ekaba buna ekebaki keria nakio gioka kiabwate esindani yogosona, igo kegatang'ana gochaka gwesonera amarionya mobere oye Ake igo gekanyara gotambururuka are nechimbaba ibere, kegatiga engoko eria nse garia.

english: The person who had wronged someone had been forced to carry stones until he was exhausted, and the bird remembered his own mistakes. He regretted the snake’s actions and the harm caused to others. But the bird flew off anyway.
ekegusii: Engoko eria ekarosa gosona egatiga esindani eria igoro yekabati nakogenda riko koroseria abana baye endagera. Rakini chinyoni chiria chinde konyora chiarorire ekabaki keria gekoiruruka are. Chikaboria engoko echikonye n'esindani eria erinde chirosie chimbaba chiabo nachirochio. Nabwo abwo chinyoni chiria chikairuruka igoro ase rire.

english: When the other birds saw the beautiful bird flying towards the coop, the snake tried to stop him, but it was too late. It began to dig holes around the coop hoping to find some eggs. But it found nothing there.
ekegusii: Ekero enyoni eria yomoiso yairanatie esindani eria yasabete, engoko eria tiyarengeoo, konyora yasokire ake. Igo ebichuchu biengoko eria bikaira esindani eria bigachaka gochiesa nero. Ekero biarosete nomochieso oria, bigatiga esindani eria ase amaraba ime.

english: Those who seek evil things will find themselves digging holes everywhere, and they will not find what they are looking for. Those who plan evil things will find themselves facing difficulties.
ekegusii: Emarogoba eyio, ekebaki gekairana. Gekaboria esindani eria erinde kenyare gosonerera amarionya konyora achakire korua ekero ki'orogendo rwaye. Engoko eria ekarigererIa ekabati igoro. Ekarigia chikoni, isiko keorori, gotatiga teyenyoreti sindani eria.

english: The snake felt ashamed and regretted his actions. It remembered the holes he had dug searching for eggs and realized he had wasted his time. The bird who had flown away was already far gone.
ekegusii: Gaki ing'a rituko erimo rioka inkorigerie esindani," Engoko ekaebereria ekebaki. Erinde onyare gosonerera amarionya ao nakonyara kaoiruruka korigia endagera yende.

english: “What kind of rain is this that makes it difficult to dig?” the snake complained to himself. He regretted having angered the owner of the birds and fearing being caught on the ground.
ekegusii: Ero bono nakoire rituko erimo rioka, "ekebaki kegateba. "Inyore timokonyora sindani eyio, goika ong'akane n'egechuchu kiao ekemo." Ekero ekebaki giachete rituko rikobwatia, gekanyora engoko eria kegendererete gokura nse ase omochanga okoba sindani tiyarenge kororekana ande. Igo ekebaki kegaika nse bwango gekabogoria egechuch ekemo gekaira.

english: “This is a good punishment for the rain,” said the snake. “Let us suffer because of this hole, maybe then you will remember your misdeeds.” Then the snake finished digging the hole and regretted having disturbed the bird and causing trouble. It also regretted having spoken badly.
ekegusii: Korwa abwo nonya mbono, ekebaki ekero kegoeta, nigo gekonyora engoko kegokura nse korigia esindani eria yasirete. Kera ekero omorengari bw'echimbaba chiekebaki ogoeta, nigo engoko ekoagama ebichuchu biaye. "Ama korwa ase aasioku na ase eroro." Nabirobio biaraneria: "Titori bariri. Tiga tominyoke.

english: After that, he thought about something else, the snake was angry, and he regretted the bird escaping and crawling on the ground near the coop. He remembered his mother telling him, “Evil deeds have consequences and bring sorrow.” And everyone agreed: “That is true. Don’t be greedy.”

english: We greet Petronillah Ogoti well. Gusii.com Proverbs, Culture And Customs Editor. June 9, 2012.
ekegusii: Buna twakabeire na Petronillah Ogoti. Gusii.com Proverbs, Culture And Customs Editor. Ebwagi [June] 9, 2012.

english: It is good to say that people who respect traditions and customs are honored, and they cherish their heritage greatly. These traditions belong to the Abagusii people, and it is important to remember that they strengthen the Ekegusii language. Traditions. The Abagusii people respect traditions very much, and these traditions help maintain the dignity of the Omogusii community. Time passes quickly. The Abagusii people have always been known for their hospitality and kindness. It is true that sometimes things happen unexpectedly, but they strive to overcome them.
ekegusii: Ntwe ntomanyeti buna ninki kiagerete bagateba amangana aya na koyaereria korwa ekegori ekemo, gochia aase ekegori kende. Aya na amang'ana gete y' Abagusii, ayio eise koba buna kwayakorire, nigo arenge koba mamincha y' Ekegusii. Emegiro.Abagusii nigo babagete amang'ana ayio, emegiro aase eng'encho arenge koba mamincha y' oboseera bw' Omogusii. Tari igo rioka. Abagusii nigo beegenete buna oise koyakora, n' chimuuma. Nigo ebinto, gose chinkore gete chiimbe, chiare gocha koba, gose kogokorekanera.
