english: Those who come from afar, let us examine the importance of the traditions of Ekegusii, both old and new, especially the Traditions of Ekegusii [ I ]. Also, let us understand that wise elders teach young people about the value of tradition.
ekegusii: Aase amatuko amake aerire, ntwasomete igoro y' emegiro y' Ekegusii, etano n' ebere, aase Emegiro y' Ekegusii [ I ]. Ase okoinyora, nigo omongina magokoro baba ominto atebete buna kera egesaku aase ense eye nkiabwate emegiro.

english: Also, they teach them to associate with elders and leaders, so that they can learn more about the Ekegusii culture. But sometimes, wise people may not want to share their knowledge. Associating with elders, and the traditions of Ekegusii, ensures that they remain alive:
ekegusii: Ase boigo, nigo baba atebete buna kobwatekana n' abagaka n' abangina abakoro, gokora amang'ana ayio nigo yarenge koba mamincha y' Ekegusii. Ase rituko ria rero, magokoro nigo atagete kogenderera n' enkwana eyio. Kobwatekana na baba ominto, emegiro ende y' Ekegusii nigo ere buna iga:

english: 8. A strong man does not fall: Among the Ekegusii, a strong man never forgets his roots. Indeed, it is said that strength comes from remembering one's origins. Also, know that the character of the Abagusii people is defined by their strong foundations.
ekegusii: 8. Mosacha mogima bori: Aase Ekegusii, monto mosacha mogima tarenge gosoa irongo. Yaya. Nigo yare koba chimuuma, aise korina engasi kwagachia gose gosoa irongo riinde rionsi. Ase boigo, inyora buna chimuma chia Abagusii nigo chiare gocha n’ amaakwa amanene.

english: Generations pass, but the foundation remains. A strong root should not be uprooted, lest its branches wither. An elder should not forget his ancestors and his past. Below: Look at the history of the Omogusii.
ekegusii: Amasikani aase iso biara. Obori bori bogocha gosiegwa ,erinde sokoro aroiseririgwe erongori nao bore irongo. Sokoro tagosoa irongo ime. Yaya. Irongo n' ya magokoro. Kona gotakuna obori aange na iso biara nkwarengeo. Below: Ekee k' obokima bw' Omogusii.

english: 9. Children are precious: A child should not be denied meat on a special occasion. Indeed, allowing a child to enjoy such occasions brings blessings. A child who behaves well deserves praise, and a younger sibling should respect an older sibling! A child who cries should be comforted so that they don't feel neglected.
ekegusii: 9. Ebimwana ebike: Omwana omoke tarenge koegwa enyama y' riini erinde arie. Yaya. Gaise koegwa riini, aye rirorio nario okwerorera. Nigo akamwana buna akwo karenge koba agatamu, naende akamwenu ekianda gia ikomi! Omwana buna oyio, nkware komotoma gose komoboria akore kende.

english: 10. Servants should not speak ill of their masters or reveal their secrets: A servant should not disclose the master's plans to others, because doing so would be disrespectful and harmful. Time passes quickly, my friends.
ekegusii: 10. Abasacha baria banchete kona gotirigoyia na kona goita abakungu babo bokaira: Ekero omosacha are goita omokungu oye bw’ enywomo, omokungu oyo nigo arenge gotama gochia irongo, gose nyaaro. Tari igo rioka Bosibori ominto.

english: That master should be respected so that he can protect his property, and the servant should not betray his trust. Indeed, it is important to avoid causing trouble. That servant who gossips will eventually face consequences, and will regret revealing the master's secrets – this is the way of the Ekegusii!
ekegusii: Omokungu oyo okona goitwa aaise koba buna okunire chimbere chiaye, omosacha oyo oye tarenge komoaka. Yaya. Eye nigo yarenge kobwekana buna ogosaba amabera. Omosacha oyo nyagotwanga mokaye arenge goaka omokungu oyo naende gakunire chimbere, echio n' chimuuma aase Ekegusii!

english: Furthermore, that servant who is disloyal may be dismissed, and anyone who does wrong will be punished accordingly, so that they learn to behave.
ekegusii: Komenta nayio, omokungu oyo nyagotwangwa arenge kobwata omwana kwaa, ekero agoitwa, nigo are gotiga goitwa ekiagera okwo nakwo okwoorikia buna osabire okwabera.

english: 11. A widow should not remarry too soon: It is customary among the Ekegusii for a widow to wait before remarrying. Respect this tradition, and the master will honor the woman who honors her late husband, and rejoice!
ekegusii: 11. Nyomenda nkobugia are omorori: Korwa bokoro ase Ekegusii, mokungu tarenge kobugia morori. Aaise gokora igo, omokungu oyo nigo arenge kogera omosacha oye aanse koema, na gokwa!

english: 12. A good name is better than wealth: A good reputation is more valuable than possessions for generations to come. Indeed, it is what defines being an Ekegusii. Therefore, a master who acts like this will be remembered by future generations. Generations pass, and stories endure, leaving a lasting legacy. Respect our fathers and mothers, and thank you for listening.
ekegusii: 12. Moka momura ngotakuna are endagera: Moka momura tatakeire gotakuna obori aase ise biara are. Yaya nonya. Okwo nigo kwarenge ogosaria Ekegusii. Eng’encho ende, omokungu buna oyio, nigo arenge kong’ong’ori ise biara. Amasikani aera. Bobe mono.

english: God commanded his angel 4, to appear, God remembered Abraham from Mesopotamia and told him, "Leave your country, and your relatives, and your father's house, and go to the land I will show you. I will make your descendants a great nation." Abraham obeyed the Lord and went to the land of Canaan where he lived and had a son named Isaac and begot Jacob, who was also called “Israel.”
ekegusii: Goetania emiaka chirifu 4, chiaetire, Nyasae akamoorekera Abraham aaria Mesopotamia na komotebia, "Imoka orwe ense yao, na ase egesaku kiao, na ase enyomba ya’iso, ogende ase ense indakoorokie. Nainche ningokore egesaku ekenene." Abraham akamoigwera Omenene na kogenda ase ense ya Kaanani ase amenyete na momura’oye Isaka na mochokor’oye Yakobo, oyochete korokwa “Israeli.”

english: Israel and his twelve sons migrated to the land of Egypt because of famine, and they settled there in the land of Canaan, but they multiplied and became a great nation. The Egyptians were afraid of their numbers and mistreated them severely, so they enslaved them and made them work hard. After four hundred and thirty years in Egypt, Moses arose as a deliverer, leading the Israelites out of Egypt and across the Red Sea, and God brought them to the mountains of Sinai.
ekegusii: Israeli na bamura baye 12 bagatirimboka gochia ense ya Misri ase’engencho enchara yachete ase ense ya Kaanani, naabwo bakamentekana na koba egesaku ekenene mono. AbaMisiri bagasogwa no’obwoba ase’enencho ye’egesaku eke ekenene kiamenyete amo na’barabwo, erio bakabakora abasomba na kobakoria chigasi chinkong’u. Nyuma ye’emiaka chimii inye ne’emerongo etato (430) ase ense ya Misri, Musa akabaraaa korwa ase obosomba, bagatamboka Enyancha Embariri na gosoa Bw’Arabu, ase Nyasae abaerete amachiko ase Egetunwa gia Sinai.

english: The journey of the Israelites from Egypt with Moses led them across the Wilderness and through the land promised to them by the Lord. They wandered in the desert for forty years until the generation that did not obey the Lord died off, and Joshua led them across the Wilderness.
ekegusii: Ekiare kia’Abaisraeli kiarwete Misiri na Musa tigiancheretwe gosoa Ense yo’Omwando ase’eng’encho getabwate okwegena ase Omonene. Gekaragaya ase eroro ase emiaka 40 goikera ekiare ekeyia kiabwate okweegena ase Omonene gegakina na gosoa ense yo’Omwando na Yoshua.

english: After another four hundred years, the twelve tribes of Israel were judged by judges, starting with Deborah after the death of Moses. Later they asked for a king, and God chose Saul as their first king; he reigned for forty years; he was succeeded by David, who reigned for forty years, and he was succeeded by his son Solomon who reigned for forty years. During the reign of Solomon, the kingdom of Israel reached its greatest glory, and the Temple was built; therefore the king’s palace for Solomon pleased God greatly; God spoke to him saying; the ten tribes of Israel would not be ruled by his son.
ekegusii: Ase emiaka ang’e chimii inye (400), ebisaku 12 bia’Israeli bikagamberwa na’Abagambi buna Richiko ria Musa riare goteba. Ekero bagania koba no’Omoruoti buna ebisaku binde, Nyasae akabaa Sauro abe Omoruoti obo; nere akabagambera ase emiaka 40; akabwatiwa na Daudi, oyoogambete emiaka 40, nere akabwatigwa na momura oye Solomoni oyoogambete emiaka 40. Ekero gia Solomoni, nario Omoruotu bw’Abaisraeli arenge neesiko enene, na Ekaru entang’ani ekaagachwa; korende enkoro yo’omoruoti Solomoni ekamogechia Nyasae ase obogotu bwaye; Nyasae akamotebia buna; ebisaku 10 biaIsraeli tibikogamberwa na momura oye nainde.

english: When Solomon died, the kingdom of Israel divided, and the ten northern tribes were ruled by rebellious leaders, who did not follow the example of David and Solomon. That rebellious leadership led to the downfall of Israel and the destruction of Samaria. But the tribe of Judah remained loyal, and Jerusalem remained the capital and was ruled by the line of David. From those sixteen kings, the people of the rebellious kingdom were known as “Jews” and the kingdom of Judah.
ekegusii: Ekero Solomoni akwa, oborwoti bwa Israeli bokabagekana, na ebisaku 10 bia’sugusu bikagamberwa na baruoti ababe, batarenge b’ororeri rwa Daudi na Solomoni. Oborwoti obo bwa’sugusu bokagenderera kweroka Israeli na gokora Samaria omochie oye omonene. Oborai oboke bwa’Irianyi bokaba nabwo Yuda, na Jerusalem Omochie oye omonene na kogamberwa no’ororeri rwa Daudi. Gochakera Abaruoti ya kabere 16, abanto boboruoti bwa Irianyi bakamanyekana buna “Abayaudi” ase’eng’encho yo’oboruoti bwa Yuda.

english: During the time of the division of the kingdoms of Israel and Judah, they were attacked, conquered, and exiled by Assyrians. The Israelites had repeatedly turned away from the Lord and worshiped false gods. Those people were called Samaritans, and the ten tribes of the north disappeared completely.
ekegusii: Ase eng’encho ye’ebibe bia Israeli ya Mocha, bakarwanigwa na gokobugwa na gokorwa abasomba na Abaasuri. Abaisraeli bari batigarete bakasoanana na abanto bebisaku batamwegenete Omenene abachete komenya nabwo. Aba nabwo bachete korokwa Abasamaria, erio ebisaku 10 bia’ Mocha bigasira pi.

english: Later, the kingdom of Judah was taken captive to Babylon because of their continued sinfulness, and the Temple was destroyed, resulting in seventy years of exile. The Jews returned to Judah, rebuilt the Temple in Jerusalem, and continued to be ruled by the descendants of David. At the time of Jesus, the region of Judah was known as Judea and was under Roman rule. Jesus Christ and his disciples traveled throughout Judea preaching the good news of the Kingdom of God. After three and a half years, the Jews condemned Jesus as a blasphemer and handed him over to the Romans to be crucified. Three days later, he rose from the dead and appeared to his disciples, instructing them to preach the gospel to all nations.
ekegusii: Nyuma yaye, Oboruoti bwa’Irianyi bwa Yuda bokairwa obosomba ase ense ya Babiloni buna egesusuro giogosasima chinyae chinde, na Ekaru egasarigwa, koronde nyumba ye’emiaka 70, Abayaudi bakairana Yuda, bakaagacha Ekaru Jerusalem na kogenderera kogamberwa na abaruoti bo’ororeri rwa Daudi Ase engaki ya Yeso, egesaku kia Yuda ekiamanyekanete bua Judea na ekiagambeire na Abarumi. Yeso O’Kristo na abatomwa baye bakarandia Enchiri Judea bakorigia ching’ondi chinsiru chie’enyomba ya Israeli. Nyuma ye’emiaka 3 na enusu, abayaudi bakamokana Yeso buna Omoboria obo na komokora omogabana o’Rumi komobamba. Amatuko 3 keraeta, akaboka korwa ase abakurena kobaorokera abatomwa baye, ataratira gochia Igoro ase bono aikaransete ase okoboko okorio gwa Tata.

english: But before being arrested, Jesus predicted the destruction of Jerusalem and the Temple, and the scattering of the Jews. This event happened in AD 70 when the Roman general Titus destroyed Jerusalem. For eighteen hundred years, the Jews have been scattered among all nations.
ekegusii: Ekero egeke atarabambwa, yeso akabana ing’a Jerusalem nesambwe buna amaakwa yaokomokana, Ekaru nesarigwe, na Abayaudi mbasebererekane ase ense yonsi. Obobani obo bogaikerana ase omwaka bwe’70 A.D. ekero omoruoti bw’Abarumi Tito asoete Jerusalem. Ase emiaka 1800, Abayaudi bagasebererekana ase ense yonsi.

english: In the twentieth century, in 1948, this prophecy came true. The nation of Israel was reestablished, and once again the Jews returned to the Land of Promise. Christians around the world rejoice and praise God, but still, why is there so much suffering in the world? This story has a purpose.
ekegusii: Ase omwaka elfu eyemo, chimii kianda na emerengo ene ne’etano etato (1948), egetakageire gekaba. Ense ya’Israeli ekabekwa, erio naende abayaudi bakairana ase Ense yo’Omwando. Abakristo abange batebire ing’a oko nogwancha kwa Nyasae, korende, naboo gose echi nechinguru chio’Omosunte? Esinema eye nebwate richibu.

english: Our condolences to the family, we have been informed of the passing of our colleague. University Lecturer, and former presenter on Omoraria TV, Professor Joseph Nyasani has passed away. Professor Nyasani died yesterday morning at the Aga Khan Hospital, Nairobi while undergoing treatment for an illness that had troubled him for a long time [ January ] this year. We were informed that Prof Nyasani was admitted to that hospital several days ago while battling a serious illness.
ekegusii: Mwanyagetinge ominto, twatebiigwe amangana amakong'u. University Lecturer, naende Omoraria bw' TV, Professor Joseph Nyasani osirire. Professor Nyasani nigo asirete igoro emaambia aaria ase enyagitari ya Agha Khan, Nairobi abwo ase konyora agendererete kobwenigwa koru etariki eyemo Engatiato [ January ] omwaka oyo. Nigo twatebigwa buna Prof Nyasani nigo airetwe ase enyagitari eyio ekero achagete korwara ase enkoro amo n' riini.

english: Professor Nyasani was born in 1936 in Central Kitutu Chache. Later, Prof Nyasani went to study theology, then switched to studying Philosophy. After completing his studies, Professor Joseph Nyasani became a Kenyan who tirelessly commented on issues of life and education in schools.
ekegusii: Professor Nyasani nigo aiboretwe ase omwaka o 1936 aaria ime ya Central Kitutu Chache. Ritangani, Prof Nyasani nigo atagete gosomera obosasiroti, korende agachaka gosomera Philosophy. Goetera ase ogosoma kwaye, Professor Joseph Nyasani nigo arenge Omokenya ori orenge komenta abande omoyo ase ogokong'ia ase amosomo amo n' esukuru.

english: Let us remember his contribution: This Kenyan man, Mr. Engencho Mono, said that his home was an academic treasure trove of books, documents and numerous resources.
ekegusii: Tarenge gotuguta chingaki chiaye nonya: Omokenya ominto Bw' Engencho mono, omomura oyo nigo atotigerete an academic treasure trove y' ebitabu, amariko amo' n' obotuki obonge.

english: This remarkable man owned over 41 books!! These books and resources will benefit Kenyans for many years to come.
ekegusii: Tata omomura omwoge kerage, nigo arigete ebitabu goetania 41!! Obotuki amo n' ebitabu ebi ariigete nigo birakonye AbaKenya abange for many years to come.

english: This scholar and worker was great, and he will remain an inspiration to many people for many years to come.
ekegusii: Omoki oye bw' ogosoma na gokora emeremo nigo ore, naende orabe an inspiration ase abanto abange for many years to come.

english: Professor Joseph Nyasani [1936-2016].
ekegusii: Professor Joseph Nyasani [1936-2016].

english: Academic Legacy: Professor Nyasani did not waste his time
ekegusii: Academic Legacy: Professor Nyasani tatotigeti bosa igo

english: Professor Nyasani successfully defended his PhD dissertation in Latin in 1963, setting a record of 300 years. Upon his death, Professor Joseph Nyasani leaves behind 41 books on metaphysics, logic, cosmology and legal Philosophy!!
ekegusii: Professor Nyasani nigo achiete nguma ase okorika a dissertation yaye ya PhD ase omomwa o Latin ase omwaka o 1963 na kobuna e record y' emiaka 300. Buna asirete igoro iga, Professor Joseph Nyasani konyora orikire ebitabu goetania 41 bia metaphysics, logic, cosmology amo na legal Philosophy!!

english: Of those 41 books, some include:
ekegusii: Gati y' ebitabu ebio 41 ariikire, ebinde nigo bire:

english: Highly acclaimed academic
ekegusii: Highly acclaimed academic

english: Professor Joseph Nyasani studied at Cambridge Secondary Education in Kakamega County. From there, he went to Rome Italy where he studied Latin, literature, English and history. Professor Nyasani obtained an Arts degree from Urbaniana University, Rome (1963), a Diploma in Social Ethics from Woodstock College, Oxford in 1964, a PhD from The University of Cologne, Germany in 1969, and a Law Degree, New York University, School of Law in 1972.
ekegusii: Professor Joseph Nyasani nigo asomete aaria Cambridge Secondary Education aaria kakamega County. Koru abwo, akagenda aaria Rome Italy abwo ase asomerete Latin, literature, English amo na history. Professor Nyasani nigo abwate Arts degree koru ase Urbaniana University, Rome (1963), Diploma in Social Ethics koru ase Woodstock College, Oxford ase omwaka o 1964, PhD koru ase The University of Cologne, Germany, ase omwaka o 1969, amo na Law Degree, New York University, School of Law ase omwaka o 1972.

english: In his work, Professor Nyasani worked at the United Nations Secretariat in New York as the Political Affairs Officer in the Department of Political and Security Council Affairs in 1971. Afterwards, Professor Nyasani became the Associate Professor at the City University of New York in 1973.
ekegusii: Ase ogokora emeremo, Professor Nyasani nigo akorete emeremo ase the United Nations Secretariat aaria New York buna the Political Affairs Officer ase the Department of Political and Security Council Affairs ase omwaka o 1971. Koru abwo, Professor Nyasani akaba the Associate Professor aaria ase the City University of New York ase omwaka o 1973.

english: As a commentator and reporter, Professor Nyasani was a presenter at the Voice of Germany (Deutsche Welle) in Cologne, Germany and the Voice of Kenya which is now KBC. Additionally, Professor Nyasani was a reporter at The University of Nairobi from 1970 onwards.
ekegusii: Komenta na koba Omwoorokia, Professor Nyasani nigo arenge omoraria ase the Voice of Germany (Deutche Welle) aaria Cologne, Germany amo na Voice of Kenya eyio bono ere KBC. Ase boigo, Professor Nyasani nigo arenge omwoorokia ase The University of Nairobi koru ase omwaka o 1970 goikera bono.

english: In addition to his work, Professor Nyasani was also the first chairman of the Council of the Kisii University from 2008 to 2013. It is said that during his time, Professor Nyasani received the Alexander Von Humboldt Foundation Fellowship and DAAD Foundation Scholarship in 1987 and 1992.
ekegusii: Ase emeremo emenge akorete, Professor Nyasani boigo nere orenge the first chairman of the Council of the Kisii University koru ase omwaka o 2008 to 2013. Gati y' ebieegwa b' ogosoma kw igoro Professor Nyasani aetwe nigo bire the Alexander Von Humboldt Foundation Fellowship amo na DAAD Foundation Scholarship gati y' omwaka o 1987 and 1992.

english: Professor Joseph Nyasani, a son of Kenyans.
ekegusii: Professor Joseph Nyasani, omwana bw Abakenya.

english: Also broadcast on KTN, Nairobi
ekegusii: Igwa bono koru ase KTN, Nairobi

english: Gusii.com publishes news about relatives, friends, colleagues and family members of the Kenyan son, Professor Joseph Nyasani. With great respect from Omonene Tata Nyasae.
ekegusii: Gusii.com nigo tokoru engora gochia ase abamwabo, abasani, abairi amo n' abaamate ba omwana bw' Abakenya, Professor Joseph Nyasani. Kera egento ase Omonene Tata Nyasae.

english: It is good to gather people together at Gusii.com so they can help each other. And now this is a great story that has come out. But they say that we will work hard to maintain the culture of the Abagusii people.
ekegusii: Nigo nkoira ribaga eri kobaarigania abageni ba Gusii.com mwensi ase mwabeta. Nche nigo nde n' omogoko omonene ase ogoika engaki eye. Bono nabo togoteba maiso marore buna twakorire korika omogano oito Bw' Abagusii.

english: Greetings to all people, my sister Kwamboka Mireri. We plan to discuss things so that we can develop the Ekegusii language so that we Abagusii can progress, and she helps my sister Kwamboka. Thank you very much to those who remember.
ekegusii: Magokoro baba ominto, omongina Kwamboka Mireri. Amangana goetania enusu twarikire y' ekemira n' Ekegusii giato buna ntwe Abagusii twakabeire, nigo are goetera ase omongina Kwamboka. Mbuya mono baba ase kera egento.

english: Even though we did not know what was remembered, we have learned it, because we have chosen well. Now we have reached a point of understanding this year's challenges. But it seems this year and next, there will be more difficulties ahead.
ekegusii: Nonya titomanyeti kera egento, twamanyire make, kobwa ekero twachagete. Nigo twaansete obotuki ase omochakano bwo omwaka oria oerete. Bono nigo yaaira omwaka oyomo n' enusu, kobeka obotuki obo aamo.

english: This time we have found ourselves in a difficult situation. The truth is that we have managed to speak to the elders and leaders of the Gusii people who are still alive, so that they can be reminded of this culture. Let us not forget this important matter.
ekegusii: Gaki ka moranche twabere ase okoira chingaki chintambe. Ekerenga nigo twatagete kogamba n' abangina n' abagaka ba Gusii bari bare moyo, naende bainyorete buna batebetigwe igoro y' omogano oyo oito. Tiyarenge egasi ere engororo igo.

english: So we write this today, so that the Abagusii and their children may unite, and they understand this culture. Because we write this message again, so that it does not get lost, this culture is for the Abagusii and their generations.
ekegusii: Ntwe nigo twanyorete ng'a ase bono, Abagusii n' abake batigarete, abwo bamanyete omogano oito. Obokongu bonde twanyorete mbori ng'a, buna otarigetwe aande onsi, emegano yaito ntwe Abagusii n' emenge.

english: The leader is Kenyanya Marube. He wants to understand the time of Mokendu O' Iruma, who is no longer here. Thank you very much to everyone.
ekegusii: Omogaka Kenyanya Marube. Ntware gocha komanya igoro y' Mokendu O' Iruma, onye tari aye. Mbuya mono sokoro ominto.

english: And let this story spread far and wide, so that it reaches those who were scattered, and it brings unity and peace, and maintains this culture. And when considering its importance, it should be known that even if there are few of us, this culture is strong and enduring.
ekegusii: Ase engencho emegano eye ere ao ao, ekabetereria buna goika abariki baikaranse aamo naende, goitona na kobeka obotuki obo aamo, erinde korika omogano oyomo. Ase okogenderera gotuka, nigo yaikerete buna nonya kere emenge, emegano yaito emenene nigo ere ebere.

english: This culture teaches us that we once went to Egypt. This culture also tells us that we came from Mokendo O' Iruma [Mombasa]. But it spreads so that it reaches Petronillah and Abner, the elders and leaders of the clans, so that they can be reminded and honored.
ekegusii: Omogano oyomo nigo ogoteba buna nigo twarwete aaria Misri (Egypt). Omogano onde ogateba buna nigo twatirete korwa aaria Mokendo O' Iruma [Mombasa]. Bono ekabetereria buna goika Petronillah amo na Abner barigie abagaka n abang'ina abakoro, baria bainyorete buna batebetigwe.

english: Note: Leader Samuel Omare Nyambisa wrote this story. Thank you very much to his father for supporting him. But we have learned that the Abamanyi clan knows the history of the Abagusii.
ekegusii: Gatigati: Omogaka Samuel Omare Nyambisa ngotega are omogano. Mbuya mono tata ase ogotosemia. Bono twamanyire buna Abamanyi mbabwate amanyinga y' Abagusii.

english: And now we greet Petronillah Ogoti and Abner Nyaberi, and thank them for their support. Come let us work hard to promote this blog about this culture, which is not forgotten. And finally, we say that we thank the elders and leaders of the community, so that they continue to support this culture. Very truly, do not forget those who contribute to this work and appreciate their efforts, saying:
ekegusii: Nche nigo ngoakera Petronillah Ogoti amo na Abner Nyaberi, buna mbuya mono ase egasi engiya. Kende tikiare gocha korikwa ase ebulogi eye igoro y' omogano oito, onye tari barabwo. Ase boigo, nigo ngoteba buna mbuya mono ase abagaka n' abang'ina abange, abwo batotebetie amange igoro y' omogano oito. Mono mono, tiga toakere abakobwatia ase okorwa chingaki n' oboremereria bwabo, gotosemia:

ekegusii: Omongina Kwamboka Mireri, (Ichuni) Bomobea, Nyaribari Masaba;

ekegusii: Omogaka Samuel Omare Nyambisa, (Gesure) Bosansa, Bobasi Chache;

ekegusii: Omogaka Kenyanya Marube, (Otamba) Bogeka, Nyaribari Chache;

english: Thank you very much for your contributions and support. The support of Petronillah and Abner, these blog posts are valuable.
ekegusii: Mbuya mono ase okoremeria amaborio aito, na gotoa obosemia. Obotuki bw' Petronillah amo na Abner obwo, ase blog posts chikobwatia.

Be aware that some accounts may be biased, so do your own research and think critically. Don't believe everything you hear without verifying it yourself. Thank you very much and enjoy.
ekegusii: [II]. Kobwatekana n' ogotarikwa kw' omogano oito n' Abagusii ntwe tweka, emegano yaito nigo ere emenge, naende ebwate "versions' ao ao. Kerabe buna obotutukanu mboreo ase oboriki obo, ka moranche totebie, erinde tobogorore. Nigo togoteba iga ase engencho tomanyete buna ntomanyeti kera egento. Mbuya mono ase kera oyomo and enjoy.

english: Gusii Culture And Customs CXXXIII: Is a person honored when they have many possessions and wealth, or is it because of their character?
ekegusii: Abagusii Culture And Customs CXXXIII: Bono Omokungu Kanywomirwe Ngokora Arenge Kende Gionsi Buna Eeigwete?

english: By PETRONILLAH OGOTI, Gusii.com Proverbs, Culture and Customs Editor. Thursday [ September ] 4, 2015.
ekegusii: Na PETRONILLAH OGOTI, Gusii.com Proverbs, Culture and Customs Editor. Tureti Ya Kebaki [ September ] 4, 2015.

english: Don't despise a poor man who has little property, a generous person honors people and I respect them because they share what little they have, they don't refuse to be helped by others. A generous person respects them because they share these things, whether it's a small gift or a large gift. Because of friendship, a young goat doesn't hesitate, those who help each other always have support.
ekegusii: Tokare konywa rikairo bono emorogoba, omongina magokoro Binsari ominto nigo antebia buna amang'ana nare akanire, atarenge gokorwa n' ebigori gete. Nigo magokoro antebia buna amang'ana aya nigo arenge koenanwa korwa gochia ase ekegori ekenene, gochia ase ekegori egeke. Ase omobwekano, ekero enyangi yarenge koba, aba banywomanire nkoegwa barenge amachiko.

english: A clean person doesn't hesitate to offer support to his community. Because of this custom, someone is respected when they have the ability to give generously. But sometimes, generous people don't understand the importance of supporting those who are less fortunate than themselves.
ekegusii: Omosacha nkoegwa arenge amachiko y' enywomo. Ase boigo omokung'u nere nkoegwa arenge amachiko buna abwenerete kwebwata bono kanywomirwe. Ase rituko ria rero, magokoro Binsari ominto nigo atagete gotosemia igoro y' amachiko aria arenge korenga abakung'u baria banywomire.

english: However, people say that anyone who helps another person should be considered a friend, just like a close relative. They say it's good to be kind, but a helper should also be careful about helping a bad person, lest it affect their reputation.
ekegusii: Ritangani, magokoro nigo antebetie buna onye omosubati ochire bwoye nigo agwenerete koba omwegenwa gochia ase omogaka oye. Nigo yarenge bobe naende chimuma, ase omosubati gosanga kemobere n' omosacha omoao, otari oye bw' enywomo.

english: In conclusion, a person shouldn't be praised for boasting about their wealth. Indeed, a person should be praised for being humble and respectful towards others, rather than flaunting their possessions. Through this, others will learn to appreciate them.
ekegusii: Eriakabere, omokung'u oyo tarenge konywomwa na koruga mwaye obwango obwo obwo. Yaya. Nigo omosubati oyo arenge koragera na koruga mwa ng'ina biara ase amatuko atari make. Korwa abwo, ng'ina biara omanya komoarekera mwaye.

english: Finally, a generous person, especially one with wealth, should not look down on anyone!! It is said that a generous person honors people and understands that a person's honor depends on how they treat others.
ekegusii: Eriagatato, omokung'u bono kanywomirwe, tancheire koria amagena gose enyama y' engoko !! Koigwa iga, nche bono naboretie magokoro Binsari ominto erinde antebie buna ninki kiarenge kogera omokung'u akanigwe erinde taria chindagera echi.

english: People say that one should not be arrogant!
ekegusii: Baba ominto nigo antebetie buna tari kera egekoro giaito kebwate eng'encho yaye. "Ase okoba abaigweri, ntwe nigo twarenge kobwata Ekegusii giaito buna twarenge gotebigwa korwa ase ekegori egekoro, gochia ase ekegori egeke na gokora buna kegoteba" Magokoro nabo amentete ogoteba buna karanyore richibu rie ribori eri ase obwango, natotebie.

english: In essence, people say that a family that is united and works together will prosper, and its future generations will be blessed. It is important, however, that a leader does not become corrupt or selfish. This is said, so that leaders may learn humility.
ekegusii: Ekero bokorugwa, onde bwensi tarenge kobooncha !!

english: People say that the old Gusii people used to value hard work more than material possessions. Today, people say that the Gusii language is valued more than acquiring wealth or status.
ekegusii: Eriakane, magokoro nigo antebetie buna ekero obori bwamire na kogeswa, obokima bori obotongore nigo bwarenge koba obwa ise biara. Kibokorugwa, nonya n' omogango torenge gokombwa n' omoyio. Egete gioka kiarenge kobokomba !! Ase boigo, onde tancheire kobooncha nonya. Ise biara kaboonchire na koragera, abande nabarabwo bamanya kobega.

english: Let us end here.
ekegusii: Magokoro nigo antebetie buna Abagusii abakoro mbanchete korwa amasikani gochia ase abanto abanene. Aaiga, magokoro nigo abetebetie buna Ekegusii eke nigo kiarenge gokorwa ase okwoorokia amasikani gochia ase omogaka bw' omochie.

english: Finally, people say that a wealthy person should not despise anyone. It is also said that acquiring wealth or status is not enough; one must also have good character. One who has both wealth and character is truly respected, and those around them recognize their worth.
ekegusii: Tiga kong'ong'oria iso biara

english: It is important that the Gusii people remember their traditions. Let us respect our ancestors, whose wisdom guides us like a light. Those who disrespect their ancestors bring misfortune upon themselves and their families.
ekegusii: Eriagatano, baba nigo antebetie buna omokung'u ore bwoye tancheire gotakuna obori ase ise biara. Ase boigo, aaiga n' okwoorokia amasikani gochia ase ise biara. Gotakuna obori nigo yarenge kororekana buna nigo arenge kong'ong'oria ise biara !!

english: Oh my goodness!! A person's shame is a heavy burden.
ekegusii: Eriagatano na rimo, omokung'u orenge koba bwoye tatakeire gosereta nyomba. Ase ki? Koru Omogusii omokoro, emeremo y' okoagacha chinyomba nigo yarenge koba ey' abasacha. Nonya yarenge koba buna omosacha bw' omokung'u oyo taiyo, abasacha abaamate, gose bagisangio b' omosacha oyo nabwo barenge komoagachera enyomba.

english: Finally, a person should not reveal another person's secrets. However, sometimes things happen unexpectedly, and a person's secret becomes known. People say that when this happens, one should show compassion and understanding towards the person whose secret was revealed, rather than judging them harshly.
ekegusii: Kai tata !! Omokungu gokuna chinsemo chia nsoni igo mbobe

english: Is there a reason why someone would want to steal from another? A person should not steal.
ekegusii: Eriagatano na kabere, omokung'u taganeiri gokuna chinsemo chia nsoni chi' omogaka oye. Bono nonya rero ebinto bianchokire, omokungu gokuna chinsemo chia nsoni ch' omogaka oye nigo yarenge koba chimuma. Magokoro baba ominto nigo antebetie buna ase chingaki echio chinkoro, nonya omokung'u barenge komanyana kemobere n' omogaka oye, nigo arenge gosika chinsemo echi chia nsoni chi' omogaka oyo oye.

english: Finally, disputes should be resolved peacefully and fairly. The truth should prevail, and justice should be served. Children should be taught to respect others, and people should not take advantage of each other. But even then, a person should not interfere in matters that do not concern them, lest they become entangled in conflict. Oh yes. A person should not encourage others to engage in wrongdoing, especially if it involves harming others.
ekegusii: Bono tinkoria amagena y' engoko buna inyeigwete? Omokung'u nigo arenge gwesika.

english: A person should not boast about their strength or abilities. It is better to remain humble and modest.
ekegusii: Eriagatano na gatato, amaru nigo arenge kwengwa na konywegwa ase emeyega ao ao. Ekero endagera yagesirwe, amaru nigo arenge gosikwa ase egetera, aengwa na konywegwa. Omwana gaachiire iburu, amaru nkonywegwa arenge. Nonya nabo igo, omokung'u taganeiri kobera eero ekero abagaka bakonywa amarwa. Yaya. Nigo omokung'u arenge kobamentera amaru gose amache a morero, erinde oirana chikoni ase abakung'u bande.

english: Let us listen to the wise words of our elders, and I thank you for listening. May peace reign among the Gusii people. This series will continue next week.
ekegusii: Omokung'u taganeiri koereria omosacha oye egento n' okoboko okobee. Gokora igo, nigo yarenge kororekana buna ayio n' amachayo. Aaiga ase eriakianda, omokung'u bw' amasikani nigo arenge koereria omosacha oye egento, goetera ase okoboko gw' okorio.

english: To PETRONILLAH OGOTI. Mwamogusii.com Proverbs, Culture And Customs Editor. March 23, 2011.
ekegusii: Na PETRONILLAH OGOTI. Mwamogusii.com Proverbs, Culture And Customs Editor. Egetamo (March) 23, 2011.

english: She was among those who were circumcised in the land of Ekegusii and initiated into adulthood. This story is true. She was initiated into adulthood until she became a member of the SDA Church area Nyanchwa. The late Paulina Bosibori Nyandusi.
ekegusii: Nigo anywometwe ase enyangi ye Ekegusii na kobekerwa ebitinge. Tari igo rioka. Nigo abegete ebitinge mbaka ekero abatisetwe ase the SDA Church aaria Nyanchwa. Omongina Paulina Bosibori Nyandusi.

english: After completing the initiation ceremonies, the late Bosibori gave birth to her son, Dr. Musa Nyandusi while many people gathered around. The late Paulina Bosibori Nyandusi. A Gusii woman who was circumcised and initiated into adulthood in modern times.
ekegusii: Nyuma yo okorusia ebitinge ebio, nigo omongina Bosibori aboretie omwanchwa oye, omogaka Musa Nyandusi erinde bonsi bagancherana. Marehemu omongina Paulina Bosibori Nyandusi. Omongina o Gusii onywometwe goetera ase enyangi y' ebitinge in modern times.

english: Don't be surprised!
ekegusii: Ntotagete obochege!

english: The ceremony ended with celebrations. In ancient times during the circumcision ceremony, it was customary for people to share food. Therefore, the elders were sent to look for a beautiful girl who could cook food so that they would not lack something to eat (don't be surprised!).
ekegusii: Enywomo nigo yasikire na abakoro. Ase chingaki chia kare enyangi ye ebitinge nigo yagakorirwe ekero gio okonywomana. Ritangani, esigani nigo yare gotomwa gochia sobo enyaroka yaira eng'ana egoteba buna imbatagete kobanywomera (ntotagete obochege!).

english: Let us move on to the explanation.
ekegusii: Togende ase ekerorano

english: The work of the explanation committee was completed. What does an explanation mean? Ask those who know. An explanation involves both young men and old men coming together. Old men and their wives were sent to find a beautiful girl so that she could marry a young man.
ekegusii: Korwa aiga rituko rie ekerorano nigo riare kobekwa. Yaani ekerorano ninki? Nabo oraborie. Ase ekerorano nario omosubati no omomura bare kororana ritangani. Omomura na abasani baye nigo bare gochikwa gochicha sobo omosubati erinde barorane no omoiseke.

english: A young man who doesn't have a wife, he risks being ridiculed. Why? So that they know that he doesn't have anyone to help him with his household chores. That is why it is important to respect others in a polite way. It is good to respect them.
ekegusii: Omosubati onye tatageti momura oyo, nigo are kwabusa risiko riabo baroo. Ase ki? Erinde bamanye inga ere tatageti gose tancheti momura oyio. Yaani eyio nigo yarenge enchera yo okobaseria in a polite way. Egere kobaseri aba.

english: Therefore, someone should not hesitate, he should ask. The truth about this matter has been revealed, because people used to steal from each other. But now this habit of eating another person's food has decreased. The old men also send their wives to look for a young man. They send their wives to look for a young man so that they can have peace of mind.
ekegusii: Korende onye bwanchire, tare kwabusa. Ekeriboko ekero kiaariganigwe, ogotera nigo kware goterwa abanto batwara omogoko. Bono korwa aaiga chiombe chio okonywoma omoiseke oyo, nigo chiare gokwanerwa.

english: They should therefore ensure that this young man doesn't cause problems for others. This young man should not cause trouble and disrespect, they should be fined according to the law. The old men don't understand. Let them learn. If they continue to behave like this, they will remain with the young man until he marries an old man.
ekegusii: Abamura abangaini nigo bare koba na riso rimo ase omoiseke!

english: Things are changing. Be careful!
ekegusii: Ritangani, embori amo n' eeri y' egesicho amo ne chiombe nigo chiare korwegwa. Abanyene omosubati amo no omomura nigo bare koigwana. Ekero kio ogoakana chiombe, esira ngotigara yare. Korwa abwo, abamura bono nigo bare gochikwa bagenda sobo omoiseke. Abwo sobo omoiseke, nigo barenge gotenga bwakia, korende bare na riso rimo ase omoiseke !

english: Therefore, let it be. Understand carefully. Traditions are disappearing, and customs are being forgotten in this society where people no longer want to be known, and they are disrespectful to their leaders. They are careless.
ekegusii: Nigo bare korenda erinde omoiseke oyio tatama gochia bongina rome. Omoiseke oyio aise gocha gotama na kobasireria, nigo bare goakwa a fine ye embori eyemo. Abamura batamanyeti gasi. Oigwe bono. Ko bakorire gotenga ase rimaambia, nigo bare kogenda no omoiseke oyio korwa aiga mpaka sobo omomura.

english: They complain that things are changing (meaning old men and young men are doing things differently), and many people disagree, saying that a young man shouldn't be allowed to participate in ceremonies. Know that a young man may not understand some things, there are no ceremonies!
ekegusii: Ebinto mbuya bire. Taraire mosisi!

english: But if this happens, the world will be confused, and the community will suffer. Old men and women are ready for conflict. The mediator and the elders and the old men are also ready. It's not easy. The situation is tense.
ekegusii: Korende bado. Mangana taraera. Amatuko atato kaerire, obokima n' embori nigo bware koirwa ase omosubati oyo osogete egere bamanyigwe gose mbaigwananete no omogaka oyo oye, gose nigo ararete mosisi !

english: That person who speaks against the elders is like someone who insults a cow. That story is not true; those mediators were involved with the mediator. Because of the actions of the old men, we have suffered, the mediator has become stubborn, the spokesperson, and the interpreter have caused problems for the community and the mediators, causing chaos and confusion in the villages.
ekegusii: Bakonyora ng'a amangana mbuya are (yaani omomura no omoiseke mbakorete egasi buya), na bonsi mbaisanegete, omoiseke oteba atimigwe ebitinge. Manya ng'a omoiseke arenge gokana inga binto tibiarenge buya, hakuna ebitinge!

english: The wealth of the community is being wasted!
ekegusii: Bono korwa abwo, enyangi yaariganigwa ekorwe, n' omosubati oirana sobo. Abamura n' abasubati baba tayare na amakano. Omonyakiore n' esumati amo n' omoimari n' abamura nao bare koba aaiga. Bado maneno si rahisi hivyo. Enyameni nigo yare kobekwa.

english: This world is full of lies. Respect the Gusii people. Love everyone and don't discriminate. The spokesperson is destroying everything, the wealth of the community is circulating around and around, wasting away.
ekegusii: Oyo okobua ase enyameni eye nere ore koegwa ritana rie engombe. Ekondo nero yarenge aroro, eyio omoimari are gotanganigwa no omonyakeore. korwa ensemo ya abamura nigo tware gotwara, omonyakeore ore gotangana motwe, omongwasi, nere omonywomi nakorwa ase omosubati no omoimari, omoriakari, agasagane ko obosi ne enyaroka ya amaguta.

english: Know that complaining won't help solve the problem. Everything has its time. This world is always changing, and this world is full of lies.
ekegusii: Emanwa ye embori nigo yare komosinyorera amagoro!

english: Good afternoon, we greet PETRONILLAH OGOTI. Gusii.com Proverbs, Culture And Customs Editor. June [June] 19, 2012
ekegusii: Buna twakabeire na PETRONILLAH OGOTI. Gusii.com Proverbs, Culture And Customs Editor. Ebwagi [June] 19, 2012

english: A person who loves Moraa does not reveal her secrets to anyone. A father also does not reveal his wife’s wealth to a stranger who comes to his home. It is good for a home to have its own people, Ekegusii has its own traditions which are respected, so a person who loves Moraa respects them.
ekegusii: Omongina magokoro Moraa ominto nantagete gontebia engana. Baba nigo atagete gonsemia igoro y' ogosira kw' omogaka oria obwate abakung'u abange. Ekero omogaka ore n’ abarugi abange akuure, Ekegusii gete ki' eng’encho nkiagakorirwe, buna omong’ina magokoro Moraa agoteba.

english: Let us discuss the customs of Ekegusii
ekegusii: Ogokobani nkwarengeo ase Ekegusii

english: Know then that when a home is built, it is better than a rented house, because a rented house can be taken away from you anytime. Indeed, what is a rented house? Go and build yours.
ekegusii: Bono buna omogaka oyo atweka mo iga, nigo kera omokung'u oye, arenge kominyoka gochia mwaye ogokobani. Inee, bono ogokobani ninki? Nabo oraborie.

english: Oh, strangers, I am saddened by this current situation. Things were different, and things changed, and now they are being discussed, like a home owner who is grieving. Below: Like Gusii
ekegusii: Eee abakungu abange mbakanywomirwe n' omogaka oyomo ase chingaki echio chi kare. Ebitega mbiakaarekirwe, n' ebinto biaturekwa, naende biagororokigwa, ko omogaka bw' omochie asirire. Below: Nka Gusii

english: A person who loves Moraa respects the homestead, a loving person. It is a loving person who grieves if their homestead is taken away, let them grieve. Because of this, know that taking away someone’s homestead is grief, and it causes pain!
ekegusii: Omong’ina Moraa nigo agoteba buna ogokobani n’ ogoonchora chianga, omong’ina akobeka. Nigo omong'ina nyene nyagosira arenge kobeka chianga chia ime, maonchorerane. Korwa abwo, omanya kobeka chianga chia nyagosira korwa igoro, nachirochio maonchorane!

english: And a loving person will not allow ruin, so that their home may remain. The days are coming. Before, a person would not allow ruin, but nowadays. Comment on this, before a person allows ruin. Yes. All the days of life, it is good for that home to remain, that person will not be impoverished, so that their children may prosper.
ekegusii: Naende omong'ina nyene nigo arenge kweyaka riibu, ko omogaka oye asirire

english: It is said that Moraa commented that allowing ruin is like losing a homestead. It is like a homestead that is lost forever, that person will never recover it. The suffering of that home is great, before a stranger allows ruin.
ekegusii: Tari igo rioka. Kera omong’ina nigo arenge koeyaka riibu, buna omware. Komenta nayio, kera omong'ina tarenge gwesibia. Yaya. Aase engaki eye yonsi y' ebirero ekero omogaka oyo akuure, omong'ina oyo tarenge gokwanigwa n' okoboko, goikera ebirero biaerire.

english: It is a homeowner who grieves if they are evicted from a large plot of land.
ekegusii: Nigo baba Moraa akomenta buna mong'ina oyo tarenge koererigwa endagera koboko. Nigo endagera yarenge goterekwa nse, omong'ina oyo omanya koyeimokia korwa nse. Emorogoba y' omogaka oyo gosira, kera omokung'u nigo arenge kobera mwaye.

english: Because of this, the property of that home is sold and bought on a large plot of land [ a stranger ]. Understand that a large plot of land is not life, a stranger who owns it does not have life either, and the property will be destroyed.
ekegusii: Nigo omogaka nyagosira arenge kobekwa mw' mosera ibu omonene ritang'ani

english: Before a large plot of land is allowed to be ruined, look for a small piece of land to cultivate. The stories about that small piece of land, the property will be protected. Because of this, seeds are sown. The fruits of those seeds are harvested, a large tree grows and provides shade.
ekegusii: Korwa abwo, omobere bw’ omogaka oyo orentwa na gosoigwa mw’ mosera ibu [ omokung'u ] omonene ritangani. Korende onye mosera ibu tari moyo, omokung'u o kabere ori ore moyo nao omobere orenge koirwa.

english: Anyone who plants a large tree knows how to plant it. Yes.
ekegusii: Kera mosera ibu nigo arenge kobera mwaye, orara goikera rituko riria ri' ogotindekwa. Emaambia yaye ase rituko erio ri' ogotindekwa, omobere nigo orenge gosokigwa. Korwa abwo, embera yaremwa. Magega y' embera koremwa, omomura omonene bw’ enyomba enene nere orenge goaka egekamago ki' oboina.

english: That shade is found where there is coolness and water, protecting anyone who grieves. The stories about it are remembered, everyone associated with that home wants to share their thoughts.
ekegusii: Onye omomura omonene bw' enyomba enene taiiyo, omochokoro bw’ omomura omonene bwe enyomba enene nere orenge goaka egekamago ekio ki' oboina. Ekero engaki y’ ogotindekwa yaikire, abang’ina b' omogaka oyo bonsi nigo bare koruta amaraba gochia ase embera.

english: As they share their thoughts, understand that someone will come and ask questions. Because of this, respect is given, and boundaries are established. Once those boundaries are established, the belongings of the grieving homeowner are protected.
ekegusii: Mosera ibu omonene nere orenge gochaka koyaruta amaroba aya, abande babwatia korwa magega. Omobere gotubereirwe, kera oyomo omanya kogenda mwaye. Emorogoba oyio ko omogaka atindekirwe, kera omong’ina nigo arenge konyenya eming'ichi y’ ogokendi enyomba.

english: But who protects them? I ask you. This is because leaving things to chance can lead to misunderstanding and grief. Truly, the time when the homeowner grieves is when it is most vulnerable. Because of this, the current situation is very difficult, and it needs to be addressed!!
ekegusii: Abakiare ba nyagosira mbange koria emingichi eye. Yaya.

english: This is spoken about in Ekegusii.
ekegusii: Eming'inchi eye nigo yare koriegwa n' onde bwensi ase eamate, otatiga abakiare ba nyagosira. Emaambia yaye bogokiamoka, abang’ina b' omogaka oyo bonsi nigo barenge kogingerana etuki, aase oboina igoro. Ase boigo, abangina aba nigo barenge kobutorwa ebitinge, bamanya kobibeka ase embera igoro.

english: If you leave things to chance, disputes arise, causing conflict and division. Moraa's heart says that because of this, things should be discussed. But why discuss them? I ask you to explain the reason. The time of the grieving homeowner and the current situation need to be understood, so that peace can prevail.
ekegusii: Ko babekire ebitinge ebi aase embera igoro, kera omongina nigo arenge koirana mwaye. Korwa abwo, egoree yanyenywa, erinde ebitega biaarekwe. Ekero ebitega biakorire koarekwa, ebinto bi' omogaka nyagosira nigo biarenge goturekwa.

english: These things have been done, people know how to handle matters peacefully, and through good guidance, they protect everyone, helping those who are suffering and children grow up well. Moraa's heart also encourages others to work together and remember the importance of unity.
ekegusii: Bono ogoturekwa ninki? Naende nabo oraborie. Oko n' ogotureka ebinto ebinene b' nyagosira kwoorokia gose koba ekemanyererio ki' ogosira kwaye. Ritangani, ritimo rio omogaka nyagosira nigo riarenge goturekwa, riarigereria gochia nse. Korwa abwo, ekerogo kiaye nyamagoro atato, nakerokio nigo kiarenge goturekwa !!

ekegusii: Okogororokigwa nkwarengeo ase Ekegusii

NYASAE NA ABAKUNGU BABO BABERE: Aiga nigo togosoma ng,a Nyasae nigo bare babaere.Tata na omwana.Yeso n,Omwana oye omomoima buna togosoma Yohana1:1.Oyio okorete no goikerenia emeremo yaye buna Omalaika Michael.Nyasae n,Omwanchani oito naende omonyaboronge.Goika toorokie ng,a Kristo nigo achete ore Mwanayabanto naende nairane gocha kwoyia Ekanisa yaye eria Kabere.Naende goika tomanye ng,a abanyaborimo mbache bagoteba na,a nabwo Kristo buna togosoma ase Okomanoka 7 na 14 naende abaregende Igoro na abanto chilifu 144,000 abwo bare ase ororeria rwa Adamu na hawa. Soma omochakano 2:18,Abagalatia 4:24 na Yohana 14:26.Aseigo Yehovah nabwate Omokungu oyio ore Omoika Omochenu,oyio okogambera emeika yonsi .

english: 7. THE SEAL OF GOD: The seal of the Sabbath is proclaimed by the Holy Spirit. For those 144,000 people, they share the 144,000 seals and are marked with the seventh seal. That seal corresponds to the book of Daniel 12, which speaks of the five angels 5:1-11. Anyone who knows the truth, remains steadfast, and does not deny his faith should study these truths.
ekegusii: 7. OBORWOTI BWA NYASAE :Oboruoti bwa igoro nigo bokogamberwa amo no moika omochenu.Ase ense abanto 144,000, nigo babaganire ase oborwoti 144,000 na nigo bakogamberwa na omorwuti igoro. Oborwoti obo nigo bogokwanerwa ase egetabu gia Daniel 12, ogokora kwa abotomwa 5:1-11.Onye kore omonywa amarwa, esigara, enyasore orakonyeke koraigwe amang’ana aya erinde okonyeke nande koraganie konyuoma nabo arasome amang’ana aya.

english: Therefore, the true church should not have members who drink wine or engage in witchcraft and harm their children.
ekegusii: Aseigo Ekanisa yekeene goika ebe na abarai batari konywa edivai yogotindia naende abagambi ase enka na ase abana babo.

english: Let us remember the Holy Spirit so that we can be united in the seven pillars of wisdom (referring to the story of Ananias and Sapphira), and let us also remember those who were baptized because Peter commanded them to be baptized (Acts 2:41).
ekegusii: Titong’aina omoika omochenu buna twancheranire ase ebitambokero ebi 7 biokwegena ase LW. (Rigereria igoro ya Ananias amo na Sapphira) nagoika amonto ancherane amo nomoika amanye kobatiswa buna Petero anchete akabatiswa( Ogokora kwa abatomwa 2:41).

english: Those who serve God greatly should live holy lives without any shame (1 Timothy 3). Those who have children should raise them according to the scriptures, and their families should be known for being faithful and living righteously.
ekegusii: Abokoreria ba omonene koika babe nomokia mono batari ne chitangatangu chio oromeme (1 Timoteo 3) Onye bare na abana boiborete isiko ye,enywomo yabo nabarabwa tibari kobarenda goika banse kobarenda ase chichera chionsi.

english: The meeting is ongoing, the school headteacher has been transferred to another school, and they say he was fired due to disagreements. However, people are saying that this happened because of those who want to cause trouble. It is said that the issue concerns the land and that people are fighting over it.
ekegusii: Rituko erimo, omomura oyomo gakorwa esukuru gochia sobo, agaeta ase rikori erio riasimekire chimengere. Aaiga, aganchera nkarenge aroro abwo ase abanto barenge goeta. Bono agaika ase omogondo oyo na konyora buna aganchera nigo karenge gotiira aiga mogondo gati.

english: The disagreement is serious, and it could escalate.
ekegusii: Chimengere chiasomoiri, na koba chintambe

english: This disagreement is serious and may lead to further escalation, making it difficult to resolve the matter completely. The headteacher was transferred to Osoro, and people are saying that he left because of the problems caused by those causing trouble at the school.
ekegusii: Chimengere konye chiasomoiri na nigo chiarenge chintambe, goikera tikwarenge korora omonto ekero agoeta chibando ime. Omomura oyo orenge korokwa Osoro, kagoeta aaiga, nigo abwate omote koboko arenge gosukeria amasabo ye chibando tamoara kagweta gochia sobo.

english: Information from the reporter. The land belongs to Botabori, Magombo, Nyamira County. Photo and files by Petronillah Ogoti, Gusii.com.
ekegusii: Endemero y' omogaka. Omogondo aaria Botabori, Magombo, Nyamira County. Photo na Petronillah Ogoti, Gusii.com files.

english: It is said that when someone buys land, they should check its boundaries and ensure there are no disputes, and all documents are clear. But if there is a dispute, Osoro will be involved to help resolve the boundary issues. The elders of this land have agreed to work together to find a solution and prevent future conflicts.
ekegusii: Kare ang'e gosoka korwa mogondo, agaaka ebando eyemo konye yaberekire na ekagwa inse, n' ebando yonsi nyakeemba. Bono kiyagwa inse, Osoro akaigwa bobe mono ase ogosaria ebando eye. Akabogoria ebando eye erinde achie koyesamba kagoika inka sobo ayerie, korende akanyora nigo ere endere.

english: This situation has caused anxiety among the residents, and they are worried about what might happen next. Recently, a person was attacked near Nyanchera while returning home, and the attackers were armed.
ekegusii: Akaruo akayeruta gochia ase obonyansi ime ekiagera konye teraba ekoriegwa. Nigo yarenge endere kegima. Keri keri, omonyaroka oyomo orenge korokwa Nyanchera agaeta mbarabare, gakorwa rinani ime gotenya.

english: Nyanchera is now very insecure, and people are afraid to walk around alone at night.
ekegusii: Nyanchera nere bwetwekire chiinko, na gochaka kobongorora chinyeke korwa ase ekeemba

english: But Nyanchera has been strengthened and is trying to improve security. People are saying that if anyone causes trouble, they should be arrested and taken to court. Those who attack others and destroy property will face consequences.
ekegusii: Bono Nyanchera nigo etwegete chinko na konye orosire. Gaaika aiga ang'e nase chibando chiasimekire, agatora chinko erinde atimoke, amanye kogenda mwabo. Akarora ebando egwete obonyansi ime na akayeimokia.

english: People are working to improve security and address the issues facing the community. The youth are cooperating with the authorities, and efforts are being made to restore peace and order. As a result, the youth are becoming more responsible and contributing positively to society.
ekegusii: Akanya kobongorora chinyeke na gochiruta gochia are korwa ase ateneine. Ekeemba kegatigara kebwate chinyeke nkeigo, na kerokio agakeruta gochia ase obonyasi bwameete obotambe. Korwa abwo, akaruo akaimokia chinko chiaye na koayerera gochia sobo ase amenyete na sokoro yaye.

english: However, birds continue to fly high above.
ekegusii: Bono chinyoni chiachakire korigia ganto chibeke mboto

english: In the evening, birds fly towards their nests, carrying twigs and building materials, and they sing songs praising Nyanchera, hoping that the birds will remember the good things they have seen.
ekegusii: Emagoroba eyio, chinyoni gichikoiruruka kwerigeria ganto chibeke mboto, chikanyora chinyeke chigwete na chigatocha chinyeke chiri Nyanchera arutete inse korende chinyoni echi tichiaroche ase ekeemba kiare.

english: The rain continues to fall heavily, soaking everything and causing rivers to overflow. The water flows everywhere, destroying crops and homes, and leaving people devastated.
ekegusii: Rituko riare kobwati ebikondo bikarwa rinani ime na gosoa ase ebitii biare. Egekondo ekemo gekarora ekeemba na gekaimokia ekeemba ekio na gegachaka koria achinyeke chie chibando chiria chiatigarete ase ekeemba eke.

english: As the rain intensifies, the rivers swell and flood the surrounding areas, washing away soil and damaging infrastructure. This leads to erosion and makes it difficult for people to rebuild their lives.
ekegusii: Korora iga, ebikondo binde bikarora eke kegakare koria chinyeke gioka na gotema koura egekondo kiamwabo ekeemba eke. Korende egekondo eke gekaminchoka na korina omote igoro nyuma y' ebikondo binde komoikera.

english: And the roads are impassable due to the mud.
ekegusii: N' ebikondo nabirobio mbitagete ganto kobeka mboto

english: The water carries debris and sediment, blocking roads and making them dangerous to travel on. It also damages bridges and washes away farmland, affecting food production. Birds come down and perch on trees. People say that the owner of the land is generous and kind, and that the birds bring good luck.
ekegusii: Egekondo eke gekaruta chinyeke inke gochia igoro, echio chiachite chikagwa kw'omogaka oyomo konye ogotire. Chinyeke echi chikamera na kwama. Aiga ase omogondo bw'omogaka oyo nigo orenge omotobu na chinyeke echi chikaama buuya, mogaka oyo nigo amenyete bweka igo endagera nigo yaichire kiage kiaye.

english: Therefore, the landowner is respected by everyone and is known for his generosity. However, some people believe that he is hiding something.
ekegusii: Ase boigo, omogondo oye nigo omosinyete koburuga. Nonya nabo, tachiete komanya gose chinyeke chiamete kwaye chitari inke. Engaki yare kobwatia ye risimeka, omorakera okaba omonene ase ekenyoro eke.

english: Some people have gathered to discuss their problems and find solutions. They want to ensure that everyone benefits from the development projects taking place in the area.
ekegusii: Abanto abange bagatara gochia ase chinse chiare erinde banyore endagera bache koria ne chiamate chiabo. Ase egonga y'abanto aba bare kogenda korigia endagera omochokoro bw'omogaka oyo nere nao arenge.

english: The landowner has promised to help, and he is committed to improving the lives of the people in his community. He wants to create a safe and prosperous environment for everyone.
ekegusii: Omochokoro oyo agatara, na goika ase omogaka oyo konye ogotire. Bono oogaka oyo nigo arenge kobagera abanto endagera yaye erinde baria amo ase obwanchani n'obwororo. Engaki eyemo omoiri bw'omogaka oyo akamotarera.

english: The landowner has warned those who cause trouble, telling them to leave peacefully and return when they are ready to cooperate. But the words were ignored.
ekegusii: Omogaka oyo nigo atigaretie endagera enke mono korende akabwata akamoa endagera eri yonsi yatigarete ase ekiage kiaye, na agatebia omochokoro oye buna, "Genda orosie omogondo oo buuya erinde ocha gosimeka ekiagera gochia amatuko are motwe egiateko gi'enchara nkebe

english: But the message was not heeded, and the landowner sent someone to persuade the troublemakers to leave. Fortunately, the person succeeded in convincing them to abandon their destructive behavior.
ekegusii: Bono emaambia yare kobwatia, omochokoro oyo akaboka akagenda mogondo ekiagera nigo atagete kogokia sokoro yaye. Kagasaine korema ase endemero, akarora chibando chiamete aiga ase orosana konye rwamerire omogondo oyo ang'e bwensi.

english: The landowner then went back home, and he regretted sending the person because he realized that he had made a mistake. The person returned empty-handed, unable to understand what had happened.
ekegusii: Omochokoro bw' omogaka oyo akaburuga aiga buuya, na akarangeria sokoro yaye ache kweenekeria endagera buna yaamete buuya ase omogondo oyo. Sokoro yaye akagoka korora endagera yameete enyinge atamanyete.

english: However, the landowner continued to work hard to improve the lives of his people, and he encouraged them to support each other.
ekegusii: Bono omogaka oyo okung'untire endagera yaye yonsi pi, na koyea abaamate kobeka mboto

english: They came together and decided to help the landowner rebuild everything that had been destroyed. After much effort, the rain finally stopped.
ekegusii: Ekero basamorete, buna yare botambe omogaka oyo akaa eamate yaye yonsi endagera eye na gosanga ase oboamo. Nyuma y'engaki etari ntambe, embura egachaka gotwa.

english: But many people still suffered due to the damage caused by the flood, and they sought assistance from others. Eventually, they managed to convince the landowner to provide them with resources so that they could rebuild their homes and farms. The landowner remained steadfast and determined to restore order and prosperity to the region, despite facing numerous challenges.
ekegusii: Bono bari bonsi bang'anyete gochia chinse chi'are bakairana nchisobo, korende nyuma batarairana omogaka oyo akabarangeria na kobasesenia aba bonsi na akabaa kera omonto chinyeke erinde bachie gosimike chinsobo. Omochokoro oyo ere agatigara na sokoro yaye erinde amorende na komoroseria endagera na kera risimeko na risamora korwa ase omogondo bw'omogaka oyo nigo riare rinyinge.

english: And with the help of the community, the landowner achieved his goals.
ekegusii: Bono kera omonto ase ekenyoro, agaancha omogaka oyo.

english: Father's Bananas
ekegusii: Amatoke A'Baba

english: Catherine Groenewald
ekegusii: Catherine Groenewald

english: My father’s compound is very beautiful – it has shade, trees, and gardens. Because of this, all people come to visit my mother, and they know that I also live with my father and sometimes see the children there. She told me about her worries today. And she showed me her hands which were dirty. My mother said those hands will never be clean: because of the work she does when harvesting bananas.
ekegusii: Omogondo o'baba nigo orenge kororekana buya – nigo obwate amaemba, obori, n'emiogo. Korende ekiya ase bionsi pi biria barengeoo namataoke Nonya baba obwate abana abange, nigo namanyete buna ninche anchete ase abachokoro baye bonsi. Nigo anarete kondangeria gochia mwaye. Naende ontebia obobisi bwaye bokeboke. Nonya nigo obobisi obomo mbore atatagete gontebia: nabwo mboria bwa'se arenge gotoberia amatoke aye.

english: This story involves a disagreement between a woman and her father regarding the garden. The woman said something like this: “What the woman planted doesn’t grow well.” The woman from the garden took banana peels and started scattering them around the story. The argument continued, “Why did you take these peels?” Then she said something like this, “These are the same peels that don’t grow well.”
ekegusii: Rituko erimo inkarora egekabu ki'amakendo kebekire ase omogaso isiko mwa'baba. Ekero namoboretie buna negiaki, richibu nanyorete ndiria buna: "Ekio negekabu kiane kiogokorera ebikone" Ensemo y'egekabu keria amagoma y'eritoke narengeoo anarete gonchoreria kera rituko. Inkarengereeria inkamanya komoboria, "Amagoma aya nayaki?" Richibu naende nanyorete ndiria buna, "Aya na amagoma ane y'ogokorera ebikone.

english: The pot began to boil over with anger, the peels were both in the woman and in the garden. Because the father came to stop what was happening. “Listen, father, let us resolve this.” “Don’t bother the child, otherwise you will regret it,” he stopped her completely. The large flies made a lot of noise trying to interfere.
ekegusii: Inkagoka rende korigereria magokoro, amagoma aria amo n'egekabu keria ki'amakendo. Korende baba agantoma ing'ende komokorera egasi gete. "Gaki, baba tiga indore buna okorosia." "Tiga konyogerera omwana oyo, kora buna ogotebigwa," agantebia kare buna oyobeete. Inkaminyoka ebirundo ebinene gochia gokora egiatagete.

english: I realized then, my father calmed down his temper so that the woman and the peels would calm down too. “Father, let the woman have the garden, let her have the peels, and that’s it.” Then I heard him say, “Everything is fine as long as it grows well.” The matter ended peacefully.
ekegusii: Ekero nairanete, inkanyora baba gainkaransete isiko riaye korende gekabu keria amd n'amagoma aria tibiarengeoo. "Baba ing'ai kwaira egekabu keria, ing'ai amagoma aria are, naende ing'ai." Richibu nanyorete ndiria buna, "Noo bionsi bire ase ane yogokerera ebikone." Inkaigwa bobe sana.

english: Bananas ripened, and the father came to inspect his song which was meant to praise his house of rest. Meaning that now the house is full, the pots of bananas overflow. From that time onwards, the woman from the garden helped the father to cultivate their land together with great strength. The overflowing strength brought forth good crops.
ekegusii: Amatuko abere agaeta, na baba agantoma inchie komwoyeria akanyimbo kaye agatereire korwa enyomba yaye y'okorara. Yaani buna nasoete nyomba iga, inkaigwa rimisu ri'amatoke amatubo. Ase erumu eria yaime, noo egekabu keria ki'ababa kiogokerera ebikone biaye kiarengegetubire buya n'oborangeti obonene obogotu. Inkaimokereria oborangeti boria igoro ake igo nagotiokerera rimisu riria rigiya.

english: The father’s day arrived when he questioned, “What are you doing with the pots?” “Just beautifying my home,” he replied. “What are you looking for?” he asked her. To continue the story, it turned out that she knew how to plant bananas.
ekegusii: Eriogi ria'baba rigantaborora ekero andangeretie, "Ninki ogokora imabwo? Kora bwango ondetere enyimbo yane." Inkairana bwango nenyimbo yaye. "Ninki ogosekere?" akamboria. Okoboria gokagera inkainyora buna nigo naichanete ase okomanya koria ase abisete amatoke.

english: This story begins when the father went to find his wife, the flies making noise near the house while inspecting the bananas. The woman complained about the difficulty of life. She mentioned a banana tree that had given her a small yield. The garden was ruined and she was upset. It was very difficult, and her life was hard to endure due to the poor harvest.
ekegusii: Rituko rikobwatia ekero baba achete minto gokwania mama, inkaminyoka gochia nyomba mwaye korigereria amatoke aria naende. Inkanyore egesabo ekemo konyora giatobire. Intatabora ritoke erimo nakobisa eyanga yane ime. Inkakuneka egekabu keria naende nagosoka. Ingaeta isuku nyuma yenyomba eria inkariria. Nigo riarenge gwansa sana, ase obogima bwane konyora tindaria itoke rigwansa igo.

english: This story continues, the father again found his compound empty. He saw his wife holding a bunch of bananas. She was busy inspecting the bananas. This is a sign of hope. The house was quiet after the previous quarrel. It was very peaceful, and her life became easier thanks to the abundant banana harvest.
ekegusii: Rituko riria riarenge kobwatia, baba noo arenge mogondo oye akwaa ching'eni. Inkechobanesia na korigereria amatoke aria. Bono konyo ange onsi atobire. Ingasinywa gotiga kobogoria make, ingatabora amatoke ane. Ingasonsogoria ng'oora gochia ase omorangu, inkaigwa baba kagokora isiko. Inkanyara tu kobisa amatike aria eyanga yane ime nakomoetania gochia isiko.

english: This story continues and is like the first story. Now the father has more bananas than ever before. They decided to share them with others. Let us remember to always be generous.
ekegusii: Rituko riarenge kobwatia nigo riarenge rituko riechiro. Nigo baba arenge koira amatike aye echiro koonia. Tichieti koayerera kogenda mwaye ituko erio. Korende tinyareti komoina ngaki tambe.

english: These days passed and were remembered by mother, father and children, they wondered who helped them. That story ended, they realized they should thank each other, because the heart makes everything possible.
ekegusii: Emarogoba eyio ekero narangeretiwe na mama, tata na magokoro, inkamanya ninki bandangereria. Obotuko obwo ekero naraire, inkamanya tinkoirorera koiba naende, ebe korwa ase magokoro gose onde bwensi.

english: The father was very angry with Matongo, and Basweti and Okangoko were disturbing the children who were crying. The things they did were spoiling the homestead, and their children didn't have peace. Okangoko knew about the bad thing, so Basweti also understood the matter well.
ekegusii: Abwo kare kare ase ekenyoro kia Matongo, nigo Basweti amo n' Okangoko barenge abasani b' ogokumia. Ebitongwa ebi nigo bianchaine ekianda gia ikomi, na nigo abana babo bare gotiena aamo. Okangoko nigo amenyete egesera ime, korende Basweti ere ekamenya engoro ime.

english: However, Basweti and Okangoko were disturbing people, causing their children to cry a lot. Okangoko was trying to get medicine. The elders were discussing something. And Basweti was trying to get medicine, to discuss matters concerning Basweti.
ekegusii: Bono Basweti amo n' Okang'oko nigo barenge gochia barigeria abana babo endagera korwa chinsana ime. Okang'oko nigo arenge kobiara amagena. Oomoerio oye oturagia ebichuchu. Nere Basweti nigo arenge kobiara amagena, ko oturagia chimanu chi' ebasweti.

english: He walked around and kept looking, Okangoko went to disturb people again because he wanted to find someone to help him.
ekegusii: Okare gosegasega na koayerera, Okang'oko oyio kwagachia gochia korora buna erino riachandire omosani oye

english: That good day when it came, Basweti and Okangoko planned to disturb more people. However, those things and those stories became known. Truly, the stories which spread and the news reached the village.
ekegusii: Engaki eyemo buna yare botambe, Basweti amo n' Okang'oko bakamanora gochia korigeria amage abo endagera. Bono ebichuchu amo n' ebimanwa bigatigara bigotiena. Aaiga, ebimwana ebi mbiarenge n' ekioge ki' orwembe.

english: Be careful! The stories of Basweti were spreading everywhere.
ekegusii: Takari gwansa! Ebimwana b' Basweti nkomena bire amanyinga

english: Quickly quickly until they realized they had peace, the behavior of Basweti annoyed people together with Okangoko. Because of this, the rumors started to become true, because of the words spoken, they annoyed people greatly, making them feel uncomfortable, and they began to work together to annoy people, and truly the words spread. They annoyed people, and they made rumors start to spread.
ekegusii: Keri keri buna bakonya gotiena, emanu y' Basweti ekanyenya egechuchu gi' Okang'oko mobasokano. Korwa abwo, amanyinga agaiteka atari make, korwa ase ebigoti aria ase egechuchu kianyenyetu. Ebimanu ebi bikaoboa kerage korende bigatema chinchera ao ao erinde amanyinga gose natige goiteka, goikera bagakorera komena egechuchu eke aiga ebigoti. Bakamena egechuchu eke igo, goikera manyinga agatiga goiteka.

english: Don't let it happen again, let it be like before regarding the annoyance. The eyes of the leaders looked around, their helpers went and disturbed people. It seemed that those things were happening repeatedly because they weren't being stopped, so the child of Basweti could realize and understand.
ekegusii: Nonya nabo igo, nabo kware korora ase egechuchu eke kianyenyetu. Maiso a' bakungu igoro igoro, abaibori babo bagacha bare n' endagera. Kibaiika iga, ebichuchu bikare goteba ritangani buna ekiamwabo kianyenyetu kibagotiena, korende omwana bw' Basweti agakonya gotanga amanyinga goiteka.

english: The stories were not clear, so they needed explanation.
ekegusii: Ebimwana mbitagete goteba egento gete, korende biasinyirwe

english: It is said that Okangoko regretted the stories of Basweti that he had caused. Don't let it happen again, the stories of Basweti, sometimes they would fight and argue, but they wouldn't be clear and explained, so they continued to happen.
ekegusii: Koigwa iga, Okangoko akairaneria ebimanwa bi 'Basweti mbuya mono ase ogokonya egechuchu kiaye. Nonya nabo igo, ebimanu bi' Basweti korwa aare nabo biare kororekana buna mbiare n' eng'ana biatagete gotebia eng'ina ko bisinywa buna bigoteba.

english: A person who is wise should look at what will happen. The ancestors thought about their problems and how they would solve them, and the path led to Basweti realizing his mistakes. The ancestors thought carefully, Basweti and his stories were arguing about the path.
ekegusii: Kera oyomo akaayerera gochia ase are korara. Amatuko akanya goeta amange n'obosani bwabo bokaba bore obuya buna bware korende enchara egacha na ekaba akang'u ase Basweti konyora endagera. Amatuko amange, Basweti n'ebimanwa biaye nigo bare korara nchara.

english: The home of Basweti was very small and narrow, and the home of Okangoko was wide and spacious. But today, Okangoko refused to walk on the path. The stories of Basweti, the elders were thinking about how to stop them from speaking badly and continuing, so the rumors about the bad things and Okangoko would cease, and they would calm down and be happy.
ekegusii: Endagera y 'Basweti nigo yare ching'iti chiri chinsinini korende eye Okang'oko nigo yare bwango konyora. Eke nakio kiagerete Okangoko ere atarenge korarera nchara. Ebimanwa bi 'Basweti omoerio oye bakarora mbuya batige kobisa eng'ina na komotebia buna amanyinga y' egechuchu gi Okang'oko nigo agotononta buya kerage ekiagera ekero erwembe yanyenyete egechuchu ebigoti igoro, nabo bayamenete bakaigwa buna agwansa.

english: Truly, Basweti did not want to hear the stories of the past, but he wanted to understand the meaning of the stories. It seems that Basweti didn't listen to Okangoko, and he kept asking questions. Basweti worked hard and this time he understood, and he went to tell Okangoko.
ekegusii: Bono Basweti eere tachia koegena ebimanwa ebi amang'ana aya y' amanyinga y'ebichuchu buna agwansa korende enchara ekaba entindi mono, goikera ebimanwa b' Basweti gokwa bitari bike. Aiga nario bono Basweti abangete aite Okang'oko, erinde anyu amanyinga aye. Baswetu agaekora buna erino riamorire, na gotoma emanwa enkogoti echi korangeria Okangoko.

english: The story of the elder was told. Truly, Okangoko tried to explain and apologize, wanting to understand Basweti.
ekegusii: Emwana Enkogoti yatomirwe. Bono Okang'oko oyio okare koayerera na gosegasega, gochia gokonya Basweti

english: The story was explained and understood by Okangoko. Truly, Okangoko realized and apologized greatly, and he spoke to Basweti kindly. Basweti thanked Okangoko and promised to remember everything he had learned, and he would never forget the advice of the ancestors!
ekegusii: Emanwa eye ekaayerera na korangeria Okang'oko. Bono Okang'oko koigwa iga, okare koayerera na gosegasega bwango, na goika ase Basweti araire. Basweti agatebia Okangoko buna amorigerie monwa oye ime arore ndino ki eri rikomwatia botuko bogakia!

english: Basweti agreed with Okangoko and decided to work together to improve things. Don't let it happen again, Okangoko shouldn't refuse to learn and understand, and he shouldn't repeat the mistake. Truly, Okangoko felt sorry for hurting the feelings of Basweti.
ekegusii: Basweti agaasama n' Okang'oko agatema gose narore erino erio riachandete omosani oyo oye. Nonya nabo, Okang'oko akanyora buna tari konyara korora nonya n' erino erimo. Bono Okang'oko agasoi omotwe oye ase omonwa o Basweti ime.

english: Now it is finished. Yes! Let us try to help, Okangoko should think and find good ways to understand the feelings of Basweti!
ekegusii: Nare N' egesio. Kai! Kagendererete kogekeria, Okang'oko okare kominchoria na gotiga amarionya ime y' omonwa o Basweti!

english: Yes! Basweti calmed down and shared his feelings with him, and he revealed the secrets of Okangoko. Okangoko revealed and helped willingly. The understanding was strong, so Basweti decided to protect the head of Okangoko, which he had damaged, and he found good ways to understand the feelings of Basweti!
ekegusii: Kai! Basweti akagoka kerage na kobwatania omonwa oye na kong'usa ebigoti bi' Okang'oko mono. Okang'oko akang'usa na kogekeria kerage. Amanyinga agaiteka korende Basweti tachia kobutora omotwe ekiagera Okang'oko oyo nigo aminchoreti, agatiga amarionya aye ime y' monwa o' Basweti!

english: Truly, I also believe that Okangoko will not waste the opportunity to understand the secrets of his people, because it is important.
ekegusii: Bono eke nakio kiagerete Okang'oko nyagotichanga atatwarereti amarionya ase ebigoti biaye, nonya ngoikera rero.

english: People were saddened by the news. The former Cabinet Minister Hon Simeon Nyachae, his wife Esther Nyachae have been reported to have passed away in Nairobi hospitals due to illness. Enka nigo ere aaria ase ekenyoro kia Nyosia, Nyaribari Chache, Kisii County. Omosike Hezron Nyandusi, koru ase enka y' Mhe Nyachae nigo ateba buna emeroberio y' ebirero nechiche ebe bwango iga.

english: And indeed, prominent people from the Gusii community like Kisii County Senator Chris Obure, and Kisii County Deputy Governor Joash Maangi have conveyed their condolences. All the Gusii people, and Kenyans generally mourn the loss of this great leader. Condolences to the family of Hon Nyachae and comfort to Mama Esther.

Abagusii bonsi pi, amo n' Abakenya twensi twasiririe omong'ina omonene bw' eng'encho. Pole naende ase omochi o Mhe Nyachae ase ogosira kw' Mama Esther.
