english: Abagusii Culture And Customs XXXVIII: Remembering Our Ancestors
ekegusii: Abagusii Culture And Customs XXXVIII: Konywoma Omoiseke Otaarogeti

english: Indeed, my fellow Gusii people, don't you think we have forgotten our traditions because of modernization? Know that when someone dies, gets sick, has problems, has bad dreams, steals, or has disputes, they seek the help of elders. Many people today, due to changing times, no longer believe that these things can be solved:
ekegusii: Inee, aye tata Omogusii ominto n' omanyete buna amarieta nare togokorekania ekero tokoyakwanera? Inche namanyete buna kogenda bware, gosarwa, gochia iburu, gochia nyangi, kwaroka ,gochia maguta motwe nigo atabwekaini. Nonya nabo igo, omongina magokoro baba Nyareso ominto nigo antebetie buna amarieta aya tabwekaini buna ekobwatia:

english: 1. Dealing with Illness: This disease is widespread, and it is important to prevent it through proper hygiene for everyone. Both young and old should be vaccinated against diseases. A child who refuses medicine should be forced to take it, and treatment should be sought quickly so that the illness does not worsen!!
ekegusii: 1. Ogochia bware: Eke nakio egekamago, ogosomigwa buna obwenerete koba otarakorerwa egetambokero kende gionsi ki' omokebi gose omosari. Nigo abamura gose abanyaroka barenge kobekwa aamo basomigwa aya bagwenerete komanyigwa erinde banya korema.

english: 2. Preventing Theft: All thieves and robbers should be punished by the elders. The guilty and innocent should be investigated thoroughly. A child who steals something should be disciplined so that Enkuuri (traditional punishment) is carried out, and they should not repeat the offense, otherwise their family will face shame!!
ekegusii: Amachiko buna aya naro aregotebwa ase bari barenge koirwa bware: Obe omoremu, torigereria omokebi ekero ogosarwa, tobaisa kobwata omosari okoboko kwaye ekero akogosara, bakungu mbarenge konacha egonde ekero omware arenge koirwa inka, abamura nigo barenge korusia esimbore batari gokira goikera inka, ekero baisire goika inka abamura aba nigo barenge kobisa omware ase egetutu goikera marogoba eike ekiagera tatakeire kororwa n' onde. Ase boigo, omoyega nigo orenge kwariganigwa aare mono korwa ase omware ekiagera abanto mbaganeiri korora mware ekiagera tare gocha kogwena.

english: 3. Handling Disputes: If there is a disagreement, it should be resolved. Also, people should live peacefully and avoid conflict. Let the judges investigate the matter carefully and resolve the dispute fairly. What is a dispute? A dispute is a problem that arises from misunderstanding, which can lead to fighting and damage property.
ekegusii: Omokuuri nigo arenge gokoreranwa !!

english: The fight should not continue!!
ekegusii: 2. Ogosarwa: Aya nari enyaroka gose omomura are gokorerwa n' omokebi gose omosari. Oboremi nao aiga bwatakeire na tatakeire gokuura gose kwegosa. Omwana aise gokuura oyio nigo arenge koramwa buna Enkuuri korende nigo arenge gokoreranwa ekiagera are koba takoreranigwa, nigo kaa enywomo yaye yarekoba n' obokong'u obonene !!

english: The fight itself has caused much suffering and destruction. People say that when someone is wronged, they should seek justice and not retaliate, so that the dispute can be resolved peacefully. The mediator should help those involved find a solution and restore peace.
ekegusii: 3. Gochia iburu: Inyora buna ekero omware ataraikigwa sobo, nigo arenge kobiswa. Aaiga, abamura baganya egesunte kebe erinde bamoira sobo. Ritangani, nigo nigo abagaka barenge goikaransa bweri erinde omware oirwa nyomba. Nyuma ya amatuko atato, nigo omware arenge koroserigwa riburu. Bono riburu ninki? Riburu n' egento kebwekaine egesumu, ekio kiarenge korosigwa saiga nyomba giasimekwa esuguta erinde omware orara aroro.

english: 4. Respecting Elders: This applies to everyone regarding respect for elders. During times of hardship, elders should be given support and honored by everyone. It is not good to disrespect them or speak ill of them. By doing so, one shows respect and gratitude.
ekegusii: Esuguta tiyatakeire kwoma !!

english: Good manners are essential.
ekegusii: Esuguta eye nigo yare korendwa ase ogosiarerwa amache tebaisa kwoma. Abaminto inyora buna omware nigo arenge gouterwa omorero ase ogosegeswa na nigo orenge korendwa torima, goikera rituko omware are korwa nyomba. Omosegi nigo are koba n' omware onya komokonya esuguta tebaisa kwoma gose omorero korima.

english: By doing so, that person gains wisdom. Therefore, they should be treated with kindness and respect, especially during difficult times.
ekegusii: 4. Gochia nyangi: Eke nakio ke' eng'encho ase omware. Obotuko bw' okorwera nyomba, omware nigo arenge gokorerwa ebinto gente erinde koenekia gose obeire omomura. Nigo atakeire gosimora ebiundi korwa ase amakara arenge gwooka. Korwa abwo, nigo arenge koegwa emeri amo na amatunda amaororo erinde atakune.

english: Respectful behavior – an elder who is mistreated should not reveal it to others!!
ekegusii: Amang'ana taraera.

english: 5. Inheritance: After respecting the elders, the deceased should be mourned and remembered. A child should be raised properly so that they can carry on their parents' legacy. People say that a respectful child will never forget their roots. These words also apply to the mediator and the deceased, who should remember the teachings of their ancestors.
ekegusii: Korwa abwo, omware oyo omanya korurigwa chinyanduri. Ase boigo, nigo arenge kobugerigwa chinyabubu buna enyang'au !! Oboremereria: Nigo omware arenge gosomigwa ekero akoirwa bware erinde oboremereria bwaye bwatemwa, aiga ekero eke gie chinyangi.

english: These words, both the mediator and the deceased, agreed on a custom among the descendants of the deceased and were able to say “Yes, we agree.” And the others said, “Yes, we agree with the children.” The deceased said, “Father, we agree,” while the others said, “Yes, father, we agree with the children.” But they all disagreed about how to share the inheritance and how to distribute the wealth. Sharing inheritance is important for maintaining relationships with the descendants.
ekegusii: Oboamate obuya - omosacha okoreire enyangi tatakeire koibera abamwabo !!

english: Anyone who does not participate in this process should not interfere.
ekegusii: 5. Okwaroka: Nyuma y' ogoetera enyangi ekong'u, nigo omware arenge koirwa ase abaibori erinde bamosesenie. Ise omwana nigo arenge korwa gesarate gose saiga erinde ogenda mwaye baba n' omorugi oye kemobere !! Inyora omosacha okoreire chinyangi chia bware tatakeire koibera eamate yaye gose egesaku kiaye etugo.

english: 6. Going to Seek Help: Today, I will tell you about a situation where someone needs help and seeks assistance. They should look for trustworthy people and ask for guidance. By doing so, strong men will come forward and offer their support, helping the person overcome their challenges and achieve success.
ekegusii: Bono emaambia yaye, nigo omosegi amo n' omware baregotenena isiko mwa abaibori b' omware erinde omanya kobora "Ee borania ngo" Ise oiraneria "Ea borania chiombe n' abana" Omware oboria "Baba borania ango" ng'ina oiraneria "Ee tata borania chiombe n' abana" Aiga baruo bairana saiga kwarigania gochia roche gwesibia na kwearigania kobekerwa amaguta. Okoborania oko nakuo kwarenge koba ogosesenia kwa abaibori.

english: It is important to protect those seeking help, especially children!! One should also protect their own possessions. The person should be shown compassion and understanding. By doing so, today, they have found a way to express their gratitude to those who helped them.
ekegusii: Onye omware oyo tarenge na ise, nigo arenge gochia oise moke.

english: Today, they have realized the importance of kindness and generosity. These words also apply to the evening, when someone remembers past events. Yes. They decide to visit their friend and seek advice, sharing their concerns and discussing matters with their neighbors. Through this, the person finds solutions to their problems and gains strength from their community. Here are some guidelines for achieving success:
ekegusii: 6. Kogenda maguta motwe: Eye nero enchera y' omoerio omware arenge goetera erinde orwera nyomba. Amarwa nigo arenge gosiikwa ase egetera na koengwa. Korwa abwo, amabere nigo arenge kororanigwa n' abagaka abanene baturwa na gochikwa erinde omware oretwa ase bare erinde ache goakwa maguta motwe.

english: [ I ]. Respect everyone and show humility, allowing wise people to guide you and teach you wisdom.
ekegusii: Ise nigo arenge gosiberia amarwa, osiarera omwana oye !! Eriakabere nigo arenge gosiba amabere naro oyamosiarera. Nigo omware arenge gosiarerwa obosio igoro. Korwa abwo, Ise nigo arenge kobwata amaguta, omoaka omotonyeria omotwe igoro. Eye nero yare koorokia buna oyo obeire omomura oisaneire.

english: [ II ]. Be humble and seek knowledge from those who possess it, striving for excellence.
ekegusii: Bono emogoroba eye, oyo orure bware tarenge koirana ase aaramerete. Yaya. Nigo arenge kogenda sobo omosegi oye orara, erinde bogokia mambia yaye, baumerana na abande barure nyomba. Korwa bono, omomura oyo nigo arenge kobwatia amachiko aetwe buna:

english: [ III ]. Be patient and persevere, working hard towards your goals.
ekegusii: [ I ]. Tagosoa mwa ng'ina goikera oite eng'iti gose arigie embori aitere abagaka amanye gosoa mwa ng'ina !!

english: [ IV ]. Be diligent, honest, hardworking, resourceful, courageous, compassionate, and strive for perfection in everything you do.
ekegusii: [ II ]. Tare gosoa mwa ng'ina goetera egesieri kia borenge korende kia gesaku.

english: [ V ]. Be grateful for the blessings you receive and acknowledge the contributions of others. Show respect to your ancestors and honor their memory, remembering those who came before you.
ekegusii: [ III ]. Tancheire gosoa ase ng'ina na ise bare korara !!

english: Please remember and cherish the lessons learned from Maguta Motwe and the spirit of Baba Nyareso Ominto. Mwanyagetinge.com/2015
ekegusii: [ IV ]. Tancheire gosia, gotenya, koruga, gochia roche, kwaga enchagu, gosonga, gochia etinga gose gokora chigasi chiri chinyaroka chiare gokora.

english: Thank you for your attention, Baba Nyareso Ominto, my mother and thank you for listening.
ekegusii: [ V ]. Taganeiri konya kobera ase abanyaroka bare. Nigo aganeiri gosika abaibori baye, abanene baye gose bari ba nsoni.

english: Long ago, a story was told about people who lived in those days. This story is also known by the people of Bondonya, Bomachoge. This story involves customs, traditions, rituals, and laws. Some stories are true, some are known within homes, and some are known outside homes.
ekegusii: Abwo kare kare, ching’iti chi’orosana nchiarenge aroro. Bono chingiti echi nigo chiamenyete n’ oboamo amo n’ omorembe aaiga ase rinani ria Bondonya, Bomachoge. Chingingiti echi nigo chiarenge buna ebikondo, chinyang’au, ebiobiri, amo n' chingabi. Nchire chiare koria amato, nchire chiamenyete amache ime, na nchire chiamenyete ebiswa ime.

english: In this current time, a leader has emerged who understands the ways of the world. Let us work together so that we can improve our lives. This matter concerns the entire community of Bondonya. This matter requires cooperation from the entire community.
ekegusii: Engaki eyemo, omorakera omotindi ogaateka ase rinani eri ime. Riberera rigaichora mono, goikera amache akaba botu boke. Endo nero yatenenerete ching’iti echi chionsi aiga Bondonya. Bono Endo ekarangeria omosangererekano bwe ching’iti echi chionsi.

english: Regarding that cooperation, the story that has been passed down has ten chapters, which makes it easy for people to understand. Because of this story, the story that has been passed down is true and helps people live well.
ekegusii: Ase omosangererekano oyo, ching’iti echi chikaigwana chireme egesima, erinde gose nchinyore amache chinywe. Obwango obwo obwo, ching’iti echi chikaigwana buna nigo chiare kobwaterana, erinde chireme egesima eke n' oboamo.

english: This elder speaks strongly and encourages people to embrace development!!
ekegusii: Bono Ogasusu otameire buna onyorire orogendo gochia mache ng'umbu !!

english: The story that is being discussed has ten chapters. Remember this, the elder has completed his mission and has shown that he cares about the progress of the people, embracing development. Because of this story, the story that belongs to the elder is remembered.
ekegusii: Ching’iti echi chigakunama gokunya egesima. Nonya nabo igo, Ogasusu ere taikerana ekiagera nigo atebete buna nigo anyorete esabari ya mobasokano, kogenda mache ng’umbu. Obwango obwo, chingiti echi tichieegena Ogasusu nonya.

english: This friend Ogankuru supports the efforts of the elder and wants everyone to know what he has done. Ogankuru carries a message of support for the elder’s efforts, wanting everyone to understand that the elder’s actions are beneficial and help people remember and appreciate their heritage.
ekegusii: Bono chigatebi Ogankuru akore obotuki bw’ Ogasusu erinde bamanye ase achiete. Ogankuru agatwara engaki enkong’u gokora obotuki bw’ okomanya ase Ogasusu arenge koreng’ana nase engaki eye ching’iti chinde chiare gokunya egesima gose mbanyore amache nonya n’ amasinini.

english: All along, the elder has shared wisdom and knowledge with the people, helping them understand their culture. Ogankuru appreciates the teachings of the elder and wants him to continue guiding them.
ekegusii: Chingaki echi chionsi, Ogasusu nigo ebisete mbarabare nase egesima eke kiare gokunywa, korende Ogankuru tamanya. Ogankuru akairana agatebia ching’iti chinde buna taigeti konyora ase Ogasusu aberete.

english: This important event took place in Bondonya, and the story spread throughout the land and beyond. The council decided to share the knowledge with the people of Bondonya, Bomachoge Chache district, Kisii County. Mwanyagetinge.com/2014
ekegusii: Bono ekero egiateko ekene giachicha aaria Bondonya, chingiti chinyinge chiagatwara erango y' amache enene na korea mono. Ogakondo ogatengerete korwa mbarabare y' egesima aaria Bondonya, Bomachoge Chache yaito, Kisii County. Mwanyagetinge.com/2014

english: Finally, the people who were involved in the story returned home and rejoiced because the elder did not refuse to listen. They thanked the elder for listening to their concerns, and the story continued to be told so that future generations could learn from it. The spokesperson spoke eloquently, encouraging the elder to continue listening to the people’s needs.
ekegusii: Keri keri, amache agatoka n' ching’iti echi chikaigwa buya na gotiana buna Ogasusu tabaisa koyanywa. Gotanga Ogasusu tanywa amache aya, ching’iti echi chigatebania buna nere buya bebange erinde barende amache aya. Oganchogu akaba eng’iti entang’ani koyarenda erinde Ogasusu tabaisa koyanywa ekero bataiyo aang’e.

english: In conclusion, the elder realized the importance of understanding the people. During this gathering, the elder promised to always listen and address the issues affecting the community, ensuring that everyone benefits from progress. The elder assured the spokesperson that he would never neglect the welfare of the people.
ekegusii: Chintunde nke igo, Ogasusu okare komingiriara goikera aiga ase egesima. Ekero aaika mbarabare n' egesima, Ogasusu agachaka goseka na goaka omonu gakomena oboke na goteba buna bokomwansera mono. Ogasusu agateba buna ere tarenge na botonu bw’okonywa amache, korende agatebia Oganchogu nere aigwe buna oboke obo bware gotonontera monu.

english: This spokesperson is respected by everyone.
ekegusii: Bono Oganchogu osibirwe ase omote

english: The spokesperson praised the efforts made and expressed his gratitude for the positive impact on the community!! He acknowledged the elder’s dedication to improving the lives of the people and commended his commitment to unity. The spokesperson was honored by the elder, who wrote a letter recognizing his contributions to the community and praising his leadership qualities!! This matter will be remembered forever as a symbol of cooperation.
ekegusii: Oganchogu akarusia oboke nakomena na agataka arie obonge !! Aaiga nario Ogasusu amotebetie buna tiga amosibe ase ekiiriri kere, erinde amene oboke obo obwansu, goikera bomoisane. Oganchogu agasibwa ase omote n' Ogasusu akanyora ribaga akarindoka gochia ase egesima eke na konywa amache, na gwesibia akaraba se !! Korwa abwo, akarwoo akagenda bwoye ase arenge koebisa.

english: However, this story also highlights the importance of listening to others. The spokesperson encouraged everyone to embrace dialogue and work together to achieve common goals. The story emphasizes the need for mutual respect and understanding.
ekegusii: Bono ching’iti ekero chiairanete konywa amache chikanyora amache taiyo n' Oganchogu nigo asibire na tare konyara gwesibora. Chingiti echi chikaigwa bobe pi. Rituko riare kobwatia, bakabeka Emamba erende amache aya erinde Ogasusu tabaisa koyanywa na koyaesiberia.

english: The elder agreed to support the initiative and promised to provide guidance and resources. However, Emamba opposed this idea, fearing that the elder might refuse to listen and disregard their concerns.
ekegusii: Ogasusu agasoa ekebuyu ime na gochaka goturungana kagokwana na goseka gochia ase Emamba yarenge. Bono Emamba korora aya, ekarora nebikone na gotama egatiga Ogasusu okonywa amache na gwesibia.

english: The story concludes with a message of hope and resilience. It emphasizes the power of collaboration and the importance of staying true to one’s values. All voices deserve to be heard, and everyone should strive to create a better future for themselves and their communities.
ekegusii: Ching’iti chionsi ekero chiairanete chikanyora Emamba nigo yatamete ekero yaroche ekebuyu kegoturungana na gokwana na goseka mono. Ebioto bionsi bikanyorera ribaga na gosoa amache aya ime na gochaka kwoga na goaka ontimbu.

english: This final chapter ends with a call to action and encourages everyone to participate in building a stronger society. The story reminds us that we all have a role to play in shaping our destiny and creating a world where everyone can thrive. The council resolved to ensure that the elder continues to listen to the people and address their concerns, fostering a sense of belonging and empowerment.
ekegusii: Endo ekaigwa bobe na gotogonya ase eriogi rinene. Ching’iti chionsi chikaondoka kerage ekiagera Endo nigo yagechetigwe mono. Ogakondo agaesokia na goteba buna tiga ateme nabo arabwate Ogasusu oyo obachandire ase a matuko atari make.

english: The council decided to investigate the matter further and seek clarification from the elder regarding his intentions. The council wanted to ensure that the elder would continue to prioritize the needs of the community and remain accountable to the people he serves.
ekegusii: Ogakondo agaancherwa korenda egesima eke kiabo erinde Ogasusu tabaisa goika konywa amache gose koyatumia gwesibia omobere oye naende. Ogakondo akarosia omobwekano bw’ omorabera omuuya omonyakieni kerage.

english: This issue sparked debate among members, and the council decided to hold a meeting to discuss the matter further. The council believed that transparency and open communication were essential for maintaining trust and ensuring accountability. They hoped to reach a consensus that would benefit both the elder and the community.
ekegusii: Ching’iti chikagokigwa ne ekebwekane eke. Ogankondo akabeka ekenanti erinde onde aise koyebwata nigo kware konanterera. Omobwekano oyo okabekwa aang’e ne egesima n' Ogankuru akeebisa erinde tarorekana n' Ogasusu ase aberete.

english: But the elder refused to compromise!!
ekegusii: Bono Ogasusu okare kwerindori gocha buna botambe !!

english: The elder insisted on continuing the discussion, hoping to find a solution that would satisfy everyone involved. Indeed!! The elder walked away, his eyes filled with determination, ready to face any challenge and overcome any obstacle.
ekegusii: Ogasusu agacha buna botambe korende tarora onde orendete egesima eke. Kai !! Ogasusu akagenda rioka korende amaiso aye akagokigwa n’ omorabera oteneine aang’e n’ egesima eke korende otarenge gokwana na Ogasusu.

english: The elder rejected the proposal, believing it would undermine his authority. But when he realized his mistake, he apologized and pledged to cooperate fully. And then he understood the value of humility!! He learned a valuable lesson, realizing that true strength lies in admitting one’s mistakes.
ekegusii: Ogasusu akaruo agakuna omorabera oyo. Bono buna amokunete okoboko kwaye gokananta na akaira okoboko koria gwatigarete erinde ang’use oko konde. Naboigo oko gokananta na agasinywa buna are gokora !! Agachia gotema igo, ekaba akong’u.

english: Throughout the entire process, the council remained committed to finding a fair and equitable resolution. Ultimately, the council challenged the narrative presented by the elder, demanding honesty and transparency. The story shows how the elder manipulated events to gain favor with the community.
ekegusii: Chingaki echi chionsi, Ogakondo nigo amotengerete korwa egetutu kiare mbarabare ne egesima eke. Ake ake, Ogankondo akarangeria ching’iti chiamwabo. Chingiti echi chikaminyoka gocha na konyora Ogasusu nigo anantete ase ekebwekane eke ki’ omorabera. Bono ching’iti echi chigachaka koa Ogasusu ebinyerere.

english: The elder was saddened by this turn of events, realizing that his actions had caused harm. But they warned him that if they discovered he was deceiving them, they would expose his deceitful behavior and prevent him from exploiting the community. The deception was revealed by a witness who testified against the elder, exposing his manipulative tactics. After the witness spoke, the elder became remorseful and sought forgiveness. This incident served as a cautionary tale, reminding everyone of the importance of integrity.
ekegusii: Ogasusu akarera igo, korende onde taiyo omorocherete amabera. Bono bagateba buna nigo bare gwokia omorero eriinde basambe Ogasusu oyo obachandete ase amatuko atari amake. Omorero okabekwa n' Endo ekanantoria Ogasusu na komobwata amorute riiko. Riria Endo yamobwata iga, Ogasusu akaminchoria na koniantoka ne chimbero chimbariri. Ching’iti echi chigachia komominyoki igo, tichiamoikera.

english: In conclusion, the elder acknowledged his wrongdoing and vowed to make amends. He promised to be more honest and transparent in his dealings with the community.
ekegusii: Korwa erio, Ogasusu karorire ching’iti chi’ orosana, nigo agotama.

english: Long ago, Oganchogu went to visit his father Egucha who lived in Ogembo. Later, he also went to talk to Okang'ubo, a very wealthy man who owned many cows. His homestead was beautiful, and his cows were numerous and he had many herdsmen.
ekegusii: Abwo kare kare, Oganchogu narenge ase engegu y' oroche rwe Egucha aaria Ogembo. Abwo mbarabare, nigo arenge kogamba n' Okang'ubo, oyio ocheng'enaine amache igoro. Ase engaki eye, oroche oro nigo rwarenge orosinini na ndwarenge n' mache mange.

english: “What did Okangubo say to him?” Oganchogu asked curiously.
ekegusii: Inaki yaa Okangubo mbokiete abwo?" Oganchogu okare koboria, kagosiberia amache

english: His homestead was beautiful, and his cows were numerous, so Oganchogu decided to go and thoroughly investigate Okang'ubo’s wealth. This made him think, Oganchogu told Okang'ubo, “You are rich and yet you still carry things on your head. Don’t be ashamed of working hard. It is good to work like others, don’t despise work because it is considered lowly.”
ekegusii: Ase eng'encho oroche oro rwarenge oroke mono Oganchogu nigo yare komobera aororo komorora Okang'ubo ekero are roche. Bono kibagendererete kogamba, Oganchogu agatebia Okang'ubo buna "Aaye n' omonene na nigo ore n' omobere omonene kerage. Nainche tindi moke. Igo nere buya aye obe omoruoti ase oroche, nainche imbe omoruoti bwe ense enkamoku

english: Okangubo listened attentively to what Oganchogu said and then replied, “Listen, people should not boast about their wealth; they should remember that everything they have can disappear quickly and they should avoid arrogance and pride.”
ekegusii: Okangubo akanya gocheng'enena ang'e n' ase Oganchogu ateneine mbarabare n' engegu y' oroche oro na goitaberia buna "Toise koba abaruoti nabo togokora kende gionsi toratake engaki ende yonsi onde atari gotokania na tokore ching'iti chiri chinsiniini chikore egasi torachitebie

english: But Ogasusu, who understood everything, warned them against greed!!
ekegusii: Bono Ogasusu oyio oikaransete otengerete korwa egetutu ime, kagosiiba erongori rikairo !!

english: Despite this, Ogasusu also went later, wanting to see the wealth that everyone was talking about. And Oganchogu and Okang'ubo didn’t realize that Ogasusu had come to find out whether they would share their wealth, lest their children suffer from poverty and hardship.
ekegusii: Nonya nabo igo, Ogasusu nao arenge mbarabare, ebisete egetutu kiarenge aange n' oroche oro. Bono Oganchogu n' Okangubo tibamanyete buna Ogasusu nao atengererete buna bare koroberia, erinde bachiche gochanda ching'iti chiri chi'orosana chinke engaki chiabeire chikogamba aiga.

english: Ogasusu arrived quietly and heard their conversation about life, realizing that they were discussing how to avoid greed. But unfortunately, Ogasusu failed to make Oganchogu understand his point. And again, he noticed something strange that made Oganchogu appear unwilling to listen.
ekegusii: Ogasusu akaigwa bobe na gweteb ase omoyo oye ime buna goika atange Oganchogu n' Okangubo korwa ase ogotenenera ching'iti chi'orosana. Ase boigo, Ogasusu tatagete Oganchogu atenenere ching'iti chie ense. Ase ig,o akarigia chinchera chio ogocha gotangaOganchogu taira oboteneneri.

english: “I will give you some advice,” Ogasusu said loudly.
ekegusii: Gaki nkonye ase ogwancha kwao" Ogasusu okare koruta enduru

english: Then Ogasusu began to explain how important it was to help those in need, reminding them that someday they too might face difficulties. And Oganchogu continued to drink beer while visiting his father’s homestead. Because of this, Ogasusu observed carefully and walked over to tell Okang'ubo, “I will give you some advice.”
ekegusii: Bono Ogasusu akarengereria korigia obong'ainereria erinde atange ching'iti echi ibere tichibaisa kogamba nonya nake. Ekero Oganchogu akora konywa amache agasuka korwa ase engegu eye y' oroche. Korwa abwo, Ogasusu akarigia engori entaambe na kogenda goikera ase oroche oro rware na gochaka korangeria Okangubo okomoteba buna "Gaki nkonye ase ogwancha kwao

english: Okangubo asked, “Why are you saying that?” Then Ogasusu explained, “A cow today may stumble and fall. So, let me advise you to always have some reserve for emergencies.” Okangubo wondered, “What does this mean?”
ekegusii: Okangubo akaboria buna "Nninki kiaba gose?" Abwo nario Ogasusu airanereretie ogoteba buna "Eng'ombe yane nigo yaratera etintira ime. Bono nasinyirwe koyekonya erwe etintira eye ime" Okangubo agaitaberia buna "Ninki oroche indagokonye ?

english: It happened that Ogasusu said, “Let us slaughter this cow, and distribute the meat among the poor, and let us also slaughter another cow which we shall save for times of famine. Let us therefore share this cow so that when there is drought, we will have something to eat.”
ekegusii: Koigwa iga, Ogasusu agateba buna, "Tiga insibe engori eye, erinde inyeranderere omobere oo bwensi na insibe eng'ombe eria ekare ensemo eri ya moino. Bono kinasibire engombe yane na kingoteba buna ng'usa, ong'use bokong'u ekiagera eng'ombe eye n' enene kerage

english: Okangubo responded, saying he was afraid of losing his possessions, but he pretended to agree. And Okangubo went back to his homestead and secretly informed Ogasusu. With the cow that was slaughtered, they shared it with the needy people of Okangubo’s clan.
ekegusii: Okangubo agateba buna nabo akonyara kong'usa n' chinguru, atabwati mochando nonya. Bono Okangubo agatenena ase engegu igoro na gotenena aang'e n' Ogasusu. Ne engori egasibwa obogatigati bw' enda y' Okangubo.

english: Because of this, Ogasusu rejoiced and decided to share the remaining cow with Oganchogu and offer him guidance. “Oganchogu, I will give you some advice,” Ogasusu said with determination. “What is it?” Oganchogu inquired. Ogasusu explained that his cow had stumbled and fallen, and he needed to find a way to recover it.
ekegusii: Korwa abwo, Ogasusu akabogoria na kong'usa engori gochia ase Oganchogu arenge na komonyora. "Oganchogu gaaki inkonye" Ogasusu okare gokwana n' amabera. "Ninki ekebe?" Oganchogu akamoboria. Ogasusu agaitaberia ogoteba buna eng'ombe yaye nigo yaratera etintira ime, naende yasinyirwe kwerusia ime.

english: “What prevents you from doing so?” Oganchogu asked. “I say, let us slaughter this cow and distribute the meat among the poor, and let us also slaughter another cow which we shall save for times of famine, so that when there is drought, we will have something to eat,” Ogasusu reiterated.
ekegusii: Ninki otagete nkore bono?" Oganchogu akaboria. "Gaki tiga insibe engori ase omobere oo erinde insibe n' eng'ombe yane ase eraterete, erinde imanye kogotebia buna ng'usa na ong'use bokong'u ekiagera eng'ombe eye nigo ere enene kerage" Ogasusu akairaneria.

english: Again, Oganchogu replied that he was also afraid of losing his livestock due to hardship, and he feared being left with nothing!!
ekegusii: Korora amabera, Oganchogu agateba buna ere nabo akongusa chiombe isato ase entunde eyemo, naende taigwa kende nonya !!

english: Again, Oganchogu stated that he would rather hoard his wealth than share it with others, fearing future problems. Ogasusu took the cow and went to hide it near the riverbank, away from them. After a while, he returned and found everyone still arguing about sharing, constantly changing their minds.
ekegusii: Korora amabera, Oganchogu agateba buna ere tabwati bokong'u ekiagera nabo akong'usa chiombe isato ase entunda eyemo atari nabokong'u bonde bwensi !! Ogasusu agasiba engori na kogenda akeebisa ase egetutu kende kiarenge ang'e n' oroche oro. Korwa aaiga ase ebisete, nabo arenge korora ching'iti echi chionsi ibere buna chiare kong'usanana, chiarigerereti chisemo ao ao chitari kororana.

english: Because of this, Ogasusu questioned why they weren’t willing to share the cow. Oganchogu and Okangubo wondered and considered sharing the cow. It became clear that their reluctance stemmed from fear and selfishness.
ekegusii: Korwa abwo, Ogasusu akababoria gose babeire aang'e kong'use engori. Oganchogu n' Okangubo bagaitaberia na gochaka kong'usa engori. Chikaigwa buna oborito bwarenge na kogasana kong'usa ne chinguru chinene kerage.

english: These people then shared the cow with the needy families.
ekegusii: Aba babere bakang'usa engori ase engaki entambe.

english: Oganchogu was upset. Suddenly, Okangubo began to milk the cow and carelessly spilled the milk everywhere!! This caused anger and frustration, and he quickly hid the cow from Okangubo and ran away. Oganchogu accused Okangubo of stealing Ogasusu’s cow.
ekegusii: Oganchogu akarosa. Omoerio, oye, Okangubo akamong'usa na komoiyeraia akagwa roche ime !! Bono gasoa ase oroche, akarora engori gesibire ase Okangubo na koigwa bobe. Oganchogu akaboria Okangubo buna ninki akorera eng'ombe ya Oasusu.

english: Oganchogu walked with a heavy heart and tried to understand why Okangubo had stolen Ogasusu’s cow. But Okangubo fell into a trap and confessed to Oganchogu, saying, “Yes, I did it. Is it really Ogasusu’s cow?”
ekegusii: Oganchogu akaba n' obororo obonge na gotaka komanya buna ninki Okangubo akorerete eng'ombe y' Ogasusu. Nere Okangubo akaigwa obororo na gotebia Oganchogu buna "Aye nigo okong'aina. Ingai eng'ombe y' Ogasusu ere ?

english: Ogasusu and the elders gathered, and because of their wisdom, they resolved the dispute and brought peace. The elders agreed that the cow should be returned to its owner. Okangubo was ashamed and apologized to Oganchogu and started milking the cow again.
ekegusii: Ogasusu engaki eye ching'iti echi ibere chikonya koborania amaboria, nigo ebisete egetutu ime gekonya goseka ng'ora ng'ora. Ching'iti echi naende chigachaka kong'usa engori eye buya. Okangubo akarosa entunde eye n' Oganchogu akamong'usa na komorusia amache ime.

english: Ogasusu visited Matiebo and expressed his gratitude.
ekegusii: Ogasusu obeire Matiebo, na gosaria emeroberio

english: During that time, the cow gave birth to a calf, and Oganchogu was overjoyed. Meanwhile, Okangubo continued to steal and hide the milk. Because of this, Oganchogu realized his mistake and sought forgiveness. Okangubo also admitted his wrongdoing and promised to stop. Ogasusu happily witnessed the reconciliation and praised them both for their honesty.
ekegusii: Obwango obwo obwo, engori ekabutoka na Oganchogu agaaka inse ne chinguru chinene. Ase boigo, Okangubo akairana na goaka inse amache ime. Korwa abo, Oganchogu akaimoka na gotama gochia orosana ime. Okangubo nero agaaka ontimbu gochia oroche gati gati.

english: Tucker Childs: People are saying that people from Kim area of Sierra Leone are suffering. Those who say this are saying it's bad.
ekegusii: Tucker Childs: Ingotepu are omonwa bwa abanto ba Kim aaria Sierra Leone otarasira. Abanyene omonwa oyio tibari na acha.

english: I read in the NYtimes yesterday that people from Kim area of Sierra Leone were kidnapped 24 people. It seems this issue is serious because people are saying that this kidnapping has happened to them too. Very sad. The people there are saying that they are afraid because of this situation. That means those people are scared because of this kidnapping happening around them.
ekegusii: Inasomete ase NYtimes igoro inga egesaku gia Kim aaria Sierra Leone nigo kebwate abanto 24 boka. Kiabeire inga obwoba imbore aroro inga omonwa bwe egesaku eke nabo orasire torigereretie iga. Maiso marore. Abanto abange ase egesaku eke batigire gokwana omonu obo. Yaani inga abande nigo banchete gokwana omonu bwe egesaku kende ekeao.

english: It's very difficult. Mende. They are talking about people being afraid of the Mende. Some people are able to help people from Kim but they are afraid of the Mende. But some people have already started running away, because of this fear, they are also running away. This thing is really making things hard for people to live comfortably. These problems are very big and causing trouble for everyone. Who can help these people so that they can overcome this problem? Who will help those people who are currently struggling? I don't know.
ekegusii: Ekerage sana. Mende. Nigo bagokwana omonu okorokwa Mende. Abange bari bagakwanire omonwa o Kim bono nigo bagokwana Mende. Bari abagotu buna bagendererete gosira, omonu obo noro nabo ogendererete gosira.Eke tari kerokio egesaku egetangani gosira pi korwa ense gose gosiria omonu obo. Ebisaku ebinge sana biasirire korwa ense eye enchera enga buna eyio.Ninki kiabete ase omonu oyo gose egesaku eke gosira ekabira eyio? Ninki gekogera abanyene omonu oyo batari gochari? Inche timanyeti.

english: I remember when I was young, we used to play games with our friends, and we always felt proud to be Gusii. We had a game we played, which showed how strong the Gusii culture was. I remember well the story of teacher Sebelius Nyangau, who taught us about the history of Gesure. Being a Gusii person, it's something to be proud of, and it's something to carry forward. Because I also grew up with this pride of being a Gusii. Our traditions. Our customs. The pride of being a Gusii person has been passed down through generations.
ekegusii: Ninginyorete ekero narenge kerasi eyemo impaka isato, nabo tware gwancherwa gokwana Ekegusii. Ekero twaika kerasi inye, togakanigwa titokwana Ekegusii esukuru ime. Ninginyorete sana ekiagera omwarimu Sebeliusi Nyangau nere orenge omwarimu bwe Egesongo ase epuremari ya Gesure. Kware gokwana Ekegusii, nigo kware kwerorera aya agocha na aya kogenda. Bono inche nabo nakinete inde na obwoba bwo ogokwana Ekegusii. Omonu intachorete. Omonu naiboreretwe. Obwoba bwa ogokwana Ekegusii bogaonchoka bokaba obosoku gokwana Ekegusii.

english: We also went to Nyamagwa, where people spoke proudly about the Gusii culture, and they said it was like a treasure. Wonderful. Beautiful. That village. We learned. Stories. We realized that growing up with this tradition helps build character. This pride makes people think deeply. The traditions of the Gusii people have helped shape their lives over many years.
ekegusii: Ekero narenge Nyamagwa, onde bwensi orenge gokwana Ekegusii ere nigo arenge gochaywa inga nigo are omonto bwe risabu. Elokol. Mshamba. Oyo ushago. Otasometie. omoriri. Ekero okinete kobwate obosoku bwo ogokwana omonu oo. Obwoba bwo ogokwana omonu oo. Akongu sana gosamusa ebinto buna ebio korwa obongo bwao. Ayio naro amberete inche ekero ingokina. Obongo bwane. Ebirengererio biane igoro ya Ekegusii nigo biaigoka emiaka etato yaerire.

english: We also went to Kangema, Muranga, and we saw how people from Egeswaeli celebrate the culture of Egesongo. Kangema has raised children who respect their heritage. There is a school there, and we found about 20 Gusii people. America also celebrates the culture of Egesongo. Is it possible to establish a connection between Americans and schools that support the Gusii culture? Americans may not understand the importance of Egesongo. Is it right to ask them? Maybe we should show them what they are missing out on.
ekegusii: Ekero nagenda Kangema, Muranga, bono ekarasimisa inga inkwane Egeswaeli gose Egesongo. kangema nigo yabwate abana korwa ase kera ekabira. Ase esukuru engima, nigo twarenge Abagusii ange 20. Amerika nero ekarasimisa inkwane Egesongo. Amangana e chigasi amo na esukuru ingai ogochia gokwanera Ekegusii? Abaamerika nigo batagete okwane Egesongo. Tari sobo ore? Tindi kobarusia amagoso korengereria igo.

english: It's true that they don't know much about Egesongo. They don't understand its value unless they become part of it. They need to learn about its accent. Those who haven't experienced it, they too can learn about it, just like everyone else. It's like discovering hidden treasures. The accent is important.
ekegusii: Tari igo rioka inga nigo batagete okwane Egesongo. Nigo batagete okwane buna bagokwana. Goika bweegeri eaksenti yabo. Onye tari bo, aye nabo okona koborigwa kera rituko inga ingai seino. Neba inga kwaairwe amasakara ya obomenyo.Eaksenti nigo egokorwa.

english: It's true that many Americans don't understand the value of their own cultures. Many people around the world don't understand how important it is to preserve their traditions and appreciate the richness of African cultures. The experience of Americans is often shaped by someone like Tucker Childs, who comes from Sierra Leone. Teacher Childs studied at Portland State University in Oregon. He also collaborated with the University of London in England. He didn't understand the importance of preserving and appreciating his heritage.
ekegusii: Tari kera Omoamerika otagete okwane buna agokwana. Abande imbare aroro batagete inga kera egesaku gekwane omonu oye na gokora ebinto bie ekemira biaye. Bono abande bachire seito Afrika erinde baanse korika na gotepu emenu ya AbaAfrika etarasira. Oyomo bwa AbaAmerika abwo nigo akorokwa Tucker Childs oyio okare aaria Sierra Leone. Omwarimu Childs nigo agosomia aaria Portland State University ime ya Oregon. Nigo abwateranete amo ne yunivasiti ya London aaria Bongeresa. Nigo atagete gotepu na kogacha emenu yaito etarasira.

english: When I read that story, I wondered: If those people were alive today, would they understand why it's important to preserve our traditions? Would they work with Americans to achieve this goal? What about their descendants? What will happen to future generations? This pride can help us overcome challenges. This knowledge is worth more than 6000 things.
ekegusii: Ekero nasomete omogano oyo, nigo neboretie: Ase abanto aba be egesaku gia kim batigarete, onde taiyo otagete korika omonu obo? Nigo bagotiga omonu obo orikwe amo na AbaAmerika? Ingai abagaka babo bare? Abasae rende? Obongo bwane bokagenderera koberoroka. Ense eye nigo ebwate emenu 6000.

english: Of those 6000 things, 2000 come from Africa. Of those 2000 things that came from Africa, where did they end up? Are they on the internet? Is there anyone who doesn't care about history? Do they even have a place? Does history repeat itself because we don't learn from it? How many years will it take for them to remember history? Let's think about it. One thing is certain: If we don't learn from history, we are doomed to repeat it. But history has shown that people can overcome obstacles.
ekegusii: Ase emenu eyio 6000, emenu 2000 nigo ere ime ya Afrika. Ase emenu eye 2000 etigarete Afrika, yarikiru ande? AbaAfrika Intochareti? Gose titori gochari impaka Omosongo ototebereiri? Nabo ere igo? Mosongo ataratotebia igo gento ekio tikeri kiya? Emiaka nerenga totagete Omosongo anya gototebereria? Inche timanyeti. Egento imanyete neke: Eke tari gento getagete eserikali etotebereri. Gose Omosongo arine endege gocha gototebia. Nabo togoansa gwekorera intwe tweka.

We know that those things are still being discovered. It's like uncovering ancient artifacts. These things tell stories about our ancestors.

Timanyeti gose emenwa eye yarikirwe gose kogachwa. Naratebigwe inga inga imbuya emenwa esire. Inga emenwa nigo ekorenta obokenyomba.

It exists on computers and phones. It exists on Facebook, Myspace, Ekegusii.Org, Kisii.Com….The Gusii people want to connect with each other and share their experiences.

There's no point in saying that history repeats itself if we don't learn from it. The Gusii people don't believe that. They understand this.

english: Parajubaea torallyi grows natively in the moist forests of South America. Currently, it is cultivated as an ornamental tree and in arboretums, Bolivia being its main center of interest due to its large population, which is threatened by deforestation.
ekegusii: Parajubaea torallyi n’omote omuya korwa Amerika ya maate. Korende, tori gosimekwa mono isiko y’ase yachakerete na abaremi, Bolivia, esengencho y’echintetere chiaye chinene, eyio emoneti rigori rinene ase ogoetigwa enyancha.

english: Found in Bolivia, it grows at altitudes between 2700–3400 meters above sea level in the Inter-Andean dry forest; however, some populations grow at lower altitudes in more humid environments. It flowers after about 20 years and has a trunk diameter of up to 1 meter. It can reach heights of up to 7 meters in cultivation (with a crown spread of 5 to 8 meters) and lives for approximately 550 years.
ekegusii: Oiboreire Bolivia, igo okwama ase aome naende are n’ebuse , emetaroekorakwa Inter-Andean chire n’oboigoro bwe chimita 2700–3400 igoro ya nyancha; aseigo, epamu eye nero eimogete igoro ase chikabira chionsi ense engima. Iberera ndiri goetania chidigiri 20 n’obokendu bwa botuko mbioyo. Reberera ngogenda rire inse gioka chidigiri 7 are emetienyi y’obokendu (omotienyi ogatano na kabere na omotienyi o gatano na gatato) n’embura egotwa omwaka omogima nigo ere chi mirimita 550 chioka.

english: It needs well-drained soil to thrive, prefers full sun, a trunk, and also requires adequate drainage to prevent root rot, benefiting people who want to plant it because it is easy to grow. Large trunks become hollow and those associated with old age are prone to decay, making them unsuitable for use as timber. It is said that in Europe, trunks can reach diameters of 3 meters. The palm thrives in areas where temperatures rarely drop below -8 degrees Celsius. Many birds feed on its fruits, but they remain mostly in the highlands, beautiful palms!
ekegusii: Nigo ore omoremereria ekero kio’omorakera, riberera, obokendu, amo nechinde chinkong’u amo nokonyara gotigaria ekieni kiaye , bikogera abanto abange banyorora buna nabo okoba omuya ase okogita ase are riberera. Ase obokendu obonene bogotoka n’ase amache akobwatana nigo otakeire orendwa,amache ayio arusigwa takonyosaria mono korwa ase obokendu obwo. Nigo gekoba buna ime ya Yuropu nigo obokendu bokomenta goika akaberera ge chidigiri 3.Riberera rike ase epamu eye yabeire gekwameraase ogosimekwa nigo rire chidigiri –8.ebimeri ebi ebiatugutete anato abo onsi ,lakini ogatigara kwama naende ekero ki’omogaso,amato amanyia akarorekana!

english: In Bolivia, the palm grows to a height of 14 meters with a trunk diameter of 25–35 centimeters. The palm can live for 100 years and reach a height of 30 meters with a trunk diameter of 50 centimeters. Some individuals have been reported to reach heights of 20 meters! The trees are common in the cloud forests of Bolivia.
ekegusii: Ime ya Bolivia, epamu eye nigo ekwama yaika chimita 14 neritina rire chisentimita 25–35 are obonetu. Chipamu chiabeire emiaka 100 na goetania, nabo egoika chimita 30 ase obotambe n’obonetu bwe chisentimita 50. Ekobi engiya nkwerosia ere ya amato 20 akoba goika chimita 5! Ebimeri bikwanma isikop ya Bolivia nigo bire ebike ake.

english: It is a relatively fast-growing palm, but it does not grow as quickly as other species due to its size. This species is classified as P. torallyi var. microcarpa with smaller leaves and P. torallyi var. torallyi with larger leaves. However, there is confusion, var. microcarpa tends to grow more slowly, while those in drier and warmer climates grow faster. Its conservation status is considered vulnerable due to habitat loss. Nevertheless, its seeds germinate easily, provided they are fresh and kept moist, and planted shallowly. Well-maintained plants, with adequate watering and fertilization, benefit greatly from this care, especially during the first few years, and the seedlings will be strong and healthy. It needs regular care, including pruning, fertilizing, and protecting against pests and diseases, benefiting people who appreciate this native tree and also helping to conserve the species and its habitat.
ekegusii: Nigo chikabira chikwama ao ibere chitari kobwakana esengencho y’obonene gose oboke bw’amatunda . Ritunda rike rikorikwa P. torallyi var. microcarpa ne rotunda rinene rikorokwa P. torallyi var. torallyi. Nonye tebwekaini, var. microcarpa tori goikera mote omwabo omonene, korende ase akonara are n’okwama, nigo onyobwakaine. Chintetere cnhimanyire bobe ase ogotamera bwango. Nonye chintetere chikonyoru komera, ngocha chire chiamera ekero chisimekire ase agwenererete, buna igoro bosa ase riroba, chihbekire enusu gochia riroba, naende chikabekwa ase omoika. Ekero chirendire buy, ase oboendu bwa gati gati n’omogaso ogatoka, ebimeri mbiame bwanko bibe ebitambe, biamete buya bibwate amato anga chikobi . okoremereria kwaye gochia ase omorakera, riberera, obokendu, obokendu obonene, n’asande, na okonyara gotwara ekieni ekenene mono, nigo bikogera abanto bateba buna omote oyo okare tari orabe oyo bwamaritati oka akorende nabo naende okonyara kogitere ase abwateriberera ne riberer ria gatigati.

english: Parajubaea torallyi and its relatives are important ecologically and economically. In Ecuador and Colombia, Parajubaea cocoides grows at altitudes between 2500–3000 meters – the palm is found on slopes and is not very common. It is closely related to Parajubaea torallyi, and sometimes confused with other species of Parajubaea torali.
ekegusii: Parajubaea torallyi n’ekemeri kemanyire ase amaritati naende nigo ogosimekwa ase ebitii gose chinchera. Ime ya Ecuador na Colombia ya maate, Parajubaea cocoides nigo okwama ase aimofete igoro goika chimita 2500–3000– epamu neroo ekwama ng’ora naende teri koremeree]ria buna echinde. Ekiagera ebwekaine Parajubaea torallyi, na ase yachakerete tamanyiri, neancheire korokwa egesaku gia parajubaea torali.

english: Other populations were discovered in Peru in the 1990s, identified as Parajubaea sunkha which is similar and was described in 1996. It grows up to 8 meters tall and is found in the Andean foothills near Vallegrande in the Santa Cruz region of Bolivia at elevations between 1700–2200 meters. There has been some confusion about whether Parajubaea tirali is the same as Parajubaea sunkha.
ekegusii: Egesaku egeke pi ki’emnego eye nigo gekorokwa Parajubaea sunkha ekio kiamanyekanere na gotebwa omwaka o 1996. Nigo gekwama giaoka chimita 8 ase obotambe, n amigo gekwana ase emetero ya Andean as e akorokwa Vallegrandeime ya Santa Cruz ase ense ya Bolivia eimogete goika chimita 1700–2200. Kiabeire kegotamburigwa bobe buna ekere Parajubaea tirali goika bwanko iga ekero okorigarigia gwakorwa okamanya korokwa Parajubaea sunkha.

english: The seed of Parajubaea germinates easily. The fruit is used locally for food. Those interested should collect the fruits, but they need to be cleaned well and sown fresh, and they need moisture throughout the year. The seeds sprout readily when kept moist for several months. Old seeds may take longer to germinate. Flowering occurs annually, producing abundant flowers. The flowering period lasts for several months each year.
ekegusii: Chipamu echi chia Parajubaea nigo chigosimekwa raisi. Enchera engiya nogotumia chintetere. Korende netakeire omoremi abe omoremereria mono ekiagera chintetere chikoira egeka komera nonya nase orosana, naende chikoira omwaka oyomo n’enusu komera. Chintetere cnhire chigochaka komera magega y’omotienyi korense cnhire chikoira egeka egetambe goika omwaka gose emiaka ebere. Mbuya gokebeka ase riberera rike ekiagera riberera rinenw erigosaroa okomera. Riberera rinene erikworokia omorakeria oyio otari muya ase okomera

english: Typically, the seeds collected from the fruit are approximately 20 mm long and 5–7 mm wide. The seeds are covered with a hard shell. The shells are often cracked during collection. The seeds also require stratification before sowing.
ekegusii: Chitarabusurwa, chintetere echikobekwa amache ime ase riberera rire chidigiri 20 ase amatuko 5–7. Chintetere chirwete ase amatunda amanene goika chibekwe amache ase chiwiki ibere. Amache ayio aonchorwe kera rituko. Chintetere nabo chigosigikigwa nario chiremere bwanko.

english: To germinate the seeds, it's necessary to simulate the conditions of the rainy season (wet and dry periods), mimicking the environment where they grow (especially in Bolivia - areas with distinct wet and dry seasons).
ekegusii: Okobeka chintetere amache ime nigo kogokora obworo bw’okomera, kobe buna nokorenta embura, ere enguya ase okomera. Obworo obwo ebokogera nchintetere nchikomera ekero ki’obokendu ase Bolivia (obokendu obonene bw’omotienyi ogatano na rimo amo n’omotienyi o gatano na kabere).

english: After cracking the shells, the seeds that have been collected should be soaked in water for several weeks, alternating between soaking and drying.
ekegusii: Ekero chiabekirwe amache ime, chinteter echio echigwenererete kobusurwa ase enyongo gose esagasaga- renda buna n’enusu y’entetere etubire n’amaraba naende riberera ribe chidigiri10–20.

english: Stop watering the seeds and let the soil dry out for few months. Take the seeds out of the soil, put them back into water for around a week and then sown them again.
ekegusii: Okomera okuya nigo gokorenta n’etobauti ase ribera mogaso (igoro) na botuko (inse). Ekero chintetere chiabusuiru, tichibasi kona kobekerwa amache rioka rioka ekiagere arachisari ekero ebimeri bire ebike. Ogosimaka ebimeri bia Parajubaea nigo kore etobauti n’ebimeri binde ekiagera otagete riberera rike amo na amache amake.

english: Don't delay planting the seeds and provide adequate moisture. Soak the seeds first, then place them in damp cloth and sow them.
ekegusii: Stop watering the seeds and let the soil dry out for few months. Take the seeds out of the soil, put them back into water for around a week and then sown them again.

english: The seedlings take about a year to mature and produce leaves. Any damaged seedlings, discard them along with those that don't sprout after being watered.
ekegusii: Otige konya koumora amache na oige riroba rioma ase emetieni mekeigo. Rusia chintetere oas riroba, chibeke ase amache ang’e echuma eyemo naende chioiranie ase riroba.

english: The germination rate of Parajubaea can reach 100%, producing strong sprouts, and the seeds are very resistant to damage.
ekegusii: Chintetere chisimekire igo echigwenererett komera ekero omwaka oyomo n’enusi oerire. Onye ntetere chinde cnhikomera, irora ne chintetere chionsi nchimere ekero embura egotwa naende.

english: In some cases, there may be a small hole, which indicates good viability; otherwise, the seed will not germinate unless it's fully intact. A large hole indicates a better chance of sprouting.
ekegusii: Okwamera kwa Parajubaea nigo kogoikerana 100%, kogincha omonto abe omoremereria, ae chintetere chiri ching’oro enkaki yokorakera.

english: Parajubaea is native to isolated areas of eastern South America. A major reason for its decline is deforestation due to agriculture, leading to habitat loss and fragmentation. The palm tree that grows here is unique and rare. Larger seeds are more likely to survive. The growth of these seeds is affected by animals like the spectacled bear (Tremarctos ornatus), which disperse the seeds across wider areas.
ekegusii: Ekero obwate e pamu enke, nigo ekoba enyomo pa, inyora tonyeumorera amache amange moono. Epamu enke nigo egotaka ase are gati gati (ekero chisimekire ase chiachakerete, nigo chogosimekwa ase ekiriri gi’echipamu chinene), korende chiri chinene echigotaka omogaso.

Esababu enene ekogera nesengencho emete ekonachwa korigia amaremo yogosimeka endagera, korugia chibao nma korisia chiombe. Chipamu echi echigotika ase ake mono, naki chigosarerigwa bwanko igo chiaisire gosire pi. Ekiagera chintetere chiabo chire chinene, okwama ase aange nkori konyarekana. Eng’iti yorosana enene ekoira chintetere echi isiko y’ase echigotoka n’ebea ekorokwa naende (Tremarctos ornatus), korende neero negosire ase engencho abanto ebagochiseri gose gochiita.

english: Thus says the Lord: “Strengthen your faith among the nations, and let the nations come to know my name.” For the Lord strengthens his faith, and he brings the nations to know his name, and he makes them holy.
ekegusii: 14Erio Nyasae agachiika “Tiga emebaso ebe ase oboiko bw’aaria igoro, bwatanane omobaso korwa ase obotuko; erio ebe ebimanyererio bikworokia ebiro bi’amatuko, ne chingaki, n’emiaka, 15ebe emebaso ase oboiko aaria igoro, boyee ense omobaso na oborabu,” ayio onsi akaba boigo. 16Erio Nyasae agakora emebaso ebere emenene, Risase rigaambere ekero kia mobaso n’omotienyi ogaambere ekero kia botuko; agakora ne ching’enang’eni boigo. 17Akayebeka ase eanga aaria igoro, eyee ense oborabu, 18egaambere omobaso na obotuko, na gwatanana oborabu korwa ase omosunte. Nyasae akarora ayio ng’a namaya. 19Erio agwo rikaba mogoroba, naende bogakia mambia, rituko ria kane.

english: 7He strengthens his faith forever. Thus says the Lord, and it will be done today, and they will proclaim his name, and they will be saved.

10He strengthens those who love him, and the nations that are gathered together will be blessed. The Lord strengthens them and shows mercy.

Ngokobeeka inde ogaambere chinswe, ne chinyoni, n’echingiti chionsi chi’orosana. 29Nabaeire kera ekemeri gekwama chimbusuro, na kera omote okwama amatunda ebio nabio biraabe endagera yaino. 30Korende ching’iti chi’orosana ne chinyoni chionsi nachieire ebimeri ebibese bionsi bibe endagera yabo.” Ayio onsi akaba boigo. 31Nyasae akarora ebinto ebio bionsi akorete, na birobio nigo biareenge ebiya mono. Erio agwo rikaba mogoroba, naende bogakia mambia, rituko ria gatano na rimo.

english: Long ago there was a person called Enyancha of Victoria who lived in Emanga. It was a person who owned land in Emanga. And now it is in Manga near Manga Escarpment where people gather. Emanga is about 100 years old. It is located in Manga District and Kisii Town. In Manga it borders Kitutu Masaba and Kitutu Chache. It has connections to Manga, also reaching Kisii Town, Bogore, Victoria Falls and even some parts of Nyamira District.
ekegusii: Embeo nigo ekogusa korwa Enyancha ya Victoria yaaka Emanga. Nigo embeo egotengia emete ye emanga. Eye nero e Manga gose Manga Escarpment buna abande bakoyeroka. Emanga nigo ere ange chieka 100. Nigo ere ime ya Manga District ange na Kisii Town. Nigo E Manga ere ase orobebe rwa Kitutu Masaba na Kitutu Chache. Goteneine ase e Manga, nabo okorora Kisii Town, Bogere,Enyancha ya Victoria amo ne chinsemo chinde chia Nyamira District.

english: The homesteads of the Gusii people were usually “round”. The fences were very short. This Manga homestead was built by the Ritongo Cultural Group and is well known. Mwanyagetinge.com/2010
ekegusii: Enyomba yo Omogusii nigo yarenge "round". Omosongo nere orentete chikona. Enyomba yaito Manga yaagachetwe ne Ritongo Cultural Group yagotire. Mwanyagetinge.com/2010

english: Together with the elders of the Gusii people they say that Manga is where the Gusii people used to meet for consultations, perform ceremonies and resolve all important matters. Elder Omondi Onkundi, 70, says that the colonialists found the Ritongo (Cultural Center) already established within the territory of the Gusii people specifically at Manga. Elder Onkundi says that when the colonialists came to Gusii, Ritongo was moved to Nyamira.
ekegusii: Abangina na abagaka abakoro ba Gusii nigo bagoteba inga E Manga nigo yarenge ase Abagusii barenge koumerana gosaba, gokora ebingwanso ne emeyega yende yonsi emenene. Omogaka Omondi Onkundi, 70, nigo agoteba inga abakoloni nigo baagachete Ekoti (Ritongo) entangani ime ya Gusii aaiga ase E Manga.Omogaka Onkundi nigo agoteba inga ekero omokoloni arwete Gusii, Ritongo rikanganyigwa gochia Nyamira.

english: The Wealth of the Clan of Kegancha
ekegusii: Engoro No Omosasa O' Kegancha

english: Elder Onkundi says that it is not widely known that this area, Manga, was very significant to the ancestors. The Gusii people believed that their strength came from God (the Creator) and they respected tradition. Elder Onkundi comments that the name "God" was first heard in Bogore. God’s creation for the Gusii people is referred to as "Engoro".
ekegusii: Nigo omogaka Onkundi agoteba inga, otatiga ogotamanyekana ase chingaki echi chie ekerero, E Manga nigo yasikire sana ase amatuko amakoro. Abagusii nigo beegenete inga chisokoro na Nyasae (Engoro) nao bameneyete igaa. Omogaka Onkundi nigo akomenta inga erieta "Nyasae" nigo twasumete korwa Bogere. Nyasae tiriri rieta rie Ekegusii asiri. Erieta rironge ase Omogusii ribaga ria Nyasae nigo rire "Engoro".

english: However, in ancient times, the Gusii people had many different ways of life but they always united to solve problems. Elder Onkundi says that because of tribal conflicts, things often deteriorated leading to chaos in Manga. People would travel far and wide spreading rumors causing anxiety.
ekegusii: Buna ebisaku binde, Abagusii nigo bare gosuma amarieta goeta goeta kobwatekana buna barenge goetanana ase okonganya. Omogaka Onkundi nigo agoteba inga engaki ya botuko, nabo emerero yare kororekana egwoka ase chinsana chie E Manga. Nigo abanto bare kogenda maambia korotota banyora inga kende tikeyieti.

english: Elder Samuel Ongeri says that this place and its surroundings are sacred and he comments that the name Engoro originated from the ancestor Okorokwa Omosasa O'Kegancha. The clan of Omosasa O 'Kegancha and the Gusii people worshipped Engoro and offered sacrifices, performed rituals and sought blessings.
ekegusii: Omogaka Samuel Ongeri nigo agoteba inga ekio ne ekeene rakini nigo akomenta inga omoika bwe Engoro nigo omenyete ase omote okorokwa Omosasa O'Kegancha. Aaiga ase Omosasa O 'Kegancha nao Abagusii barenge gosaba ase Engoro na komoboria aramere ababisa, gosibia emechie na koyesesenia.

english: “Therefore, Omosasa O'Kegancha and his descendants are in Manga. He did not move anywhere during his lifetime. This is his home and burial ground.” Also said elder Ongeri.
ekegusii: Goikera rero, Omosasa O'Kegancha nao oteneine ase E Manga. Onde takoyobutora gose atumie chinko chiaye. Echio ne chimuma." Nabo omogaka Ongeri amentete.

english: Omosasa O' Kegancha. Descendants live everywhere. Mwanyagetinge.com/2010
ekegusii: Omosasa O' Kegancha. Oteneine korwa kare kare. Mwanyagetinge.com/2010

english: The Name of the Year
ekegusii: Ngoro Mwaga

english: This year has passed. A celebration took place in Manga and the name given was “Ngoro Mwaga”. It was a unique name which attracted attention and caused excitement. It was agreed upon that this name represented the strength of Engoro. Anyone who understood its meaning knew how important it was to protect it.
ekegusii: Tari igo rioka. Egento kende kere ase E Manga ne engoro ekorokwa "Ngoro Mwaga". Nigo engoro eye echakerete egetare igoro, egaeta gati na goika inse. Nigo gekoba inga engoro eye nigo ere eya amasikani ase Engoro. Onye gotagete goika ange, goika okore emeroberio gete erinde omanye koyerora.

english: The Name of the Year is celebrated. Mwanyagetinge.com/2010
ekegusii: Engoro Ya Mwaga tegoichora. Mwanyagetinge.com/2010

english: “It is good to respect both the living and the dead. Therefore, let us protect this heritage both now and in the future so that this name continues to be remembered.” Also commented Elder Onkundi. However, this name does not celebrate the living and the dead equally. The Gusii people believe that their ancestors have power and they honor them in Manga. They offer gifts, worship and pray for prosperity and peace.
ekegusii: Goika osibe obonyansi bore machani kabichi amo ne chinko. Basi omanye koruta obonyansi obwo amo ne chinko echio ase engoro eyio ime. Korwa abwo chisokoro nabo chikogwanchera origererie engoro eyio". Nabo omogaka Onkundi akomenta. Nonya nabo igo, engoro eyio tiyana goichora obonyansi ne chinko gesa na gesa. Abagusii nigo beegenete inga emioyo ye chisokoro nao yamenyete aaiga ase E Manga. Nigo bare gocha igaa korwa ebingwanso, gosaba na gokora emeyega ende yonsi emenene.

english: Respect both the living and the dead to preserve the Name of the Year. Mwanyagetinge.com/2010
ekegusii: Renta obonyansi ne chinko momanye korigereria Engoro Ya Mwaga. Mwanyagetinge.com/2010

english: The Story of Okari
ekegusii: Enyancha Yo Okari

english: Like Ngoro Mwaga, this story also happened in the past called the Story of Okari. It is said that the history of the Gusii people tells of a man named Oyomo who lived near a tree whose roots were deep and branches spread wide. That tree was associated with a story. This story is about what happened to the elder named Okari.
ekegusii: Ange na Ngoro Mwaga, enyancha neroo etari kororekana ekorokwa Enyancha Yo Okari. Nigo Omogano Bwa Abagusii ogoteba inga omochie oyomo nomenyete igaa rakini enyomba yabo ekarimera gochia inse ne echancha ekamanya gotoka. Yaani enyomba eyio nigo yanywetwe ne enyancha. Enyancha eyio nigo erokire erieta rio omogaka bwe enka eyio yanywetwe, omogaka Okari.

english: A Certain Person
ekegusii: Igena Monto

english: There are things in Manga and elsewhere. Let us remember a certain person called Igena Monto. Both things from Manga and elsewhere have meaning to the Gusii people and are remembered as Igena Monto. This memory is about a person. In the past, it was about a person who was respected by everyone, and it is still remembered today.
ekegusii: Ebinto bie E Manga ne ebinge. Eariganie koumera Igena Monto. Gati ye ebinto ebinge bie E Manga bire ne maana ase Omogusii ne rigena rikorokwa Igena Monto. Rigena eri nigo rikororekana buna omonto. Korwa aare, nigo rikororekana buna omonto oikaransete rakini ekero gwaikire ange, kwanyora inga ne rigena.

english: The Gusii people also have traditions. It is believed that there was a time when a young man named Ajua went looking for traditions in Manga. William Marianga and Andrew Okera also searched for traditions and found that those traditions were preserved by Engoro. There is much more to learn.
ekegusii: Omogusii nigo anchete goaka oboche. Nigo togoteba igo ekiagera chingoro chio ogoakera oboche bwa Ajua nao chichongire ase egetare igoro ase E Manga. Nigo William Marianga and Andrew Okera bagoaka oboche rakini nigo batebete inga oboche obo nigo bwarosetigwe ne Engoro. Tari monto oboroisetie.

english: Searching for Traditions in Manga. Sometimes we just want to pass the time! Mwanyagetinge.com/2010
ekegusii: Goaka oboche E Manga igoro. Aba imbamanyete go kill time! Mwanyagetinge.com/2010

english: The elders of Manga have realized that something needs to be done, a building should be built and a museum established to showcase the culture of the Gusii people and the items they used. For generations, organizations like the Ritongo Cultural Group have worked hard to preserve our heritage, bringing together leaders, experts and elders to promote the culture of the Gusii people. We need to support them in this endeavor.
ekegusii: Abamenyi be E Manga nigo batagete ogobago robekwe, chioteli chibekwe amo ne Museum ebwate Omogano o Gusii ne ebinto Abagusii bagatwarire. Ase amatuko aetire, ekeombe kia NGO kie Ritongo Cultural Group ingiatagete koagacha enyomba ye egetamaduni, babeke abateri bo obokano na abangina na abagaka bagototebia omogano bwo Omogusii. Kende tikeraba goikera bono ase engencho yo oboremerwa bwe chibesa.

english: Let's continue to develop Manga. Mwanyagetinge.com/2010
ekegusii: Togende gotara E Manga. Mwanyagetinge.com/2010

english: Leaders of the Ritongo Cultural Group, Ezra Abuga and George Morara, have stated that the land allocated for this purpose is sufficient. It is land that belonged to a former leader, Zachary Angwenyi. People say that Chief Angwenyi gave permission for the construction of a house with twenty rooms and six bathrooms!
ekegusii: Abanene be Ritongo Cultural Group, Ezra Abuga Na George Morara nigo bagoteba inga enyomba yaagachetwe bono yagotire. Nigo enyomba eye yaagachire ase ekegambero kio omochifu omokoro, Zachary Angwenyi. Aaiga nao gekoba inga Omochifu Angwenyi nigo agambete na korwa ogochika

english: “I urge all the clans of the Gusii people to come together.” Ezra said. They encourage the clans to contribute towards building twenty rooms and six bathrooms.
ekegusii: kwo ogokeia enamba ye chiombe chie enyangi korwa 20 impaka 6!

english: Gusii.com reports that efforts are underway to persuade the government to declare Manga Escarpment a National Monument. These plans are progressing. And there is hope that future generations will benefit from this.
ekegusii: Eke nakio kiagerete Abasacha abange ba Gusii bagaansa konywoma naende". Nabo Ezra abuga akomenta naende. Konyora abasacha abange batigire konywoma ase engencho yo ogotatwara chiombe 20 na gochia igoro.

english: According to the Minister for Culture and Member of Parliament for North Mugirango, Hon. Wilfred Ombui, he supports the idea of preserving and developing Manga. “Manga has a lot of history and it can attract tourists if developed properly,” Hon. Ombui added.
ekegusii: Gusii.com iyakorete obotuki na konyora inga eserikali iyatagete kobeka Manga Escarpment ebe e National Monument. Emepango eyio teraba. Nigo ensemo eye ere engiya ase obotari rakini tebwati batari bange.

english: Assistant Minister For National Heritage and MP, North Mugirango Borabu, Hon. Wilfred Ombui. Mwanyagetinge.com/2010
ekegusii: Ase okogamba no omowaziri bwe Egetamaduni naende omobunge o North Mugirango, Mhe. Wilfred Ombui, nigo egotebekana inga emeroberio neroo yo okorenda na koroisia E Manga. "Nigo E Manga ebwate ekieni sana naende nabo erarente amagenderero sana toise koyerenda". Nabo Mhe. Ombui amentete.

english: Hon. Ombui further stated that the government should help fund the construction of the Manga Cultural Center. Additionally, he mentioned that funds should be allocated to renovate the existing structures so that their importance is recognized.
ekegusii: Assistant Minister For National Heritage and MP, North Mugirango Borabu, Mhe. Wilfred Ombui. Mwanyagetinge.com/2010

For whoever calls upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.” Romans 10:9-10,13
ekegusii: |“Korende koramoorokie Yesu Kristo as'omonwa oo, nakomwancha as'omoyo oo, ng'a Nyasaye namobogetie korwa as'amakweri, nokonyeke: naki as'enkoro abanto igobakwegena baikera oboronge; nas'omonwa oorokia goika onyora ogotoreka. naki, onde bwonsi orarangerie erieta ri'Omonene nakonyeke.” Aba Rumi 10:9-10,13|

english: The foundation of Christian Faith-The importance of resurrection

english: Paul the apostle wrote to his friend in Corinth: “And if there is no resurrection of the dead, then Christ has not been raised;” (1 Corinthians 15:13). He continued to say: “And if Christ has not been raised, then our preaching is empty and your faith is also empty,” (Corinthians 15:14)
ekegusii: Omotomwa Paulo nigo agotonenekeria ase rirube riaye ritangani ase Abakorintho: “Korende onye okobokigwa kw’abakure tikori, rirorio Kristo nere tobogetiwe, “(1 Abakorintho 15:13). Ase egesieri ekio nigo agoteba:” Naende Onye Kristo nere tabogetigwe, rirorio okorandia gwaito nokwa bosa, na okwegena kwaino nokwa bosa,” (Abakorintho 15:14)

english: The foundation of Christian faith is connected to belief and trust in the resurrection so that the church of today can stand firm (the fellowship of the apostles (2:31, 4:33,17:18,26:23.) And even now it is through believing in the resurrection that we become followers who are saved.
ekegusii: Engencho yakobokigwa gwa Kristo nigo ekororekana ase obonge na omogoko ase okorandia buna ekanisa ya ritangani egokina (omobwekano ogokora kwa Abatomwa (2:31, 4:33,17:18,26:23.) Ange kera kirori bwenchili nigo akoraga okobuka gwa Kristo koba ogosemeria ase baria baganetie ogotooreka.

english: Mark writes, “And I delivered unto you first of all that which I also received, how that Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures; and that he was buried, and that he rose again the third day according to the scriptures;" 1 Corinthians 15:3-4.
ekegusii: Amariko nigo agoteba, “Naki nkabaranderia amang'ana ayananyorete ritang'ani, ng'a Kristo igakwete as'engecho y'ebibe biaito, buna agoteba amariko; naende ng'a agatindekwa, naende akaboka, rituko ria gatato, buna agoteba amariko;” 1 Abakorintho 15:3-4.

english: Therefore, the Bible teaches that belief and following Jesus leads to the fulfillment of life.
ekegusii: Aye’ngencho mono, Ebibilia nigo egotebereria naze ki ogokwa na okoboka kwa Yeso kogotoa egesoero kia igoro.

english: The consequences of sin and transgression.
ekegusii: Egesusuro kie’bibe namakweri.

english: God judges humanity because of disobedience. When Adam and Eve disobeyed God’s command, they fell into sin, The penalty for sin is death, but God’s plan to save people from sin is revealed in His Son Jesus Christ, "For the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord." (Romans 6:23).
ekegusii: Nyasae agatonga mwanyabantho kare omoikeranu. Korende Adamu na Hawa bakamocha koigwera amachiko a Nyasae, nere akabaa egesusuro, Omogambi oyokwabera abakobuna amachiko, tari Omogambi omonyakeene Naboigo “Aba Naki eng'eria y'ebibe namakweri; korende ekeegwa kia Nyasaye nobogima bwa kare nakare ase Yesu Kristo Omonene oito.” (Aba Rumi 6:23).

english: But despite knowing the truth about God, people still choose to disobey Him, rejecting His forgiveness. “All have turned aside, together they have become worthless; no one does good, no, not one.” (Isaiah 64:6b). Because of this. Adam’s descendants are all born with a sinful nature and are unable to please God. “for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God;” (Romans 3:23). Sin is not just big things like murder or blasphemy, but also includes love of money, hatred of enemies, and deceit of tongue and pride. Because of sin, everyone has deserved death – eternal separation from God in hell. Sin causes many problems in life, leading to broken relationships with God, others, and ourselves, resulting in guilt, shame, and emptiness. This condition of sin separates us from God and prevents us from experiencing true joy and peace.
ekegusii: Nonya nogokora amaya takonyara korogeiya amabe ase Nyasae, onyore omochenu koreng’ania nobuya bwaye. “Oboronge bwaito bwonsi nigo bore buna amachanchabe are ne riko.” (isaya 64:6b). Korwa ase ekebe gia. Adamu, mwa nyabanto nigo are nokomocha kwogotaigwera amachiko ye’keene aya nyasae.“naki bonsi bakorire ebibe, barorire ng'a baremeirwe nobonene bwa Nyasaye;” (Aba Rumi 3:23). Sin is not just big things like murder or blasphemy, but also includes love of money, hatred of enemies, and deceit of tongue and pride. Because of sin, everyone has deserved death – eternal separation from God in hell. Ekebe tari amang’ana amarito buha ogoita, gose okomorama Nyasae, korende ng’amo na ogwancha chibesa, okobagacha ababisa, oborimo bwo’romeme, amo nobweanchi. Asengencho ye’kebe kera oyomo nigo aganeirie ogokwa – ogoatananwa na Nyasae ase omorero ogosamba.

english: Eve also believed in the lie instead of the truth.
ekegusii: Eira nigo yaganetie amakweri atari no’komocha.

english: However, God promised Adam and Eve hope through a descendant, who would crush the serpent’s head and restore their relationship with God. (Genesis 3:15)This promise pointed forward to God’s ultimate solution—His own Son (Jesus)—who would conquer sin and its effects on humanity.
ekegusii: Nonya Nyasae obaseretie Adamu na Hawa korwa ase omogondo,tabatigete batari nogosemeria kwa igoro. Akabaa eira ng’a nabatomere ekeng’wanso egetari nekebe korusia egesusuro eki baganeirie konyora.(Omochakano 3;15)aiga noobore obasiani bw’omoroberio omoikeranu o Nyasae; Nyasae omonyene akaenena ekeng’wanso(yeso) oyoranyare korusia ebibe bia abanto baye.

english: Jesus willingly went to the cross, suffering the punishment we deserve, and rose again triumphantly from the grave.
ekegusii: Yesu agakwa ase omosaraba,agatindekwa koenekia ogokwa kwaye,naende akabooka nobobui nyuma ya amatuko atato.

english: The sacrifice of Jesus provides a way for us to be reconciled to God, and those who believe in Him receive forgiveness and new life; therefore, anyone who trusts in the life of Jesus will experience forgiveness and restoration.
ekegusii: Ogkwa kwa yeso nigo kwarenge okwengencho buna ekeng’wanzo kia amanyinga aye,naboigo ogotindekwa na okoboka kwaye nokwengencho; korende onsi ayakorekanete ase obogima bwa yeso nigo are gokoorera ogoakwa amanyinga igoro.

english: And Christ has indeed entered the heavenly realms and is now seated at God’s right hand—above all angelic powers and authorities and kingdoms and dominions. And he will reign until he has put all his enemies under his feet! But when everything is subjected to him, then the Son himself will be subject to the One who sent him, so that God may be all in all. For there is no other foundation upon which anyone can build than the one laid down—namely, Jesus Christ! If anyone builds on that foundation with gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, or straw—the quality of each person’s work will be evident, for the Day will reveal it, because it will be tested by fire. If anyone’s work stands up to the test, that person will receive a reward. If anyone’s work is burned up, that person will suffer loss, but they themselves will be saved, though only as through flames. Don’t you know that you yourselves are God’s temple and that God’s Spirit dwells within you?" 1 Corinthians 3:24-26
ekegusii: Naki Kristo tasoete aas'aachenu akoretwe namaboko, naro omogwekano bw'aachenu asare aachenu ekeene; korende agasoa igoro anyene, arorekane bono obosio bwa Nyasaye as'engecho yaito intwe: gose tari buna ng'a erue omonyene ebiro ebinge, buna omokuani omonene ogosoa aas'aachenu ker'omwaka namanyinga atari ayaye; onye nabo, anga yamogwenerete achandwe ebiro ebinge korwa ogotongwa gw'ense: korende bono, ara rimo rioka, as'omoerio bw'ense ororekanire, arusie ebibe as'ekeng'wanso ki'omobere oye.” Abaibirania 9:24-26

" Naki as'abwo batiekire koegwa omobaso, nakomena ekeegwa keria kia igoro, nagokorwa ababwatani b'Omoika Omochenu,

ekegusii: Twatoorigwe korwa ase ensemo y’ebibe (Abaeteso 2:8,9). Oko nakwo tokoroka okobarwa koba abanyene oboronge.

ekegusii: Rengereria ango igoro ya oria oyomoni,”oyotooregete” korende bono nomanyate buna abeire omonyabibe, na amang’ana amabe aria arigetie gokora. Naki erabe baraita omonto gose- eri- eki barakure???

(And you are saved by grace, through faith, and this is not from yourselves, it is the gift of God: Ephesians 2:8-9). ekegusii: Amachiko nareo ao ao ase ense eye tomenyete agototang'ana naende boigo amachiko nareo ayagototang'ana gochia ase Nyasae.

ekegusii: Richiko rie

english: 1.GOD LOVES THE WORLD, AND GAVE HIS ONLY BEBORN SON THAT WHOEVER BELIEVES IN HIM SHOULD NOT PERISH BUT HAVE EVERLASTING LIFE.
ekegusii: 1.OMONENE NYASAE NAGWANCHETE, NAENDE OKOEIRE OMOROBERIO BWOGOKUMIA ASE OBOGIMA BWAO.

english: Father Jesus Christ, I confess. I give you my life and I surrender myself to you, and I want to live according to Your will and do what pleases You. Lord, cleanse me from my sins. Give me strength to live according to Your life. Amen

english: IF YOU KNOW THIS ABOUT JESUS HE GIVES YOU HIS LIFE
