english: So what? Will you accept Jesus into your life? Why not? According to Revelation 3:20, is Christ waiting for you today? Christ promises to enter and live in your life. What are you waiting for? Do you know that God loves you and wants to answer your prayers? (Consider this truth carefully, so that no one deceives you and causes you to reject the inheritance of the Son of God!)
ekegusii: Bono inee? Kwamwariganeirie Yeso ime yobogima bwao? Naki omanyete? Kobwatekana na Okomanoka 3:20 Ng'ai Kristo are bono iga? Kristo otebire buna nachiche ime yobogima bwao. Inee nang'ainererie gose? Naki oramanye ng'a Nyasae okoiraneirie ogosaba kwao? (Egekogera natebete ng'a onde bwensi oranyegene amo na amariko ane nakonyeke ekiagera ariegenire erieta ri'Omwana o Nyasae!)

english: LIVE WITH JESUS NOW AND FOREVER
ekegusii: OYORE NA YESO NARE NOBOGIMA BWA KARE NA KARE

english: Why would you refuse, when God offers eternal life, and that life is only through His Son? If you join the Son, you have eternal life; if you reject the Son of God, you do not have eternal life. Remember these words, and understand that eternal life is only through the Son of God. 1 John 5:11-13
ekegusii: Naki obo nabwo oborori, ng'a Nyasae otoeire obogima bwa kare na kare, na obogima obo nigo bore ime ase Omwana oye. Ere oyore n'omwana, nare nobogima; ere oyotari n'Omwana o Nyasae, tari nobogima. Nabarikeire inwe amang'ana aya, erinde momanye ng'a more nobogima bwa kare na kare, inwe abwo mwariegenire erieta ri'Omwana o'Nyasae. 1 Yohana 5:11-13

english: Always remember that God, our Father, has promised to be with Christ always, giving eternal life. “And surely I am with you always, to the very end of the age” (Matthew 28:20). Receive eternal life.
ekegusii: Mwaakere Nyasae imbuya mono kera rituko kiagera Kristo nare ime yobogima bwao. "Mokoborokereria kobwata aya onsi nabachigete; na rora, inche nigo inde amo nainwe amatuko onsi goika omoerio bw'ense" (Mathayo 28:20). Okoeire obogima bwa kare na kare.

english: Christians should honor God above all things and obey His commandments found in the Bible. But if someone does not love him, know that Christ will never depart from his life. “Let your conduct be without covetousness, and be content with such things as you have, saying, ‘God has said, “Never will I leave you nor forsake you.”’” (Hebrews 13:5)
ekegusii: Abakristo nigo bagwenerete kwegena omonene Nyasae oito amo nering'ana riaye buna erikire ase ebibilia. Neba buna oranyare kweigwa aye omonyene, manya nga Kristo ere tari goonchoka ase obogima bwao. "Timoba abanchi chibesa, moisaneke nebi more nabio, ekiagera ere omonyene otebire, "Tinkogotiga nonya ng'ake, gose tingokoremera" (Abaiberania 13:5)

english: The pillars of faith are based on the teachings of the Bible. Honoring and obeying them lead to a fulfilling Christian life.
ekegusii: Ebigicha eye yegari igo egotworokia obomaene bwe Ebibilia. Okwegena amo na okweigwa igo bigokora emeremo ase obogima two omoknisto.

english: - The pillar of honoring is to offer everything willingly – (Offerings)
ekegusii: - Obomaene bwomonene igo bobwate chinguru chiogototang'ana - (Einchini)

english: - It is not right to offer something unwillingly and dishonestly – (Electronic money)
ekegusii: - Igo tobwateranetigwe nechinguru chiobomaene na okwegena - (Amaguta ye ebetironi)

english: - If you fail to honor, its consequences will bring misfortune. - (Bad luck)
ekegusii: - Buna tokoigwera obomaene, ebirengererio biaito igo bikobwatia enchera endonge. - (Orotuba gose eturera)

english: - To honor God with what He has given us means we must also do what He commands, so that we can live according to His will.
ekegusii: - Igo tokwegena Nyasae nobomaene bwaye korende tari okweigwa gwaito Ekero twakorire ebibe nigo egwenerete twangame nere natwabere.

english: Therefore, do not hesitate to give generously, knowing that it pleases God.
ekegusii: Ase go tonyara kwegena ebirengererio biao korende bwegene obomaene bwe ring'ana ria Nyasae.

english: TRUE BENEFITS OF KNOWING CHRIST
ekegusii: BONO KWAMONYORIRE KRISTO

english: Knowing Christ brings countless benefits.
ekegusii: Ekero kwamonyorete Kristo ase enkoro yao ebinto ebinge igo biakoregete.

english: - Christ gives life abundantly (Revelation 3:20 and Colossians 1:27)
ekegusii: - Kristo agasoa ime yenkoro yao (Okomanoka 3:20 na Abakorosai 1:27)

english: - Your sins are forgiven (Colossians 1:14)
ekegusii: - Ebibe biao bikaberwa (Abakorosai 1:14)

english: - Becoming a child of God (John 1:12)
ekegusii: - Okaba omwana o Nyasae (Yohana 1:12)

english: - Having a full life, enjoying peace and the love of God throughout eternity (John 10:10 and II Corinthians 5:14, 15, 17).
ekegusii: - Kwanyarire konyora omoroberio omyuya noborai obuya bwa Nyasae ase obogima bwao (Yohana 10:10 na II Abakorinto 5:14, 15, 17).

english: Think about this: What more could you desire than to receive abundant life through Christ?
ekegusii: Inee nonyare korengereria igoro ya kende gionsi ekiya kebuete Kristo oyore ime yenkoro yao?

english: Pray to God, our Father, asking Him to show you how to live according to His will.
ekegusii: Onye nabo mwaakere Nyasae imbuya mono ase ogosaba bono iga ase amaya agokoreire.

english: Thank God, our Father, and seek to honor Him. Pray sincerely and faithfully.
ekegusii: Goakera Nyasae imbuya mono igo gokworokia okwegena. Tosabe bono tosibogete.

english: What is your decision?
ekegusii: Egento kende ninki?

ekegusii: BUNA ORANYARE GOKINA ASE EKEMOIKA

ekegusii: Buna omwana omoke agokina naboigo egwenerete omokristo nere akine ekemoika.

english: These words will help those who may hesitate.
ekegusii: Amang'ana akobwatia nabo aranyare kogokonya.

english: THE CHURCH SHOULD ALWAYS STAND STRONG
ekegusii: EKANISA IGO ERE YENGENCHO ENENE MONO

english: The church, like a building, needs strong foundations. Just as a house needs a solid foundation to withstand storms and remain standing, the church needs strong faith to endure trials. And remember this: It offers eternal life—life in Christ—to everyone who believes.
ekegusii: Ekero chinko chibekire amo, igo chikoyia noborabu obonene mono. Beka oroko rokoyia ase riraba rire nobokendu nomorero oye igo okorima naende obe ekegenga, chinko chinyinge nigo chigwoka buya. Ase omobwekano oyo: igo ere obogima obokong'u mono ekero ogotema komenya obogima bwegekristo aye bweka.

english: It is important to gather with fellow believers regularly (Hebrews 10:25)
ekegusii: Igo ere buya mono kegima ekero mokobwaterana nabakristo bande baria bamomanyete Yeso Kristo buna omotoria obo (Abaibirania 10:25)

english: Go and join a church where people worship God based on the Bible, which is the Word of God, and where Jesus Christ is proclaimed as the Son of God.
ekegusii: Goika ogende ekanisa eria abanto begenete buna Ebibilia nering'ana riobomaene ria Nyasae, naende ase Yeso Kristo agotogigwa buna nomwana O Nyasae.

english: While we wait for the blessed hope—the glorious appearing of our great God and Savior, Jesus Christ (Titus 2:13)—let us also be eager, with a great expectation, for the fulfillment of the Christian faith.1 The basis for this waiting is the promise of resurrection, which is central to Christianity: Resurrection guarantees that we will not experience permanent death because of our sins (1 Corinthians 15:12–18).
ekegusii: Okobokigwa No’omochakano

english: Important background information
ekegusii: Engaki yo ogokwa no kobokigwa abanto abange ngochengera bare nakogokera okobokigwa kwo omotori oito omonene, Yeso Kirisito (Tito 2:13). Ase bare, eri nario rituko rinene rio amotimoko ase ekarenda yegekirisito.1 Amangana yo kobokigwa naro amangana yengencho mono ase obokeresito: Kobokigwa gotaiyo titobwati komanya ase ogotorigwa gwaito korwa ase ebibe biaito (1 Abakorinto 15:12–18).

english: This waiting is based on certainty, and it involves understanding certain things, namely, how the beliefs of Christians were established during the time of this waiting. This matter is discussed in 1 Thessalonians; specifically, Paul's account of his visit, which occurred around AD 50.2 Several years after the crucifixion of Christ. The purpose was to encourage believers who were being persecuted and to remind them of the promises; and also to ensure that those promises remain valid. Continue reading this chapter to understand more. After about three years following these events (approximately AD 30–33), there began to spread the teachings of the earlier apostles.3 However, these earlier teachings did not contradict the later teachings of Paul. This is why we can confidently say that they both convey the same message regarding the essential truths.4
ekegusii: Ebimanyererio ebitangani

english: “The foundation of the hope of Christ and the foundation of everything else for Christians: Resurrection guarantees that we will not experience permanent death because of our sins (1 Corinthians 15:12–18).”
ekegusii: Okobokigwa nigo kore ase ringana, naboigo ase ebimanyire mono, mbiri bioka gose ebimanyererio ebitanganitobwate bia abakeresito biokorikwa igoro you okobokigwa. Ebio esiko ekogenda gochi 1 Abathesaloniki; ekemo kiomochakano bwo amarube a Paulo, ayio arigetwe AD 50.2 Emiaka chirifu ibere nyuma yogokwa kwa kirisito. Omoganda norengeo bwabanto abwo bare koiranerania nga ere nabogetigwe korwa ase amakweri, naboigo akaagacha oboroso obuya ase amangana aya; naboigo amangana buna aya tari koba botuko. Korende enchiri ngoteba ere. Nonya ne miaka chiribu nyuma yebikoro ebio bigotebererwa (sirika AD 30–33), genda magega ase amangana a kare gose ase ogobwatia ogokoro.3 Naboigo amangana aya a kare tabwati amangana amange ayio are rirube riengencho ria Paulo. Ekio naki gekogera twateba nga ngogenda ere magega mono ogochaka ogotangani okuo kwabwatetu nakogachwa.4

english: The early church
ekegusii: “Ringana rio okobokigwa gwa kristo ne ringana rie engencho mono gochi ase abakeresito:Kobokigwa gotaiyo,Nto bwati gosemeria gwo okoborigwa kwe ebibe biaito (1 Abakorinto 15:12–18)”.

english: This waiting was understood by the leaders (who lived from approximately AD 67–855) to mean that some things would happen, while others would not occur until much later, and these latter matters were often misunderstood. These things included the persecution of rulers, along with angels and messengers who claimed to have revelations. Some of these claims were true, but most were false; and the false revelations often lacked credibility. Nevertheless, the truth remained clear despite these distortions.
ekegusii: Ekanisa entangani

english: Therefore, let us diligently examine what the teachers teach, ensuring that their teachings align with the fundamental principles and do not introduce innovations that contradict established doctrines. There should be no teaching that contradicts the teachings of the apostles, for the resurrection is at the heart of our faith.6
ekegusii: Okobokigwa ngoteberera kore ase chinchera inye (gwachagete AD 67–855) ngotebwa bire buna nigo bire ebiogotantania, korende ebinge bioogatantani mbirio ao nainde buna torakagere ase chingencho echi inye chingao chie egento emaiaka emenge nyuma yo okoba. Nigo bire ne binto ebinge buna nongo orosetie omoganda bwa abakungu abwo bachiete ase rikuruma, nga amaraika na abere arenge ao gose nerimo nakogenderera. Ebinge bie ebi mbiri bio ogotantani, buna bitamentiri aroro, ase ekio orokererio; ekemo ngetebe rimo nga riraika riakwanete, naboigo ekeorokererio ekende getebe nga’ amaraika nonsi akwanete. Nebe ogotantania onye ekeo rokererio gegoteba riraika erimo rioka.

english: Moreover, this waiting has been likened to a man who entrusted his property to servants while he traveled abroad, expecting them to manage it responsibly during his absence. The Jewish leaders questioned John the Baptist about his identity and authority, seeking confirmation that he was indeed the expected messenger. They also debated whether they should believe in Jesus, questioning whether He had come to fulfill their expectations (as suggested by the Sadducees – Matthew 22:23). And they questioned whether they should accept Him based on His own merits, because the Jews did not recognize Him as the Messiah until after the events unfolded. But now, let those who are resurrected testify to the abundance of life that Jesus offers, and let this testimony lead others to believe in Him.
ekegusii: Nkorenta ere engencho nga abasacha baarigete baarigete amangana aya nabo barainyore amangana amangao nonya gakororekana amangana amange ase otebia kwabo kwe ebinto biakorekanete. Teri korenta engencho goteba nga’ ase engencho ya abakungu bare ase erisiti, Kobokigwa ngokorekaneti bi.6

english: The beliefs surrounding Christ's return concern those who are awaiting it.
ekegusii: Naboigo, okobokigwa kwo obobui ngaange kware koba ase enchera etakageire ase emeganda emetangani ya abayaudi bare gocha goteba rikuruma ritabwati kende. Abayaudi abatangani mbaegenete mono igoro yo obogima nyuma yobonde, abande mbaegenete okobokigwa, nabende tibaegenete (buna abasadusesi (Mathayo 22:23). Nabande mbaegenete nga mbande babo bara bokigwe; korende onde tari ase abayuda baegenete nga’omonto oyomo narenge gochi kobokigwa nyuma ya onde bwensi. Eke nakio kiagerete abaorokigwa batabwate bomanyi bonde bwenshi igoro yeki yeso are goteba ekero abanete ogokwa kwaye naboigo nokobokig.

english: These beliefs include the hope of reunion with loved ones who have passed away, and the expectation that Christ's return will bring comfort and joy to believers. As Paul wrote in 1 Thessalonians 4:13–18, he shared his understanding of the resurrection; explaining that when Jesus returns, those who have died in Christ will rise first, and then those who are still alive will join them in the air to meet the Lord. Therefore, the resurrection of Jesus is the foundation of the Christian hope, surpassing all earthly expectations. In Philippians 3:20–21, we find assurance that our citizenship is in heaven, and we eagerly await the coming of our Savior, the Lord Jesus Christ.
ekegusii: Ebimanyererio bio okobokigwa gwa kristo gochia ase aba orokigwa baye

english: The history of our ancestors among the Gusii people. It is said that the Gusii people originally came from Egypt. According to this legend, our ancestry goes like this:
ekegusii: Emegano y' ororeri rwaito ntwe Abagusii n' emenge. Nigo togotebigwa buna ntwe Abagusii twensi nigo twarwete aaria Misri. Kobwatekana n' omogano oyomo, ororeri rwaito nigo rore iga:

english: This man gave birth to Enonko. Enonko gave birth to Ribiaka. Ribiaka gave birth to Magoma. Magoma gave birth to Osogo. This Osogo then gave birth to Mogusii. This lineage of Mogusii knows his descendants, namely Mogusero, Mochorwa, Mobasi, Nyaribari, Mogirango, Mogetutu, Monchari, and Momachoge.
ekegusii: Omonto akaibora Enonko. Enonko akaibora Ribiaka. Ribiaka akaibora Magoma. Magoma akaibora Osogo. Bono Osogo nere akaibora Mogusii. Bono sokoro yaito Mogusii, akamanya koibora Mogusero, Mochorwa, Mobasi, Nyaribari, Mogirango, Mogetutu, Monchari, na Momachoge.

english: Visiting and being visited brings great joy to those who have wealth: The people of Transmara and their fellow Gusii people often visit Koinania and are honored by the elders and respected. Because of this respect, they travel along our paths to Botende. Today, there are also those among us who live with the elders and learn good manners from them.
ekegusii: Okonywoma n' okonywomwa gochia ase ebisaku binde nkare gwaansete: Aaiga Transmara nao omosubati oyomo o Gusii orenge korokwa Koinania anywometwe n' Omomanyi na gotigara. Gatigara oo, ntwe tokagenderera n' orogendo rwaito gochia Botende. Ase igo, twensi n' abamo n' Abamanyi egekogera mbabwate amanyinga aito.

english: Ancestors of the Mogusii clan
ekegusii: Abangina b' omogaka Mogusii

english: Mogusii had five sons when he settled down:
ekegusii: Mogusii nanywomete abakungu batano buna ekobwatia:

english: 1. Moguche Ibu, who was born to Kemunto and raised in a homestead near Bonareri.
ekegusii: 1. Moguche Ibu ore korokwa Kemunto akaegwa erieta rie ebitinge akarokwa Bonareri.

english: 2. Nyamisanchu, who was born to Kwamboka and Nyaboke, also in a homestead.
ekegusii: 2. Nyamisanchu ore korokwa Kwamboka oetwe Nyaboke, koba erieta rie ebitinge.

english: 3. Bosibori, who inherited property from Mocharwa.
ekegusii: 3. Bosibori nere obwate omomura okorokwa Mocharwa.

english: 4. Bwari, who inherited property from Omache, of Monchari. Omache was named after Onchari Omache, a descendant of Bokendu.
ekegusii: 4. Bwari nere oiborete omomura okorokwa Omache, o Monchari. Omache nere naende orogetwe Onchari Omache, Chindiba Chia Bokendu.

english: 5. Mokeira, who inherited secrets from Omogusero.
ekegusii: 5. Mokeira, oyio oiborete Sereti ore Omogusero.

english: The traditions and unity of the Gusii people are very strong. However, this tradition has not been fully documented. That is why we remember what was said. However, it is said that once upon a time, when the land was full of peace, the Gusii people lived in harmony and shared everything equally.
ekegusii: Emegano yo ogocha n' okonganya kwa Abagusii nigo ere emenge. Ase boigo, emegano eye tiyarigetwe aande. Ntwe nigo tokoyerika bono buna togotebigwa. Ase boigo, nigo togotebigwa buna ase chingaki echio chionsi , eganga ya Abagusii nigo yarenge konganya ase okorigia ense entobu ase ebimeri.

english: Let us be careful. Anyone whose eyes are closed does not see, so the elders say, “Look carefully.”
ekegusii: Gotenena nkwarengeo. Onye ememiso gose mesabakwa tiyarengeo, abagaka nigo barenge goteba nga "Togenderere gochia motwe".

english: During their gatherings, they always share stories and discuss important matters. Those who are present often boast about their wealth. The story that is told goes like this:
ekegusii: Ase okonganya kwabo, nigo barenge korigia ase ememiso amo n' emesabakwa ere emenge. Ebi nabio biare kobaorokia buna ase ayio natobu. Omogano omotangani nigo ore iga:

english: This story says that the Gusii people migrated from a place called Irianyi, all the way to Mombasa, until they reached a point where they recognized the land as Gusii. The Gusii people, at Mombasa, were later led by Mokendo of Iruma.
ekegusii: Omogano oyo nigo ogoteba buna Omogusii nigo arwete korwa chinsemo chia Irianyi gose ensemo ya Mombasa, mbaka agacha goika aiga nka Gusii. Ase Abagusii, Mombasa eyio, nigo naende yare yare korokwa Mokendo o' Iruma.

english: It is said that the Gusii people did not travel alone; they were accompanied by Otere, who also led Mogikoyo. These leaders brought people from Irianyi of Mokendo and Iruma (Mombasa) and settled in the central region of Kenya.
ekegusii: Nigo togotebigwa buna Mogusii narenge na momura omwabo ore korokwa Otere oyio onaende ore korokwa Mogikoyo. Abamura aba babere nabwo batirete korwa Irianyi ya Mokendo o Iruma (Mombasa) na gocha gatigati ya Kenya.

english: In the central region of Kenya, Otere also settled. The Gusii people and their companions agreed that their stories and discussions should not be forgotten in the central region of Kenya. Therefore, the Gusii people, along with their companions, decided to send Otere to settle in the central region of Kenya.
ekegusii: Aiga gatigati ya Kenya, Otere nao atigarete. Mogusii amo na basubati bamwabo bakanyora buna ememiso amo n' emesabakwa tiyarenge aaiga gatigati ya kenya. Korende Mogusii, kare na abasubati bamwabo bakagenderera ase okong'anya ko batiga Otere aaira gatigati ya Kenya.

english: One companion, born to Moragori, settled near Mount Elgon (Boruya) during their travels, associating with the Abamaragoli. Another companion, Mosoba, settled in the area of Suba. Also, another companion of the Gusii people, born to Mokogoti, went to Mokoro and finally settled in Botende (Kurian).
ekegusii: Omosubati oyomo ore korokwa Moragori, nigo atigarete aaria aange na Mt Elgon (Boruya) ase okonganya, akaba ngina Abamaragoli. Omosubati onde, Mosoba agatigarera igaaria Suba. Ase boigo, omosubati onde omwabo Mogusii, ore korokwa Mokogoti, naende gose Mokoro, nigo achiete agatigara aaria Botende (kuria).

english: From the central region of Kenya, the Gusii people moved to Boruya. But despite this, they continued to visit Boruya and consult Moragori. From there, they migrated to Irianyi of Boruya and settled in Egesumu (Kisumu).
ekegusii: Korwa gatigati ya Kenya, Mogusii nigo atorete aaria Boruya. Nonya nabo igo, nigo banganyete naende korwa Boruya na komotiga Moragori aroro. Korwa abwo, bagatirimboka gochia chinsemo chia Irianyi ya Boruya na goika Egesumu (kisumu).

english: Below: Beautiful Mokendo O' Iruma: It is said that the Gusii people and their fellow tribesmen traveled together, including Otere [Mogikoyo], Momeru, Mokamba, Moragori, and Moembu, on their journey to Mokendo O' Iruma [Mombasa]. It is known that Mogikoyo, Momeru, Mokamba, and Moembu settled in Central Kenya, while Moragori and the Gusii people continued their journey.
ekegusii: Below: Beautiful Mokendo O' Iruma: Omogano onde bw' Abagusii nigo ogoteba buna Mogusii amo na abamura babwabo abwo barenge Otere [Mogikoyo], Momeru, Mokamba, Moragori amo na Moembu nigo baimogete ase orogendo korwa aaria Mokendo O' Iruma [Mombasa]. Ntomanyeti buna ninki kiagerete Mogikoyo, Momeru Mokamba, amo na Moembu bagatigarera aaria Central kenya, korende Moragori amo na Mogusii barabwo bakagenderera n' orogendo.

english: From the shores of Lake Kisumu, they began to explore and discover (fish) around Egesumu (Kisumu), and this became a common practice. The Gusii people sought sustenance, and Egesumu (Kisumu) provided them with abundant fish.
ekegusii: Aaiga ase ensemo ya Egesumu, bakaagacha egesarate gio okomenya (ebisumu) abwo Egesumu (Kisumu), korende chimori chikaagacherwa ebisumu ebinge. Mogusii akaroka asaya, Egesumu (Kisumu) korwa ase ebisumu ebi baroseti.

english: As it is said, the shores of Kisumu and the surrounding areas near Orechi [the banks of River Ekegere] were discovered. Furthermore, the shores and surroundings near Kemunto (the Gulf of Ekenyamorero) were also discovered.
ekegusii: Buna togotebigwa, aaiga Kisumu nao omomura oyomo orenge korokwa Orechi [Enswe ase Ekegere] aiboreretwe. Ase boigo, aaiga nao omoiseke orenge korokwa Kemunto (gulf ase Ekenyamorero) aiboreretwe.

english: The Gusii people started exploring around Kisumu and its environs. The people of Abagere and their traditions helped the Gusii people navigate towards Egesumu, heading towards Gwasi. In Gwasi, the tradition was very strong.
ekegusii: Mogusii tachieti komenya abwo Kisumu ase amatuko amange. Ogocha kwa Abagere amo n' riroba gotaba riitobu gokagera Abagusii naende bakanganya korwa Egesumu kogenda ase akorokwa Gwasi. Aaiga Gwasi, riroba itobu ndiarenge aroro nonya.

english: During those times, the Gusii people and others associated with Mosoba (the Basuba) also mingled. The people of Bosoba and their children near Mosoba were also discovered. From Kisumu, the Gusii people returned and camped near Ekemunto (the gulf) and collected resources from the land of Gusii.
ekegusii: Ase engencho eyio, Abagusii amo na abande naende bakanganya na gotiga Mosoba (Abasuba) aroro. Aaiga Bosoba nao omwana omomura orenge korokwa Mosoba aiboreretwe. Korwa Kisumu, Mogusii bagaeta na gotamboka ase Ekemunto (gulf) na kwamboka gochia ase ebitunwa bia Gusii.

english: When they left Gusii, they dispersed. One group went to Botende (Kuria), and another moved towards Bosoba (Suba). Over time, the Gusii people remained in Gusii, and their descendants are still Gusii today. This is the story of our ancestors and origins.
ekegusii: Ko baika Gusii, bagaatanekana. Mokoro akagenda Botende (kuria) na Mosoba akamboka kogenda Bosoba (Suba). Nonya nabo igo, Mogusii ere agatigara Gusii na mbaka rero nao are Gusii. Oyo noro omogano bw' okonganya gwaito omotangani.

english: These are all clans. Omokamba, Omoragori, Omogikoyo, Omoembu, Omomeru, Omotende, Omosoba: These are the names of the clans. These tribesmen and their families are numerous.
ekegusii: Aba bonsi n' abaminto. Omokamba, Omoragori, Omogikoyo, Omoembu, Omomeru, Omotende, Omosoba: Nigo tokona goitana bosa. Aba mbamura n' baiseke baminto.

english: It is said that the history of the Gusii people tells us that the Gusii people came from Egypt. Traditionally, it is said about the Gusii people, that they, along with their fellow tribesmen like Moragori, Mokamba, Mogikoyo, Moembu, and Momeru, migrated together.
ekegusii: Omogano onde bw' omochakano bwo Omogusii nigo ogoteba buna Abagusii nigo barwete Misri (Egypt ase rero). Ritangani, nigo togotebigwa ng'a Mogusii, oyio ore ise bw' Abagusii bonsi, narenge amo na bamura babwabo abwo barenge Moragori, Mokamba, Mogikoyo, Moembu, amo na Momeru.

english: Where did these people come from?
ekegusii: Baminto ng'ai twarwete?

english: It is said that the Gusii people, along with their fellow tribesmen, crossed the great river Nile and reached the lands of Ethiopia. From there, they traveled to Sudan and settled in the area of Uganda. From Uganda (Boganda), the Gusii people continued their journey until they arrived near Mount Elgon.
ekegusii: Nigo togotebigwa buna Mogusii, kare na bamura bamwabo, nigo atirimbogete ase chingegu chi' oroche rwa River Nile na goeta gati gati y ense ya Ethiopia. Korwa abwo, akagenda Sudan na gosokera aaria Uganda. Korwa Uganda (Boganda), Mogusii nigo agendererete n' orogendo mbaka agaika aange na Mt. Elgon.

english: It is said that near Mount Elgon, the Gusii people separated from their companions and continued onward. Moragori settled in his own area near Mount Elgon, and interacted with the people of Abaluhya. Following his companions, the Gusii people continued to explore the area near Siaya, which is now called Bogere.
ekegusii: Nigo togototebigwa aaiga Mt. Elgon, nao Mogusii aatananakenate amo na abamwabo, na kogenda kobwaye. Moragori ere agatigara aaria ange na Mt Elgon, na koba ase egesaku kia Abaluhya. Gatiga abamwabo, Mogusii akang'anya na kogenda komenya aaria aange na Siaya, eyio ere Bogere ase rero.

english: I understand that this is where Mogusii settled with his people during their migration. In the region of Siaya, among the people of Abagere, Mogusii continued on, and then proceeded to explore the area of Egesumu (Kisumu).
ekegusii: Ntomanyeti buna ninki kiagerete Mogusii agatiga abawabo ase okonganya oko. Ase engencho y' chisegi korwa ase Abagere be ense eyio ya Siaya, Mogusii akang'anya naende, korwa abwo na kogenda komenya aaria Egesumu (Kisumu).

english: The name “Kisumu” comes from Ekegusii.
ekegusii: Erieta "Kisumu" n' rie Ekegusii

english: From there, in Egesumu, the Gusii people found abundant resources including livestock, and the land was fertile (Gesumu) Kisumu. It is said that in Gesumu, Mogusii and his people prospered, and were blessed with plenty.
ekegusii: Aaiga, Egesumu, nigo Abagusii baagachete ebisumu ebinge bie chiombe, ekagera bakayaroka (Gesumu) Kisumu. Nigo togotebigwa buna aaiga Gesumu nao Mogusii amo na ng'ina, oyio ore korokwa Nyakomogendi basirerete na gotindekwa.

english: Over time, the livestock increased greatly, and there was a large settlement in Egesumu. Because of this settlement, the children of Mogusii did not need to search for food from distant places. In the vicinity of this settlement, prominent leaders emerged from various areas, such as Mobasi, Oibabe, Mochorwa, and Mogusero, who organized the affairs of the Gusii people in Egesumu, working to protect the wealth of Gusii.
ekegusii: Nonya nabo igo, chiombe chigaansa gokwa n' enchara enene ekaba abwo Egesumu. Ge enchara yaba, abana ba Mogusii tibachieti komenya igaa ase amatuko amange. Ase engencho y enchara eye, abagaka abanene b' egesaku giaito ase engaki eyio, abwo barenge Mobasi, Oibabe, Mochorwa na Mogusero bakaroberia okonganya kwa Abagusii korwa Egesumu, kogenda gochia ase ebitunwa bia Gusii ya rero.

english: Through this organization, they began to move from the gulf and settle in the territories of Gusii. From the territories of Gusii, they continued to organize themselves until they reached Kericho [which is also known as Kabianga].
ekegusii: Ke emeroberio eye y' okonganya yaera, bagatamboka ase ekemunto (gulf) na goika ase ebitunwa bia Gusii ya rero. Korwa ase ebitunwa bia Gusii, bakagenderera konganya mbaka bagaika Kericho [eye nero naende ekorokwa Kabianga].

english: When they arrived at Kabianga, there was conflict. The ground was very swampy. The weather was hot. The land was difficult due to the presence of the Abamanyi and Abasigisi people. However, despite these challenges, the elders and warriors persevered. All this hardship led the Gusii people to settle here, in Kabianga.
ekegusii: Ko baika Kabianga, obokongu bokaba. Ndagera tiyare kwama. Tari igo rioka. Esegi korwa ase Abamanyi amo no Abasigisi ekaba entindi. Komenta nayio, oborwaire obonge ase etugo amo na abanto bokabucha. Bono emechando eye yonsi ekagera Abagusii bakaroka ase aya, Kabianga.

english: As more settlements developed around Kabianga, the Gusii people moved further and established settlements in Sotik, Gelegele, Ikorongo, Trans Mara [Transmara, Mara Motobo, the ridge of Gamba].
ekegusii: Ke emechando emenge yaba aaiga Kabianga, Abagusii bakanganya naende na koirana bagotirimboka gochia Sotik, Gelegele, Ikorongo, Trans Mara [ Emara gose Transmara, Mara Motobo, Igena ria Gamba].

english: And then they started to spread out. The Abamanyi people understood their ways just like the Gusii people.
ekegusii: Naende nigo tokona goitana bosa. Abamanyi mbabwate amanyinga aito ntwe Abagusii.

english: From Mara Motobo and its surroundings, the Gusii people extended their territory towards Nyakoinania, interacting with both the Abamanyi and the Bomanyi people. From there, the Gusii people continued to organize themselves and expand towards Migori (Botende), Nyangarora, Nyakoe, Getembe [including Marani], Manga Isecha (the plains of Ogeto, and Monyerero) in the central highlands, and also the plains of Ikuruma.
ekegusii: Aaiga Emara Motobo nao omosubati oyomo bwa Abagusii orenge korokwa Nyakoinania anywometwe amo na Abamanyi na gotigara Bomanyi. Korwa abwo, Abagusii bakagenderera ase okonganya gochia Migori (Botende), Nyangarora, Nyakoe, Getembe [ ange na Marani], Manga Isecha (Emanga y' Ogeto, na Monyerero) ime ya Central kitutu, amo na aaria Emanga nse ya Ikuruma.

english: The land became increasingly populated. People built homes everywhere.
ekegusii: Egesaku getabwati abarai nigo kegotagoka. Abarai mbakabeiroo korwa kare

english: Because of this extensive migration from Egesumu, the Gusii people remembered the prominent leaders who came from different regions. The stories of these leaders and their deeds have been passed down through generations, becoming part of the history of the Gusii people:
ekegusii: Abwo ase obomenyi n' okonganya gwaito gwensi korwa Egesumu, Abagusii ntwabwate abagaka abanene abwo barenge korwa oborai amo n' obosemia. Gati y' abagaka abwo ase chingaki echio nigo barenge koraa chinyomba chia Abagusii nigo barenge buna ekobwatia:

english: [I]. The warriors [The leader Oisukia who was also a warrior].
ekegusii: [I]. Abanchari [Omogaka Oisukia nere orenge omorai].

english: [II]. The priests [Mogichoncho, who was also a great healer of Mobasi and a warrior].
ekegusii: [II]. Ababasi [Mogichoncho, oyio orenge omomura omonene o Mobasi nere orenge omorai].

english: [III]. The diviners [The leader Manyanta who was also a warrior]. They say that the Abanyaribari and the Abamachoge were also diviners. The Gusii people remember them fondly, remembering their wisdom and knowledge. The leader Manyanta was particularly skilled in dealing with the Abanyaribari and the Abamachoge.
ekegusii: [II]. Abasweta [ Omogaka Manyanta nere orenge omorai]. Ka moranche inyora buna Abanyaribari amo na Abamachoge nabwo Abasweta. Abagusii mbebagete amarieta gete ye chingiti ao ao, amarieta ayio akabwata. Omogaka Manyanta nigo arenge koraaa Abanyaribari amo na Abamachoge bonsi.

english: [IV]. The rainmakers [The leader Sakawa who was also a warrior]. It is said that Omobani Sakawa possessed the power to control the weather for the people of Bogetutu. These people also had the power to influence events among the Abagusii. Honor the rainmakers.
ekegusii: [IV]. Abagetutu [ Omobani Sakawa nere orenge omorai]. Ase okoinyora naende, Omobani Sakawa nigo arwete ase enyomba ya Abageka aaria Bogetutu. Abageka nabwo barenge enyomba enchorwa ya ababani ase Abagusii. Tochiesera Abageka.

english: To the Colossians
ekegusii: Abakolosai

english: 1 Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Timothy his brother, 2 to the saints and faithful brothers in Christ who are at Colossae: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. 3 We always thank God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, when we pray for you, 4 having heard of your faith in Christ Jesus and of the love that you have for all the saints, 5 because of the hope laid up for you in heaven, which you have heard about through the word of truth, the gospel 6 which has come to you, just as it also does throughout the whole world, and is bearing fruit and increasing—just as it has done among you since the day you heard it and understood the grace of God in truth, 7 just as you learned from Epaphras, our beloved fellow servant, who is a faithful minister of Christ on your behalf, 8 who has told us of your love in the Spirit. 9 And so, from the day we heard this, we have not ceased praying for you, asking that you may be filled with the knowledge of His will in all wisdom and spiritual understanding, 10 so that you may walk in a manner worthy of the Lord, fully pleasing Him, bearing fruit in every good work, growing in the knowledge of God, 11 strengthened with all power according to His glorious might, for all perseverance and patience with joy, 12 giving thanks to the Father who has qualified you to share in the inheritance of the saints in light, 13 who delivered us from the domain of darkness and transferred us to the kingdom of His beloved Son, 14 in whom we have redemption, the forgiveness of sins. 15 He is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn over all creation. 16 For by Him all things were created, both in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible, whether thrones or dominions or rulers or authorities—all things were created through Him and for Him. 17 And He is before all things, and in Him all things hold together. 18 He is the head of the body, the church, He who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead, so that He might be supreme in everything. 19 For in Him all the fullness of God was pleased to dwell, and through Him to reconcile to Himself all things, whether on earth or in heaven, making peace by the blood of His cross. 20 And though you were once alienated from God and hostile in your mind because of your evil deeds, 21 yet He has now reconciled you in His flesh through death, in order to present you holy and blameless and above reproach before Him. 22 But you, being made alive in Christ, were raised up together with Him and seated with Him in the heavenly places in Christ Jesus, 23 to demonstrate His surpassing greatness in generations to come, so that with eternal glory He might show the wealth of His grace in kindness toward us in Christ Jesus. 24 To Him be the glory forever and ever. Amen. 25 Now I rejoice in my sufferings for your sake, and in my flesh I am completing what is lacking in Christ’s afflictions for the sake of His body, which is the church. 26 I have become its servant according to God’s plan entrusted to me for your benefit. 27 To them God willed to make known how great are the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles, which is Christ living in you, the hope of glory. 28 We proclaim Him, warning everyone and teaching everyone with all wisdom, so that we may present everyone mature in Christ. 29 For this reason I also suffer, striving according to His power that works within me.
ekegusii: 1 Paulo, omotomwa o Yesu Kristo as'obwanchani bwa Nyasaye, na Timotheo oyominto, 2 as'abaminto abachenu nabegeni abare ime ase Kolosai: Obuya bobe asemore nomorembe okorua ase Nyasaye Tata oito nas'Omonene Yesu Kristo. 3 Twamoakeire ng'a mbuya mono Nyasaye, Ise Omonene oito Yesu Kristo, amatuko onsi twabasabeire, 4 ekero twaigwete amang'ana aya okwegena kwaino ase Kristo Yesu, nobwanchani more nabwo as'abachenu bonsi, 5 as'engecho y'ogosemeria mwagacheirwe emonga igoro, amang'ana aya mwayaigwete kare ase ring'ana ri'ekeene as'enchili, 6 yaikire asemore buna ere as'ense yonsi, ekwama amatunda nagokina, buna yakinire asemore, korwa rituko mwaigwete nakoinyora mono obuya bwa Nyasaye as'ekeene; 7 buna mworokereretigwe na Epafra omogisangio omwanchwa oito, ore omokori omwegeni ase Kristo as'engecho yaino, 8 nere agatworokereria obwanchani bwaino as'Omoika. 9 Naki as'ayio naintwe korwa rituko twaigwete, titotigeti kobusabera, nogosaba asemore, moichorigwe chisemi chi'obwanchani bwaye as'obong'aini bwonsi, nokoinyora kw'omoyo ime; 10 mogende buna abagwenerete as'Omonene, momogwenere kegima; ase ker'emeremo emiya mokwama amatunda, momenteke ase chisemi chia Nyasaye; 11 momentwe chinguru as'okobua gwonsi, as'okoreng'ana gwe chinguru chi'obonene bwaye, as'oboremereria bwonsi amo nomogoko, 12 mokomoakera ng'a mbuya mono Tata, oyotogweneirie intwe tonyore ensemo y'omwando bw'abachenu as'omobaso; 13 otokonyete korwa chinguru chi'omosunte, agatong'anyia nagotosoyia as'obonda bw'obwanchani bwaye; 14 ekiagera asere ntore nokoborigwa as'amanyinga aye, okwabera kw'ebibe: 15 nere nomogwekano o Nyasaye otarikororekana, omotongi as'ebitongwa bionsi; 16 naki asere ebinto bionsi bigatongwa, ebire igoro nebire igoro as'ense, ebikororekana, nebitarikororekana, nonya nebirogo bi'obonene, gose oboruoti, gose obonene gose okobua; ebinto bionsi bigatongwa as'enchera yaye, nas'engecho yaye; 17 nere igo arengeo ritang'ani ri'ebinto bionsi, nebinto bionsi bibwataine asare. 18 Nere nomotwe bw'omobere, engecho yaye ekanisa: nere nomochakano, omoiborwa bwe ritang'ani as'abakwete; erio abe omotang'ani ase bionsi. 19 Naki ise agancha boria bwonsi oboikeranu boikaranse asare; 20 nas'ere kobibwatania ebinto bionsi nere, gakorire omorembe as'amanyinga omosalaba oye; nas'ere kobirabe ebinto hire igoro as'ense, gose ebire igoro. 21 Nainwe, igoniwareuge agwo ritang'ani, mwatananetwe nere, nababisa as'ebirengererio biaino, as'ogokora kwaino okobe, obasang'ananirie bono, 22 as'omobere bw'euyama yaye as'ogokwa kwaye, erio abarente inwe as'obosio bwaye, abachenu, motari nokomocha gose kemoa: 23 komoraikaranse botambe as'okwegena, mwabaire igoro as'oboroso naende abakong'u, motaonchoiri nagotiga ogosemeria gw'enchili mwaigwete amang'ana aye, arandigwe as'ebitongwa bionsi bire inse as'erioba; as'ayio inche Paulo ngakorwa omokori oye. 24 Bono nagokeire ogochandwa inde nakwo as'engecho yaino; naende nayaikeranirie aria aremete as'ogochandwa gwa Kristo as'omobere one, as'engecho y'omobere oye, engecho yaye ekanisa yayej 25 as'ayio nabaire omokori oye, as'oborendi bwa Nyasaye, naetwe ensemo yaino, ng'ikeranie ring'ana ria Nyasaye, 26 obobisi boria bwabisetwe korwa kare nakare, nakorwa ebigori bionsi: korende bono bwaigoreirwe as'abachenu baye. 27 Korende Nyasaye agancha koborokia engecho y'obotenenku bw'obonene bw'obobisi obo as'Ebisaku, nario Kristo ime yaino, ogosemeria kw'obonene: 28 ere twarandirie amang'ana aye, komokurera ker'omonto, nakomworokereria ker'omonto ase chisemi chionsi, tonyare komoreta ker'omonto omoikeranu ase Yesu Kristo; 29 nainche ngokorande emeremo as'engecho eyio, nagokora omokia koreng'ana as'ogokora kwaye, ogokora emeremo asende ase chinguru.

english: 1 So then, just as we have received from the Lord and taught you, you must live in love with one another, as you learned from God. 2 And further, we instruct you to live a life worthy of the calling you have received. 3 Be eager to maintain unity in the Spirit, binding yourselves together with peace. 4 There is one body, one Spirit—just as you were called to one hope when you were called— 5 one Lord, one faith, one baptism, 6 one God and Father of all, who is over all and through all and in all. 7 But to each one of us grace has been given according to the measure of Christ’s gift. 8 Therefore it says: “When He ascended on high, He led captivity captive and gave gifts to men.” 9 What does this mean? That He descended to the regions below. This is the One who ascended far above all heaven, so that He might fill everything.) 10 Now to Him who is able to do immeasurably more than all we ask or imagine, according to His power that is at work within us, 11 to Him be glory in the church and in Christ Jesus throughout all generations, forever and ever. Amen. 12 For we write to you, brothers and sisters, encouraging you to recognize and acknowledge God’s grace toward you, which was shown to you through our ministry. 13 Therefore, we urge you not to become discouraged because of the suffering of our fellow believers. It is God’s will that you endure hardship for His name. 14 For just as we told you earlier, we tell you again: The kingdom of God is not about eating and drinking, but about righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit. 15 For those who live according to the flesh set their minds on earthly things, but those who live according to the Spirit set their minds on spiritual things. 16 But if anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, they do not belong to Him. 17 However, if anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, they do not belong to Him. 18 But God has chosen the foolish things of the world to shame the wise; and He has chosen the weak things of the world to shame the strong. 19 For God’s wisdom seems foolish to this world, but God knows that its wisdom is true. And the world’s wisdom seems wise, but God knows that it is foolishness.  20 So let us not boast about what we can do, but rather rejoice in what God has done for us. 21 We are fools for Christ’s sake, but you are wise in worldly terms. 22 Let others think we are crazy, but you know that we are sane when we speak of God. 23 We are weak, but you are strong. You dishonor us, but we honor you. 24 We appear foolish, but you are respected. We are hungry and thirsty, while you are well-fed. We are poorly dressed, while you are clothed in fine garments. 25 We are treated like the scum of the earth, but you are esteemed by the world.
ekegusii: 1 Korende nindigetie momanye omokia one inde noro as'engecho yaino, nase baria ba Laodikia, nabaria batarandora obosio bwane as'omobere; 2 erinde baremigwe chinkoro chiabo, kobarabwatanigwe as'obwanchani, banyore obotenenku bwonsi bw'okoinyora oboikeranu, banyare komanya kegima obobisi bwa Nyasaye, engecho yaye Kristo, 3 ime asare nchireo chinibo chionsi chi'obong'aini nechisemi chibisekanete. 4 Nakwanire ring'ana eri, omonto tacha kobang'aina as'amang'ana ay'okoebereria. 5 Naki nimba tindi aroro as'omobere, igande amo nainwe as'omoika, kondagoke nakorora okorobera kwaino, noboremu bw'okwegena kwaino ase Kristo. 6 Gaki buna mwamonyorire Yesu Kristo Omonene, genda boigo asere, 7 abanyene emeri, nokoagachwa asere, mwakorirwe abakong'u as'okwegena, buna niworokereretigwe, momenteke as'okoiraneria ng'a mbuya. 8 Rigereria monto onde tabaisa kobasiria as'obong'ainereria bwaye, nokong'aina kwa bosa, as'engecho y'ogotunyana chisemi chia mwanyabanto, as'engecho y'okworokereria gw'ense, korende tari as'engecho ya Kristo: 9 naki asere nao boikaransere oboikeranu bwonsi Obonyasaye as'engecho y'omobere. 10 Nainwe mwaichoirwe asere, oyore omotwe bw'obonene bwonsi nokobua: 11 asere mwarokigwe as'okwaroka ogotakoregeti as'amaboko, as'okorusia oria omobere bwe chinyama, as'okwaroka gwa Kristo; 12 kamoratindekwe amo nere as'ebatiso, nas'okwo mwabokigwe amo nere, as'okwegena ogokora kwa Nyasaye oyomobogetie korwa as'amakweri. 13 Nainwe, konyora mwakure ekiagera as'okomocha kwaino nas'ogotaroka kw'emebere yaino, akabakora moyo amo nere, gatiekire gotwabera okomocha gwaito gwonsi; 14 gatiekire gotinyia riria rirube riarigetwe as'amachiko, rigotosoera; eriarenge nobobisa asetore: oritigeirie, tiriba gati yaito nere, akariakeraas'omosalaba; 15 gatiekire kwerusia obonene nokobua, akabiorokia maiso marore, akagoka igoro ase biro bio as'omosalaba. 16 Gaki, monto tabagambia inwe as'endagera gose ebikonyugwa, gose as'engecho ye rituko rinene gose okooroka kw'omotienyi, gose esabato: 17 amang'ana ayio nekiriri as'amang'ana agocha gocha; korende omobere noyo Kristo. 18 Monto onde tabaura ekeegwa kiaino as'okorigia kwaye, as'okweororobia as'ogosasima amalaika, nakwebeka as'amang'ana ayarorire, nakoenena bosa as'obong'aini bw'omobere oye, 19 korende tabwateti Omotwe, ekiagera korwa as'oro, omobere bwonsi okonyora onsi nakobwatanigwa ase chinengo nemeki, gokina as'ogokina koruete ase Nyasaye. 20 Gaki onye mwakure amo na Kristo mogatiga okworokereria gw'ense, naseki mokoba inse as'ekina, buna nabamenyete as'ense, 21 timobwata, timoigwa, timokuna. 22 (Amang'ana ayio onsi igagosareka ekero ki'ogokorerwa), komokobwata amachiko nokworokereria kwa mwanyabanto? 23 Amang'ana ayio arorekanire buna nare nechisemi, nase chingecho cht'ogosaba, nobokanyeku, mwekoreire inwe mweka, nas'okogambera omobere as'obotindi; korende takogwenera gento as'okorengereria kw'omobere.

english: 1 Now those who are believers should live according to the example of Christ, who gave himself up for us, so that we might have eternal life with God. 2 Those who are not believers should not judge those who are. 3 For our lives are hidden with Christ in God. 4 Christ will reveal his glory in us, and we will share in his splendor. 5 Let us not be proud or arrogant, but humble ourselves before God. 6 Let us not seek our own interests, but the interests of others. 7 Let us not think highly of ourselves, but instead look to God for guidance. 8 Let us not compare ourselves to others, but focus on pleasing God. 9 Let us not be lazy or idle, but work hard to serve God. 10 Let us not be selfish or greedy, but generous and compassionate. 11 There is no difference between Jew and Gentile, circumcised and uncircumcised, barbarian and Scythian, slave and free—for Christ is all, and in all. 12 Therefore, as God’s chosen people, holy and beloved, clothe yourselves with compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, and patience. 13 Bear with each other and forgive one another, just as the Lord forgave you. And above all, love each other deeply, because love covers over a multitude of sins.  14 Let peace reign in your hearts, and let the peace of Christ control you. 15 Be thankful in everything, for this is God’s will for you in Christ Jesus. 16 Let the message of Christ dwell among you richly, teaching and admonishing one another with all wisdom, singing psalms and hymns and spiritual songs with gratitude in your hearts to God. 17 And whatever you do, whether in word or deed, do it all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through him. 18 Wives, submit to your husbands, as is fitting in the Lord. 19 Husbands, love your wives and do not mistreat them. 20 Children, obey your parents in everything, for this pleases the Lord. 21 Fathers, do not provoke your children to anger, but bring them up in the discipline and instruction of the Lord. 22 Slaves, obey your earthly masters in everything, as though serving Christ. 23 Whatever you do, work at it with all your heart, as working for the Lord, not for human masters. 24 Remember that you will receive an inheritance from the Lord, for you are serving the Lord Christ. 25 So whoever practices deceit, let him know that he will reap what he sows.
ekegusii: 1 Gaki onye mwabokire amo na Kristo, rigia ayare igoro aase Kristo aikaransete, as'okoboko gw'okorio kwa Nyasaye. 2 Rigia ayare igoro, tari ayare as'ense. 3 Ekiagera mwakwete, nobogima bwaino bwabisirwe amo na Kristo ase Nyasaye. 4 Kristo karache kororekana oyore obogima bwaito, erio nainwe namororekane amo nere as'obonene bwaye. 5 Gaki biite ebimo biaino bire as'ense; obotomani, eubi, okorengereria okobe, okogania okobe, nokorengereria, nakwo ogosasima esanamu; 6 as'engecho y'ayio endamwamu ya Nyasaye yabaikeire abana b'ogosaria. 7 As'ayio nainwe igo mware gotara kare, iga mwabete as'aya. 8 Korende bono yabeke are aya onsi; okobea, endamwamu, nobobe, nokorama, nogokwana okobe gokorua as'emenwa yaino: 9 timotebania oborimo; ekiagera mwamorusirie omonto okare, amo nogokora kwaye, 10 mwamobekire omonto omoyia, okorirwe omoyia anyore chisemi as'omogwekano oye ere oyomotongete. 11 Agwo tari Omoyunani gose Omoyahudi, okwarokigwa gose ogotarokigwa, oyotamunyeti gento, gose Omosikuthi, omosomba, gose omobiare; korende Kristo nas'onsi, nase bonsi. 12 Gaki ekiagera more abachore ba Nyasaye, abachenu banchire, beka omoyo bw'amabera, obuya, oboitongo, obwororo, oboremereria; 13 mobogoreranie, nakwaberana, omonto karabe nering'ana igoro as'omonto onde; buna Kristo ababerete inwe, naboigo nainwe kora boigo. 14 Igoro as'aya onsi beka obwanchani, nabwo egesibo ki'oboikeranu. 15 Nomorembe o Nyasaye ogambe ase chinkoro chiaino, noro mwarangererigwe as'omobere oyomo; mobe abanto bakoiraneria ng'a mbuya mono. 16 Ring'ana ria Kristo rikaranse as'obonge ime yaino ase chisemi chionsi, mworokereranie nagokanania as'esaburi nogotera, nogotera kw'omoyo, as'obuya mokomoterera Omonene ase chinkoro chiaino ime. 17 Na kera erimogokora, ase ring'ana gose ogokora, kora onsi as'erieta ri'Omonene Yesu, mokoiraneria ng'a mbuya Nyasaye Tata asere. 18 Inwe abakungu, igwera abasacha baino, buna egwenerete as'Omonene. 19 Nainwe abasacha, ancha abakungu baino, timoba nobororo asebare. 20 Nainwe abana moigwere abaibori as'amang'ana onsi; naki ring'ana eri ndigwenerete as'Omonene, 21 Nainwe abatata, timochegia abana baino, tibabaisa gokwa emioyo. 22 Nainwe abasomba mobaigwera abwo bare as'omobere ng'a nabanene baino; as'amang'ana onsi, tari obosomba bw'amaiso buna abakwegwenia ase mwanyabanto, korende as'obuya bw'enkoro, mokomosika Nyasaye, 23 Rinde rionsi mogokora, rikore as'omoyo, buna as'Omonene, gose tari ase mwanyabanto; 24 komoramanye ng'a namonyore as'Omonene eng'eria y'omwando; ekiagera mokomokorera Omonene Kristo. 25 Naki oyorakore bobe, igo aranyore naende obobe bwaye akorire: korende gwanchereria tikoiyo.

english: 1 Now we who are strong ought to bear with the failings of the weak and not to please ourselves. 2 Each of us should please our neighbors for their good, to build them up. 3 For even Christ did not please himself, but took on the form of a servant, being born in the likeness of men. 4 And being found in appearance as a man, he humbled himself by obeying to death—even death on a cross! 5 Therefore God exalted him to the highest position and gave him the name above all names. 6 This is why, at the mention of the name of Jesus every knee should bow, in heaven and on earth and under the earth. 7 And every tongue acknowledge that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father. 8 Now about Philemon, our dear brother, and Archippus, our fellow prisoner: 9 I send greetings to you, along with the church that meets in your home. 10 Greetings to Epaphras, my fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus. 11 To Mark, who ministered with Barnabas and Paul. 12 And to Aristarchus, my fellow prisoner. Instructions to you: give comfort to my friend Onesimus. 13 Also greet those who meet in the house of Nympha and to all the churches. 14 Greet Luke, Demas, and the others. 15 Give my greetings to the brothers and sisters at Laodicea, and to Nymphas and the church in his home. 16 After you have read this letter, see that it is also read in the church at Laodicea, and that you exchange letters with them. 17 Tell Archippus: “See to it that you complete the ministry you have received in the Lord.” 18 I, Paul, write this greeting with my own hand. Remember me!
ekegusii: 1 Ninwe abanene bae abasomba baino ekere kia boronge, mokomanya ng'a nainwe more n'Omonene igoro. 2 Kora mono as'ogosaba, komokorenda as'ogosaba nakoiraneria ng'a mbuya; 3 nogotosabera naintwe twensi, Nyasaye atoigorere egesieri ase ring'ana riaye, tokwane obobisi bwa Kristo, naki as'engecho yaye nasibirwe, 4 erio ng'orokie, buna ingwenerete gokwana, 5 Genda as'obong'aini as'obosio bw'abwo abare isiko, mogokorera ekero. 6 Amang'ana aino abe nobuya amatuko onsi, ansere buna omonyo monyare komanya buna chagwenerete koiraneria ker'omonto. 7 Tukiko, oyominto omwanchwa, omosomba omwegeni, omosomba omogisangio one as'Omonene, naborokie amang'ana ane onsi; 8 ere namotomire asemore, as'engecho eyio eyio, momanye amang'ana aito, abaremie chinkoro chiaino; 9 amo na Onesimo, oyominto omwegeni, omwanchwa, ore omonto oino. Nababorokie amang'ana onsi ayare aiga. 10 Aristariko, osibetwe amo nainche obakwanirie, na Marko, omoigwa o Baranaba, oyio mwanyorire amachiko as'amang'ana aye; karaikeasemore moroisie. 11 Na Yesu, okorokwa Yusto; abwo nabanto barogete: abwo boka nabakori emeremo amo nainche as'engecho y'obonda bwa Nyasaye; nabarabwo igo barenge kondemia. 12 Epafra, ore omonto o seino, omosomba o Yesu Kristo, obakwanirie, okorire omokia amatuko onsi as'engecho yaino as'ogosaba kwaye, erinde motenene abaikeranu abamanyete mono as'obwanchani bwonsi bwa Nyasaye. 13 Naki nabaire kirori ng'a nare nomokia omonge as'engecho yaino, nas'engecho y'abwo bare ase Laodikia, nas'engecho yabwo bare Hieropoli. 14 Luka, oria omorwaria omwanchwa, obakwanirie, na Dema. 15 Bakwanie abaminto bare ase Laodikia, na Numfa, nekanisa ere as'enyomba yaye. 16 Rirube eri karirasomwe asemore, tiga risomwe naende as'ekanisa ya Laodikia; nariria ria Laodikia risomwe nainwe. 17 Motebie Arikippo, arigererie mono obosomba boria kwaetwe as'Omonene, erio aboikeranie. 18 Ogokwania kwane inche Paulo, as'okoboko kwane inche bweka. Inyora ebisibo biane. Obuya bobe amo nainwe.

english: Edwin Okong'o, the son of Mache Ng'umbu, was known for being a thief. It means he was always found stealing things from people. This is true.
ekegusii: Edwin Okong'o, Omwana Oito Mache Ng'umbu okarangire chibando. Yaani nere bweka okona koria chibando saiga mwaye. igwa bono

english: Omoriki and Edwin Okong'o, the son of Mache Ng'umbu.
ekegusii: Omoriki ne Edwin bw’ Okong’o, Omwana Oito o Mache Ng’umbu

english: He went to Nairobi intending to look for work and find someone who could help him with Motanya and his wife Mogeni. The wife of Nyakerario had prepared food consisting of vegetables and meat, beans and ripe bananas, very large mushrooms which she cooked with groundnuts.
ekegusii: Kero kende konde Nairobi togaikaransa emesa koragera no omosani one okorokwa Motanya na momura oye Mogeni. Omong’ina oye Nyakerario konye ominire obokima bw’ obori ne enyama ye embori, chinsaga na amabere amaruranu amaroro se abwate amakombi amanene ndagoake bwateke erogoma.

english: They enjoyed the food greatly, and the wife of Nyakerario continued preparing more.
ekegusii: Tokaigatera bono obokima egesamaro, no omong’ina Nyakerario okona gototiotereria.

english: The wife said, "You have eaten well today. You have satisfied yourselves.
ekegusii: Omong’ina agatotebia, “Bobege moigote kegima. Ninwe abamura mogokiina.”

english: Motanya replied, "My friend, I don't want this kind of food anymore. I will go and look for something else.
ekegusii: Motanya akamotebia, “Omwanchi, gaki inche no omogaka omogotu tari bono ngokina. Nche nigo nkoria bosiniini.”

english: The people did not agree. They refused to let their children go to school because they were afraid of what might happen to them. However, they remembered Mache Ng'umbu saying that he would never forget the kindness shown to him, so they decided to try. I appreciate the food, I respect the Gusii people, I enjoy the meat and beans, and I will remember this day. Because of the ripe bananas.
ekegusii: Intwe abamura tokagenderera. Tokabosimbaga buna abana be esekenderi enchara eitete ekero abarimu barire chibesa chibwenerete kogorera abana endagera eisaine. Nainche buna konye narure Mache Ng’umbu ase ntari konyora bosie bwa bori, nkaigatera. Mbwata obokima, mbobata ekegusii, mbwaterania enyama ne chinsaga, mbeka gochia monwa. Kobogotirimboka, ng’iyereria na amabere amaruranu.

english: We often see how a woman can ruin her husband's reputation by revealing secrets.
ekegusii: Ekero twakoora bwonsi korwa ekee omong’ina akarangeria omosubati ore komokonya koruga arete obonde.

english: I pleaded, "Mother, I understand.
ekegusii: Nkamokania, “Yaya, Mami, inche naigotire.”

english: The wife told her husband, "Go to Mogeni and the American who says he doesn't know where the property of Mache Ng'umbu is.
ekegusii: Omong’ina agatebia omosubati, “Retera Mogeni bono Omoamerika ere tiga ange onarire ebitoche bia Mache Ng’umbu.”

english: Mogeni then responded, "Mother, yes. I will go when I am ready.
ekegusii: Mogeni nere agakana, “Mami, yaya. Nabeire buna riria nabete.”

english: I laughed and laughed and laughed until we were reconciled. And I kept laughing and laughing until I grew up. And I kept laughing and laughing, meaning I laughed until my friends came back. The pot was boiling.
ekegusii: Ngachia koigwa igo, ngaseka, ngaseka, ngaseka, mbaka ngaturungana. Naende ngaseka, ngaseka mbaka nkarera. Naende ngaseka, ngaseka, yaani ngaseka mbaka bagakaga nabeire richara. Chimbaru chikang’atia.

english: He asked while laughing, "Mogeni, do you remember that story?
ekegusii: Konakora goseka kamoboria, “Mogeni, ng’ai omanyerete omogano oyio?”

english: Mogeni answered, "What story?
ekegusii: Mogeni akaboria, “Mogano ki?”

english: It was about Motanya and the Banyaribari, and the story of those people from Nyamira, Bogirango Bosongo.
ekegusii: O Motanya na Abanyaribari, no omogano oyio no oyoseito, aria Nyamira, Bogirango Bosongo.

english: Makairo the elder was a man who was known for helping people with their problems. A time came when an elder named Nyakundi fell ill and needed help with his livestock. Then everyone gathered, and Gesokera helped them until he was exhausted. That day he received a gift of gratitude for his efforts. The gift was a cow, but it died due to illness. The people blamed him, accusing him of witchcraft. Five men came to investigate.
ekegusii: Seito Makairo omogaka oyomo narenge ore korokwa Gesokera Nyandagesera bwanchete enyama mono. Rituko erimo omogaka onde ore korokwa Nyakundi akamochiika ekegeni komana chiombe. Ekero baika aroro, Gesokera agasokera endagera mbaka agasinywa koimoka. Endagera eyio aigaterete egachaka komobeta korwa nda. Agachaka gokema na kwana buna emori yarire chibando chinyinge ekooreka. Abamura makamobogoria gochia sukunyoma bakamwengera esabuni aroka endagera abanto batano bararie baigote.

english: The relatives of the elder gathered to discuss how to avenge themselves. They agreed that they would not allow anyone to help Gesokera again.
ekegusii: Abagaka ba seito bagasoka ase ogochika omonto okobasareria obogeni. Kobairana nka Makairo bagatiana buna onde tabase gochika omogaka Gesokera gochia kegeni kende.

english: Later, Makairo learned that the elder named Ndemo had been accused of witchcraft. He called the relatives together and told them that they should not accuse Gesokera. Gesokera went to the elder Ndemo and apologized to him and his people. He explained everything to them.
ekegusii: Naende rinde bono Makairo gekirete tokoigwa buna omogaka onde okorokwa Ndemo nere orangerigwe ekegeni. Agaetia abagaka bande tachiika Gesokera. Korende buna seito Makairo totari gokiria ng’ana, omonto akamonyerera Gesokera. Gesokera akagenda bw’ omogaka Ndemo akanyora abande no bare bakobanga esabaria. Akababoria gose mbamoire obogeni nere.

english: Ndemo said, "Yes, Gesokera, I forgive you for the great offense against Nyakundi. But this matter will not be forgotten.
ekegusii: Ndemo kamokania, “Yaya, Gesokera, nkwaretete obosoku obonene o mosubati o Nyakundi. Aye ne esese embe etari bogeni.”

english: Gesokera replied sadly, saying, "Yes, father Tingonkora, Ndemo.
ekegusii: Gesokera agachaka gosorora buna omwana obwatirwe na amamocho ogosorora taitwa, “Yaya, gaki Tingonkora bo kabere, Ndemo.”

english: Ndemo continued, "Yes! You have caused trouble for our community.
ekegusii: Ndemo akanga pi, “Yaya! Orabaise gochia gokwera aria oboko otoreterere.”

english: Gesokera begged him and pleaded, "Father, father, father, please don't let us suffer.
ekegusii: Gesokera agatugama nse na gosorora mono, “Gaki, gaki, gaki, abagaka baminto timontiga.”

english: The people of Gusii also gathered and pleaded, saying that the child should not be punished because of what happened. The relatives consulted each other about how to deal with Ndemo and the people of Nyamusi Etari Bitutu, Bigirango Irianyi.
ekegusii: Seito Gusii monto mosacha gocha gotugama nse na gosorora buna omwana nabo ogokaga buna na amaene agoteba. Abagaka bagancherana komoira oboko bwa Ndemo aaria Nyamusi Etari Bitutu, Bigirango Irianyi.

english: Then they took the livestock to a place where there was plenty of grass. They drove the cattle and goats to a pasture near Gesokera, where he was still suffering.
ekegusii: Ekero baigete ekegeni endagera ekarosigwa enyinge. Kobakona koragera botuko rende seito Gusii sitima etaiyo mono ne ebibeya togwokia. Bakaragera igo onde tachia korora Gesokera gagosokera naende.

english: That evening, they walked until they reached a dark place. Then they began to plan how to punish Gesokera and make him regret his actions. They decided to take revenge on him.
ekegusii: Akaigatera bono naende mbaka enda ekaba buna omonyocho. Ekero yachaka komoresania Gesokera akaimoka korwa nyomba akagenda gochia gesona. Agetoora ebwobi okonagokema.

english: An old woman named Momanyi approached him and started asking questions. She asked, "Elder, why are you so sad?
ekegusii: Omosae oyomo bw’ ekenyoro ekio okorokwa Momanyi akamorora. Akamoboria, “Omogaka, naki imbuya okare bori?”

english: Gesokera replied, trembling slightly, "Because I am afraid of being beaten.
ekegusii: Gesokera akamotebia, ogotogota but ekeragita, “Nabeire buna riria nabete.”

english: Momanyi asked, "Why are you afraid?
ekegusii: Momanyi akamoboria, “Naki kwabete?”

english: Because I am afraid of being beaten.
ekegusii: “Nabeire buna riria nabete.”

english: Momanyi grabbed Gesokera and beat him severely. She then sent him to Christopher Monyoncho's house, the son of Araka, which was a place of worship.
ekegusii: Momanyi agakaga Gesokera no oborwaire akabwate. Akaminyoka gochia eero ase abanto bare kona gosiba ekegara na gotengera chisani chia Christopher Monyoncho omwana bw’ Araka, riyo ri ebasweti.

english: Momanyi said, "Mochumbe, confess your sins.
ekegusii: Momanyi gateba, “Mochumbe, kararimia ekenada.”

english: Yes, Momanyi, but what about those who have wronged me? Should I tell them my sins too? Let everyone speak their truth.
ekegusii: “Yaa, Momanyi bono ne ebirecha bikoriete? Ndimie ekenanda abageni bagotenga? Tiga esani eye eraera.”

english: Yes, yes, Mochumbe, the elder has forgiven you.
ekegusii: “Yaya, yaa, Mochumbe, oMogeni orwarire.”

english: Mochumbe confessed his sins.
ekegusii: Mochumbe akarimia ekenanda.

english: Momanyi said, "The elder has forgiven you because you are afraid of being beaten. Is that why you came here?
ekegusii: Momanyi akaboria, “OMogeni orwarire aa ogoteba buna obeire buna riria abete. Ng’o obwate eriogo riaye?”

english: The elder Ndemo sent someone to ask, "Is it true? Is it true? Is it true? This story is unbelievable. Bring me Omo soap!
ekegusii: Omogaka Ndemo akaminyoka gochia isiko ogoteba, “Obe! Obe! Obe! Oyio eriogo riaye ntomanyete. Mwengere esabuni Omo.”

english: They brought Gesokera the soap. They washed the child thoroughly, hoping to cleanse him of his wrongdoing. He slaughtered a young goat and cooked it, knowing that something bad would happen.
ekegusii: Bakengera Gesokera esabuni. Bakamobetereria keero buna omwana ekengwerere bwangire konya erongori. Akaroka chinyama echinde chingima atatakuneti akamanya gocha koba buya.

english: After that incident, they went back to planning how to punish Gesokera further. It is said that the people of Makairo heard about this event and were saddened. They gathered together and discussed it, saying, "Because I am afraid of being beaten.
ekegusii: Korwa erio onde tachia komochika Gesokera gochia bogeni bonde. Ekero seito Makairo twaigwete omogano oyio, togaseka. Gatwarageire twaigotire togachaka togoteba, “Nabeire buna riria nabete.”

english: Everyone laughed at this, saying, "Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha! Because I am afraid of being beaten.
ekegusii: Tomanya goseka bono buna amachore arorire chibando. “Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha! Nabeire buna riria nabete.”

english: And the people of Gusii always say that when someone speaks foolishly or makes empty promises, they are like Nyaribari, the wife of Mogeni.
ekegusii: Na seito Gusii bono buna tonarete goakaakania amang’ana buna embori ekonia egesero, ani amang’ana aikire Nyaribari sobo Mogeni.

english: Edwin son of Okong’o, a prominent person in the Gusii language and the author of the book "The Child of Eight," Mache Ng’umbu.
ekegusii: Edwin bw’ Okong’o, Omosani omonene bwe Ekegusii nere omoriki bwo Omwana Oito o Mache Ng’umbu

english: Photograph taken at Cambria Cemetery, California. Flikr/Wonderlane
ekegusii: Chimbera chie chisese, Cambria Cemetery, California. Flikr/Wonderlane

english: The author and Edwin son of Okong’o, the child of eight, Mache Ng’umbu.
ekegusii: Omoriki ne Edwin bw’ Okong’o, Omwana oito Mache Ng’umbu .

english: People. Storytellers. Ancestors, children of the past. Remember this lesson well!
ekegusii: Minto. Mwanyagetinge. Nyaituga, omwana o baba. Tegerera ngotebie rero amang'ana araa amakong'u pa!

english: Once upon a time, when the land was still new, the elder from Makairo, a man who understood the Gusii customs, went to Kebirigo to learn more about the Gusii traditions.
ekegusii: Kare, kare riria chingoko chiagakamirwe omogaka narenge seito Makairo, aria amaninko Gusii, ang'e ne echiro eria yakumete mono Gusii ekorokwa Kebirigo.

english: Anyone who wants to know about our history should listen carefully to the stories told by our ancestors, or seek guidance. Anyone who wants to understand our culture should respect the wisdom of the elders and honor their teachings. It is important to remember that our ancestors faced many challenges, but they persevered through hard work and determination.
ekegusii: Onye gokagete buna oyo no omogano igoro buna seito tware konywa erongongori etainekiri, kana koganya. Gose onye gokagete ngogotebia nde buna seito tware gokama chingoko, kana gokenderera agwo ekiiriri kio omotembe. Tindi gwatora bobisi buna seito tware gokama chingoko ekero oboremo bwabete chincherere totabwate ase nonya n’ embori okoriisia.

english: That is the story of the elder who lived a long life, and how he taught his children and grandchildren to live in harmony with nature and with each other. The elder was known as Mogaka. Every evening, he would gather his family around the fire and share stories of the past. (This is a good example of how to teach children about their heritage.) Our ancestors worked tirelessly to ensure that future generations would inherit a rich cultural legacy, and we must continue to uphold those values.
ekegusii: Oyo no omogano bw' omogaka oyomo obwate chisemi, korende ekero twarenge abana nigo tware komosekerera. Omogaka oyio nigo are korokwa Mogaka. Magoroba iga ko omobaso okendire nigo agaterekire ebusaa yo obori na abasani baye. (Tari eye ye chibando rero nonya na abaisia abasiniini bakonywa). Kobasiibire ekegara ne chinkore bakonakoererania buna abana ba ng’ina omo, nigo bagaterire emeino emiya. Oyo nanchente ginkonakobategerera nigo orenge korokwa “Mosaiga.”

english: Siberia is cold, oh Siberia is cold, Mosaiga
ekegusii: Siberia ong’e, aye siberia ong’e, mosaigaa

english: Ayeee, ayee Mosaiga
ekegusii: Ayeee, aye mosaiga

english: Give me strength, Mosaiga give me strength to persevere
ekegusii: Toa monto, mosaiga toa monto okobayabaya

english: Our ancestors also say that Mogaka named his clan "Mong’ina". He then went to conquer Mong’ina. He did so with courage and determination.
ekegusii: Kobasiibire bono Mogaka orangeria omong’ina oye ore korokwa Mong’ina. Korende tare komoroka Mong’ina. Nigo akamorangeirie na amasikani.

english: “Yes, my father, I will obey Bosire,” Mogaka declared.
ekegusii: “Aye, baba yane, mosubati on Bosire,” Mogaka arangeria.

english: “Good!”
ekegusii: “Ee!”

english: “I will bring you the head of an enemy.”
ekegusii: “Gaki tomentere a mache a morero.”

english: Mong’ina refused to accept this offer and instead chose to reconcile with his enemies and make peace.
ekegusii: Mong’ina nere okonyora erio konye orasiibire ekemite na abang’ina abaamate kobakona kogosoria na goteera.

english: Therefore, let us remember, let us…
ekegusii: Rero ndero, toe

english: The shield of the warrior, let us…
ekegusii: Echae ya morero toe

english: “I will obey Bosire, but first,” Mogaka said thoughtfully. “Let me see what this shield can do.”
ekegusii: “Mosubati o Bosire naye gaki,” Mogaka omotebia kagoseka. “Ntomanyete buna tari chae ya morero mokonywa agwo chikoni.”

english: “Nyakerario,” Mong’ina replied respectfully. “It has the power to protect us from harm and to guide us on our journey.”
ekegusii: “Nyakerario,” Mong’ina arangeria mosubati oye. “Ereria iso amache gose natotigane tonywe echae eye Kemuma arosia.”

english: Everyone laughed until they were breathless. Mong’ina then became the leader of his people.
ekegusii: Abang’ina na abagaka bonsi baseka mono mbaka baturungana. Mong’ina nigo arenge omong’ina bwamaseko mono.

english: Nyakerario skillfully crafted shields, and the elders cherished them greatly. They also remembered the day when the people of Mong’are gathered together to celebrate their victory, singing and dancing joyfully.
ekegusii: Nyakerario kabamenteire amache, abagaka basiiba ake igo. Nabo rinde kware konyoora abasae bande buna oyomo ore korokwa Mong’are bakonywa bwango, bwango ne endamwamu.

english: “Yes, that Ratemo was very brave,” the elder from Nyambati remarked.
ekegusii: “Aye omoisia oyo Ratemo gwatindire,” omogaka onde ore korokwa Nyambati amotebia.

english: “Yes, let him go,” everyone agreed.
ekegusii: “Ee, tiga agende,” abagaka bonsi bancherana.

english: Mong’are and Ratemo set out on a mission to prove their worth.
ekegusii: Mong’are o Ratemo gachiire bachaka kogamba buna are omonywa bobe.

english: “My friends, let us pray,” Mogaka began. “What shall we offer to appease the spirits?”
ekegusii: “Mbuya twamoseria,” Mogaka ateba. “Mwaigwa bono buna rinde anywa akooga bogakia?”

english: “Bring some honey,” Nyambati suggested. “And some tobacco, so that Momanyi may find ‘esagasaga’ and discover the secrets of the forest.”
ekegusii: “Ayio na amake,” Nyambati ateba. “Rinde momura one Momanyi taigwa ‘esagasaga’ botuko agachia gosoka akamonyora araire omochachaku ime?”

english: “Why does she ask for that?” the elder inquired curiously.
ekegusii: “Naki amokorete?” omogaka onde akaboria.

english: “Because Momanyi is wise and knowledgeable. She knows how to interpret dreams and visions, and she can use her powers to help us overcome obstacles.”
ekegusii: “Gaki Momanyi one ne emechando. Nigo amokururete akamobeka as konye arorire chinsanako magoroba.”

english: Everyone laughed again until they could laugh no more.
ekegusii: Bonsi, abagaka, abang’ina, na abana bagaseka mbaka bagaturungana. Omomura oyomo ekegara gekamotokeria. Tamanyete buna ka abagaka bakogamba nigo okoratiga konywa gwategerera.

english: “Yes, let us allow them to pass,” Nyambati concluded.
ekegusii: “Yaa naye karwe aa tonara egento eke kia abagaka,” Nyambati akamotebia.

english: “Let them go,” Mogaka agreed.
ekegusii: “Tiga bagende bonsi,” Mogaka ateba.

english: “Yes, let Mochumbe go and bring back news of the outside world,” Mong’ina added.
ekegusii: “Ee, tiga Mochumbe ache atwaterie chinko botaraira,” Mong’ina akabatebia.

english: “Alright,” Mogaka conceded. “Let us send messengers. Mochumbe is skilled at gathering information and reporting accurately.”
ekegusii: “Yaya,” Mogaka agakana. “Tumia ebiemba. Egento eke Mochumbe asiiba kiamokorire richara arabaise gweaka egesire.”

english: Mochumbe and his companions traveled far and wide, listening to the BBC Swahili Service.
ekegusii: Mochumbe na bagisangio baye bakagenda gochia saiga gotegerera eretio “BPC Swaeri Sabesi” (BBC Swahili Service).

english: The elders decided that the people should accompany Nyakerario on a visit to the market. They went with gifts. Mogaka refused to sleep, staying awake all night to contemplate his thoughts.
ekegusii: Abagaka bakorora buna abasae bachiire bagatoma Nyakerario gochia kiage abaretere ebuga. Bagatiera na konywa. Mogaka agaansa go kwana amang’ana onde ataare komanya engencho yaye.

english: “This is a good omen, a sign of prosperity! This is a good omen, a sign of prosperity!”
ekegusii: “Esese isiko, ekemoni nyomba! Esese isiko, ekemoni nyomba!”

english: That is when the young boy was born. We know his name, "This is a good omen, a sign of prosperity." He grew up quickly, becoming strong and healthy like an American.
ekegusii: Inche erio nigo narenge omwana omosiniini. Tinamanyete eng’encho ye, “Esese isiko, ekemoni nyomba.” Korende ngakina, ngakora esekenderi ngacha mache ng’umbu, Amerika.

english: First, he told stories about how Americans had destroyed everything with weapons. To make a prosperous home, one needs a cow, a goat, and a hen. The land was fertile and abundant, providing plenty of food. And because of this abundance, people were able to raise children and prosper.
ekegusii: Gaki tiga mbatebie buna Abamerika nigo banchete chisese ne ebimoni mono. Okonyora ekemoni keroseirie nyomba kemenyete buya, nonya mbeba nchiyo kebwenerete goita. Endagera nigo gekogorerwa enga ebisuguti kiabekerwa na amabere. Nonya nase gekobeka echabu go kiabutiarire nigo kebwate abanyene bana goitora.

english: But this story is just beginning. A prosperous home, a beautiful garden, and a television set where people gather to watch. The American way of life has spread throughout Kenya, bringing both benefits and challenges. Meat is expensive, but American meat is readily available. Remember that Ondieki once lamented the loss of traditional foods, saying that they were healthier and more satisfying. But the American way of life, the American dream, is being promoted through special programs and events.
ekegusii: Ne esese nero nigo yanchire mono. Emenyete nyomba, egoikaransa esoba seti igoro yarigereria etelebiseni na abanyene. Esese ya Amerika oise konyereta seito Kenya nigo erakwe bwango mono. Nyama mbese sese ya Amerika terikoria. Tenga buna Ondieki yaito yakaminyokirie egesusu gose egechure yabwata twaria, twanyea amauga. Buna ekemoni kia Amerika, esese ya Amerika nigo ekoroserigwa endagera special ekogorwa korwa etuka.

english: We continue onward, people of Gusii, remembering our traditions. Americans are now involved in politics, claiming that they can bring progress and development. These politicians often use empty promises and lies to deceive people, causing confusion and chaos. The consequences of their actions are felt by everyone, especially the poor and vulnerable.
ekegusii: Tiga bono naende, Omogusii ominto, ngotebie egento kende kiamaseko. Abamerika naende nkoratwara bare amasindano korora buna ning’o obwate esese gose ekemoni egeseera. Amasindano ayio ataraika nigo bakoira chisese ne ebimoni baakana chibesa biasibigwa na konintwa chinchara. Omobui bwa amasindano nigo akoegwa egekombe buna keria abagosoria bakoeegwa.

english: I remember hearing someone say, “What will happen next? Will this dream ever come true?”
ekegusii: Nimanyete ngoteba ore buna, “Etwini gaki naye! Esese eegwe egekombe kiamaminyoko?”

english: Many years later, my mother, Nyaituga, passed away. She left behind a legacy of strength and resilience.
ekegusii: Maene pi ndie esese, tindigokong’aina, Nyaituga o baba. Boria onde bwensi omenyete mache ng’umbu.

english: Americans' obsession with wealth prevents them from finding happiness. They accumulate possessions and money endlessly. I heard that an American spent $4,000 (Ksh. 300,000) to bury his pet.
ekegusii: Chisese ne ebimoni kobiarwarire Abamerika tibari gotiga bikwe. Nigo bakobiira chinyagetari chi ebimoni ne chisese. Nimanyete Omoamerika oyomo oakanete $4,000 (Ksh. 300,000) kobaara esese endwaire.

english: When a pet dies, they perform a ritual called "Putting it to sleep" - they take the animal to a special place. It is said that there is a place called Pet Cemetery, where Americans bury their pets, along with their toys and belongings. They then grieve and mourn, comparing their grief to losing a child.
ekegusii: Esese koyangire kobwena nigo bagokora egento gekorokwa, “Putting it to sleep” – bakonyebeta esindani yakwa ng’ooora. Koyakuure, banyeira ase akorokwa, Pet Cemetery, ase chimbeera chie chisese, ebimoni, ne ching’iti chinde Abamerika batugete nyomba chigotindekwa. Kobanyetindekire nigo bachachana na gwechwanachania buna omoibori okwereirwe no omwana.

english: This is a good omen, a sign of prosperity.
ekegusii: Esese isiko, ekemoni nyomba.

english: --end of article--
ekegusii: --omoerio--

english: Edwin Okongo is also a columnist for Mshale newspaper and maintains his own blog, Okongo's Policy. He studied at California State University in Hayward and the University of California in Berkeley. He is passionate about representing the interests of the Gusii people both within Kenya and abroad. For more information, read his articles on his blog. This man, Okongo, has videos and interesting stories.
ekegusii: Edwin Okongo nere omoriki omonene bwe e bulogi ya Mshale naende omoriki bwe e bulogi yaye omonyene ya Okongo's Policy. Nigo asomete California State University aaria Hayward amo na University ya California aaria Berkeley. Nigo are oyomo bwa Abagusii bari barikire amangana amaya naende amange sana igoro ya Gusii na Kenya. Ka moranche, soma amariko aye ase chibulogi echio nabatebirie igoro. Imbuya mono Okongo ase e vidio amo na egasi engiya.

english: They celebrated with the saying “A good seed grows well during a field trip”, so with joy and enthusiasm they visited the area of The Otenyo Omogusii Cultural Festival, Keroka Town, recently. Initially, I was hesitant, but when I saw it, I liked it, and I felt proud of our culture and heritage because the Abagusii people were represented, and things were done well.
ekegusii: Bagoteba ng'a "Rero mochokoro goika tokoire e field trip", sokoro amo na magokoro nigo bangira aaria ase The Otenyo Omogusii Cultural Festival, Keroka Town, recently. Initially, nigo narutete chintacho, korende ki naika aroro, nigo nabete no omogoko ase ogosomigwa na kwoorokigwa buna Abagusii twakabeire, ne ebinto twagatumiire.

english: Unless we visit the museum which displays our artifacts and our customs of the Abagusii people, and this is the best repository we have for now, with The Otenyo Cultural Group, and others scattered online too. It is possible that artifacts of Omogusii are elsewhere, and they are scattered in many places. Therefore we have no central repository. We hope that things will change in the next few years with the establishment of the Omogusii Museum and Cultural Center.
ekegusii: Unless twaagachire e museum yaito ekogacha our artifacts amo no omogano oito bwa Abagusii, eye nero the best repository we have for now, with The Otenyo Cultural Group, and others scattered online buna eye. It is possible nga artifacts chio Omogusii ne chinyinge, and they are scattered in many places. Korende we have no central repository.
